description: On 1 December 2023, the Kebbi militia shot and killed a member of an unidentified armed group in Tunga village (Bunza, Kebbi). The suspect was killed while shooting arrows indiscriminately at the people.

On 1 December 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians at Gwamatse village in Wurno LGA (Sokoto) and killed two persons. The police claimed that at least three people were killed, and one other person was injured.

On 1 December 2023, an unspecified number of policemen abducted a civilian at the Choba axis (Obio, Rivers) and demanded for a ransom of 1 million naira. The abductors were arrested by the police and the victim was rescued around 5 December.
On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a fisher in Twon-Brass (Brass, Bayelsa). They injured many fishers and abducted an unspecified number of others.

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the security officials (coded as the police) while trying to attack the INEC Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) at his residence in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The firefight raged for about 30 minutes before reinforcement arrived, and the militia fled. Properties were destroyed, including one of the attacker's cars. There were no fatalities.

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a school girl on her way back home from school at Ikotun (Alimosho, Lagos). The abductors assumed that the victim's father is a wealthy politician capable of paying ransom, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Jakana (Konduga, Borno) and forced the soldiers to retreat. 1 was wounded, and 2 ISWAP fighters were killed before they were forced to flee.

On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two CJTF members after they attacked their checkpoint in Katarko (Gujba, Yobe). They seized three rifles. Another source reported that ISWAP lost an unspecified number of fighters.
On 1 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two Nigerian soldiers and injured many others in Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The militia seized the rifles of the slain soldiers.

On 1 December 2023, the Nigerian military killed an unspecified number of IPOB/ESN in the Umuogwo forest (Ohaji, Imo). They recovered numerous weapons. Unknown fatalities coded as 3 (low-intensity conflict).

On 1 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians across different areas of Tangaza LGA (Sokoto). The assailants were enforcing strange laws on the residents, collected zakat (alms) and flogged defaulters. The sum of 500 naira was collected as levy for cows and 200 for rams from households that own livestock.
On 1 December 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed three vigilantes in an ambush on the outskirts of Kankara (Kankara, Katsina).
On 2 December 2023, a Sokoto militia killed five residents when they attacked Kojiyo ward (Goronyo, Sokoto). Many other residents were abducted.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian military and local vigilantes repelled an attack launched by the Katsina militia on Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). The group invaded the village, aiming at abducting people from five houses. There were no fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, a Niger militia attacked commuters between Luma and Babanna villages (Borgu, Niger), the bus driver was killed and at least eight passengers were abducted. A ransom of 17 million naira was demanded for the abductees.
On 2 December 2023, the Sokoto militia attacked and injured one person in the Atakwanyo community (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). They abducted three others.
On 2 December 2023, a Kaduna militia killed an off-duty soldier and abducted eleven residents of Anguwan Tudu in Azzara coded to Gidan Azara (Kachia, Kaduna). One of the abductees was later released.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP when they invaded a vigilante post in Katarko (Gujba, Yobe). The vigilante had engaged them before the military reinforcement arrived. ISWAP fighters retreated and fled with gun wounds. Two vigilante members died in the clash, but ISWAP fatalities were unknown. 2 fatalities coded.

On 2 December 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops at a checkpoint between Jakana and Mainok, coded to Mainok (Kaga, Borno). Two ISWAP fighters were killed in the encounter, and other fighters escaped with gun wounds. a Nigerian soldier got injured in the clash. There were two fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, the Nigerian troops repelled the ISWAP attack at Charles One, along the Monguno- Maiduguri road, coded to Monghuno (Monguno, Borno). The militia came on two gun trucks and 20 motorcycles. There were no fatalities.

On 2 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a student of the Gateway ICT Polytechnic at their off-campus hostel in the Larufi area of Ode-Remo (Remo North, Ogun). They injured many other students.

On 2 December 2023, an unidentified armed group of six abducted three workers on a poultry farm at Atoyo town in the Itele area (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The abductees were initially 5, before two of them were released by the abductors on the same day. 20 fowls were killed by the assailants while the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the attack.

On 2 December 2023, over 10 NSCDC operatives beat up and wounded a journalist in Awka (Awka South, Anambra) over unspecified reasons. The victim claimed that the assailants boasted about being untouchable over the attack.
On 3 December 2023, the Sokoto militia attacked Chaco or Chacho village (Wurno, Sokoto). The militia injured one person and abducted twelve others. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen and hunters who invaded their hideout in an armed clash around Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa).Two members of the group were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, four rifles and 92 rounds of live ammunition were recovered.

On 3 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two landlords from their houses at Asokoro extension, coded to Asokoro (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The victims were abducted around 11pm and a ransom of 20 million was demanded for their release.
On 3 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army checkpoint in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). The soldiers were forced to abandon the post and retreated. There were no fatalities.
On 3 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have shelled the Nigerian Army base with five mortars in Waijroko (Damboa, Borno). No damage claim was made. There were no fatalities.

On 3 December 2023, DSS officials clashed with NSCDC officials and private security guards at a hospital in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The clash was over a disagreement over a DSS official who was brought in sick. An unspecified number of NSCDC and private guards were wounded.

On 4 December 2023, Icelanders loyal to General Danger abducted and later killed three civilians at Egbe community, coded to Akinima (Ahoada West, Rivers). The victims' whose bodies were found a few hours after they were abducted had an altercation with the mother of the militia leader, and he threatened to deal with them.
On 4 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and wounded some residents in Gandu (Lafia, Nasarawa). They abducted many others. The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 4 December 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists belonging to a local defense militia killed 33 civilians, 10 in Ganpeto, 21 in Garbatau and 2 others in Hawan Mata villages in Bali LGA (Taraba). Many cows were rustled and up to 30 motorcycles belonging to the victims were stolen while other pastoralists fled to Adamawa state. Other sources report that the assailants disguised in the regalia of the local defense militia.

On 4 December 2023, NDLEA operatives were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group that blocked the road in an attempt to prevent the operatives from gaining access into Opuje community (Owan West, Edo) where a warehouse containing marijuana was located. Three operatives were wounded including one who sustained head injuries in a clash that lasted for two hours, their operational vehicles were riddled with bullets. At least three suspects were arrested.
On 4 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a minibus, killed the driver and abducted 8 people along the axis Luma-Babana, coded to Babanna (Borgu, Niger).

On 4 December 2023, the MNJTF troops of 242 Battalion cleared ISWAP enclaves in Ngurnoa, Gumnari, Nairawa and engaged the militia in a firefight in Amburam village, coded to Gunmari (Monguno, Borno). They killed five ISWAP fighters, and one Nigerian soldier got injured in the clash. They recovered 1 x GPMG and 4 x AK 47 magazines.

On 4 December 2023, the Nigerian police engaged ISWAP in a firefight at a police checkpoint in Mairari, coded to Konduga (Konduga, Borno). The militia invaded the checkpoint, but the police repelled them. They damaged the Police Armored Personnel Carrier and went away with two police rifles. There were no fatalities.

On 4 December 2023, policemen raided the hideout of ESN militants led by Ebube Virus and Ishaka and engaged them in an armed clash at Umuogu Amuzu, coded as Umuogu (Aboh Mbaise, Imo). One militant who was second in command to Ebube Virus was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, one rifle and 19 rounds of live ammunition were recovered.

On 4 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the house of a local traditional chief of Gujba in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Borno). They engaged in a firefight with the Chief's guards and overpowered them. They burned the house and seized five rifles. There were no fatalities.
On 4 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a CJTF member in a firefight near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). They attacked the CJTF patrol and overpowered them, forcing them to retreat.
On 5 December 2023, a Sokoto militia killed two civilians, wounded 24 others and an unspecified number of people when they invaded Rarah town (Rabah, Sokoto).

On 5 December 2023, the Nigerian soldiers, CJTF and local hunters repelled Boko Haram (JAS) and engaged them in a firefight when attempting to invade a Fulani settlement near Malari neighborhood of Konduga (Konduga, Borno). One man, likely to be a bystander, was shot and wounded. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2023, the Ambazonian invaded Belegete, also spelled Balegeta (Obanliku, Cross River) and attacked the residents. Many people sustained various injuries, including cutlass cuts. The militia opened fire sporadically and abducted some residents. There were no fatalities.

On 5 December 2023, a policeman shot and wounded a civilian at a stop and search checkpoint in Ughelli (Ughelli North, Delta) for unclear reasons. The victim who is a teenager was taken to the hospital while the policeman was arrested.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked and injured an unspecified number of Nigerian troops during a patrol between Mallam Fatori and Baga, coded to Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). They forced the troops to retreat and seized a rifle. There were no fatalities.
On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a soldier when they attacked Nigerian Army checkpoint in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). They injured another soldier and forced others to retreat.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a Nigerian soldier when they attacked the Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Borno). The onslaught forced the soldiers to retreat, and the militia seized a rifle.
On 5 December 2023, the Katsina militia attacked Gago village in Dutsin Ma LGA, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). They injured one person and abducted another.

On 5 December 2023, ISWAP claimed a machine gun attack on the Nigerian troops, but another source reported that they shot at some travelers (rather than the military) around Limankara (Gwoza, Borno). The militia retreated, and the passengers arrived safely in Maiduguri. There were no fatalities.
On 6 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a mechanic and abducted his wife and daughters in Gandu village (Lafia, Nasarawa).
On 6 December 2023, the Katsina militia killed the headmaster of the Maidabino Primary school, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 6 December 2023, the Zamfara militia attacked the Tofa Ruwan Magami community near Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) for two consecutive days. They abducted three persons within the two days of raids. They later released one of the abductees to relay the demand of a two million naira ransom to the community.
On 6 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF and injured their members near Yamtage or Yamtaji (Gwoza, Borno). They outgunned them and forced them to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 6 December 2023, an unidentified armed group injured the personal assistant of the Nasarawa State deputy governor while attempting to abduct him in the Tudun Kauri area of Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). The victim escaped abduction and was taken to the hospital for treatment of his minor injuries.
Around 6 December 2023 (as reported), soldiers killed three suspected informants of a Kaduna militia at Kohoto, coded to nearby Janjala (Kagarko, Kaduna). Six other suspects were arrested.

On 7 December 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed a militiaman during a fire exchange with the Zamfara militia in Faru, Faru Magami ward, location coded to known village on the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). The troop acted on the information of the impending destruction of farms in the village and responded swiftly. Many of the militiamen escaped with gun wounds. There was one fatality.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman along Omuawa and Ubima road, coded to Ubima (Ikwerre, Rivers). The armed group ambushed the woman, dragged her out of her car and took her away. They left her car behind.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at the bus conveying the Sunshine Stars Football Club of Akure along the Benin-Ore Expressway, coded to Ore (Odigbo, Ondo). The gunshots injured a team official and team members. The team was travelling to Benin for a football event when the incident occurred. There were no fatalities.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted ten students of the Federal University of Lafia at their off-campus hostel in Gandu village (Lafia, Nasarawa). The armed group fired sporadically in the air before taking the students away. Other students later protested against the incessant abduction of their colleagues, coded separately. The abductees were released on 10 December, sources report that 7 to 8 students were released.
On 7 December 2023, the Sokoto militia abducted six people (four women and two men) from Bijeje village (Goronyo, Sokoto). No further details.

On 7 December 2023, the Ambazonian abducted about 30 people including the village head, some youths and women in Belegete or Balegeta (Obanliku, Cross River). The abduction followed the attack on the community by the militia on 5 December 2023, coded separately.

On 7 December 2023, the Zamfara militia, for the second day, attacked the Tofa Ruwan Magami community near Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). They abducted three persons in two days of the raid. They later released one of the abductees to relay the demand of a two million naira ransom to the community.

On 7 December 2023, the joint troops of Operation Hadarain Daji shot and killed two militiamen when they engaged the Zamfara militia in a firefight in Danjibga village (Tsafe, Zamfara). The clash thwarted the militia invasion of the village. Many of them escaped with bullet wounds, and the army recovered two AK-47 rifles, two magazines and one motorcycle. There were two fatalities.

On 7 December 2023, an unidentified armed group of up to 20 engaged policemen and a local defense militia in an armed clash at Kuchibiyi area in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). One defense militia member was shot and wounded in his hand, three civilians including a couple and one other person were abducted.

On 7 December 2023, the CJTF killed two ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters during a firefight along the Maiduguri-Mafa road, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). CJTF recovered two rifles and two motorcycles from the militia.

On 8 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man in Nsukwa (Aniocha South, Delta) and demanded a ransom of 5 million naira. The victim was rescued by policemen the following day (coded separately).

On 8 December 2023, the Nigerian military engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight in Birnin Yero (Igabi, Kaduna) after the militia raided the village and abducted eleven people. Two of the hostages were killed, and the military rescued nine others. The militia withdrew and fled the scene. There were two fatalities.

On 8 December 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians who were part of the eleven persons that they abducted from Anguwar Maharba and Dandami in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The other 9 abductees were rescued by troops who ambushed the militia [coded separately].

On 8 December 2023, troops of 1 Division ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash while on a clearance operation in the Kanzaure general area of Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The ambush followed a report that the troops received over the abduction of 11 civilians by the militia from Anguwar Maharba and Dandami villages. 9 of the abductees were rescued by the troops who also recovered weapons and ammunition. Casualties are unknown.

On 9 December 2023, policemen were engaged in armed clash with an unidentified armed group when they invaded their hideout in the bush at Egbudu-Akah (Aniocha South, Delta). The group fled and left an abductee behind, one member of the group was killed as a result of bullet wounds that he sustained.

On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one local defense militia member and wounded three others at Bakatumbe village in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). Four civilians were abducted by the assailants who shot sporadically during the raid, and fled towards Lukutu forest after.

On 9 December 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged the IPOB/ESN fighters in a firefight along the Orsumoghu-Ukpor Road, coded to Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). The troops recovered weapons, two handheld radios and pairs of police uniforms from the militia. There were no fatalities.
On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Kpambo Yache village (Ussa, Taraba). No further details.

On 9 December 2023, a Katsina militia engaged a joint security team comprised of soldiers, policemen and Katsina security watch corps operatives in an armed clash at Zakka forest (Safana, Katsina). The security team who were joined by the state governor and his convoy rescued an abductee. There were no fatalities.
On 9 December 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians at Tungun Tudu community near Asara (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). One person was killed, many others were wounded.

On 9 December 2023, some Nigerian soldiers tortured and wounded a police officer (off duty) around the Nigerian Army's 63 Brigade in Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta) over an allegation of wrong parking and refusal to comply with a soldier's directive. The victim was taken to a hospital for treatment.

On 9 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted residents in Dei-Dei community (Abuja Municipal, FCT). 23 persons were initially abducted, 7 of them were rescued by a local defense militia who trailed the abductors, leading to their release.
On 9 December 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian troops around Malari, along Maiduguri-Konduga Road, Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Casualties unknown. No further details.

On 10 December 2023, a Kaduna militia were repelled by policemen who responded to a distress call and rescued a woman whom the militia abducted at Dogarawa (Sabon Gari, Kaduna). Casualties are unknown.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the aide of the traditional ruler of Akpabuyo LGA and abducted the ruler from his residence in Asin Ufot (Akpabuyo, Cross River) coded to Ikot Nakanda.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia and private security guards in an armed clash at a night club in Oba (Idemili South, Anambra) following the guards' and militia's resistance to the attempted abduction of the club owner by the group. Between 3 to 24 persons including security guards, defense militiamen and club goers were killed, the security guard who resisted the group's entry initially was decapacitated, his head and leg were cut off and taken away.
On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted another when raiding the Beti Giware community (Fufore, Adamawa). No further details.

On 10 December 2023, the Nigerian police engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight after the militia abducted a woman from her residence in the Sabon Gari area, Zaria (Zaria, Kaduna). The police rescued the hostage. There were no fatalities.

On 10 December 2023, a Katsina militia engaged policemen and operatives of the Katsina security watch corps in an armed clash at Kwari Mai Zurfi in Makera district (Dutsinma, Katsina) when the joint security team responded to a report that the militia had blocked the road. Three militiamen were killed and one Katsina security watch corps operative was wounded.

Around 10 December 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia attacked civilians and killed many people in Kidandan community (Giwa, Kaduna) over their inability to meet up with the militia's demands. The militia stole from the residents, abducted an unspecified number of persons, other residents fled the area. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 10 December 2023, ISWAP claimed that they attacked a position of Civilian JTF operatives and engaged them in an armed clash at Chul (Askira Uba, Borno), forcing the operatives to withdraw. Casualties are unknown.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed four civilians and wounded an unspecified number of others when they attacked Dungwel community in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The house of the community's monarch was set ablaze with the occupants inside, until soldiers arrived and rescued them. Some sources report that the monarch escaped, others report that he was wounded in the attack.

On 10 December 2023, the Police engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight and killed three militiamen on the Dutsin Ma-Kankara highway, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia had blocked the highway and attacked the commuters before the Police were deployed there. There were three fatalities.
On 10 December 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 30 residents of Unguwan Liman in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically when they invaded the community.

On 10 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and three of her children including a six-month old baby at Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductors shot sporadically when they invaded the area, other sources report that 7 persons were abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands. Three abductees were released.

On 11 December 2023, soldiers in collaboration with policemen and a local defense militia raided the hideout of IPOB/ ESN militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra). 1 militant was killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, ammunition, locally made hand grenades, police uniforms and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 11 December 2023, the Katsina militia abducted a woman and her baby in Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 11 December 2023, the Police engaged the Sokoto militia in an armed fight in Lugu village (Wurno, Sokoto). The Police intervened after the militia had killed two people in the village. One police officer was killed in the clash, and many militiamen escaped with gun wounds. There were three fatalities.

On 11 December 2023, a Niger and Zamfara militia led by Ali Kachalla and Dogo Gide engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash at Mangoro community (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The Nigerian Air Force provided air support to the ground troops, and killed 32 militiamen including Ali Kachalla, several others fled with gunshot wounds from the clash which lasted five hours.
On 11 December 2023, the Community Watch Corps and the vigilante group clashed with the Katsina militia in Kinfau, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina). Two militiamen were killed.

On 11 December 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering nine, two of whom were dressed in military uniforms attacked commuters at the Fidiwo axis (Obafemi, Ogun). One person was shot and killed, another person who attempted to escape sustained injuries and seven others were abducted. Policemen rescued the abductees after 4 days, and claimed that they combed the bushes and found them.

On 11 December 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked civilians and killed a Civilian JTF operative who is presumed to have been off-duty after he was identified by the trousers he was wearing at an IDP settlement in Shuwari (Jere, Borno) coded to Khaddamari. The militants shot sporadically, looted goods from shops, punctured the tires of some vehicles and stole several motorcycles, four of which were recovered by soldiers two days later.

On 11 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a position of Nigerian troops and Civilian JTF operatives and engaged them in an armed clash at Azir, coded as Azir Multe (Damboa, Borno), forcing the troops to withdraw. The militants also claimed to have seized two rifles and burned the position. Casualties are unknown.
On 11 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a position of Nigerian troops and engaged them in an armed clash at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno), forcing the soldiers to withdraw. Casualties are unknown.
On 11 December 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops on patrol in Miyanti village, Bama (Bama, Borno). The militiamen were forced to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 11 December 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops at the Pump House in Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). The clash forced the militiamen to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 11 December 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian troops at the Ngala Bridge, Ngala (Ngala, Borno). The ensuing firefight forced the militia to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 11 December 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 15 engaged a local defense militia that attempted to resist their attack in an armed clash at Gbaupe village, coded to nearby Lugbe (Abuja Municipal, FCT). One defense militia member was killed, 12 persons including a 13-year old girl and a 9-year old boy were abducted while two of them escaped as they were being taken away.
On 11 December 2023, the Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of people from Kwarom-Kwarom village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.

On 11 December 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted 30 villagers around Unwar Liman under the Gwada ward in Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). The militia released sixteen of the hostages, keeping the remaining fourteen captives with them.

On 11 December 2023, soldiers attacked farmers on their farms, wounded them and looted their properties over claims that the lands which were allocated to the farmers belonged to the military, as claimed by the farmers. Location coded to Ikeja (Ikeja, Lagos).
On 12 December 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked Zurmi town (Zurmi, Zamfara). The militia shot sporadically in the town, killed one person, wounded two and abducted 15 others.

On 12 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four civilians along Igwuruta - Airport road (Ikwerre, Rivers) and took them to their hideout in Emohua LGA . The abductees were rescued by the police on 14 December [coded separately] after the sum of 800,000 and 1,900,000 respectively were collected from some of the abductees by the armed group.

On 12 December 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed four soldiers who were on escort duty along Ahoada/ Abua road (Obua, Rivers). Two civilian drivers were also killed, two Korean expatriates were abducted. The abductees were released around 31 December, the police claimed that their abductors released them following pressure that was mounted on them by tactical teams and the military.

On 12 December 2023, the Nigerian military clashed with the Kaduna militia in Kwanar Mutua, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They recovered three motorcycles from the militia. There were no fatalities.
On 12 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted a farmer from his farm in Kwanar Maje (Anka, Zamfara). No further details.

On 12 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man after he boarded a cab along Giri highway coded to Gwagwalada (Gwagwalada, FCT). The abductee is the president of Abuja newspapers distributors association, 15 million naira was demanded as ransom.

On 12 December 2023, the Nigerian military ambushed and engaged the Kaduna militia in a firefight around the Dogon Dawa Damari area, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). They recovered weapons from the militia. There were no fatalities.
On 12 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted seventeen people from Marraraban Kunini, Kunini (Lau, Taraba). No further details.

On 12 December 2023, the Plateau militia shot and killed four people in Gundum village, coded to Gindiri (Mangu, Plateau). The militia injured many people and set houses on fire. The Nigerian security agencies were deployed to calm the situation.

On 13 December 2023, the Nigerian military, in conjunction with other security agencies (likely to be the police and DSS), raided an IPOB/ESN hideout at Christ the King Catholic Church in Ameta, Mgbowo (Agwu, Enugu). The Autopilot faction of the militiamen was in a meeting, planning to overthrow the leadership of the group, when the troops invaded them. The troops shot and wounded the commander of the militia as he tried to escape. He was arrested together with three other militiamen. The troops retrieved one AK-47 rifle, two AK-47 magazines, 25 rounds of 7.62mm NATO special ammunition and one pump-action rifle. There were no fatalities.

On 13 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have engaged Civilian JTF operatives in an armed clash at Yuye, assumed and coded as Yoyo (Kukawa, Borno) and that an unspecified number of operatives were wounded, others fled while an unspecified amount of ammunition was seized.

On 13 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Civilian JTF headquarters and engaged the operatives and soldiers in an armed clash at Ngwom (Mafa, Borno). Three soldiers and three Civilian JTF operatives were killed and one SUV was destroyed. The militants also claimed to have detonated an IED on a patrol, killing and wounding the occupants of the SUV which was also destroyed. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3. 9 fatalities.

On 13 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a military checkpoint and engaged the soldiers in an armed clash in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The militants also claimed to have wounded an unspecified number of soldiers while the others fled.

On 13 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted ten passengers along Ette - Umuopu Enugu-Ezike Road, coded to Umuopu (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The victims were travelling from Abuja when they were abducted. One of the passengers escaped, and the group drove the remaining passengers and the driver into the bush.

Around 13 December 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted 13 civilians from their residences in Unguwar Liman, Igabi LGA (Kaduna). The abductees were part of the 30 abductees who were abducted from the area during the month (coded separately), a total of 22.5 million naira was paid as ransom for the victims who were released in two batches.

On 14 December 2023, the Nigerian Navy patrol engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight on the Atlantic Ocean on their way to Oron, coded to Oron (Oron, Akwa Ibom). The militiamen who had abducted the Paramount Ruler of Akpabuyo were intercepted by the military, killing ten of them. The traditional ruler was rescued and taken to the hospital for treatment. There are ten fatalities.

On 14 December 2023, the Nigerian troops of the OPHD engaged the Zamfara militia in a firefight in Rukudawa (Zurmi, Zamfara), Dumburum and Dada villages, coded separately. The troops killed one of the militiamen in the three encounters (fatality coded to Dada) while others escaped with gun wounds.

Around 24 December 2023 (between 23 - 25 December), the joint security team, involving the police, DSS and hunters, engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in Tukuba Forest, Tukuba (Kuje, Federal Capital Territory). The troops killed six militiamen and wounded others who later escaped with gun wounds. There were six fatalities.

On 24 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed twelve people and abducted three women in Kurya village (Rabah, Sokoto). A woman, her daughter-in-law and two children were burnt to death during the attack. The military later engaged the militia in a firefight, coded separately. There were twelve fatalities.

On 24 December 2023, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with the Sokoto militia in Kurya village (Rabah, Sokoto). The military intervened after the militia had killed twelve people and abducted others from the village, coded separately. The militia suffered heavy losses but went away with the bodies of their members. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted twenty-five passengers along the Ofante-Emodu-Unyi Ogugu Road in Ofante (Olamaboro, Kogi). The armed group dressed in military uniforms blocked the highway during the abduction.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded three people attempting to escape abduction in Tokulo (Bwari, Federal Capital Territory). The armed group abducted six others. The injured were taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 24 December 2023, the Plateau militia, in a coordinated attack, killed 79 persons in Ndun, Ngyong, Murfet, Makundary, Tamiso, Chiang, Tahore, Gawarba, Dares, Meyenga, Darwat and Butura Kampani village in Bokkos LGA, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). The militia also killed 17 others in Barkin Ladi LGA on the same night, coded separately. The militia burned down over two hundred houses, twenty-seven motorcycles and eight motor vehicles. Other sources reported over 150 persons were killed in all the attacks. Seventy-nine fatalities coded.

On 24 December 2023, a clash between suspected Eiye and Black Axe cult groups resulted in the killing of a journalist, the head of a vigilante group and another person at different locations in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The attacks were suspected to be a reprisal over the cult clash in the previous week, where the mother of a cult member was killed when the militia missed their target, coded separately. There were three fatalities.

On 24 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a truck driver in his house in Etiti village in Enugwu-Agidi, coded to Enugu-Ukwu (Njikoka, Anambra). The armed group released their hostage on 26 December 2023 and dumped him by the roadside. No ransom payment was reported.

On 25 December 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a youth leader and abducted four others in the Nde Three Corners community, also known as Nde 3 (Ikom, Cross River). They dragged the body of their victim into the bush and proceeded to shoot and wounded two other people who were returning from the farm.
Around 25 December 2023 (as reported), a suspected cult group shot and killed a student in Nkwagu (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). No further details.

On 25 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted seven farmers in Yarkofoji (Bakura, Zamfara). The abduction was a reaction to the military invasion and displacement of the militiamen from their camps.

On 25 December 2023, the Guyik and Daklam communities clashed in Jakusko (Jakusko, Yobe) over the control and ownership of a river bordering the two communities. An unspecified number of people were injured. There were no fatalities.

On 25 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a pregnant woman in Ijebu-Igbo community (Ijebu North, Ogun). They seized the woman and the husband in front of their house but left her husband behind; the police rescued the hostage the following day.
On 25 December 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base with seven mortar shells in Waijroko (Damboa, Borno). No further details.
On 25 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed 1 person in Warankai village (Goronyo, Sokoto). The militia also injured one person and abducted four others.

On 25 December 2023, a security guard of a private company shot and killed a man in Elele Alimini (Emohua, Rivers). The victim was returning from the farm when the guard shot and killed him. The community youth deposited the victim's body at the gate of the company, but the company returned it to the killing scene. No further information.

On 25 December 2023, the suspected Boko Haram militants (JAS) shot and killed two people in the Kwapre community, also called Kopre (Hong, Adamawa). They invaded the community on motorcycles, carted away food items, and escaped into the Sambisa Forest after killing two people. There were two fatalities.

On 26 December 2023, a Nigerian soldier beat a truck driver to death for refusing to bribe him at a checkpoint crossing along the Dikwa-Gamboru Ngala road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The Nigerian Army arrested the soldier.

On 26 December 2023, the police, in conjunction with a local hunter group, engaged a Bauchi militia in a firefight and killed six militiamen in Ningi LGA, coded to Ningi (Ningi, Bauchi). The police recovered two AK-47 rifles, 55 live ammunition rounds, the sum of four million, five hundred and eighty thousand naira and other stolen items from the militia.
On 26 December 2023, suspected pastoralists killed a man at a village in Logo LGA, coded to Ugba (Logo, Benue). The militia also abducted their victim's parents. No further details.

On 26 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of travelers, including a groom and his family members, along the Lokoja- Abuja Road, Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductors demanded a 250-million-naira ransom. They released the hostages on 27 December 2023 after receiving an unspecified ransom payment.

On 26 December 2023, the Katsina militia opened fire at the Community Watch Corps' vehicle in an ambush around Dutse na Tara, Faskari LGA, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina). Two of the Corps died instantly, and two others died at the hospital. There were four fatalities.
On 26 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person for resisting abduction in Sakamaru (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia attacked and injured another.

On 27 December 2023, about 50 members of an unidentified armed group abducted many traders after raiding a market in Gongon Maliki (Yorro, Taraba). The armed group invaded the market on motorcycles and blocked all the entrances to prevent the traders from escaping. They dispossessed the traders of money and other valuables and abducted some.

On 27 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a lecturer at the Nasarawa State University after raiding his house in Old Barracks, Kokouna (Kokona, Nasarawa). The hostage was rescued on the following day after the police engaged the armed group in a firefight in Ogba Forest, coded separately. The police arrested a student in connection with the abduction.
On 27 December 2023, an unidentified armed group raped a 14-year old girl at Elekahia (Port Harcourt, Rivers) and threatened to kill her if she reported the incident.

On 27 December 2023, ISWAP fighters engaged in a firefight with the Nigerian military in Kwada village (Chibok, Borno). The militiamen shot and injured four soldiers and burned one armored personnel carrier. They seized a gun truck from the military. There were no fatalities.

On 27 December 2023, the Zamfara militia ambushed some commuters and abducted seven along the Federal highway in Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The militia opened fire on the vehicles and forced them to halt. They set fire to a vehicle together with the passenger's luggage. They took the abducted away through the Dangaza village.

On 27 December 2023, the Kaduna militia shot and killed two villagers in Fina village, under Gwada ward, Igabi LGA, coded to Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). They abducted seven villagers and wounded three others, who were later taken to the hospital for treatment. The militia went away with several motorcycles.

On 27 December 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted an off-duty Air Force officer, his wife, and a teenager who was visiting them from their residence in Igabi (Igabi, Kaduna). The assailants invaded the staff quarters of the National Eye Center Kaduna where they resided and went directly to the victims' house which they forcefully entered. The soldier's wife is an ophthalmologist at the eye center, and a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded. Only the officer was released on 8 March after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom. The female medical doctor and her nephew were released on 30 October 2024 after a series of protests by the Association of Resident Doctors.

On 27 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and injured a woman and her baby in the Chimola community (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia fired shots indiscriminately, and the stray bullets hit the victims. There were no fatalities.

On 28 December 2023, the police, in conjunction with the vigilante group, engaged an unidentified armed group in a firefight in the forest at Ogba village, Nasarawa Egon (Nasarawa Eggon, Nasarawa). The police were on the trail of an abducted University lecturer when they clashed with the armed group. They rescued the hostage and took him to the hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 21 travelers along Ajaokuta - Itobe road (Ajaokuta, Kogi) and took them into a forest in Ajaokuta. The abductees were rescued by security operatives and local defense militia men on 30 December [coded separately], some of the abductors were also arrested. Other sources report that 24 abductees were rescued.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group that was fleeing from the police killed two civilians at Wulko community (Nasarawa Eggon, Nassarawa) coded to Nasarawa Egon. The group had abducted a lecturer [coded separately] and had police forces on their trail after their hideout was discovered.

On 28 December 2023, a suspected cult group attacked and stabbed one member of the Amotekun Corps with a knife at the entrance of the Osun State Polytechnic, Iree (Boripe, Osun). The Corp members had been invited to an Anti-cultism campaign on the campus, but the militia attacked them and prevented them from entering the campus. There were no fatalities.
On 28 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person in the Basana Community, coded to Gada (Gada, Sokoto). They also abducted an unspecified number of people from the community.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted eighteen people from Kuduru village (Bwari, Federal Capital Territory). Other sources report that seven persons were abducted and one of them was murdered on 23 February 2024 (coded separately) due to the inability of the victims' families to pay the 290 million naira demanded as ransom.

On 28 December 2023, ISWAP fighters, armed with anti-aircraft guns, invaded the Mobile Police Base in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The militiamen overpowered the police after a gunfire exchange and proceeded to open fire at the civilians indiscriminately for about an hour before they voluntarily left the town. There were no fatalities.
On 28 December 2023, the Sokoto militia shot and killed one person in the Mallamawa community (Goronyo, Sokoto). No further details.

On 28 December 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Chris Uba's convoy (a politician) and killed two of his police escorts in Uga junction, Aguata (Aguata, Anambra). The target, who was in a bulletproof SUV, escaped unhurt. Other police officers exchanged gunfire with the assailants, who later fled the scene. The police recovered a Lexus SUV used by the armed group and defused an IED found therein. They also recovered an AK-47 rifle belonging to a dead officer. There were two fatalities.

On 29 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted six women in Mallamawa (Maru, Zamfara). The raid was a result of the accusation that the community men were joining the state security outfit to combat the militia. They moved the hostages towards the Dajin Gwari forest for camping.

On 29 December 2023, the Nigerian police intercepted the Zamfara militiamen and engaged them in a firefight in the Sabon Garin Damba area of Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The militia had abducted a watchman after invading the house of a Staff of Zamfara College of Art and Science (ZACAS). The militiamen shot the hostage in the hand when they were outgunned by the police and escaped. The hostage was rescued and taken to the hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities.
On 29 December 2023, the Niger militia shot and killed three people and abducted eight others in Azu village (Tafa, Niger). No further details.

On 29 December 2023, the Zamfara militia abducted seven women and a one-year-old infant in Barayar Zaki (Anka, Zamfara). The raid was a result of the accusation that the community men were joining the state security outfit to combat the militia. They moved the hostages towards the Dajin Gwari forest for camping.

On 29 December 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians at Lut village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau) when they went to pick up their stranded relatives who escaped the previous attack on the area [coded separately].
On 29 December 2023, a Fulani militia attacked partygoers in Aguamede (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and killed two people. Other people were wounded by the attackers

On 30 December 2023, a Kaduna militia that attacked farmers were engaged in an armed clash by a local defense militia at Katakaki forest in Kakangi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). 19 local defense militiamen and over 40 Kaduna militiamen were killed, two local defense militiamen were declared missing.

On 30 December 2023, police forces and a local defense militia engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group at their hideout within the Adogo axis (Ajaokuta, Kogi). 24 abductees were rescued and the abductors fled. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian from Jakpa road, coded to Warri (Warri South, Delta). The victim was sitting in a car which was also driven away by the abductors, he was later rescued by the police [coded separately].

On 30 December 2023, police forces invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Ekakpamre (Ughelli South, Delta). The group had abducted a civilian from along Jakpa road [coded separately], the abductee was rescued, two members of the group were killed, one escaped with gunshot wounds and firearms were recovered.

On 30 December 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked a checkpoint in Anka (Anka, Zamfara) and killed one NSCDC operative and a retired policeman who was working on a farm as its security officer. Other sources report that the attack was in retaliation for an attack on the militia's camps by security operatives previously.

On 31 December 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded three civilians and abducted an unspecified number of others when they shot at travelers around Nde 3 Corners at Akparabong junction (Ikom, Cross River).

On 31 December 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a 70-year old man as he was on his way to church in Ijebu-Igbo (Ijebu North, Ogun). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded by the abductors.
On 31 December 2023, Nigerian troops killed an unspecified number of ISWAP fighters and captured two alive in Tumbulla, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 31 December 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Kwahaslalek village in Mangu LGA (Plateau), killed two civilians and wounded two others.

On 31 December 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed the commander of a local defense militia who is presumed to have been unarmed at a tricycle motor park in Ekoshodin near Benin City (Oredo, Edo).

On 31 December 2023, police forces raided the camp of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Ogboji (Orumba North, Anambra). Two members of the group were killed, one abducted was rescued, his car was recovered, two IED which were later defused [coded separately], two guns and 16 live cartridges were recovered.

On 1 November 2023, the Bauchi militia abducted six people after raiding Gwalada village in Toro LGA, coded to Toro (Toro, Bauchi). The militia moved their victims to a rocky forest in Bassa LGA in Plateau state, where the police clashed with them and rescued the victims, coded separately.

On 1 November 2023, the Nigerian police, on a rescue operation, clashed with an armed group in a rocky forest between Tumu, Tsaya and Rumfar Gomna in Bassa LGA, coded to Bassa (Bassa, Plateau). The militia had abducted six people from the neighbouring state (coded separately) and kept them in the forest before the police raided their camp. A hunter supporting the police and one of the militiamen lost their lives in the operation, and the police rescued the six hostages.

On 1 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Journalist around Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The victim was returning from Calabar when the group took him. They demanded 10 Million naira to release the hostage,

Around 1 November 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group shot at farmers at Temidire farm settlement (Odigbo, Ondo) coded to Ore. The assailants also destroyed farm settlements and cocoa plantations, there were no casualties. One of the assailants was caught and handed over to the police.

On 1 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with the Nigerian troops and the CJTF near Alagarno Forest, Alagarno (Biu, Borno). They claimed the Nigerian military retreated, and they captured two RPG warheads. There were no fatalities.

On 1 November 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed four Kaduna militias in Kamfanin Doka village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troops recovered one AK 47 rifle, one AK 47 magazine, one machete, one mobile phone and fourteen Motorcycles.

On 1 November 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed two people and abducted others on the Funtua - Gusau highway, Kutcheri village (Tsafe Zamfara). The militia blocked the road and attacked motorists and their passengers. A former House of Representatives member of Mafara/Anka (Zamfara State) sustained a gun wound in the attack and was taken to the hospital for treatment. Another source reported that many people were killed in the attack.

On 2 November 2023, five members of the Adamawa militia abducted the Chief of Staff of the Adamawa House of Assembly from his house in Wuro-Chekke, coded to Karewa (Yola-South, Adamawa). The armed group demanded a 20 million naira ransom to release the hostage, it was reduced to 5 million; the victim was released on Tuesday and there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 2 November 2023, five members of the Adamawa militia abducted the Chief of Staff of the Adamawa House of Assembly from his house in Wuro-Chekke, coded to Karewa (Yola-South, Adamawa). The armed group demanded a 20 million naira ransom to release the hostage.

On 2 November 2023, Kaduna militia abducted three laborers working at Nura Suraj Phase 2 Estate, near Millennium City, Doka village, Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna). The police rescued the hostages on the same day.
On 2 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a CJTF checkpoint in Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). They claimed two CJTF were wounded, and others retreated. There were no fatalities.

On 2 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians from Bmuko community in Bwari (FCT). The abductees were initially three; two siblings and a businessman, before one of the siblings escaped. A ransom of one million naira was demanded for the release of one of the abductees.

On 2 November 2023, the Nigerian troops, supported by some local farmers, killed a Kadnua militiaman in the western part of Sabon Sara village, coded to Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna). One of the farmers sustained a minor injury and was taken to the hospital for treatment. Other militiamen escaped with gun wounds. The troops recovered two AK-47 rifles.

On 2 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two members of NYSC in the Yargoje community (Kankara, Katsina). The victims were in transit between Edo and Katsina State when they were abducted. The Nigerian Army and the Police swung into action and rescued the victims (it was not clear if they engaged in a firefight to rescue the victims).

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian troops killed two militiamen while conducting a clearance operation around Kankomi, Gwantu, Kujeni, Kikwari, Kaso and Juji in Chikun LGA, coded to Juji (Chikun, Kadunma). The troop recovered one AK 47 rifle, one AK 47 magazine, four 7.62MM Special ammunition, one Honda motorcycle and one Techno phone.

On 3 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two women in Kiyawa town (Kiyawa, Jigawa). The abductees were the wives of the local government chairman and one of them was heavily pregnant. On 7 November, the police confirmed that the victims were released but did not provide details on the conditions of their release, a family member of the abductees claimed that an undisclosed ransom amount was paid.

On 3 November 2023, Kogi militiamen abducted a government official and his driver along Lokoja-Obajana Road in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). The militia had blocked the highway before seizing their hostages. No further details.
On 3 November 2023, the Sokoto militia killed six people in Duhuwa village, Wurno LGA (Wurno, Sokoto). An unspecified number of people were also abducted.
On 3 November 2023, Kogi militiamen killed one person at a shop in Yagba West LGA, coded to Odo Ere (Yagba West, Kogi). They injured three other people and abducted one.

On 3 November 2023, an armed group suspected to be APC killed a PDP chieftain and injured another in the Ogbolomabiri community in Nembe LGA coded to Nembe (Nembe, Bayelsa). The attack occurred about eight days before the gubernatorial election in the state.
On 3 November 2023, pirates shot and killed four NSCDC officers on the Bakana River, Bakana (Degema, River). No further details.
On 3 November 2023, Nigerian soldiers repelled an ISWAP attack on Damboa- Azir road, coded to Ajir (Damboa, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 3 November 2023, the troops of the 68th Battalion clashed with ISWAP around Kudankurgu in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno). The army recovered six IEDs. There were no fatalities.

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a gunfight as the militia attempted to invade Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). ISWAP fighters retreated after the confrontation. There were no fatalities.
On 3 November 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted a Catholic priest at Godogodo (Jema'a, Kaduna). The abductee was rescued by policemen who raided Dogon Kurmi forest [coded separately].

On 3 November 2023, the Nigerian security forces, coded as police, engaged in a firefight with an unidentified armed group along the Gwarimpa-Kubwa Expressway, in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The group abducted a victim and attempted to escape when the security engaged them. They escaped, leaving the victim and their vehicle behind. There were no fatalities.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and injured many people at the election venue of the Ano Stone Dealers Association in Isiaka (Ivo, Ebonyi). The group vandalized houses and shops and set vehicles on fire. There were no fatalities

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a judge and two other persons at Degri (Balanga, Gombe) when they went to inspect a disputed piece of land. The three victims were wounded, one of them was a court staff.

On 4 November 2023, a Zamfara militia ambushed and engaged soldiers who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Karazau village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). Several militiamen were killed and the others fled, fatalities coded as 10.
On 4 November 2023, the Kaduna militia shot and killed two people in Kudiri village Kagarko LGA, coded to Kagarko (Kagarko, Kaduna). The militia abducted nineteen others.

On 4 November 2023, policemen in collaboration with a local defense militia raided the hideout of a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Dogon Kurmi forest (Jema'a, Kaduna) coded to Jemaa. Two militiamen were arrested and two others escaped, a Catholic priest whom they abducted the previous day was rescued and one rifle loaded with two rounds of live ammunition was recovered. No casualties.

On 4 November 2023, a suspected Benue militia attacked and killed seven persons at a beer parlor in Tyoakosu (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera. The attack is suspected to be related to a supremacy battle between two militias in the area.

On 4 November 2023, a Katsina militia shot and wounded one civilian at Masaku village in Kankara LGA (Katsina). The victim who was abandoned on the roadside by the assailants was rescued by policemen.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a senior female INEC staff in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The group came in a Toyota Camry car and pretended to rent chairs from the victim. They tied one of the victim's aides with rope and put him in the refrigerator before driving her away in her car. However, a mob caught one of the gang while trying to escape and beat him up, coded separately. The abductors are yet to demand a ransom.

On 4 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor who was on duty at the university of Nigeria teaching hospital in Ituku-Ozalla, coded to Ozalla (Nkanu West, Enugu). The abductee escaped from the abductors hideout later that same day.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Harm [JAS faction] militants attacked Koshebe (Mafa, Borno) and Kakuri villages [coded seaparately] on motorcycles. The assailants who split themselves into three groups killed about 15 rice farmers whom they attacked using knives and cutlasses. An unspecified number of farmers were declared missing, 15 fatalities split across two events coded as 8. Other sources report that the victims were killed in retaliation, after rival ISWAP militants invaded JAS hideouts and demanded that the farmers who were initially abducted with the aim of ransom collection, should be released.

On 5 November 2023, Nigerian troops conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Maidaro, Ngade, Ahla and Rikau villages in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, one AK47 rifle and one motorcycle were recovered by the troops.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed a man on his farm near Bama town (Bama, Borno) and abducted four of his farm workers. The murdered victim was shot dead when he resisted being abducted.

On 5 November 2023, Fulani militia attacked a farmer in Gidankwanu village, Karshi (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The victim's family retaliated and injured a Fulani herder. There were no fatalities.

On 5 November 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Kaduna militia around Kajuru forest in Kajuru LGA, coded to Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna). The military killed one of the militiamen and injured many others. Weapons were also recovered.

On 5 November 2023, Boko Harm [JAS faction] militants attacked Kakuri village in Mafa (Borno) and Koshebe village [coded seaparately] on motorcycles. The assailants who split themselves into three groups killed about 15 rice farmers whom they attacked using knives and cutlasses. An unspecified number of farmers were declared missing, 15 fatalities split across two events coded as 7. Other sources report that the victims were killed in retaliation, after rival ISWAP militants invaded JAS hideouts and demanded that the farmers who were initially abducted with the aim of ransom collection, should be released.

On 5 November 2023, five soldiers beat up the private security guards who were guarding the house of MASSOB leader, Ralph Uwazurike in Okwe (Onuimo, Imo) as claimed by the leader himself. He also claimed that that the security guards were taken away.
On 5 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two people travelling from Batsari to Tashar Gurgu village in Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari(Batsari, Katsina).

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged in an armed clash when ISWAP demanded for the release of farmers who were abducted and later killed by JAS militants in retaliation [coded separately]. Location coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno) where the abduction took place, casualties from the clash are unknown.

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed two soldiers and injured another after attacking a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Bornu). They claimed to have seized two rifles and an RPG launcher.

On 5 November 2023, policemen and Ebube Agu operatives shot at the convoy of the Imo state LP gubernatorial candidate at Obibiezena (Owerri North, Imo) and prevented him from passing the road as claimed by the LP candidate. He also claimed that the was denied access to the road because he was going to a church where both he and the governor were invited. The police denied attacking him and claimed that he was only asked to not campaign in the area because the APC candidate was already doing so. There were no casualties.
On 5 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three civilians and wounded two others at Ayati village (Ukum, Benue). Other sources report that the attack is likely the result of a reprisal.

On 5 November 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted four others at Maru town (Maru, Zamfara). The assailants shot sporadically and moved from house to house during the attack, an unspecified number of persons were wounded and the abductees included a lecturer at the college of state education. Other sources report that two civilians were killed, a police vehicle was set ablaze by the assailants and five persons were abducted, the lecture was killed by the militia around 18 December after 2 million naira was paid as ransom (coded separately).

On 5 November 2023, a Katsina militia in dozens attacked muslim worshippers from different villages who were observing a Maulud procession at Kusa village in Musawa LGA (Katsina). At least 20 to 25 persons were killed; many others were wounded and several people were abducted. The police claimed that 7 to 18 persons were killed and 16 others were wounded.

On 5 November 2023, a Benue militia led by 'Full Fire' and another militia that was contracted by Full Fire engaged in an armed clash with a rival Benue militia led by 'Chain' at Chito (Ukum, Benue) over supremacy. 15 militia members were killed, some locals claimed that they were 10.

On 5 November 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram shot and killed eight IDPs and injured six others in Kaluwa village, coded to Monguno (Monguno, Borno). The IDPs went in search of charcoal when the militiamen indiscriminately opened fire on them.

On 5 November 2023, Nigerian troops conducted an operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Tantatu and Antenna areas in Chikun (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, one AK47 rifle and magazine and other items were recovered.

On 6 November 2023, the Sokoto militia, numbering about 100, attacked Gidan-Buwai (Rabah, Sokoto). The militia riding on motorcycles surrounded the village and opened fire indiscriminately on the residents. They rustled over 100 cows, 200 sheep, and goats. They also razed many houses, over 60 silos, ten motorcycles, and five vehicles. The group injured seven people and killed 11 others in Gidan-Buwai and Maikujera. Five were killed in Maikujera, coded separately, and six people lost their lives in Gidan-Buwai. There were six fatalities.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), Sokoto militia attacked Maikujera village (Rabah, Sokoto). They killed five people and injured many others. The injured were admitted to the Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital, Sokoto. There were five fatalities.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers who responded to a distress call at Alawa community (Shiroro, Niger) where the assailants ambushed civlians who were in transit. One civilian was killed while attempting to escape, two vehicles conveying goods and some motorcycles were burnt, the soldiers were declared missing.
On 6 November 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed nine people in the Gbutuku community, Madagali LGA, coded to Madagali (Madagali, Adamawa). No further details.

On 6 November 2023, Fulani herders attacked and injured seven people in Chirawa town in Bade LGA, coded to Gashua (Bade, Yobe). The security forces were deployed to restore order. There were no fatalities.

On 6 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Gandu (Lafia, Nassarawa) and killed one person. An unspecified number of residents were abducted including a businessman and a student in the area claimed that their phones were also snatched. Other sources report that the victim who is a student was shot and wounded but not killed.

Around 6 November 2023 (as reported), an unknown group, suspected to be the Security Watch Corps, killed a former LGA Caretaker Chairman, Alhaji Hamza Abdullahi, in Zakka (Safana, Katsina). The victim was accused of being a spy for the marauding militia group, and his killing was suspected to be part of the targeting of the alleged collaborators by the Security Watch Corps.
On 6 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted a woman from her farm on the outskirts of Garin Hambana, Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari(Batsari, Katsina).

On 6 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a CJTF checkpoint and injured an unspecified number of the force in Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). They claimed the CJTF fighters withdrew. There were no fatalities.

On 6 November 2023, a suspected Benue militia killed nine civilians at Ukoosaa-Atam community which is about 1km away from Ayati (Ukum, Benue). The victims included a tricyle rider, his passengers and some persons who were riding a motorcycle. Other sources report 10 fatalities.

On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with the APC fired indiscriminately at policemen and other security guards at the country home of the director-general of the SDP gubernatorial campaign in Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). At least one policeman and four other persons were killed, their corpses were taken away by the assailants. The police claimed that in collaboration with DSS and NSCDC operatives, it carried out an operation and killed two suspected political thugs who were housed by politicians and that two members of the team were wounded while 7 suspects were arrested.
On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two civilians at the Opolo area (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). No further details.

On 7 November 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 12 residents of Anguwar Algaita in Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and later killed two of them. The bodies of the murdered victims who were killed for refusing to follow the assailants were found in the bush the following evening and one other person was rescued with bullet wounds.

On 7 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked residents of Iyi-Owa Odekpe, coded as Odekpe (Ogbaru, Anambra). One person was assumed killed; at least 30 vehicles and 20 houses were destroyed and the chairman of the landlords association claimed that the community's monarch and president-general were responsible for the attack, a claim which they denied.
On 7 November 2023, Boko Haram (Bakura faction) engaged in a fire fight with ISWAP in the Kainowa East Mobbar LGA, coded to Asaga (Mobbar, Borno). No fatalities.
On 7 November 2023, ISWAP shot and killed two people in Kalwa (Monguno, Borno). No further details.
On 7 November 2023, Fulani herders and farmers clashed on the outskirts of Buni Yadi town (Gujba, Yobe). Two people were injured. There were no fatalities.
On 7 November 2023, the Katsina militia killed two people in Dangani village (Musawa, Katsina). They also abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 7 November 2023, the troops of the 112 Task Force Battalion of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and killed three ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters at Manawaji (Mafa, Borno). The militias were trying to assault some farmers when the troops launched an onslaught against them. Seven hostages were released, and the troops recovered one AK-47 rifle, 2 AK-47 rifle magazines, one fabricated pyrotechnic, and two motorcycles.

On 7 November 2023, the Nigerian troops ambushed and killed one ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) fighter in Gabti, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Bornu). The militiamen were trying to cross from Nigeria to Niger when the soldiers killed one of them. The troops rescued eleven hostages from the militia. Two AK rifles, hand grenades, ammunition, and over 11 million naira ($13,700) in cash were recovered from them.

On 7 November 2023, a Katsina militia engaged policemen who responded to a distress call in an armed clash when the militia invaded Sayaya community (Matazu, Katsina). Five civilians were killed, two were wounded and five others were abducted by the assailants.

On 7 November 2023, the Nigerian military opened fire at the ISWAP / Boko Haram position after sighting the militiamen around the Kuranabasa Mountain axis, Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted and killed a 13-year-old girl in Umuolu Okehi, Etche LGA, coded to Okehi (Etche, Rivers). No further details

On 8 November 2023, the Gbagyi militia clashed with some Fulani at the Beji Weekly Market, Beji (Bosso, Niger). Two persons were killed and seven others injured during the clash. Seven victims were hospitalised with various degrees of bullet wounds. The Gbagyi are agrarians, while the Fulani are pastoralists. The reason for the clash is unknown. There were two fatalities.

On 8 November 2023, some Mayaki farmers attacked a 12-year-old herder and cut off his two hands in Mayaki (Lapai, Niger). The boy went out to graze some cattle when the farmers attacked him. The police arrested one of the suspects.
On 8 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have forced the CJTF to retreat when they advanced towards ISWAP position around Sambisa Forest, coded to Bula Korege (Bama, Bornu). There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, ISWAP attacked some laborer's in Tarmuwa, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). They stole fourteen bicycles and one pushcart. There were no fatalities.
On 8 November 2023, Sokoto militia killed two people (a father and his son) in Kware village in Kware LGA, coded to Kware (Kware, Sokoto). The militia abducted five people during the attack.
On 8 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted three people from a commercial bus along the Tsafe-Funtua-Zaria Road, Funtua LGA, coded to Funtua (Katsina).
On 8 November 2023, two unidentified rival cult militia engaged in an armed clash over supremacy at Ojota (Kosofe, Lagos). Two militia members were killed.

On 9 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia shot at a school bus along Eke - Egede road, Eke (Udi, Enugu). A female student of St Paul's College, Eke, was shot dead in the process, and three others sustained gun injuries. The students were going home when the marauders attacked their school bus.

On 9 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a traditional ruler along Eke-Egede-Affa Road, Eke (Udi, Enugu). The chief was returning from a security meeting when the militia seized him. The incident occurred after the militia attacked a school bus and killed one of the students, coded separately.

On 9 November 2023, a local defense militia invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them an armed clash after they arrested informants who led them to the group's hideouts in the forest. Location coded to Bin Yauri (Ngaski, Kebbi), three members of the group were killed.

On 9 November 2023, the Nigerian troops and the CJTF killed six ISWAP fighters and rescued 78 captives at Gime and Muzuri villages near Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). The Military recovered some AK-47 rifles and 3 Dane guns. The rescued hostages included 30 women and 48 children. There were six fatalities.

On 9 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three soldiers after attacking a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Mararaba, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). They wounded two soldiers and seized a rifle and an RPG launcher.

On 9 November 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai shot and killed five ISWAP fighters during a clearance operation at Mulumti General Area of Buni Gari (GUjba, Yobe). The troop and the militia engaged in a heavy gunfight, killing five militias and forcing others to withdraw with gun wounds. The army recovered 1 CONQUEROR APC, 4 Ak47 rifles with four extra Magazines, 1 GPMG, 1 NSVT GUN 1, Baofeng Radio and 150 Quantities of 12.7 MM rounds. An IED killed one of the soldiers as they were returning to the base. There were six fatalities.

Around 9 November 2023 (as reported), some policemen attacked two soldiers in Ikole (Ekiti) over the harassment of a policewoman. The policewoman accused the soldiers of violating traffic rules, but they instead beat up the policewoman. The officer called for backup, and her colleagues responded and descended on the soldiers. There were no fatalities.
On 9 November 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram (Bakura group) engaged in a firefight for about two hours in Duji (Mobbar, Borno). The Boko Haram overpowered ISWAP and killed scores of them, coded as 20.

On 9 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed an Ex-Oyo Permanent Secretary at her residence in Ibadan (Ibadan North West, Oyo). Her body was found the next day with her hands and legs tied. The victim had reported a threat to her life by some hoodlums around her house.

On 9 November 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted 13 commuters along the Naka road (Gwer West, Benue) as they were travelling from Oturkpo to Makurdi in the state owner transport company bus. The abductees were initially 16 until 3 escaped.
On 10 November 2023, an armed group on motorcycles shot and killed two people in the Latawa area of Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). The assailants were suspected to be cult militia.

On 10 November 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted 20 civilians at a roadblock that they mounted near Yargalma village (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abductees included farmers and a health worker who were unable to bail themselves from the militia at the road block.

On 10 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted clearance operations engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Mai-Kulu Gwanda, Rafin Gora, Funtua Badaddi and Kabawa villages in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, a radio and a motorcycle were recovered.

On 10 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch on clearance operation engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kawara forest (Igabi, Kaduna). One militia member was killed; others fled with gunshot wounds, a loaded AK47 rifle, a motorcycle and one a phone were recovered.

On 10 November 2023, the Nigerian troops repelled the Boko Haram (JAS) in a attempt to invade Damboa from the Gwoza axis in Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The ensuing firefights forced the militia to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 10 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man in Oji River town or Oji River Settlement (Orji River, Enugu). No further details.

On 10 November 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Muslim worshippers who were attending a Maulud procession at Zagami village (Faskari, Katsina) and killed one person. Many people were wounded and several others were abducted.

On 10 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF along the Dikwa- Ajiri road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). They claimed to have forced the CJTF to retreat, seized two motorbikes, and burned the third one. There were no fatalities.
On 10 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the CJTF checkpoint in New Marte (Marte, Borno). They forced the CJTF to withdraw. There were no fatalities.

On 10 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an INEC official at Amassoma jetty in Sagbama (Sagbama, Bayelsa) while waiting to board a boat to his polling Unit. The officer who was to supervise the gubernatorial election at Registration Area 06 (Ossisioma) was released the following day, there are no details on the conditions of his release.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated to the APC disrupted the voting process at polling units 14, 15 and 19 of ward 11 in Opume and Emakalakala (Ogbia, Bayelsa). There were no casualties.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform attacked a PDP chieftain at constituency 4 of Southern Ijaw LGA (Bayelsa) coded to Oporoma, after the chieftain engaged them in an argument following their invasion of the area. Hundreds of voters fled, there were no casualties.

On 11 November 2023, the security forces (coded as the military) clashed with an armed group attacking Ogiadiama Ward 9 in Unit 14, Southern Ijaw LGA, coded to Azuzuama (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The attackers were forced to retreat. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group (likely cult militia) on motorcycles shot and killed one person at Ita Oba Roundabout in Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun).

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to have political affiliation shot and killed a voter at Agala Ogane polling unit in Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). Some sources report that the victim attempted to snatch a ballot box while others report that two persons were killed; one was a voter and the other attempted to snatch a ballot box.

On 11 November 2023, Zamfara militia who were in large numbers engaged policemen and a local defense militia who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Gada village (Bungudu, Zamfara). 7-8 civilians, 6 defense militiamen and several of the assailants were killed (coded as 10), many of them fled with wounds and cattle that were rustled from the community, ten of which were recovered. Total of 23 fatalities coded.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group fired indiscriminately in the vicinity of the Abuja/Imbikiri area in Brass Ward 2, Brass (Brass, Bayelsa). The shooting was likely aimed at scaring voters away from the polling units. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, APC loyalists engaged in an armed clash with security operatives (coded as military forces) at Fangbe (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). An unspecified number of casualties were reported.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the PDP gubernatorial candidate at Ikeduru LGA (Imo) coded to Iho and wounded some of his aides. The candidate claimed that one of the assailants was a member of the state house of assembly.
