On 11 November 2023, security operatives (coded as policemen) shot and killed a man for attempting to steal a ballot box at Amanwozuzu in Iho (Ikeduru, Imo). The operatives took away the victim's bag and left the body which was eventually taken away by policemen.
On 11 November 2023, a Katsina militia abducted three civilians from Gogalo village in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees were rescued by policemen who trailed the militia [coded separately].

On 11 November 2023, a Katsina militia engaged a joint team of policemen, local defense militia and Katsina security watch operatives in an armed clash when they responded to a distress call at Yankara (Faskari, Katsina). One of the assailants was killed, different types of live rounds and AK47 magazines were also recovered.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Agbeku community (Ifelodun, Kwara) and abducted three others including a pastor when they invaded a church auditorium and the victims' residence, one person was shot and critically wounded. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded for the release of the abductees.

Around 11 November 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants from the Bakoura Baduma camp invaded the camp of rival ISWAP fighters and engaged them in an armed clash at Duji village (Mobbar, Borno). The Boko Haram fighters were led to the rival camp by an ISWAP fighter whom they captured, dozens of ISWAP fighters and one Boko Haram fighter were killed, dozens coded as 12.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group of two who have an affiliation with the local palace beat up a former councilor and killed him at Precious Seed community in Oworonsoki (Kosofe, Lagos). The victim was attacked over his refusal to pay the assailants an amount they demanded because he was carrying out a construction work. The assailants fled and were declared wanted by the police.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group that were wearing masks and suspected to have political affiliation killed the YPP ward chairman for Nanka ward 1 (Orumba North, Anambra). The victim was killed shortly after he hosted the party's house of representatives candidate for the constituency over a meeting for a rerun election as directed by the Appeal court, the candidate claimed that the victim was called 'saboteur' thrice before he was shot.

On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a voting Registration Area Centre in Brass Ward 8, Oginibiri or Ogboinbiri (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The attack was likely aimed to disrupt the voting process. There were no fatalities.
On 11 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted electoral officials and stole result sheets at Umuodu Community Primary School in Ezinihitte Mbieri (Mbaitoli, Imo).

On 12 November 2023, the Kaduna militia killed nine people after attacking the Warkan community, Zangon Kataf (Zangon Katab, Kaduna). Many people were injured, and about twelve houses were set on fire.

On 12 November 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted the District Head of Kujama around Bethel Baptist School, Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). The abductors came on motorcycles and took him away with two others at gunpoint. No further details.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed three persons at Agbowa area in Shagamu LGA (Ogun). The police claimed to have recovered three bodies with bullet wounds, expended cartridges, one cartridge and a phone from the scene and also arrested three suspects in connection with the attack.

On 12 November 2023, the Taraba militia abducted a random bearer who had approached the militia to secure the release of his relative around the Muslim Council Secretariat in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The victim was released after the militia received another ransom.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a PDP supporter at the collation center in Brass town (Brass, Bayelsa) when they invaded the center. The victim was also an aide to the local government chairman, other sources report that the assailants were affiliated with the APC gubernatorial candidate.

On 12 November 2023, policemen trailed and engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash after the militia abducted three civilians from Gogalo village in Jibia LGA (Katsina). The abductees were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 12 November 2023, the government security forces (coded as the military) and the local vigilante group clashed with the Katsina militia while attacking Zakka village (Safana, Katsina). Thirteen militia and two government forces were killed in the clash. There were fifteen fatalities.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a University of Calabar lecturer from his residence within the university staff quarters in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductee was taken away via a river that overlooks the quarters, a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded. The abductee was released around 10 December, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 12 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted clearance operations and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash around the general area of Maro - Chibiya forest (Kajuru, Kaduna). One militia member was killed; others fled, one AK47 rifle, a locally fabricated rifle, ammunition and a mobile phone were recovered.

On 12 November 2023, an unidentified cult militia were engaged in an armed clash by policemen who responded to a distress call following an attack on civilians at Odimeneyi village (Ahoada, Rivers) by the militia who killed five persons before policemen arrived. A witness claimed that the assailants said the attacks would continue until their members and a chief who were in police custody were released. The police claimed that two of the assailants were killed also. Total 7 fatalities.
On 12 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed five people in the Odiemereni community or Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers). No further detail.

On 13 November 2023, Supreme Vikings Confraternity and Supreme Eiye Confraternity also called Eiye engaged in an armed clash at Ozoro community (Isoko North, Delta). One person was killed and the police arrested four suspects in connection with the incident.

On 13 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted six people after blocking the Kankara-Dutsin Ma Road near Garangamawa (Dutsinma, Katsina). The victims, including women and children, were travelling to attend a wedding ceremony in Kagara village.

On 13 November 2023, an unidentified armed group affiliated with the Baale (local chief) of Ilua abducted and beat up a lawyer whose vehicle was ambushed at Iware junction, 20 km away from Ilua (Saki West, Oyo). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 13 November 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted three people in Laying Mahuta in Tabanni village (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The militia invaded the community at night, broke into the victims' room and took them away. No further details.

On 13 November 2023, the Kaduna militia attacked the Police at Kakangi Community (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They attempted to set the police Armored Personnel Carrier vehicle ablaze. The police drove the vehicle away while they were being shot at. Two police officers sustained gun wounds in the hands. There were no fatalities.

On 13 November 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash in the general area of Juji and Telele-Kaso (Chikun, Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed; others fled, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 13 November 2023, a local defense militia engaged suspected armed Fulani pastoralists that attacked civilians in an armed clash inside the Old Oyo National Park in Sepeteri (Saki East, Oyo). One civilian was killed by the assailants, two others were abducted, one of the abductees was rescued by the defense militia. The police claimed that there were no fatalities and that three defense militiamen were wounded.

Around 13 November 2023 (as reported), a local defense militia ambushed and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash near Dan Umoru village (Danko, Kebbi) as they were returning to Maru in Zamfara after attacking one civilian in Dan Umoru. All the four attackers were killed by the defense militia, it is unclear whether the civilian was killed or wounded.

On 13 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one person and forced others to flee after invading a Christian community near Chibok, coded to Chibok (Chibok, Borno). The militia stole unspecified property.

On 13 November 2023, an armed group abducted three people along the Kwandere Road, Tudun Gwandara, Lafia LGA, coded to Lafia (Lafia, Nasarawa). The victims included an assistant manager of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Lafia branch. The abductors demanded a 10 million naira ransom to release the hostage.

On 13 November 2023, ISWAP militants from Kaushuruwa village who mounted 3 gun trucks and 4 motorcycles engaged troops of sector 2 of Operation Hadin Kai in an armed clash at the outskirts of Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). The attack by the militants was a reprisal over the killing of 5 militants in a clash with Nigerian troops [coded separately], there were no casualties on the side of the soldiers and an unknown number of militants fled with injuries.
Around 13 November 2023 (between 12 - 15 November), the Sokoto militia abducted some women and their children in Alela Sutti, known as Alela (Tangaza, Sokoto). No further details.
Around 13 November 2023 (between 12 - 15 November), the Sokoto militia abducted five people while raiding Gidan Kakale in Tangaza LGA, coded to Tangaza (Tangaza, Sokoto).

On 13 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a couple and their driver along the Naka road (Gwer West, Benue) while they were travelling the route. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 13 November 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted a suspended local government chairperson and her driver at Tyolaha Ahume village along the Naka road (Gwer West, Benue). The assailants ambushed the car the victims were travelling in and shot at them till they came to a halt. The victim was released on 16 November, there are details on ransom payment.

On 14 November 2023, troops of 1 division of the Nigerian Army ambushed a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash along Kwant - Kabai - Kubusu (Chikun, Kaduna). One member of the militia was killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, one rifle, magazine, veterinary medicine and clothes were recovered by the troops.

On 14 November 2023, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kachallah high ground, coded to Zangon Katab (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). Six militiamen were killed, others fled with gunshot wounds, arms, ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 14 November 2023, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol killed one Kaduna militia member at Kondo village, coded to Zonkwa (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) as claimed by the spokesperson of operation whirl punch.
On 14 November 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed a man and injured another on their farmlands outskirts of Kinfau village, Safana LGA, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina).
On 14 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Borno). They claimed the soldiers at the checkpoint were forced to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 14 November 2023, the Kogi militia killed a pastor held hostage after collecting a million naira ransom in Obajana (Lokoja, Kogi). The pastor was abducted on 11 November 2023, and the abductors demanded a 20 million naira ransom for his release.
On 14 November 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed a driver after blocking the Kankara-Malumfashi Road, close to Kankara ( Kankara, Katsina). There was one fatality.

On 14 November 2023, Plateau militia abducted a man in Bukuru (Jos South, Plateau). The hostage's wife works with the United Nations Agencies, Funds and Programmes (UNAFP). The abducted demanded a ransom for his release.

Around 15 November 2023 (between 12 - 15 November), the Sokoto militia shot a commercial driver on Ruawuri road, coded to Ruawuri (Tangaza, Sokoto). The militia burnt down his vehicle together with the passengers, including a nursing mother and her daughter. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 15 November 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with the Katsina militia while on fighting patrol in Batsari LGA, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). The military killed one militia and recovered one AK47 rifle, two magazines loaded with 20 rounds of 7.62 mm Special ammo and four motorcycles.

Around 15 November 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted 19 civilians from their homes in Galadimawa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). 12 of the abductees were murdered (coded separately). One of the murdered abductees was an aide to Senator Ned Nwoko.

Around 15 November 2023 (between 12 - 15 November), the Sokoto militia killed four people after invading Alkasu village, coded to Raka (Tangaza, Sokoto). The militia injured three people and abducted seventeen others.
On 15 November 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) killed two CJTF and wounded two others in Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). No further details.

On 16 November 2023, troops of the 1st Division of the Nigerian Army killed six Kaduna militia during a clearance operation in Sabon-Birni, Dogon Dawa, Saulawa, Maidaro-Ngede Allah and Kidenda in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The Nigerian military recovered two AK-47 rifles, four AK-47 rifle magazines, 14 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 40 pairs of bandits uniforms, and nine motorcycles.

On 16 November 2023, the Nigerian military conducted clearance operations and clashed with the Zamfara militia in Tugan Gama, Tugan Hausawa, Tugan Nabaru, Yarsabia and Daji Yanayin Kari villages in Anka LGA, coded to Bagega (Anka, Zamfara). The Operation was conducted again in the locations on 17 November 2023, coded separately. Two militiamen were killed, and many escaped with gun wounds. 2 fatalities split across two events, coded as 1.

On 16 November 2023, some Fulani herders attacked and injured four farmers with arrows in Dambatta (Danbatta, Kano) over grazing land issues. The farmers accused the herders of grazing their animals on their farms, and the ensuing argument led to confrontation. The Fulani resorted to using bows and arrows and injured the farmers. There were no fatalities.

Around 16 November 2023 (as reported), the Nigerian troops engaged in a firefight with the Kaduna militia along Kwant - Kabai - Kubusu, coded to Kakau (Chikun, Kaduna). The military killed one of the militia members, and others escaped with gun wounds. One AK 47 rifle, one magazine, veterinary medicine and clothing were recovered.

On 16 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three people when raiding a Christian community near Chibok (Chibok, Bornu). The militia also claimed to have burned the house of the village leader, a church, and other property. They seized a vehicle and a motorbike.

On 16 November 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) clashed with a local defense militia in Adidi Yola in Kundu district, location coded to Kundu (Rafi, Niger). 2 local defense militia members were killed and 13 civilians were abducted.

On 16 November 2023, the Nigerian military clashed with Sokoto militia (described as bandits) during clearance operations in Sabon Birni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). 6 Sokoto militia were killed. The military forces recovered weapons and items, included 2 AK47s, 4 rifle magazines, ammunition, 9 motorcycles and 40 uniforms.

On 17 November 2023, the Nigerian troops conducted clearance operations on the second day in Tugan Gama, Tugan Hausawa, Tugan Nabaru, Yarsabia and Daji Yanayin Kari villages in Anka LGA, coded to Bagega (Anka, Zamfara). Two militiamen were killed, and many escaped with gun wounds. 2 fatalities split across two events, coded as 1.

On 17 November 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a pastor of an ECWA church and abducted his wife when they invaded the victims' residence at Damakasuwa (Kauru, Kaduna). The assailants who invaded the community around 11pm demanded for a ransom of 3 million the following day for the abductee's release. The abductee was released on 19 November after 350,000 naira was paid as ransom.

On 17 November 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a student of Federal Polytechnic Offa at her off-campus apartment in Offa (Offa, Kwara). The victim was hacked to death and found in a pool of blood, the police claimed to have arrested one person in connection with the attack.

On 17 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded a man and abducted his wife who is a nurse as they were returning from their farm along Iwo - Ileogbo road (Iwo, Osun). A ransom of 20 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded.

On 17 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from his residence at Kwayama village in Dutse LGA (Jigawa). The victim was taken away by the assailants after they took 3 million naira from him.

On 17 November 2023, the police and the NIS clashed in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno) over a claim to an outpost within a housing estate alongside the Maiduguri-Kano highway. They engaged in a shootout, which caused tension within the community, and residents began to flee. The Nigerian Army troops from the 33 Artillery intervened and calmed the situation. There were no fatalities.

On 17 November 2023, the Nigerian troops responded to a distress call and engaged the Zamfara militia in a gunfight in the Yarkoria community, coded to Anka (Anka, Zamfara). The troops rescued five hostages from the militia. The militia escaped with gun wounds. There were no fatalities.

On 17 November 2023, suspected IPOB members shot and killed two police officers on patrol at Nwofe Road in Izzi LGA, coded to Iboko (Izzi, Ebonyi). One officer sustained gun wounds and was admitted to the hospital.
On 17 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have engaged a CJTF patrol in a firefight near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno), forcing the CJTF to retreat. There were no fatalities.

On 17 November 2023, an unidentified group (described as bandits) abducted four civilians in Kwalta in the Kwali Area Council, location coded to Kwali (Kwali, Federal Capital Territory). The security forces freed two of the captives (no further details on how).

Around 18 November 2023 (between 18 - 19 November), the Nigerian troops engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight in Dan Musa LGA, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and Malumfashi LGA. They also engaged the militia in Maru LGA, in Zamfara State, coded separately. The troops recovered one AK47 rifle with a magazine loaded with 13 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammo, 3 mobile phones, one motorcycle and the sum of N18,560.00'. Two hostages were released, and four militiamen were killed in the three operations. 4 fatalities shared among the three events. 1 fatality coded.

Around 18 November 2023 (week of), a local defense militia set up by MACBAN engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Kabi village (Kuje, FCT). An unspecified number of the armed group members were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 18 November 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked and killed three civilians at the outskirt of Kawuri (Konduga, Borno) when they went in search of firewood.

On 18 November 2023, ISWAP militants ambushed the convoy of the Yobe state governor and engaged his security detail who were later reinforced by soldiers in an armed clash along Jakana - Mainok highway about 6km away from Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). One policeman was killed, two soldiers, one driver and four policemen were wounded. The casualties on the side of the militants are unknown.

On 18 November 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram fighters engaged in an armed clash over rivalry at Tumbun Ali Island in Marte LGA (Borno). Scores of fighters from both groups including their commanders were killed and the clash was a reprisal for Boko Haram's attack on rival ISWAP a few days earlier [coded separately]. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 18 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed a Nigerian policeman in Bula Kudube, likely to be Bula Korege (Bama, Borno).

Around 18 November 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group abducted a school proprietor from his residence at Warah area , coded to Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). A ransom of 15 million naira was demanded, 4 million was paid to the abductors who insisted on receiving the complete amount before the victim would be released.

Around 18 November 2023 (between 18 - 19 November), the Nigerian troops engaged the Zamfara militia in a firefight in Maru LGA, coded to Maru (Maru, Zamfara). The troops also clashed with the Katsina militia in separate operations in Malumfashi and Danmusa LGA, coded separately. The troops recovered one AK47 rifle with a magazine loaded with 13 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammo, 3 mobile phones, one motorcycle and the sum of N18,560.00'. Two hostages were released, and four militiamen were killed in the three operations. 4 fatalities shared among the three events. 2 fatalities coded.

Around 18 November 2023 (between 18 - 19 November), the Nigerian troops engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight in Malumfashi LGA, coded to Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina) and Dan Musa LGA. They also engaged the militia in Maru LGA, in Zamfara State, coded separately. The troops recovered one AK47 rifle with a magazine loaded with 13 rounds of 7.62mm Special ammo, 3 mobile phones, one motorcycle and the sum of N18,560.00'. Two hostages were released, and four militiamen were killed in the three operations. 4 fatalities shared among the three events. 1 fatality coded.

On 19 November 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a mobile policeman when they invaded Ruwan Doruwa (Maru, Zamfara) and shot sporadically. An unspecified number of civilians were wounded, 13 others consisting of 6 women, 5 men and 2 children were abducted. Other sources report that 15 civilians were abducted, including the wife of the district head whose husband was the initial target.

On 19 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the chairman of the APC in Ikom LGA and his son at Nde Three Corners community which is about 3km away from Ikom (Ikom, Cross River). There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 19 November 2023 (weekend of), suspected rival cult group shot and killed a senior member of Eiye cult militia in Ojo (Ojo, Lagos). The attackers cut his head off and sent it to his cult member as a sign of dominance in the area.

On 19 November 2023, a team of policemen and an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who were part of the security detail of the factional speaker of the Rivers state house of assembly in an armed clash at his house in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The assailants who invaded the residence in an attempt to assassinate the speaker were repelled and casualties are unknown.
On 19 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three Nigerian soldiers when they attacked the Army checkpoint in Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). They wounded several others and forced many to retreat.
On 20 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted eight women who were working on a farm in Gwombe community (Kuje, FCT). There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 20 November 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group in large numbers killed one civilian and abducted six others when they invaded Yewuti community in Wako district of Kuje (FCT). The murdered victim was killed when he attempted to escape, abductees included a pregnant woman and the father of the council's vice chairman. A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 20 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a Nigerian Army-CJTF joint patrol near Alagarno Forest (Biu, Borno). The militia forced the troops to withdraw and targeted them with an IED. The explosive destroyed an SUV, killed and injured its occupants. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 20 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed four locals whose service soldiers had engaged to clear an area at Gudum community in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The assailants attacked the victims shortly after the soldiers left them.

On 20 November 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with the Sokoto militia during a fighting patrol in Tangaza LGA, coded to Tangaza (Tangaza, Sokoto). They killed four militiamen and recovered two locally made pistols, one long Dane gun, five empty cases of 7.62mm special ammo, and four mobile phones. They also destroyed two motorcycles.

On 20 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Lagos state government official from his residence at Igbe-Oloja in Ikorodu (Ikorodu, Lagos). The abductors demanded for a ransom of 20 million naira.
On 20 November 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed 2 civilians on a farm in Kundu district (Rafi, Niger). One civilian was injured.

On 21 November 2023, the Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed two Boko Haram (JAS) fighters when engaged in a firefight in Walada village, along the Damasak - Kukawa road, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Other militiamen escaped with bullet wounds. The troop recovered 2 AK 47 rifles, three magazines, and 29 rounds of 7.62 MM ammunition.

On 21 November 2023, the Nigerian troops shot and killed two Boko Haram (JAS) fighters attempting to plant an IED around Kudokurgo (Abadan, Borno). The military recovered unexploded items and other IED-making tools.

On 21 November 2023, policemen shot at soldiers who were on patrol at Target junction in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa) and wounded one soldier. The clash took place around 11pm and the soldiers returned to the police headquarters to rescue their colleague [coded separately].

On 21 November 2023, a Zamfara militia were repelled by soldiers who responded to a distress call following the militia's attack on civilians at Hayin Bakuso in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara). The assailants killed two civilians before they were dispersed.

On 21 November 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up one of the OSOPADEC commissioners when they invaded a bursary award ceremony in Akure (Akure South, Ondo) and shot sporadically. The commissioner's vehicle was also destroyed by the assailants.

On 21 November 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Sokoto militia in an armed clash at Goboro village (Tangaza, Sokoto). The militia fled and one abductee was recued by the troops. No casualties.

Property destruction: On 21 November 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) shot sporadically and set civilian houses on fire in Kalaba (Gwadabawa, Sokoto) and Dabusawa (coded separately). Many civilians fled for safety. Casualties unknown.

On 21 November 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) shot sporadically and set civilian houses on fire in Dabusawa, also spelled as Dabwasa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto) and Kalaba (coded separately). Many civilians fled for safety. Casualties unknown.

On 21 November 2023, the Nigerian military clashed with a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) in Bauni area (Tangaza, Sokoto). There were no fatalities. Several Sokoto militia members were injured and 30 previously abducted civilians were rescued.

On 22 November 2023, Nigerian troops shot and killed a member of the Plateau militia in Fobur Kassa village or Fobur (Jos East, Plateau). The troops responded to a distress call on the activities of the militia attempting to abduct some people. One militia was killed, and others escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 22 November 2023, the Gbagyi militia clashed with some Fulani at the Beji Weekly Market, Beji (Bosso, Niger). Six persons were killed including four Fulani and two Gbagyi militia. The reason for the clash is unknown. There were six fatalities.

On 22 November 2023, soldiers engaged policemen in an armed clash when they went to the police headquarters at Jimeta in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). One policeman was killed in the clash which took place in the early hours of the day, the army brigade commander claimed that the soldiers had gone to rescue a soldier who some policemen shot, wounded and hid and the policemen opened fire at the soldiers who then retaliated.

On 22 November 2023, suspected cult militia shot and killed a man in the Rumukalabo area of Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim was trailed by the gunmen and was shot on his way home after watching a football match.

On 22 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a resident and abducted eight others in Mpape, in Bwari (Bwari, Federal Capital Territory). The militiamen, numbering 30, raided six houses, including the chief's palace. The chief, his wife and three of his children were among the abductees. The chief's wife was released on 24 November and asked to bring a ransom of 100 million naira for her husband and children's release, her husband was released on 19 December after 11 million naira was paid, a balance of 40 million was demanded for the release of their children.

On 22 November 2023, the Zamfara militia killed three students in Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The students were returning from Islamic primary school when they were shot by the militia. The anguish of incessant militia's attacks has forced many people to desert the community.

Around 22 November 2023 (week of), a suspected Fulani militia raped one woman and killed two Kuteb youths which resulted in two reprisal attacks by the Kuteb group and the Fulanis [coded separately]. Location coded to Takum (Takum, Taraba).

Around 22 November 2023 (between 22 November - 23 November), an unidentified armed group killed a Fulani leader and dumped his body in a well near a hospital at Kombun community (Mangu, Plateau). The victim was abducted the previous day after he left the hospital to buy food for his sick wife.

On 23 November 2023, an unidentified armed group on motorcycles shot and killed the PDP chairman, Ife/Akpodim/Chokoneze Ward, in the Ezinihitte Mbaise LGA, coded to Okpofe (Ezinihitte Mbaise, Imo). No further details.
On 23 November 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded two civilians when they attacked Gaye village in Kwaku, also called Kpako ward (Kuje, FCT).

On 23 November 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in black attires which had Biafra insignia abducted an Abia state factional chairman of APGA alongside two of his friends along Arondiziogu - Okiwge road, coded to Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo). One of the victims claimed that they were made to transfer millions of naira into an account, it is unclear whether all the abductees were released.

Around 23 November 2023 (as reported), ISWAP claimed it clashed with pro-government militia (coded as CJTF), attempting to advance towards their position in the Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). There were no fatalities.

Around 23 November 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group consisting of a farmer killed a Fulani pastoralist at Telemu village in Ago-Owu which is also called Orile-Owu (Aiyedade, Osun) over claims that the pastoralist's cattle destroyed his farm two weeks earlier. The victim's mutilated body was found on the assailant's farm.
Around 23 November 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group abducted eight farmers in Uso community, Owo LGA (Ondo). The victims were released after an undisclosed huge ransom amount was paid.

On 23 November 2023, the NSCDC clashed with the Katsina militia, attempting to abduct some farmers around Federal University, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militia, on ten motorcycles, raided the community and targeted farmers working in their fields. The security rescued three women, but the militia escaped with two hostages. No fatalities.
On 23 November 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted three civilians in Wurno (Wurno, Sokoto), and demanded a N6 million ransom for their release.
On 24 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person in the Akparabong community (Ikom, Cross River). They abducted another.

On 24 November 2023, the Niger militia raided the house of the former APC chairman in Zungeru (Wushishi, Niger). The armed group abducted the former chairman and shot and wounded his daughter while one of his sons sustained machete cuts. No further details.

On 24 November 2023, Nigerian troops in collaboration with a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they raided the group's hideout at Kogon Damisa Hill around Saminaka (Shanga, Kebbi). Six abductees were rescued and casualties are unknown.

Around 24 November 2023 (week of), a Kuteb ethnic militia attacked Fulani pastoralists who were traveling from Takum to Kashimbila (Takum, Taraba). Two of the Fulanis were killed, two others were wounded, and 15 cows were killed as claimed by the MACBAN chairman of southern Taraba zone. The attack was a reprisal for the murder of Kutep youths [coded separately].

On 24 November 2023, MNJTF troops clashed with Boko Haram (JAS Faction) militants and killed two of them while on a fighting patrol to Kudokurgo (Abadan, Borno). Rifles, magazines, IED making materials and ammunition were recovered.
On 24 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted one person from a Fulani settlement in Sabon Garin, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina).
On 24 November 2023, a Fulani militia killed one person at Tukwog community coded to Manya (Ussa, Taraba).

On 24 November 2023, MNJTF troops clashed with Boko Haram (JAS Faction) militants and killed two of them at Walo Walada, coded to nearby Gashigar (Mobbar, Borno). Rifles, magazines, and ammunition were recovered.
On 24 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed one person at Kpambo Yache community (Ussa, Taraba), for unclear reasons.

On 24 November 2023, policemen killed a barber who was in their custody in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) after he was accused of being a cultist and arrested. The victim's family claimed that he died as a result of torture and that he was innocent of the police's claims while the police claimed he was not torture but instead took ill and died in a hospital from the sickness.
On 24 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man on the Abaji - Toto road (Abaji, FCT) as he was driving to Toto town.

On 24 November 2023, a Zamfara militia led by Damina abducted over 100 civilians from Mutumji, Sabongari Mahuta, Kwanari Dutsi and Unguwar Kawo (Maru, Zamfara) following the communities' inability to pay 110 million naira (harvest tax) that was levied on them by the militia. The communities were levied different amounts which summed up to 110 million. Other sources report that the abduction was in retaliation of an airstrike by NAF which targeted the militia some weeks earlier [coded separately].

On 24 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed ten farmers at Nyicwu community in Takum LGA (Taraba) as they were on the way to their farm. The National President of Kutep Association claimed that the attack was a reprisal following a series of attacks on Kutep and Fulanis in the area. Other sources report that 9 persons were killed.
On 24 November 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed an unspecified number of civilians when they laid siege along Takum - Ussa road, coded to Lissam (Ussa, Taraba). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

Around 24 November 2023 (between 21 - 27 November), Plateau militia abducted three women at Ndor village, coded to Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). The Nigerian troops later rescued the victims at Tent village in Barkin Ladi LGA of Plateau State.

On 25 November 2023, armed pastoralists and farmers engaged in an armed clash at Suru LGA (Kebbi) after the farmers arrived on their farms and found it destroyed by the grazing animals belonging the pastoralists. Two people were killed; other sources report 3, eight others were wounded, houses and properties were destroyed in Besse LGA [coded separately]. The affected villages included Kankure, Tungan Rimi in Suru and Tungan Mai Rakumi, Runhewan Dulmeru, Sabuwan Kendawa and Limarein in Besse.

On 25 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his residence at Nasarawa Egon (Nasarawa Eggon, Nassarawa). The victim is a former vice chairman of the state football association.

On 25 November 2023, armed pastoralists and farmers engaged in an armed clash at Koko LGA (Kebbi) coded to Besse after the farmers arrived on their farms and found it destroyed by the grazing animals belonging the pastoralists. Houses and properties were destroyed and two to three persons were killed in Suru [coded separately]. The affected villages included Kankure, Tungan Rimi in Suru and Tungan Mai Rakumi, Runhewan Dulmeru, Sabuwan Kendawa and Limarein in Besse.
On 25 November 2023, the Katsina militia abducted one person from Tsakatsa village (Charanchi, Katsina). No further details.

On 25 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the traditional ruler of Otulu community (Ezinihitte Mbaise, Imo) coded to Itu from his palace and killed him later on the same day. The victim's mutilated body was found the following day along Chokoneze - Mbutu road with his limbs cut off.

Around 25 November 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadarin Daji raided hideouts of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Tazame, Mashema, Doka, Maje and neighboring areas near Gandaya village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). Four militiamen were killed, an unconfirmed number of others fled with gunshot wounds, all the camps were destroyed, 57 rustled cattle, 900,000 naira cash and military uniforms were recovered.

On 25 November 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with policemen and a local defense militia between Kwarare and Kadoji villages in Jibia LGA (Katsina). Five of the assailants were killed, one policeman and one defense militia member were wounded. Other sources report three fatalities.
On 25 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Christian community in Takulashi Buladunya (Chibokm Borno). They forced the people to flee and burned a church and other properties.
On 25 November 2023, the Sokoto militia attacked and wounded many people in the Here community, coded to Asara (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia also abducted an unspecified number of people.

On 26 November 2023, troops of the Nigerian army responded to a distress call and raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). Two abductees were rescued, two members of the group were arrested and others fled. It is not clear if a clash occurred, casualties are unknown.
On 26 November 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted all civilians passengers from a vehicle along the Sokoto-Goronyo road, coded to Goronyo (Goronyo, Sokoto).

On 27 November 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two policemen at Ahiara junction (Ahiazu Mbaise, Imo). One civilian was hit and killed by a stray bullet, in the attack which took place when the police commissioner was visiting the area. Other sources report that the policemen were attacked inside a fuel station while they were buying petrol. The police claimed to have arrested 18 ESN members in connection with the attack.

On 27 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man, wounded his wife and an unspecified number of residents and abducted several others including the deceased's daughter when they invaded Gandu community (Lafia, Nassarawa).

On 27 November 2023, the Nigerian troops killed three ISWAP fighters after the militia attacked them around the Borno College of Basic Studies, Bama (Bama, Borno). ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian army checkpoint forcing the soldiers to retreat. The militants also claimed to have burned the checkpoint.

On 27 November 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed eleven loggers who were working at their charcoal site near Bale (Damboa, Borno) when they invaded the area on camels and surrounded the victims. The dismembered bodies of the victims were recovered in two batches of six and five respectively.

On 28 November 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged ASVG operatives and policemen in an armed clash at Aguluzigbo (Aniocha, Anambra). Two ASVG operatives were killed; other sources report four fatalities, the police claimed that the assailants were repelled.
On 28 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two farmers on their farms in Kwambai, also called Kpombal (Takum, Taraba).

Around 28 November 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked residents of seven villages in Kaga LGA (Borno) coded to Benisheikh and killed several civilians. The villages were attacked and asked to leave the area by the militants because they failed to provide information on the military's activity in the area. Several fatalities coded as 10.

On 28 November 2023, the Nigerian police, in collaboration with the Army, Hunters and Local vigilantes, engaged the Taraba militia in a firefight in Tonti village (Bali, Taraba). The clash was a response to the distress call on the invasion of the village by the militia. The security forces ambushed them and killed more than 50 militiamen.

On 28 November 2023, a Kaduna militia numbering seven abducted eight residents of Dan-Honu, coded to near by Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna). The abductees included a couple, an Imam; his wife, children and baby. The Imam, his wife and baby escaped as they were being led away.
On 28 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Arm/CJTF checkpoint in Lingir (Monguno, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 28 November 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three men while attacking a Nigerian Army and CJTF checkpoint near Mairari (Guzamala, Borno). They wounded many and forced others to retreat. They also burned three motorbikes and seized nine others, weapons, and ammunition. Other sources reported four fatalities, and the attack was an ambush in nearby Lingir. There were three fatalities.

On 28 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Bolt driver and a female passenger at the staff quarters of the University of Calabar, Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductors left the Bolt cab and went away with the driver.

On 28 November 2023, soldiers and policemen from Operation Hawk invaded the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Koka area of Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta). One policeman was killed; 125 members of the group were arrested, 8 of whom were identified as armed robbers, pistols, laptops and other items were recovered.
On 28 November 2023, the Nigerian military engaged ISWAP/Boko Haram (JAS) in a firefight around the Yaleri Kurna, coded to Konduga (Kodunga, Borno). There were no fatalities.

On 29 November 2023, the Nigerian police and local vigilante group attacked an unidentified armed group attempting to abduct a man in Kadade (Toro, Bauchi). One of the abductors was shot dead by the police, and others escaped with gunshot wounds. The police rescued three other persons, including a pastor abducted from Raddi village in Plateau State, coded separately. There was one fatality.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three people, including a pastor from Raddi Village, coded to Bassa (Bassa, Plateau). The hostages were later released when the police attacked the militia in Bauch State, coded separately.

On 29 November 2023, Nigerian security (coded as the police) engaged unidentified group of abductors in a firefight in Yogi village, coded to Toro (Toro, Bauchi), killing one of the abductors. Two hostages were released after that.

Around 29 November 2023 (as reported), Black Axe also called Aiye confraternity members killed a gate keeper at Aiyetoro area of Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos) following the victim's involvement in brokering peace between the militia and a person whom they previously robbed. The victim was lured to where he was shot before his body was hacked to a heap of meat by the assailants.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Anyiin (Logo, Benue), Ayilamo, Iorza and Gbeji [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Iorza and Gbeji (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba, Anyiin and Ayilamo [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group loyal to a candidate for the NANS president position shot and wounded some students at the venue of the NANS convention in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). A former president of the association who is currently the SSA to the president on student engagement led the assailants to the venue. The victims of the attack were delegates for opposition candidates.
On 29 November 2023, the Sokoto militia killed one person in the Dan Abba community, coded to Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia also abducted twenty people from the community.

On 29 November 2023, NSCDC officials shot and wounded two students at a secondary school in Life Camp, Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The reason for the attack is unknown and the officials were arrested.
Around 29 November 2023 (as reported), an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Iyan-Era area of Ojo LGA (Lagos). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 29 November 2023, an unidentified armed group of 5 who were hooded killed the Ogun state government house's director of finance, wounded his aides at Kuto bridge in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun) and stole unspecified amount of money. The stolen money was a large sum which the victim had withdrawn for government use from a bank about 3 km away from the scene of the attack. Other sources report that the assailants were armed robbers.
On 29 November 2023, the Nigerian troops engaged ISWAP in a firefight after the militia ambushed them in Ali Gambori village (Guzamala, Borno). ISWAP fighters retreated. There were no fatalities.

Around 29 November 2023 (between 27 November - 3 December), a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Ayilamo (Logo, Benue), Anyiin, Iorza and Gbeji [coded separately]. A total of 12 civilians were killed, several others were wounded, the assailants invaded houses and robbed victims of money. 12 fatalities spilt across three events coded as 4.

On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Catholic priest and his driver in Umuekebi, Osu Owerre (Isiala Mbano, Imo). The militia robbed some shops before moving the hostages away. A ransom of 50 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded, the abductees were released on 8 December, some sources report that 500,000 naira was paid as ransom.

On 30 November 2023, suspected Fulani herders attacked and killed a lady and six men in Pukah or Pukah Pushit (Mangu, Plateau). They also raided Pinper, coded separately. The attack was aimed at avenging the killing of a Fulani man whose body was found in a well. Other sources report 8 fatalities and updated it to 11 after 3 more bodies were found in the bush when the 8 victims were being buried. Fatalities coded as 8.

On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a popular businessman in his village of Umuezikegbu in Egbuoma community (Oguta, Imo). The victim was dragged out of his house by the assailants and shot severally until he died.
On 30 November 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one civilian and abducted seven locals when they invaded Igu community (Bwari, FCT).
On 30 November 2023, the Sokoto militia raided Gidan Marayu near Dundaye (Wamakko, Sokoto). They abducted an unspecified number of the residents.

On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the district head of Alingora community, coded as Mallam Ali Gora (Ardo Kola, Taraba) along with six other people. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two people in Eku community (Ethiope East, Delta). The victims were taken to the hospital after the assailants fled the area.

On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian at Okpara community, coded to Okpara Inland (Ethiope East, Delta) after he was trailed from Eku community. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 1 October 2023, Ovonum and Ofatura communal militias engaged in an armed clash in both communities, coded to Ofatura (Obubra, Cross River) following a dispute over a piece of land. Sources in Ovonum claim that one person was killed, other sources report an unspecified number of fatalities, over 200 houses were destroyed and thousands were displaced. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 1 October 2023, Ofatura and Ovonum communal militias engaged in an armed clash in both communities, coded to Ovonum (Obubra, Cross River) following a dispute over a piece of land. Sources in Ovonum claim that one person was killed, other sources report an unspecified number of fatalities, over 200 houses were destroyed and thousands were displaced. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 1 October 2023, Sokoto militias killed three people and abducted eighteen others in Soro village, coded to Binji (Binji, Sokoto). The militias also set houses and property on fire.

On 1 October 2023, policemen and hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in the Gurin area (Fufore, Adamawa). One member of the group was killed, other fled with gunshot wounds, two abductees were rescued by the police and one rifle, 25 rounds were recovered.
On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a woman on her farm in Ogene Iga village near Okpo (Olamaboro, Kogi).

On 1 October 2023, troops of the joint task force called Operation Udo Ka II presumed to be comprised of soldiers and policemen conducted clearance operations and engaged ESN/ IPOB militants in an armed clash at Ihube (Okigwe, Imo), Aku and Umulolo [coded separately]. The militants deployed IEDs enroute to the camps which were destroyed. Two militants were killed, four were arrested and others fled. Several items including Biafra currency were recovered by the troops, two fatalities split across three events coded as 1.
On 1 October 2023, Sokoto militias killed two people and injured many others in Kurfai village in Illela, coded to Dange (Dange-Shuni, Sokoto). The militias rustled many livestock.

On 1 October 2023, troops of the joint task force called Operation Udo Ka II presumed to be comprised of soldiers and policemen conducted clearance operations and engaged ESN/ IPOB militants in an armed clash at Aku, coded to Aku Ihube (Okigwe, Imo), Ihube and Umulolo [coded separately]. The militants deployed IEDs enroute to the camps which were destroyed, two militants were killed, four were arrested and others fled. Several items including Biafra currency were recovered by the troops, two fatalities split across three events coded as 1.

On 1 October 2023, troops of the joint task force called Operation Udo Ka II presumed to be comprised of soldiers and policemen conducted clearance operations and engaged ESN/ IPOB militants in an armed clash at Umulolo (Okigwe, Imo), Aku and Ihube [coded separately]. The militants deployed IEDs enroute to the camps which were destroyed. Two militants were killed, four were arrested and others fled. Several items including Biafra currency were recovered by the troops, two fatalities split across three events coded as 0.
On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people along the Takwa-Kwaku Road in Kuje Area Council, Kuje (Kuje, Federal Capital Territory). No further details.
On 1 October 2023, Katsina militias abducted five farmers while working on their farm in Garin Dodo, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina).

On 1 October 2023, ISWAP shot and killed two traders in Azir, coded as Ajir (Damboa, Borno). The victims had gone to Azir to sell their goods in a local market when the militia met and killed them. Two people were also abducted.
On 1 October 2023, ISWAP militants shot and killed a Boko Haram (JAS) commander in an ambush in Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno).

On 1 October 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with Boko Haram (JAS), attempting to abduct some farmers around Buduwa, Banki (Bama, Borno). The troops were on routine patrol when they bumped into them. They exchanged gunshots, and a farmer sustained gun wounds. There were no fatalities.

On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Adu village in Kwal district (Bassa, Plateau). At least nine persons were killed and many others were wounded; the murdered victims included five males, two females and two children. Other sources claim that 8 persons were killed.

On 1 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked travelers most of whom were IDPs near Tse-Awunah (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka where the victims were traveling from. One person was killed, four others were wounded.
On 1 October 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted fourteen people searching for firewood around Aulari, along Konduga-Bama Road, Aulari (Konduga, Borno). No further details.

On 2 October 2023, Adawama State police and the hunters clashed with an unidentified armed group while raiding their hideouts in Gurin, Muninga, Wuro Kesum, Parda and Boggel Districts of Gurin coded to Gurin (Fufore, Adamawa). The police killed one of the armed groups, and others escaped with bullet wounds. The police rescued two hostages and recovered one AK-47 rifle and 25 rounds of ammunition.

On 2 October 2023, a Sokoto militia clashed with soldiers, police, and a local defense militia after it attacked civilians in the Soro community, also spelled Zoro (Binji, Sokoto). The attack killed 3 civilians and injured 3 others. Several people were abducted, including a whole family, while the assailants set houses ablaze. The security forces repelled them.

On 2 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one of two siblings and abducted the other along the Ogori-Ososo Road in Ogori (Ogori, Kogi). The armed group released the hostage later without taking a ransom.

On 2 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and injured the driver of a newspaper distribution vehicle along the Benin-Onitsha highway, coded to Ukwulu (Dunukofia, Anambra). There were no fatalities.

On 2 October 2023, the Nigerian military and hunters engaged in a firefight with an armed group in the Chida Forest in Kuje Area Council, Kuje (Kuje, Federal Capital Territory). They rescued some hostages. There were no fatalities.

On 2 October 2023, the Nigerian military exchanged gunshots with Katsina militias and killed one in Yankara village (Faskari, Katsina). The militias attempted to abduct some people when the soldiers clashed with them and thwarted their plan. The soldiers recovered an AK-47 rifle after forcing the militia to retreat.
On 2 October 2023, ISWAP militants killed one civilian, shot and wounded one other person at Mugule village in Damboa LGA (Borno). Three people were also abducted.
On 2 October 2023, ISWAP fighters shot and wounded a CJTF member after breaking into his home in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The CTTF officer was taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 2 October 2023, a Katsina militia attacked civilians at Nasarawa ward (Funtua, Katsina) and killed the ward councilor. The victim who was also a member of the local defense militia was killed at his residence when the assailants saw the rifle which he collected to resume night patrol and slung over his back while he was entering his house and the rifle was stole by them.
On 2 October 2023, Sokoto militias injured many people and abducted others in Garin Idi village, coded to Kusabuni (Sabon Birni, Sokoto).

On 2 October 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering six wounded two shop owners and looted items from stores at the mini market of Usman Dan Fodio University in Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto). The assailants also fired some shots into the air.

On 3 October 2023, an unidentified armed group (suspected to be members of the Osun Transport System Management) attacked some student leaders in Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun). The students were assaulted during a solidarity visit to other NANS leaders. The armed group claimed that the student leaders aligned with a particular political leader. The wounded members were taken to the hospital for treatment. There were no fatalities

On 3 October 2023, suspected Boko Haram (JAS) abducted several farmers about 13 kilometres from Bama (Bama, Borno). The militia seized the farmers on their way to the farm and took them to the fringe of the Sambisa forest.

On 3 October 2023, a Yansakai militia attacked Fulani communities neighboring Soro community in Binji LGA (Sokoto) in a reprisal attack carried out against Soro community by a Sokoto militia [coded separately]. An unspecified number of civilians were killed, houses were set ablaze, the assailants believed that the community were aware of the attack that was previously launched against them, other sources report that there was pre-existing hostilities between the communities. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 October 2023, the Kaduna militia abducted three people on their way to Kano along the Kaduna- Abuja highway, coded to Katari (Kachia, Kaduna). The police rescued the hostages on 13 November 2023 at Kidandan village in Giwa LGA of the state.

On 3 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attempted to abduct a student of University of Abuja from the school's permanent site in Gwagwalada (Gwagwalada, FCT). The victim struggled and freed herself.
On 3 October 2023, NURTW members loyal to MC Oluomo beat up a man at the Area 1 in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT) after he was accused of carrying passengers from along the road.
On 4 October 2023, ISWAP drowned a farmer in Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The victim was returning from his farm when he was drowned.
On 4 October 2023, a Sokoto militia killed five civilians when they attacked Kalugo village (Binji, Sokoto).

On 4 October 2023, the Ifon and Ilobu communities renewed the clash over a land dispute between the two communities, coded to Ifon (Orolu, Osun), after two members of the Ifon community were shot on a motorcycle. The clash led to the death of one person. Houses were set on fire, and some resident fled their homes. The conflict raged till the following day, coded separately. Other sources report that 4 policemen were shot and wounded, their patrol van was set ablaze after they were accused of taking sides.

On 4 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a motorcyclist and wounded one other person at a boundary in Ifon (Orolu, Osun). The two victims were shot by the assailants who first asked where they were from.

On 4 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the Plateau State Chairman of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). He was abducted when returning home from work in the evening. The armed group released him the following day without claiming ransom payment.

On 4 October 2023, a Katsina militia abducted five female students of Federal University Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina) when they invaded their private hostel. A ransom of 2 million naira was demanded for one of the abductees, the police claimed that some suspects were arrested in relation to the incident. A total of 2.5 million naira was paid to the abductors and the abductees were not released. One of the abductees was released on 19 November after a ransom of 4.5 million naira was paid while the others were released on 15 December, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 5 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a ransom bearer in Ose LGA, coded to Ifon (Ose, Ondo). The victim had gone to deliver a ransom to release some hostages when the abductors detained him. He was released later.

On 5 October 2023, operatives of the joint task force presumed to be comprised of soldiers and policemen killed the chief security officer of Obelle community (Emohua, Rivers). The victim was carrying a gun and attempted to flee when he was ordered to stop which resulted in him being shot by one JTF operative.
On 5 October 2023, Sokoto militias opened fire sporadically and shot three people dead in Gidan Nashiyau village, coded to Araba (Illela, Sokoto).

On 5 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five persons who were traveling from Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi) to Imo state. The abductees include three catholic nuns, one seminarian and the driver of the vehicle. An unspecified ransom amount was demanded.

On 5 October 2023, the troops of Operation UDO KA II conducted a clearance operation in Okigwe-Umulolo communities, coded to Umulolo (Okigwe, Imo). The troops confronted the militias, and some escaped to the nearby bush with gunshot wounds. Two suspects were arrested, and the troops recovered two locally-made guns, ammunition, one PKT machine gun barrel, one big locally made Rocket Propelled Launcher (Ogbunigwe) and IED-making materials. There were no fatalities.

On 5 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a soldier after invading the Army checkpoint in Soye, coded as Ngurosoye (Bama, Borno). They claimed to have captured a machine gun, an assault rifle, and a motorbike after the soldiers had withdrawn.

On 5 October 2023, a renewed communal clash over a land dispute between Ifon and Ilobu, coded to Ifon (Orolu, Osun), led to the killing of eight people, including a baby. Many houses were set on fire, triggering a mass exodus of residents from the affected communities. Some sources reported 5 and 6 fatalities. 5 fatalities coded. Other sources report that 4 policemen were shot and wounded, their patrol van was set ablaze after they were accused of taking sides.

On 5 October 2023, an unidentified armed group (suspected to be from Ifon or Ilobu) shot and wounded four police officers in an ambush at an unspecified location between the two communities, coded to Ifon (Orolu, Osun). The attackers claimed the police were supporting one community against the other. They burnt the police patrol van. Some residents were killed in the process. unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 5 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two cattle traders in Kwande LGA (Benue) as they were conveying livestock and other goods to the south-east. 11 other persons were reported missing.

On 5 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three Catholic nuns and a seminarian on their way to a burial program in Owerri, coded to Orji (Owerri North, Imo). The armed group also took their driver away.
On 6 October 2023, Sokoto militias injured and abducted an unspecified number of people in Binji LGA, coded to Binji (Binji, Sokoto). The militia set fire to many houses.

On 6 October 2023, a Kaduna militia engaged in an armed clash with security operatives that were comprised of soldiers, policemen and KADVS operatives who repelled their attack on civilians at Unguwan Dankali, Zaria LGA (Kaduna). The militia shot sporadically to disperse the residents, four persons were killed, scores were injured, other sources report 4 wounded and an unspecified number of persons were abducted. Five of the abductees were rescued by the joint security team.

On 6 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an Anglican priest and his family around Evwreni junction (Ughelli North, Delta). The abductees were travelling from Ughelli to Uwheru community, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 6 October 2023, Boko Haram ambushed ISWAP fighters travelling on five motorcycles and killed two commanders and other fighters around Sheri Bultuwa (Mobbar, Borno). ISWAP Commanders Baa Idrissa, Baba Kano and other fighters were killed. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 6 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted at least nine persons from Kaura Namoda town (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The assailants raided Tsohuwar Kasuwa and Sarkawa areas of the town, they also rustled cattle.
On 6 October 2023, Kaduna militias attacked the Nigerian military's position in Pole Wire village near Dogon Dawa (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). They killed two soldiers in the firefight.
On 7 October 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted over 30 farmers while they were working on a farm in Chikuri (Chikun, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 October 2023, two factions of an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash at Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi) over reasons suspected to be related to sharing formula or rivalry. Two persons were killed while five others were arrested by security operatives who trailed them.

On 7 October 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with policemen who attempted to repel their attack on civilians along Mararraban-Yorro-Zing Jalingo road, coded to Zing (Zing, Taraba). The assailants abducted two commuters and stole unspecified valuables.

On 7 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a man in his house at Ihekwuenu-Aku (Igbo Etiti, Enugu) coded to Enugu and beat him up. The assailants also destroyed the man's house. One source claimed that the son of the village head was one of the assailants.

On 7 October 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 17 residents from Anguwar Bawa and Anguwar Danlele in Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The abductees included 5 infants and their mothers and ransom of 19 million naira was demanded and paid for the victims' release, only four abductees were released, the infants died after a month in captivity when their mothers took ill and were unable to feed them.

On 7 October 2023, a Zamfara militia ambushed a local defense militia that was escorting civilians at Dogon Tsauni (Gusau, Zamfara) coded to Magami where they were coming from. Ten persons including 5 local defense militiamen were killed, several others were wounded while three vehicles in the convoy were burnt.

On 7 October 2023, the Nigerian military engaged ISWAP fighters in an armed conflict after the militia had killed a man in Nguruwuri town coded to Konduga (Konduga, Borno). ISWAP set fire to food supplies and an unspecified number of houses before they withdrew. One fatality reported.

On 8 October 2023, the Yache boys beheaded three Tiv people while harvesting cassava on their farm in Yache (Yala, Cross River). They killed another two on a different farm location and publicly displayed their heads. Five fatalities.
On 8 October 2023, the Katsina militias abducted two women after raiding Tashar Bokiti village, coded to Tsaskiya (Safana, Katsina). No further details.
On 8 October 2023, the Katsina militias ambushed and abducted two people along the Runka-Safana Road near Yarsanta village, coded to Safana (Safana, Katsina).

Around 8 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a civilian at his father's compound along Oviri-Ogor/ Edjekota road (Ughelli North, Delta). The civilian was killed after the target, the victim's father, fled in to the bush. The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 8 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three people after they attacked their boat on the Isaka Waterways in Okrika LGA, coded to Okrika (Rivers). No further details.

On 8 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one civilian from his residence at Tse Digenyi (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera. The abductors trailed the abductee to his home from a football viewing center and ordered him to fuel his motorcycle with which they took him away.

On 8 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an Islamic cleric and his brother around Oshokoshoko along Lokoja-Obajana-Kabba road (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductees were conveying a corpse from Lokoja to Ayegunle Gbede for funeral. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.
On 9 October 2023, Kebbi militias abducted five people after raiding Dangan and Runguma villages, coded to Wasagu (Danko, Kebbi). No further details.
On 9 October 2023, Sokoto militias killed three people in the Barayar Zaki community, coded to Wurno (Wurno, Sokoto). The militias injured five people and abducted thirty-two others.

On 9 October 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform abducted an unspecified number of people after waylaying a passenger vehicle along the Ibillo-Ogugu Road, coded to Ibillo (Akoko Edo, Edo). The passengers were heading to Lagos from Kogi State when the armed group took them away with the driver.
On 9 October 2023, five members of an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman in Sangotedo (Eti-Osa, Lagos). The armed group sporadically shot guns and fled in a waiting boat with the victim.

On 9 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons when they invaded a residence at Shabiwa (Dukku, Gombe). The abductees were the wife and brother of a man who fled into the bush upon the abductors' arrival. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia ambushed and killed a local defense militia member at Ubulu-Uku community (Aniocha South, Delta) before other members of the militia engaged the assailants in an armed clash. The victim was at the vigilance post where he was changing into his uniform to resume duty, other sources report that two other persons including a commercial motorcyclist and a woman were killed.

Around 9 October 2023 (as reported), armed pastoralists killed a farmer in Kwanga community, (Ngaski, Kebbi) coded to Wara following a disagreement over grazing. The pastoralists had led their cattle through the farms in the area and destroyed crops.

On 9 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted seven civilians in Igaji community (Ohimini, Benue) coded to Idekpa-Okpiko. Some of the abductees were going to their farms when they were abducted; all of them were rescued by soldiers and community volunteers during a search and rescue operation.

On 9 October 2023, Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash around Jimlari village (Yorro, Taraba). The members of the group fled with many sustaining high degree of gunshot wounds, two abductees were rescued and the troops recovered items including a phone, 36 empty cases among others.
Around 9 October 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group abducted eleven commuters from along Oturkpo-Ojali-Oweto road (Otukpo, Benue).

On 9 October 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and injured 2 civilians in Gulbin Boka (Mariga, Niger), Sakiho, and Ragada (coded separately) and 21 civilians were abducted. There were no fatalities.

On 9 October 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and injured 2 civilians in Ragada (Mariga, Niger), Sakiho, and Gulbin Boka (coded separately) and 21 civilians were abducted. There were no fatalities.

On 9 October 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and injured 2 civilians in Sakiho, location coded to the closest known populated area, Bangi (Mariga, Niger), Ragada, and Gulbin Boka (coded separately) and 21 civilians were abducted. There were no fatalities.
On 9 October 2023, a Niger militia attacked and killed 1 civilian in Kwimo and Dusai in the Mariga LGA, coded to Mariga (Mariga, Niger) and Dusai (coded separately). 6 civilians were abducted.

On 10 October 2023, a Niger militia in large numbers killed the chief of Zagzaga village and abducted many other people when they invaded Zagzaga (Muya, Niger) and adjourning communities. Many livestock were also rustled by the assailants, other sources report that 15 people were abducted.

On 10 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four students of Nasarawa state university from a private hostel in Anguwan Kare in Keffi (Keffi, Nasarawa). The abductees consisted of three females and one male, a ransom of 20 million naira was demanded. Around 13 October, the state government claimed that the abductees were rescued by the troops of 177 guards battalion.
On 10 October 2023, Niger militias killed a businessman after attacking his shop in Mokwa (Mokwa, Niger). The militia abducted the victim's daughter.
On 10 October 2023, Bauchi militias killed a private security guard at the National Open University in Azare (Katagum, Bauchi). They went away with a generator set.

On 10 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted one other person when they invaded Owevwe (Ughelli North, Delta). The abductee is the wife of the president-general of the community and there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 10 October 2023, policemen abducted a man and his family members from their residence in Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The victims were released after a ransom of 1,025,000 naira was transferred from the victim (man) bank account.

On 10 October 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed an automobile technician in his car at Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The attack was suspected to be an assassination, other sources claim that the victim and a cult militia member had had confrontations over a female in the past.
On 10 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have shot and killed two Christian civilians in Garkida (Gombi, Adamawa). They also burned the victims' property.

On 10 October 2023, an unidentified armed group and a local defense militia engaged in an armed clash at Abaji (Abaji, FCT) after the armed group attempted to invade a Fulani settlement in the area. Both group shot into the air to scare the other until the assailants fled and were pursued into the bush by the defense militia. Casualties are unknown.
On 10 October 2023, Zamfara militias killed two people and abducted one in Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). No further details.

On 10 October 2023, policemen shot at a motorist in a fuel station at Ijede (Ikorodu, Lagos). Sources claimed that the policemen attempted to double cross the motorist while the spokesperson of the Lagos state command of the police claimed that policemen wanted to arrest the motorist for a traffic infraction. Casualties are unknown.
On 10 October 2023, the Katsina militia abducted one person after raiding Jaka village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.

Around 10 October 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram (JAS) militants based in Niger state, led by Sadiku, seized control of around 42 communities in Alawa, Bassa, and Zagzaga villages of Shiroro, Munya and Rafi LGAs, location coded to the largest populated area of the three villages mentioned, Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). The event displaced some 5000 civilians from their homes. The group also dislodged soldiers from their military bases (unclear if clashes occurred).
Around 11 October 2023 (as reported), troops of the 21 Armored Brigade Bama, together with the CJTF, killed four Boko Haram (JAS) on the outskirts of Bama (Bama, Borno).

On 11 October 2023, Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Yelwa village (Jalingo, Taraba). One AK47 rifle, one magazine and 7 rounds of 7.62mm special were recovered by the troops, casualties are unknown.

Around 11 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian at Lokojoro village in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). The abductee was rescued by troops of sector 4 of Operation Safe Haven after he was abandoned inside water by the assailants.
On 11 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia ambushed and wounded two civilians along Tse Abiem road, coded to Ugba (Logo, Benue). The victims sustained various degrees of injuries.

On 11 October 2023, an unidentified ethnic militia invaded Didango community market (Karim Lamidu, Taraba), killed two persons, wounded several others and stole items worth millions of naira. The attackers were countered by the youths from the community and fled back to their village which is about 4km away from Didango. The police claimed that one person was killed and five were wounded.

On 11 October 2023, Kaduna militias shot and killed a ransom bearer in Sabon Layi, Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). The victim volunteered to deliver a ransom to release a village head held hostage. The militias killed him for resisting them while trying to seize his motorcycle after receiving the ransom.

On 11 October 2023, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted two other persons from their farms in Daupe community (Tafa, Niger) coded to Sabon Wuse. One of the abductees is a serving policeman, the wife of one of the abductees was shot in the leg and wounded when she attempted to prevent their abduction.

On 11 October 2023, the 25 Task Force Brigade troops repelled an attack by ISWAP and shot six of the militants dead in Sabon Gari, Damboa (Damboa, Borno). A Nigerian soldier also lost his life during the clash. Weapons were recovered from the militia. Seven fatalities.

On 12 October 2023, the Joint Task Force North West Operation HADARIN DAJI ambushed some Kebbi militias at Karenbana village, coded to Kainya (Danko, Kebbi), trying to move their hostages across to another state. The Joint Task Force engaged them in a gunfight and rescued 17 hostages. Some militias escaped with gunshot wounds. There were no fatalities.

On 12 October 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed an NSCDC operative at Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). The operative stepped away from his duty post to ease himself when he was killed by the assailants who stole his gun.
On 12 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person when they attacked a Fulani settlement called Rawul in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 12 October 2023, Kebbi militias abducted many people at Kainya village (Danko, Kebbi). The military, acting on intelligence, ambushed the militias at Karenbana village while trying to take the hostage cross to another state. They engaged them in a gunfight, coded separately and rescued the hostages.

Around 12 October 2023 (as reported), the Nigerian military discovered unspecified dried and fresh dead bodies littered the IPOB/ESN camp in Aku Forest, coded to Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo). The bodies were presumed to have been killed by the IPOB for ritual and cannibalism. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 12 October 2023, Katsina militias abducted a man and his wife in Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina). The abductors demanded no ransom.

On 12 October 2023, a Niger militia abducted 28 civilians from Tegina and Utoro communities in Shiroro LGA (Niger). The abductees included women and children, food items were also looted from shops and houses.
On 12 October 2023, Nigerian troops foiled an attack by an unidentified armed group on Bisichi village (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). One motorcycle was recovered by the troops, casualties are unknown.

On 12 October 2023, suspected Fulani pastoralists shot and killed a Benue Links bus passenger at Tyolaha village en route to Otukpo, coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue). Several other passengers were injured during the attack. Other sources report that three passengers were killed and many others were missing.

Around 13 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified cult group macheted three suspected rival group members to death in Ijoko (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The police discovered the bodies of the three victims with their left hands chopped off by the assailants. The police identified one of the victims as a wanted notorious member of the Eiye Confraternity.
