On 13 October 2023, Nigerian troops were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group and foiled an attempted abduction by the group at Saya, coded Unguwar Saya (Bassa, Plateau). The assailants fled, casualties are unknown.

On 13 October 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a school principal and a teacher within the school premises at Ojiegbe area of Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). The assailants also stole the victims' motorcycle.

On 13 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Point of Sale (POS) operator along the Sobi Road, coded to Fufu (Ilorin South, Kwara). The abductors demanded a 100,000 NGN to release the hostage.

On 13 October 2023, policemen prevented an attempted attack an engaged with armed clash with an unidentified armed group on civilians at Yobo community (Ewekoro, Ogun). The assailants were suspected land grabber, eight of them were arrested; one car, ammunition, a gun, charms and other items were recovered from them by the police. There were no casualties.
On 13 October 2023, Katsina militia abducted an older woman after raiding Fararu village in Dabawa ward, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). No further details.

Around 13 October 2023 (as reported), suspected IPOB militants numbering over six who were dressed in police and military uniforms killed the deputy registrar of federal polytechnic Uwana at his residence in Umu Ezeala (Ehime Mbano, Imo). The assailants attacked the victim with machetes and axes and shot sporadically to scare residents away when he screamed for help; he was taken away and his decomposing body was found on 15 October. Other sources report that the assailants were suspected assassins.
On 13 October 2023, a Kebbi militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed 1 civilian in Singare in the Kalgo LGA, coded to Kalgo (Kalgo, Kebbi) and abducted several others.

On 14 October 2023, suspected armed pastoralists killed a farmer whose farm they invaded with their cattle at Apalokun community (Iwajowa, Oyo) coded to Iwere-Ile. Crops worth thousands of naira were also destroyed.

On 14 October 2023, suspected armed pastoralists ambushed and engaged Operation Burst operatives consisting of soldiers, policemen, Amotekun, OPC and Soludero operatives who responded to a distress call in an armed clash at Apalokun (Iwajowa, Oyo) coded Iwere-Ile. The assailants had earlier killed a farmer [coded separately], which resulted in the distress call that the operatives responded to, scores of persons were wounded. Other sources report that an unspecified number of persons were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 14 October 2023, Nigerian troops engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and foiled an attempted attack by the group at Denche village (Jos East, Plateau), coded to Angware. The group fled and abandoned two motorcycles.

On 14 October 2023, troops of Operation UDO KA II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in armed clashes at Lilu (Ihiala, Anambra), Orsumoghu, Mother Valley and Orsu LGA [coded separately]. The troops claimed to have encountered and detonated several IEDs and other obstacles, several camps and shrines were destroyed, an unspecified number of militants fled with gunshot wounds. One militant was arrested and several items were recovered by the troops.

On 14 October 2023, troops of Operation UDO KA II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in armed clashes at Orsumoghu (Ihiala, Anambra), Lilu, Mother Valley and Orsu LGA [coded separately]. The troops claimed to have encountered and detonated several IEDs and other obstacles, several camps and shrines were destroyed, an unspecified number of militants fled with gunshot wounds. One militant was arrested and several items were recovered by the troops.

On 14 October 2023, troops of Operation UDO KA II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in armed clashes at Mother Valley in Ihiala LGA (Anambra), Lilu, Mother Valley and Orsu LGA [coded separately]. The troops claimed to have encountered and detonated several IEDs and other obstacles, several camps and shrines were destroyed, an unspecified number of militants fled with gunshot wounds. One militant was arrested and several items were recovered by the troops.
On 14 October 2023, suspected armed pastoralists killed three civilians at Imatom village (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba.

On 14 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed at least 3 villagers and abducted an unspecified number of others from Yola village (Karaye, Kano). The assailants attacked the village on different occasions on the same day; other sources report that two people were killed and four abducted in the first attack while one was killed and two were abducted the second time. 3 fatalities coded.
On 14 October 2023, Sokoto militias on motorcycles killed five people and abducted an unspecified number of others when raiding the Kwargaba community (Wurno, Sokoto). No further details.
On 14 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier and forced the rest to flee after attacking a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Mainok (Kaga, Borno).

On 14 October 2023, troops of Operation UDO KA II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in armed clashes at (Orsu, Anambra) coded to Awo-Idemili, Lilu, Mother Valley and Orsumoghu [coded separately]. The troops claimed to have encountered and detonated several IEDs and other obstacles, several camps and shrines were destroyed, an unspecified number of militants fled with gunshot wounds. One militant was arrested and several items were recovered by the troops.

Around 14 October 2023 (week of), policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Bwari forest (Bwari, FCT). The group were suspected abductors, one of them was killed and another arrested.

On 14 October 2023, troops of the Nigerian army conducted clearance operations and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at the Hayin Tsando general area in Igabi LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed, scores of others fled with varying degrees of gunshot wounds, six abductees were rescued and the troops recovered two rifles.

On 14 October 2023, a Zamfara militia engaged in an armed clash with troops of Operation Hadarin Daji and policemen who responded to a distress call at Sabon Gida in Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara). The militiamen had attacked a students' private hostel in the area; four students who were abducted were rescued, other sources report that two students and a staff of the school were the abductees who were later rescued. Casualties are unknown.

On 14 October 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed 1 civilian in Jemaku, also known as Jimaku (Mashegu, Niger) and abducted several others. One civilian escaped two days later.

Around 15 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted eleven women while they were working on their farms in Riruwa, Toro LGA (Bauchi). The abductees were rescued by a team of policemen, soldiers and hunters [there is no report of a clash].

On 15 October 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed and engaged Yan Ba Beli local defense militia in an armed clash at Gamji village in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The local militiamen were ambushed while they were on a patrol, nine of them were killed and others were wounded.

On 15 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the councilor of Assakio ward (APC member) and his brother on the Assakio-Obi road (Obi, Nassarawa). The abductees were released the following day after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.
On 15 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a 10-year-old girl in Guyaba (Kirfi, Bauchi). No further details.

On 15 October 2023, a Niger militia abducted at least 17 civilians from Kukau community (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The abductees included ten women who were made to carry the food items which were also looted from shops and houses.

On 16 October 2023, NDLEA operatives and policemen engaged in a physical clash at a police station in Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi) when the policemen resisted the NDLEA operatives who attempted to arrest the wife of a policeman who was selling marijuana and other illicit drugs from her husband's car inside the police station. There were no casualties.

On 16 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three people in Shao (Moro, Kwara) after opening fire indiscriminately. The wife of a Kwara State House of Assembly member was among the abductees.
On 16 October 2023, Fulani herders and the Bara group engaged in an armed clash over cattle grazing on yet-to-be-harvested farms in Bara (Gulami, Borno). Two people were injured in the conflict.

On 16 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a policeman who was presumed to have been off-duty when they attacked Sakajiki community (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The community's residents claimed that the militia used a police van to loot food items and abducted an unspecified number of women and set many houses ablaze. Other sources report that several civilians were killed.

On 16 October 2023, about nine members of an unidentified armed group abducted three people in Ora, Ayetoro community, Ora (Ekiti, Kwara). The armed group wearing masks also invaded the Ora traditional ruler's palace looted and vandalized some sections of the palace.

On 16 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS faction) militants abducted 10 farmers while they were working on their fields on the outskirts of Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). Three of the abductees were later released while 7 were murdered over their failure to pay the demanded ransom (coded separately).
On 16 October 2023, Zamfara militia killed one person and abducted four women when they attacked Zamfarawa village, coded to Faskari (Faskari, Katsina).

On 16 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife and two children of a member of the Kwara state house of assembly from their residence. The assailants shot sporadically before taking the abductees away, location coded to Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The abductees were released on 18 October, there are no reports on ransom demands and payment, five persons were arrested in connection with the abduction.

On 17 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) shot and killed a police officer of the MOPOL 53 PMF Bama while working on his farm in Bama (Bama, Borno). The attackers sneaked him into his farm, seized his rifle and shot him with it.

On 17 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed three civilians and abducted over 51 others at Bagega community (Anka, Zamfara) when they invaded the area in dozens. The district head and three members of his household were part of the abductees
On 17 October 2023, two rival armed groups clashed in the Nkwegu market, Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi). Two people were killed in the clash. No further details.

On 17 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a medical doctor and wounded the okada rider who was carrying him along Jangargari-Awe road (Awe, Nassarawa) when the doctor was returning from his farm. He was inflicted with machete cuts that killed him.

On 17 October 2023, troops of 2 Battalion of the Nigerian army ambushed and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Udawa general area of Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). One soldier and three militiamen were killed, the troops recovered arms and ammunition from the militia who fled the area.
On 17 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two civilians at Mahanga town (Logo, Benue). The assailants proceeded to Ayilamo town where they killed three others [coded separately].

On 17 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Nagi camp in Mbachohon (Gwer West, Benue). Four persons went missing or killed according to some sources. An unspecified number of others were wounded.

On 17 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a woman at her residence in Gidan Dembe area of Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The victim who was the daughter of a state house of assembly member was strangled to death, her hands and legs were tied up by the assailants. the reason for the attack is unknown. The victim's husband was arrested by the police and accused of being responsible.

Around 17 October 2023 (week of), Boko Haram (JAS faction) killed seven farmers who were part of a group of ten that they abducted on 16 October from the outskirts of Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The other three farmers were released while the murdered victims were killed over failure to pay ransom. Location coded to where the victims were abducted from.
On 17 October 2023, the Zamfara militias attacked the Tsunami area on the outskirts of Gusau ( Gusau, Zamfara). No further details.
On 17 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman in Eket (Eket, Akwa Ibom). They took her to their hideout in Ikot Ubo, Nsit Ubium LGA.

On 17 October 2023, the Katsina militia engaged in a firefight with a local militia in Kuki village (Dutsinma, Katsina). The community group killed two militia members, and the rest fled. There were two fatalities.
On 17 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia shot and killed three civilians at Ayilamo community (Logo, Benue).

On 18 October 2023, APC and SDP supporters engaged in a gunfight in Idah (Idah, Kogi). Many people, including a police officer, sustained bullet injuries, and vehicles were vandalized. There were no fatalities.
Around 18 October 2023 (between 18 - 20 October), the Niger militia abducted dozens of people at Sayyadi and Kachi coded to Mashegu (Mashegu, Niger). No further details.

On 18 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Kanzanna village in Tilli district (Bunza, Kebbi). Two people were killed and three others were abducted. The abductees were rescued by security operatives on 22 October [coded separately].
On 18 October 2023, a Kaduna militia ambushed a team of hunters and killed one while they were conducting a highway patrol along Kaduna-Birnin Gwari road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 18 October 2023, the Niger militia shot and killed two people after blocking the Garun Gabab-Yakila road, Tegina Outpost, coded to Tegina (Rafi, Niger). The victims were shot when the militia fired indiscriminately at the moving vehicles. They abducted many others.
On 18 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman in Obagie (Ikpoba Okha, Edo). The Nigerian troops rescued the victims and arrested two of the abductors.

Around 18 October 2023 (as reported), the troops of 3 Battalion Operation Hadin Kai repelled the ISWAP attacks on Gamboru Ngala, Gamboru (Ngala, Bornu). The militias drove in Hilux trucks and motorcycles and attacked the military formation. The troops repelled the onslaught with reinforcement from Battalion headquarters. An unknown number of the militias were killed in the clash. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 18 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a correctional service officer at the Afokang Correctional facility in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The attackers opened fire on the joint security team, comprising the soldiers, the police and the correctional service officers, at the facility. They responded and engaged them in a firefight. An officer died, and many others were injured, but the attack did not affect the correctional facility. Another source reported that stray bullets hit and injured a woman and her six-year-old daughter. The assailants took a rifle away. There was one fatality in the attack.
On 18 October 2023, Zamfara militias abducted five people after raiding a village in Kaura Namoda LGA, coded to Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). No further details.

On 18 October 2023, an unidentified cult militia member shot and killed a member of a rival militia who is presumed to have been unarmed at Ikorodu area (Ikorodu, Lagos). The attack was a reprisal, the assailant was arrested by the police.

Around 18 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified cult group shot and killed a member of a rival cult militia in Yaba (Lagos Mainland, Lagos). The Police arrested one of the assailants on 11 October 2023 concerning a gun-making investigation.

On 18 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a checkpoint belonging to a 'militia loyal to the Nigerian Army' (suspected to be CJTF) in Kanama (Yunusari, Yobe). ISWAP burned the checkpoint after the militia withdrew. There were no fatalities.
Around 18 October 2023 (between 18 - 20 October), the Niger militia abducted many people and looted cows in Miadawa and Tabbani, coded to Kulho (Mashegu, Niger). No further details.

On 18 October 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) attacked and killed 1 civilian in Malamawa in the Mashegu LGA, location coded to Mashegu (Mashegu, Niger). The militia looted cattle and ships were also stolen.

Around 19 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group suspected to be APC members disrupted the SDP political rally at the St. Matthew Primary School in Ejule-Kogi, Ejule (Ofu, Kogi). The group invaded the venue, shot weapons sporadically and injured many people. They destroyed canopies, public address systems, chairs and the podium arranged for the event.

Around 19 October 2023 (as reported), the troops of Operation Hadin Kain, in conjunction with Hunters, engaged in a firefight with Boko Haram (JAI) around the Damboa axis, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The troops were on a clearance operation and came under the militants' fire. They captured one member of the militants, forced the rest to abandon their families, and fled. There were no fatalities.

On 19 October 2023, the Niger militia abducted a former chairman of the Ngeski Local Government Area of Kebbi State and twelve others in a commercial vehicle along Tegina-Kontagora road, coded to Tegina (Rafi, Niger). The militia waylaid the victims' vehicle, abducted the passengers and led them into the bush.

On 19 October 2023, the troops of Sector 3 of MNJTF repelled an attack from ISWAP, who invaded the Mosquito Camp military base around Mile 90 between Cross Kauwa and Monguno town, coded to Cross Kauwa (Kukawa, Borno). ISWAP fighters were reported to have come from the axis of Arinna Maimasalaci with Hilux trucks and heavy weapons. There were no fatalities.
On 19 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) killed two Nigerian soldiers after attacking an Army checkpoint in Banki (Bama, Bornu). The soldiers were shot while repelling the militia's attack.
On 19 October 2023, the Nigerian troops and CJTF killed two Boko Haram (JAS)/ISWAP in Bama LGA, coded to Banki (Bama, Borno).

Around 20 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group attacked SDP members and destroyed their properties in Ajaka (Igalamela, Kogi). The SDP members engaged them and overpowered the group. A police officer was caught among the suspects. There were no fatalities.

On 20 October 2023, troops of 33 Brigade of the Nigerian army ambushed a Bauchi militia led by Ya'u and engaged them in an armed clash at a strategic crossing point in Burra (Ningi, Bauchi). The militia were returning from an attack when they were ambushed, the leader of the militia was killed.

On 20 October 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) ambushed and killed three soldiers along the Dikwa-Ngala Road, coded to Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). Four Boko Haram fighters and eight Nigerian soldiers were injured in the clash.
On 20 October 2023, the Bauchi militia shot and killed one person in Unguwar Baba Iyalu, Misau (Misau, Bauchi). No further details.
On 20 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the village head of Kwajale village (Sumaila, Kano). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 20 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed twenty people in Oguaniocha or Oguaniocho (Ogbaru, Anambra). The group injured many other people in the bush where they were hiding after being displaced by the armed group. The injured victims were hospitalised.

On 20 October 2023, troops of 5 Brigade Operation HADIN KAI killed six ISWAP fighters in a failed ambush at Binduldul General area along MSR Maiduguri - Gubio - Kareto - Damasak Road, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Many ISWAP fighters and three Nigerian soldiers were injured in the clash. The Army recovered 2 x PKT guns, 5 x AK 47 rifles and 1 x Hummer bus.

On 20 October 2023, ISWAP ambushed and engaged the troops of Sector 3 of MNJTF in an armed clash at Binduldul (Gubio, Borno). Six ISWAP were killed in the clash and the rest were forced to withdraw. The Nigerian troops recovered two PK machine guns, five AK rifles, and one Hummer bus. Two MNJTF soldiers sustained injuries during the clash.
On 20 October 2023, Yobe militia shot and killed a man for resisting abduction in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). No further details.

On 20 October 2023, some private security guards attached to the CEO of the Awka Capital Territory Development Agency assaulted and wounded a taxi driver at the UNIZIK Junction in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). They accused the cab driver of overtaking their convoy.

On 21 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the zonal coordinator of the SDP at his residence in Aja-Odi Agojeju, coded to Agojeju (Ofu, Kogi) and beat him up. The victim's house was looted and destroyed while his vehicle was vandalized. The party's director of communication claimed that the victim was in a coma.
On 21 October 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two commercial drivers as they were retuning to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari). One other driver was shot in his both eyes and taken to the hospital.

On 21 October 2023, IPOB militants engaged policemen and operatives of the Neighborhood watch in an armed clash in Igbele village (Igbo Eze North, Enugu) coded to Enugu-Ezike. One militant was killed, others fled with varying degrees of bullet wounds, a number of items including a gun were recovered from the murdered militant.

On 21 October 2023, policemen beat up a woman into coma at the Agbarho community (Ughelli North, Delta) and wounded her husband. A child of the victims claimed that they were attacked while searching for their domestic helper, the details of the reason are unclear.
On 21 October 2023, the Sokoto militia killed two people in Sakkwai village (Tangaza, Sokoto). They also abducted an unspecified number of people.
On 21 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person in the Jekadafari area in Gombe (Gombe). The group left with the victim's phone, money and other valuables.

On 21 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants attacked and shot at customs operatives at their office in Geidam town (Geidam, Yobe). One operative was killed, the others fled. The militants set the customs patrol van, a generating set and part of the building ablaze. According to other sources, the Customs claimed to have repelled the militants.
On 21 October 2023, ISWAP fighters abducted seven women from a farm around Bulamalumbe Kanuri and Gulwa villages, coded to Gulwa (Ngala, Borno). No further details.
On 21 October 2023, the Nigerian troops ambushed and killed ten ISWAP fighters around Charlie 3, along the Banki-Bama road, coded to Bama (Bama, Bornu). No further details.
On 21 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person while attacking Gazari village (Sabuwa, Katsina). They also injured one person and abducted nineteen others.

On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty policemen from his farm at Gidan-Idi village (Kurmi, Taraba) coded to Baissa. The abductee had gone to the farm with his workers who were taken hostage in his absence and replaced with him when he returned to the farm from running an errand.
On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person at Alu Oko, Ebge Egume, Aja-Odi, coded to Agojeju (Ofu, Kogi). No further details.

On 22 October 2023, the police and the NSVC raided a hideout of the Niger militia near Dogonruwa village, close to Kaliko (Wushishi, Niger). The police engaged the militia in a firefight. Three hostages were released. There were no fatalities.

On 22 October 2023, the police and the NSVC intercepted the Niger militia and engaged them in a gunfight around Mangoro village, coded to Gini (Muya, Niger). The police rescued eighty people abducted by the militia and returned them to their families. There were no fatalities.

On 22 October 2023, a Katsina militia that attacked civilians engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash in Dan Musa town (Dan-Musa, Katsina). Five persons including a policeman were killed; other sources report 9 killed, 10 to 12 others were wounded while 5 persons were abducted.

On 22 October 2023, a joint security team comprised of soldiers, policemen, a local defense militia, DSS and NSCDC engaged in an armed clash an unidentified armed group at Kanzanna forest (Bunza, Kebbi) coded to Tilli district where some victims were abducted by the group [coded separately]. Three abductees were rescued, one of the assailants was killed, several others escaped with bullet wounds.

On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a female lecturer from her residence at Angwan Jaba in Keffi (Keffi, Nassarawa). The abductee is a staff of the Nassarawa state university. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, the abductee was released on 25 October after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 22 October 2023, Nigerian Navy soldiers engaged in an armed clash with the security details [presumed policemen] in the convoy of the Kogi state governor near Kwali (Kwali, FCT) following the convoy's refusal to stop at a checkpoint. The state commissioner for information claimed that the soldiers were suspected to be assassins targeting the governor while the state governor denied the claims. The Nigerian police claimed that the convoy's unruliness was responsible for the clash, 4 soldiers and two of the governor's aides were wounded.

On 22 October 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted five civilians as they were returning from a market in Jere town (Kagarko, Kaduna). One of the victims who was a nursing mother was released with her child a few meters away from where they were abducted. There are no reports on ransom demands for the other abductees.

Around 22 October 2023 (week of), troops of sector 4 of Operation Udo Ka II killed an IPOB militant at a checkpoint in Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo) after he attempted to escape arrest. Two live ammunitions, a motorcycle, a bag containing charms and one mobile phone were recovered by the troops.

On 22 October 2023, the Nigerian troops and CJTF engaged ISWAP in a firefight after the latter attacked a CJTF position in Ngala (Ngala, Borno). ISWAP fighters withdrew and left a CJTF injured. There were no fatalities.
On 22 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife and daughter of a university professor from their residence in Lafia (Lafia, Nassarawa). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 23 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed three IDPs who went to fish at a stream in Gbange/Tomgov ward. Location coded to Agagbe (Gwer West, Benue) where the victims left to go fishing.

On 23 October 2023, a Sokoto militia was repelled by locals presumed to have been a local defense militia when they attacked Tukandu village in Sakkwai ward (Tangaza, Sokoto). Two persons including one of the assailants were killed, the residents fled due to fear of a reprisal attack.

On 23 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people along the Warri-Sapele Expressway, coded to Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The Nigerian security later raided the abductors' hideout in Ibada Elume and rescued the hostage.

On 23 October 2023, the combined security forces, including the military and the police, supported by the local militia, clashed with an unidentified armed group in Ibada Elume, coded to Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The armed group had abducted two people on the highway, coded separately. The security launched a rescue operation and rescued the two hostages. There were no fatalities.
On 23 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person when raiding Garin Waziri village, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina). They abducted five women.
On 23 October 2023, the Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of people while raiding Shalla village, coded to Isa (Isa, Sokoto). The victims included women and children.

On 24 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two people at a fuel station in Bagoma Dam, coded to Bagoma (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Three other people sustained varying degrees of injuries, one of the murdered victims was a local defense militia member who is presumed to have been unarmed at the time of the attack.
On 24 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed six civilians when they invaded Dan Sadau town (Maru, Zamfara) in large numbers and shot sporadically. Four other persons sustained serious bullet wounds.

On 24 October 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed two people after blocking the Yan Tumaki-Dan Musa road, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina). The militia abducted an unspecified number of travellers.

On 24 October 2023, the Nigerian troops clashed with Kaduna militia while on clearance operation around the Dogon daji-Saulawa area in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The soldiers engaged the militia in a firefight, forcing them to scamper for safety. They recovered a G3 rifle, 16 motorcycles, two locally-made guns and a phone. There were no fatalities.

On 24 October 2023, a Sokoto militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers when they invaded Tukandu village in Sakkwai ward (Tangaza, Sokoto) for a reprisal attack after they were repelled the previous day [coded separately]. Several militiamen were killed, one soldier was wounded, 12 motorcycles and three rifles were recovered from the assailants. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 24 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed one person after blocking the Maidabino-Dan Musa Road, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina). No further details.

On 24 October 2023, a joint team of soldiers and DSS operatives engaged a Boko Haram militant in an armed clash when they raided his residence at Gbaganu area of Minna (Minna, Niger). The militant fled; 150 AK 47 rifles, 20 rocket propellers and 3000 live ammunition were recovered by the security agents, occupants of the house including women and children were arrested.

Around 24 October 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia abducted 23 civilians from Kudiri village in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna) and four of the abductees escaped about 2 weeks later. A ransom of 20 million naira which was later brought down to 10 million and three bags of rice was demanded with a 7-day ultimatum for the release of the remaining 19 abductees.
On 24 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base in Wajiroko (Damboa, Borno) with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher. They claimed neither damage nor fatalities.

On 24 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked worshippers at a mosque in Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The Imam and another worshipper were killed, many others were wounded. Other sources report that three persons were killed, two others were seriously wounded and that the assailants who were dressed in military uniform emerged from Kamuku forest and were en route to Tegina axis of Niger state.

On 24 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man and wounded his wife as they were on their way to their farm in Goh village (Gwer West, Benue) coded Naka. The victims were attacked with machetes.
On 24 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three travelers along Makurdi-Naka road (Makurdi, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 October 2023, an armed group affiliated with the APC attacked and shot at a supporter of the SDP at his residence in Dekina town (Dekina, Kogi) over his refusal to support the APC governorship candidate. The victim was critically wounded.

On 25 October 2023, the Nigerian troops of 159 Battalion engaged in a firefight with Boko Haram(JAS) in Jororo (Geidam, Yobe). The troops launched an onslaught following the intelligence received about Boko Haram's harassment of the civilians in the village, coded separately. The army killed two Boko Haram fighters and recovered two AK-47 rifles and two Motorcycles.
On 25 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a commercial motorcyclist and stole his motorcycle at a quarry along Obaagun-Iba road (Ifelodun, Osun).
On 25 October 2023, the Katsina militia killed five people in the Tsagengeni village, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). They also injured four people and looted an unspecified number of cattle.

Around 25 October 2023 (as reported), troops of 146 battalion of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash along Karetu-Wulgo axis (Mobbar, Borno). Nine militants were killed, while others escaped with gunshot wounds.
On 25 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one person while attacking a Christian community in Kudbe, around the western Chibok-western Askira area, coded to Askira (Askira Uba, Borno).

On 25 October 2023, the troops of the 27 Task Force Brigade repelled the ISWAP's attempt to overrun Buni Gari (Gujba, Yobe). The militia, in large numbers on motorcycles and two gun trucks, opened fire indiscriminately, but the Nigerian troops responded with firepower and forced them to withdraw. There were no fatalities.

On 25 October 2023, the Yansakai militia killed a policeman (assumed on duty) in Kaura Namoda (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). The militia accused the police officer of being a snitch for other marauding militia groups.
On 25 October 2023, the Taraba militia attacked the Mayo Lope community, coded to Lau (Lau, Taraba). Casualties unspecified. No further details.

On 26 October 2023, suspected Fulani militiamen killed two people and injured another along the Benue - Nasarawa road near Ortese, coded to Ndzorov (Guma, Benue). The militia staged an ambush at the same place the following day and killed another person, coded separately. There were two fatalities.
On 26 October 2023, the Taraba militia abducted six people in Yorro (Yorro, Taraba). The armed group raided the community at night and took away the hostages. No further details.

On 26 October 2023, the Nigerian soldiers and the police engaged the Katsina militia in a firefight after the militia invaded Domawa village, coded to Dunya (Dan-Musa, Katsina). A soldier was killed, and the police Armoured Personnel Carrier (APC) was vandalized. An unspecified number of the militia was killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. Coded four fatalities.

Around 26 October 2023 (week of), troops of Operation Udo Ka II conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at Orsumoghu forest (Ihiala, Anambra). Two militants were killed, others fled with gunshot injuries, a locally made IED and IED launchers, military boots and belt among other items were recovered.

On 26 October 2023, the troops of Sector 2 Operation Hadin Kai clashed with Boko Haram (JAS) Bajingo village, coded to Babban Gida (Tarmua, Yobe). Several Boko Haram fighters were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 26 October 2023, the troops of Sector 2 Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and killed four Boko Haram (JAS) at Kurnawa (Tarmua, Yobe). Two soldiers sustained injuries during the encounter. The army recovered one AK47 rifle and two motorcycles. Several Boko Haram fighters were also killed in Bajingo, coded separately.

On 26 October 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia attacked and killed a civilian who was a local from Yache (Yala, Cross River) on his farm as claimed by another Yache resident. Other persons claimed that the assailants were escorted by soldiers, but the soldiers denied the claims and accused Yache locals of frustrating the peace talks between both groups. The attack is related to a lingering conflict over payment of royalties between Tiv and Yache locals.

On 26 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed and beheaded a member of AVS in Isiahia village, coded to Osisioma (Osisioma, Abia). The vigilante member and the police had gone to arrest a suspect when they came under fire from the armed group. The police fled when the group overpowered them. Another report claimed the militia ambushed a police team attached to the Rapid Response Squad (RRS) while on stop-and-search duty. The police denied the report that one of them was dead.

On 26 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have damaged a Nigerian Army's vehicle with a hand grenade while attacking a checkpoint in Ajir (Damboa, Borno). They backed up their claim with the picture of a disabled/captured CS/VP3 Bigfoot MRAP vehicle. There was no fatalities claim.
On 26 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with CJTF in Ajir (Damboa, Borno). They claimed CJTF retreated, and they seized their motorbike. There was no fatality claim.

On 26 October 2023, a Zamfara militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers and policemen who repelled the militia in Maru (Maru, Zamfara). Before the arrival of the security operatives, the militia had invaded the Emir's (King) palace and killed one of his guards when they didn't meet him at home. They shot killed the other three victims within the town. The militia damaged the Emir's car with gunshots. Other sources report that 6 persons were killed and 14 others were wounded across different locations in the town.

On 26 October 2023, an unidentified armed group of up to 20 engaged in an armed clash with policemen when they invaded an estate at Kuchibiyi in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). One resident who was part of a search team was shot and wounded in the hand, three other residents were abducted from their apartments.

On 27 October 2023, suspected Fulani militiamen laid an ambush and killed one person along the Benue - Nasarawa road near Ortese, coded to Ndzorov (Guma, Benue). The attack was the second within two days. There was one fatality in the second attack.

Around 27 October 2023 (between 26 October - 29 October), a Tiv ethnic militia wounded at least nine civilians in Yache (Yala, Cross) as claimed by other Yache locals who added that the victims were abducted and they sustained bullet wounds. The attack is related to a lingering conflict over payment of royalties between Tiv and Yache locals.
On 27 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian at Okpokwu ward (Obi, Benue) coded to Obarike-Ito.

Around 27 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed the former local government chairman of Ukum LGA after they abducted him from his residence on 23 September and demanded a ransom, some of which was paid. Location coded to Sankera (Ukum, Benue) where the victim was abducted from.

On 27 October 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot three students at the Ugbowo campus of the University of Benin, Benin City (Oredo, Edo). One of the victims was shot dead, and the second victim could not be accounted for. The third person sustained gun injuries and was taken to the hospital for treatment. There is one fatality.

On 27 October 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji responded to a distress call and engaged a Zamfara militia that attacked civilians in an armed clash at Nasarawa town in Maru LGA (Zamfara). Three people were killed before the troops arrived, while the clash lasted for several hours.

Around 27 October 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a soldier (presumed to be off duty) at the Akparata axis of Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The soldier was part of the contingent deployed to manage inter-communal clashes in the area. The State government issued an ultimatum to the warring communities to provide the soldier alive by 26 October 2023.

On 28 October 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian, abducted the district head of Ruwan Rana (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and five other persons when they invaded the village and shot sporadically. An unspecified number of cattle were rustled, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 28 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman her two daughters and their house maid from their residence in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The maid was later released, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 28 October 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Ora community (Ifelodun, Kwara) when they invaded the town and shot sporadically. One woman was killed, two others were abducted. The abductees were female POS operators, the husband of one of the abductees was wounded when he attempted to rescue her.

On 28 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army base in Miringa (Biu, Borno). The militia forced the soldiers to retreat and seized two SUVs, a heavy machine gun, a light machine gun, and ammunition. There were no fatalities.

On 28 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed one soldier when they ambushed a Nigerian Army patrol team along the Katafila-Mararaba road, Bama LGA, coded to Bama (Bama, Borno). They claimed the soldiers retreated.
On 29 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two persons from their house in Gulum (Yorro, Taraba). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 29 October 2023, a Kaduna militia wounded two civilians and abducted one person when they attacked Old Tabanni, coded as Tabanni (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The residents had put up a resistance [means not stated] in an attempt to prevent the attack.

On 29 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest from his residence at Sarkin-Kudu (Ibi, Taraba). There are no reports on ransom demands, the priest was released the following day, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 29 October 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia and Yache communal militia engaged in an armed clash in Yache (Yala, Cross River) following a lingering dispute over payment of royalties to Yache locals by Tiv settlers. At least 20 persons most of whom were women and children were killed, many sustained varying degrees of machete cuts and gunshot wounds, houses on both sides were set ablaze.

On 29 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia numbering 10 attacked civilians and killed three people at Tse Gamber in Sengev council ward (Gwer West, Benue). One other person was taken away by the assailants. The attack took place in the morning, while another council ward was attacked in the evening of the same day [coded separately].

On 29 October 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Camp Nagi in Mbachohon council ward (Gwer West, Benue). Three persons were killed and several others were wounded, the attack took place in the evening, while another council ward was attacked in the morning of the same day [coded separately].
On 29 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with CJTF and killed one of their members in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They seized one rifle and five motorbikes and forced the CJTF to retreat.
On 29 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Unguwan Dorowa Bakhira settlement in Maro community (Kajuru, Kaduna). A couple and the only teacher in the community were killed.

On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed a policeman on his farm in Bama town (Bama, Borno) and stole his rifle. The policeman was also stripped off his uniform and his corpse was left in only shorts.
On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants trailed a chief Imam to his house and killed him in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). The militants proceeded to set the victim's Islamic books ablaze.

On 30 October 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Garin Moddibo town, coded to nearby Sunkani (Ardo Kola, Taraba). The monarch's wife, son and four others were abducted before the assailants proceeded to two neighboring villages where four other people including a nursing mother were abducted.

On 30 October 2023, policemen fired teargas and water cannons at the governor of Rivers state in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) following a crisis over claims of plans to impeach him. The governor also claimed that policemen shot at him while he was on the way to the state house of assembly to assess the level of damage following an explosion at the building. The police spokesperson in the state claimed that the policemen were unaware of the governor's presence and that the policemen did not deliberately shoot at him.

On 30 October 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed three soldiers and wounded two others after attacking the Nigerian Army base at Mussa (Askira Uba, Borno). They forced other soldiers to retreat and captured two rifles and ammunition.
On 30 October 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram militants abducted two hunters at Makinta Kururi village in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). No further details.

On 30 October 2023, Boko Haram/ISWAP militants attacked residents at Ngurokayya village, coded to nearby Kusur (Geidam, Yobe). Some sources report that the militants shot and killed 17 young men, wounded 4 others as punition for tax evasion, other sources report that the town was set ablaze while other residents fled to safety and that the other reason for the attack was that the villagers were accused by the militants of giving security operatives information.

On 31 October 2023, a local defense militia in collaboration with hunters ambushed and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Jajuwal village in Toro LGA (Bauchi). One member of the armed group was killed, an unspecified number of residents were abducted, some of whom were rescued by the local defense militia.

Around 31 October 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadarin Daji raided the hideouts of a Zamfara militia that was led by Dogo Gide at Dan Sadau, Mai Tunkuya and Babban Doka (Maru, Zamfara). The hideouts were destroyed, Dogo Gide fled with serious injuries, weapons were also recovered by the troops. Fatalities are unknown.

On 31 October 2023, an unidentified armed group of four beat up the gate keeper at a radio station in Idofian town (Ifelodun, Kwara). The assailants proceed to rob the other staff of the station, and also stole the network's cables and equipment.

On 31 October 2023, Nigerian troops stationed at Malekachi who were on a routine patrol engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Sangeko forest (Danko, Kebbi) coded to Wasagu. The group's leader Mainasara and two other members of the group were killed; five others who are suspected to be members of the group were arrested, two motorcycles were recovered and destroyed by the troops.

On 31 October 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Unguwan Baka community in Agunu ward, coded to Agunu Dutse (Kachia, Kaduna). One local was killed, two others were wounded and 25 people were abducted.

On 31 October 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked and shot at policemen who were conducting stop and search about 2km away from Tsafe town (Tsafe, Zamfara). Three policemen were killed; five others and the driver of the patrol van fled into the bush, the driver was later found unconscious while the other five were missing.

On 31 October 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians along Naka-Makurdi highway (Gwer West, Benue). The abductees were rescued when soldiers who were on a patrol met the abductors and pursued them into the bush, leading the abductors to flee and abandon the victims.
On 1 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 14 civilians from Mayo Dassa (Yorro, Taraba). The abductees were released at an unspecified date, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 1 September 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed two civilians at Tashin Dauda village in Ikara LGA (Kaduna). The victims who included a driver were killed by the assailants who were fleeing from an attack in Saya-Saya village [coded separately].

On 1 September 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked worshippers at a mosque and killed five persons in Saya-Saya village (Ikara, Kaduna). Other sources report that seven persons were killed including the leader of the local defense militia who some sources assume was the target. Police confirmed the attack and claimed five persons were killed and two others wounded.

On 1 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The woman was taken when she was returning home from an interview. The victim had expressed concern about being followed by some men dressed in police uniforms before she was abducted. No ransom has been demanded by her abductors.

On 1 September 2023, ISWAP attacked the Nigerian military camp in Ladari, located in the northern part of Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). The militiamen claimed to have killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. They made away with a motorbike and ammunition. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 1 September 2023, ISWAP clashed with CJTF near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno). One CJTS member was killed, and others were wounded in the clash.

On 2 September 2023, operatives of Operation Restore Peace comprised of soldiers, policemen and other security agencies engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Shande village in Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). The clash lasted for over two hours, scores of members of the group were killed, five abductees sustained injuries and 11 others were rescued. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 2 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the military checkpoint in Pulka (Gwoza, Bornu) forcing the soldiers to withdraw. The attackers burned the checkpoint after the withdrawal of the soldiers.

On 2 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his residence at El-Rufai estate in Bwari (Bwari, FCT) after scaling the fence of the house to gain entrance. The assailants also shot sporadically to scare other residents.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified armed group in large numbers attacked and abducted many civilians from farming communities around Garba-Chebe in Bali LGA (Taraba). The attack lasted for hours and the abductees included women and children.
On 3 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed a farmer on his cassava farm at Chembe village (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a businesswoman when they attacked her residence in Agbeku (Ifelodun, Kwara). The victim's motorcycle was stolen by the assailants, the town's traditional ruler claimed that four suspects were arrested by the police.

On 3 September 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a man in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The victim who was reported as mentally ill was shot at, stoned, stabbed and attacked with a cutlass by the assailants before they fled. Other sources report that the victim was dismembered.
On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four persons who were returning from the farm at Itapaji (Ikole, Ekiti).

On 4 September 2023, the police opened fire and injured Shiia members while trying to disrupt their procession along Zaria-Panbegwa Road (Zaria, Kaduna). The Shiite members were on their annual Arbaeen symbolic trek when they were fired and gassed by the police. Arbaeen Trek is a Shiite religious practice involving mass trek. Many members got injured as they scampered for safety.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with policemen at Ogbeke-Nike along Ugwogo-Nike-Opi-Nsukka road (Enugu East, Enugu). Two of the assailants were killed; others escaped with gunshot wounds, one rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered by the policemen.
On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people from Dunami Estate, Angwan Dadi, Nyanya (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The abductors asked for no ransom.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from his residence in the Area C axis of Nyanya (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory). The abductors demanded a 25 million naira ransom to release the hostage.
On 4 September 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). Three militia members were killed.

Around 4 September 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hakorin Damisa IV in collaboration with policemen and hunters engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and killed five of them at Tahuwa community, coded to Jos (Jos North, Plateau). Rifles and ammunition were recovered.

On 4 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian when they invaded Bodo community (Gonaka, Rivers). The assailants fled into a nearby bush, other sources report that the attack was linked to a chieftaincy tussle between two factions in the community.

On 4 September 2023, Boko Haram/ISWAP fighters launched an attack on MNJTF in Ladari near Gamboru (Ngala, Borno). The militants retreated following a fierce fire exchange with the Joint Task Force. No fatalities were reported.
Around 5 September 2023 (week of), a Kaduna militia abducted over 44 civilians along the Kaduna-Birnin Gwari highway (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 5 September 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kuriga Wusasa, coded to Wusasa (Zaria, Kaduna) and rescued three abductees. The militia fled into the bush and abandoned the abductees. No casualties.

On 5 September 2023, a Katsina militia shot and killed six men and a woman and abducted twelve others in the Doka community near Sabuwa (Sabuwa, Katsina). The Doka community was reported to have been impenetrable to the militia after their numerous attempts until the last onslaught. They rustled cows and many domestic animals. The police reported six people were killed and five injured.

On 5 September 2023, the Nigerian troop ambushed ISWAP fighters and killed twelve in Konduga LGA, coded to Gabchari (Konduga, Borno). The army recovered five AK rifles, two locally manufactured rifles, 2 Dane guns, ammunition, four motorbikes, and three daggers.

On 5 September 2023, a group of people mobbed and assaulted a woman in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti) over the allegation that she stole tubers of yams. The victim sustained various degrees of injury. The mobs stripped her naked, recorded her nude video and shared it on the internet. The police arrested two of the perpetrators.

Around 5 September 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with CJTF clashed with presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in Bula Marwa in Banki (Bama, Borno). The military killed many of the militants. The military discovered an IED at the militants' camp. Unknown casualties coded as 3.

On 6 September 2023, troops of sector 3 of the MNJTF engaged Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] in an armed clash at Dugushewa village (Magumeri, Borno). One militant was killed, one rifle, ammunition and other items were recovered.

On 6 September 2023, policemen and hunters foiled an attempted abduction by an unidentified armed group of five at Jangra village in Gombi LGA (Adamawa). One of the assailants was killed, and others escaped with gunshot wounds.

On 7 September 2023, Benue militia shot and killed two members of the Community Volunteer Guards in Ugba (Logo, Benue). They also shot and killed a woman at Abeda-Shitile on the same day, coded separately. Many people were injured in the attack.
On 7 September 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in conjunction with CJTF killed six Boko Haram fighters [JAS faction] while raiding their camp in Garin Ba'aba near Bama (Bama, Borno).
On 7 September 2023, Benue militia shot and killed a woman in Abeda-Shitile near Ugba (Logo, Benue) after killing two community volunteers in Ugba, coded separately.

Around 7 September 2023 (week of), a Fulani militia raped five women on their farms in Ekakpamre (Ughelli South, Delta) as claimed by the women in the community who embarked on a protest [coded separately].

On 7 September 2023, DSS officers shot and wounded a tailor in Garki Ultramodern Market, Garki (Abuja Municipal, Federal Capital Territory), while trying to arrest him for failure to deliver a sewing job given to him by a lady. The lady invited the security operatives to effect the arrest, but they shot and wounded him. In the process, a stray bullet hit and injured a sales girl in her shop. The shootings drew the anger of the people who later mobbed the security agents, coded separately. A source reported that the tailor was shot dead, but other sources reported that victims were injured and taken to the hospital for treatment.
On 7 September 2023, suspected herders attacked farmers in Ungwan Rimi and Ungwa Magaji, coded to Kaduna South (Kaduna South, Kaduna). No further details.
On 7 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 19 civilians from Bwari (Bwari, FCT). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 7 September 2023, an unidentified armed group opened fire on the operatives of the Nigeria Customs Service at their checkpoint in Umuikaa Junction near Okpuala-Ngwa (Isiala Ngwa North, Abia). The armed group burned the operational patrol van of the customs service. They shot and injured a commercial bus passenger that ran into them. The whereabouts of the customs personnel are unknown. A source claimed one of them was shot and escaped with injuries. The military stationed nearby intervened and dislodged them from the checkpoint.

On 8 September 2023, a Kaduna militia set on fire St. Raphael Parish in Fadan Kamantan (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) killing one seminarian. Other seminarians, except the deceased, escaped from the building before it was set ablaze by the militia.
On 8 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have raided a Nigerian Army checkpoint in Kawuri (Konduga, Borno), forcing the soldiers to desert their position. Unspecified equipment was confiscated.

On 8 September 2023, ISWAP killed three people and burned their vehicle in a village close to Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). The victims included a religious leader, a village head and a youth working on his farm. However, ISWAP referred to them as spies. They claimed to have killed them with machine guns and burned their vehicle.

On 8 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her two daughters at Galadima district, coded to nearby Kabusa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded, it was later reduced to 50 million then 10 million before 2.840 million naira was eventually paid and the abductees were released on 9 September.

On 8 September 2023, the Police clashed with the Icelanders cult militia while raiding their hideout in Ahoada East LGA, Ahoada (Ahoada, Rivers). The militia overpowered the police who later retreated except the Divisional Police Officer (DPO). The DPO was caught and taken away by the militia before they butchered him. The cult group posted a video where they chanted victory songs and displayed the chartered and decomposing remains of the DPO.

On 9 September 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted over 50 civilians around Darita forest while they were on transit to Bagega (Anka, Zamfara) for the weekly market. One of the abductees who escaped claimed that the militiamen were followers of Halilu Buzu and that the abduction was a response to the government's closure of the Bagega cattle market.

On 9 September 2023, policemen trailed an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Umuota village in Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). One abductee was rescued, one of the assailants was killed, two were arrested and others fled with bullet wounds.

On 9 September 2023, an unidentified armed group that was wearing masks killed three civilians in Agbada Nenwe, coded to Nenwe (Aninri, Enugu). The victims were located and killed at their various houses.
On 9 September 2023, Boko Haram abducted two farmers from a farm in Galameri, coded to Gongulong (Jere, Borno).
On 9 September 2023, a Niger militia abducted five civilians from Kakihun in Mariga LGA (Niger). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 September 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along Anka-Bagega road (Anka, Zamfara). Five abductees were rescued by the troops, casualties are unknown.
Around 9 September 2023 (between 8 - 10 September), an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Kwari Kwasa village (Maiyama, Kebbi). Two persons were killed, six others were abducted.

Around 9 September 2023 (as reported), soldiers beat up an pregnant woman at Ibaa town (Emohua, Rivers) when she went to the army base to inquire about her son's whereabouts. The victim was made to sit on the floor and other women protested over the incident which they claimed was against their culture [coded separately]. The army denied the attack.

On 9 September 2023, the hybrid forces of CJTF and hunters militia shot and killed a Boko Haram [JAS faction] militant in Bazamri (Konduga, Borno). They recovered two carbines from the Boko Haram fighter suspected to have come from Gaizuwa.
On 9 September 2023, former Boko Haram fighters attacked and killed five people in Jege village (Gwoza, Borno).
On 9 September 2023, ISWAP fighters abducted two people and injured one with a matchet in Jodiri village coded to Banki (Bama, Borno). The militants killed one of the hostages.
On 9 September 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two persons from Marke village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 9 September 2023, a Katsina militia abducted 13 civilians from Kuki village (Dutsinma, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 9 September 2023, an unidentified cult group killed a tailor apprentice in Lagos (Lagos Island, Lagos). The boy had gone to dispatch a sewn cloth when he was accused of being a spy to suspected armed robbers by the cultists who descended on him and beat him to death.

On 10 September 2023, a Tiv ethnic militia and a Yache communal militia engaged in an armed clash at Yache community (Yala, Cross River). The clash was a result of a reprisal after a mob of Tiv locals killed one Yache local [coded separately]. 7 persons were killed, 10 others including women were wounded and 15 houses were set ablaze.

On 10 September 2023, a Fulani militia killed 10 civilians when they attacked Kulben village (Mangu, Plateau). Many other locals were wounded and several houses were destroyed by the assailants who eventually fled the area, other sources report 11 fatalities.

On 10 September 2023, a policeman shot into the air and killed one person who was hit by a stray bullet from the shot at a palliative distribution center in Rijau LGA (Niger). One boy was also wounded, the assailant shot into the air in a bid to keep people in line when the orderliness of the queue was distorted.

On 10 September 2023, policemen invaded the hideout of Icelanders and engaged them in an armed at Odumude forest (Ahoada West, Rivers) coded to Akinima as claimed by the police commissioner. Four Icelanders were killed, others escaped with gunshot injuries. The clash was related to the murder of a policeman by the same assailants.

On 10 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman who is presumed to have been off-duty and a woman at Mile 6 area of Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The wife and daughter of the policeman were also abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources do not report the male victim to be a policeman, and that he was wounded not killed.

On 10 September 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot and killed two members of a rival militia while they were drinking at a pub in Ilesa town (Ilesha West, Osun). Other sources report that the attack was between members of Aiye and Eiye cult militias.
On 10 September 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one civilian and looted cattle from Bamana community (Goronyo, Sokoto).
On 10 September 2023, Nigerian soldiers killed an unknown number of ISWAP fighters in Goniri (Gujba, Borno). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

Around 10 September 2023 (as reported), Nigerian troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed some ISWAP fighters in Goniri (Gujba, Yobe). The presumed ISWAP fighters rode on two motorcycles and six bicycles when they clashed with the troops. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 10 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a presumed member of CJTF member in Benisheikh (Kaga, Borno). They claimed the victim was a militia member loyal to the Nigerian Army.

On 10 September 2023, security agents presumed to be policemen killed three civilians at Odimeneyi (Ahoada, Rivers) while they were in search of members of a cult militia who killed a policeman [coded separately]. The victims attempted to flee when they sighted the agent who shot at them.
On 11 September 2023, a vigilantes group clashed with five suspected abductors in the Bumgai community (Gujba, Yobe). A stray bullet hit and killed one person (presumed to be a bystander).

On 11 September 2023, the Nigerian military engaged in a firefight with some Zamfara militants who abducted four people in Bunkasau village near Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The abductors fled and abandoned their victims when they were overpowered by the military.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged a local defense militia in an armed clash at 1st Marine Gate (Warri South, Delta) coded to Warri. One local militia member was killed, the others fled due to superior fire from the assailants.

On 11 September 2023, policemen and hunters trailed an unidentified armed group to their hideout and engaged them in an armed clash in (Yola-South, Adamawa) coded to Tongare following the abduction of a woman from her residence. Two members of the armed group were killed, the abductee was rescued, guns charms, chains and mobile phones were recovered by the police.
On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and injured three vigilantes members in Nyibango Ward, Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The group abducted a woman in the process.
On 11 September 2023, suspected armed pastoralists killed three civilians when they attacked Opi-Agu community (Nsukka, Enugu) coded to Opi. An unspecified number of others were wounded.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a poet in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) while returning from Abuja after a performance. He was taken alongside other passengers and was taken to an unknown destination. The abductors demanded a 20 million naira ransom for his release.
On 11 September 2023, the Katsina Militia blocked the Batsari-Dutsin Ma road in Bakon Zabo, coded to Batsari (Batsari, Katsina) and abducted two people travelling on a motorcycle.

On 11 September 2023, cult members suspected to be the Aiye (Black Axe) confraternity shot and killed a transport worker at Ado community (Eti-Osa, Lagos). The victim was shot when he visited his mother-in-law with his wife. The killing was reported to be a reprisal attack, and his death raised tension over possible full-blown cult clashes in the area.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed six civilians when they attacked Mushy village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau). The victims included five pastoralists and a two-year old as claimed by the chairman of the Plateau state chapter of MACBAN.

On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted at least ten passengers around the Okene area (Okene, Kogi) while they were enroute to Lagos from Benue. The abductees were travelling in two buses owned by the Benue state government which later announced the release of 18 passengers and two drivers around 13 September, there are no reports on ransom payment.
On 11 September 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed two civilians at Umualumaku (Ehime Mbano, Imo). An unspecified number of persons were injured.

On 12 September 2023, armed pastoralists killed one local defense militia member and wounded two others in Dobi (Gwagwalada, FCT). The militiamen were attacked when they went to inspect a farm that was destroyed by the pastoralists' cattle and resulted in a clash between the pastoralists and farmers.

On 12 September 2023, the Nigerian military intercepted and engaged in a firefight with some Zamfara militias trying to escape with some rustled animals around Tsamiyar Gezozi coded to Anka (Anka, Zamfara). The militia were overpowered and fled. The Nigerian military recovered about 130 animals and handed them over to the state government. No fatalities were reported.

On 12 September 2023, ISWAP waylaid some motorists and abducted two drivers along the Bama-Banki road near Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno). They took the drivers away with two vehicles loaded with food items.

On 12 September 2023, about 17 suspected ISWAP fighters attacked the MNJTF troops stationed in Banki (Bama, Borno), attempting to infiltrate the town. The Nigerian and Cameroonian troops of the MNJTF repelled the onslaught. No fatalities were reported. The militia insisted and launched the second attack the following morning, coded separately.
On 12 September 2023, policemen beat up a young man at the Post Office in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara) after they accused him of being a suspected internet fraudster.
On 12 September 2023, the Katsina Militia abducted one person in Garhi village coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).
On 12 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of passengers along Oron road in Uyo LGA (Akwa Ibom).

On 12 September 2023, members of the NURTW and Lagos Park Management committee clashed at the union's headquarters in Garki (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The clash was related to a leadership tussle. One person was killed, several others were wounded and 23 male suspects were arrested by the police. Other sources report that the clash was between two NURTW factions.
On 12 September 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants abducted two people from the Dusuman community (Jere, Borno)
On 12 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted four people in Asara (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).

On 12 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (coded as bandits) clashed with vigilantes in the village of Gandaba, coded to the LGA, HQ, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). The militia members killed 1 and abducted three women, and burned down a mosque, shops, and three houses.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a female corp member in Eku (Ethiope East, Delta) while travelling to visit her fiance. The abductor demanded a 5 million naira ransom for her release.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group in large numbers abducted four persons from Maigemu district (Jos East, Plateau). The abductees included one clergyman and three others, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 13 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a Labor Party chieftain at a drinking joint in Amelechi, a village in the Akpukpa community near Onuaku Uturu (Isuikwuato, Abia). The armed group beheaded the victim and went away with his head.

On 13 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity militias clashed at different parts of Ilesa town (Ilesha, Osun). The clashes were reprisals for the killing of two persons on 10 September [coded separately]. Three persons were killed and the clashes occurred at Sabo/Irojo junction and Oke Omiru area.
On 13 September 2023, ISWP and Boko Haram (JAS) clashed around Baga (Kukawa, Borno). Four fishers were killed during the clash, and one of the belligerents seized 100 fishing boats from the fishers.

On 13 September 2023, suspected ISWAP fighters attacked the MNJTF troops stationed in Banki (Bama, Borno). The Nigerian and Cameroonian forces of the MNJTF repelled the attack and prevented the town from falling into the hands of the militia. No fatalities were reported.
On 13 September 2023, the Kaduna militia killed one person and injured twelve others in the Madaka area in Kachia (Kachia, Kaduna).
On 13 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 1 man in his home during an attack on Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto).

On 14 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 33 people in Alkaleri (Alkaleri, Bauchi). Other sources report that 39 persons were abducted, some of the abductees were businessmen who were returning from a market and a ransom of 50 million naira each was demanded. The police rescued the victims on the 15th of September 2023.

On 14 September 2023, Sokoto militia killed four people and abducted eighteen others in Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto). The attack forced the residents to flee the community, and the militia carted away some valuables, including livestock. The community people reported that thirty people were abducted, but the police claimed they were eleven. However, some of the abductees later escaped and returned to the community.

On 14 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a housewife and her brother-in-law in the Nasarawo area of Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The woman was abducted when her husband was not around. The armed group carted away the victims' mobile phones and 11, 000 naira.

On 14 September 2023, the Nigerian military, in collaboration with the police tactical team and the DSS, engaged the IPOB in a gun battle while trying to enter their shrine and hideout in Ekeagbebor Isu coded to Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi). The government forces killed a militant and arrested two while others escaped with various degrees of gun wounds. A police officer was shot in the leg and was taken to the hospital for treatment.

Around 14 September 2023 (as reported), Nigerian troops engaged in a gunfight with ISWAP fighters while trying to evacuate the corpse and the injured passengers from the IED explosion site in Karetu (Mobbar, Borno). The militants fled the scene when overpowered by the troops. No fatalities were reported.

On 14 September 2023, a stray bullet from an unidentified cult group hit and killed a female student of Nnamdi Azikiwe University at Miracle Junction, Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants aimed and shot at a tricycle operator but missed their target. A stray bullet hit the victim and killed her instantly.

Around 14 September 2023 (between 9 September - 19 September), ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed an unspecified number of farmers in Gwoza LGA (Borno). Ten farmers were killed in ten days, fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 15 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an off-duty police officer in Toro (Toro, Bauchi). The abductors stormed the victim's village and sporadically shot into the air before taking him away. The abductors are yet to demand a ransom.
On 15 September 2023, suspected IPOB/ESN members abducted one person along the Umuahia-Enugu Road, coded to Awgu (Agwu, Enugu).
On 15 September 2023, the Sokoto militia raided and abducted three people from Wurno town (Wurno, Sokoto). There were no fatalities reported.

On 15 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). About 20 persons were killed, 6 of whom were killed in a continuation on 17 September [coded separately]. Other sources report that many of the victims had nothing to do with the clash.

On 15 September 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Yankari forest, coded to Yankari National Park (Alkaleri, Bauchi). 10 members of the armed group were killed and 39 abductees who were abducted the previous day [coded separately] were rescued.

On 15 September 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians and abducted three others when they attacked Dogonnoma community (Kajuru, Kaduna). Other sources report that 15 people were killed, several others were wounded and 32 residents were abducted.

On 15 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a PDP chieftain in Ada (Boripe, Osun). The victim was shot dead by three men, pretending to be customers, when eating in his wife's shop.
On 15 September 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed two people in Birnin Tudu Community, coded to Talata Mafara (Talat Mafara, Zamfara).

Around 15 September 2023 (week of), two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash in Ilorin metropolis (Ilorin West, Kwara). The body of one student who was declared missing on 13 September was found on the streets on 17 September and was reported to have been mistakenly killed in the clash.

On 16 September 2023, a Kaduna militia engaged and overpowered a local defense militia at Maraban Rido, coded to nearby Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). One civilian was killed, a woman and three of her children were abducted.

On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group opened fire on the police in Isu Aniocha (Awka North, Anambra). The police were on a peacekeeping mission following a chieftaincy tussle in the community. The armed group invaded the community despite the police presence and fired shots sporadically, causing tension in the community. There were no fatalities.
On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of civilians along Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi road (Nsukka, Enugu). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 16 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed one person in Rumuodomaya (Obio, Rivers).

On 16 September 2023, ISWAP attacked a Nigerian army checkpoint in Mairari (Guzamala, Borno). The onslaught forced the soldiers to abandon the post and flee. The militia damaged four motorbikes and seized six others and ammunition before withdrawing. There were no fatalities.
On 16 September 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two women from Bakin Hanya Hamilate in Jan Tsauni village, Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina).

On 16 September 2023, a Niger militia killed two local defense militia members and a businessman who attempted to confront them during an attack in Pan Dongari (Rafi, Niger). An unspecified number of residents were abducted.

On 16 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed on civilian and wounded several others along Edem-Nrobo-Ezikolo-Abbi road (Uzo Uwani, Enugu). The assailants laid seige on the road for several hours.
On 17 September 2023, the Sokoto militia blocked the Wurno-Goronyo Road coded to Goronyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). They shot and injured one person and abducted many others.
On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the Evangelical Church of West Africa (ECWA) in Nuku, Maigemu (Jos East, Plateau). There was no fatalities or injuries.

On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted several passengers traveling in at least five vehicles on the Otukpo-Enugu expressway, coded to Okpoga (Okpokwu, Benue). One of the buses belonged to the Benue state transport company, other sources report that 15 passengers including the driver were abducted from the state owned company's bus and a ransom of 50 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million was demanded for an abductee who is a staff of the Nigerian Television Authority.

On 17 September 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). 6 persons including secondary school students were killed. Other sources report that many of the victims had nothing to do with the clash.

On 17 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted a catholic priest along Eke-Egede-Affa road (Udi, Enugu) while he was on the way back to his parish. There are no reports on ransom demands. Other sources report that the priest was abducted alongside 6 persons and that a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.

On 17 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian when they invaded the palace of the Olokanla at Okanla community (Irepodun, Osun) coded to Ilobu.
