The assailants who were up to 20 set the victim's body ablaze in a car and also burnt the palace, the target who was absent during the attack claimed that it was likely related to a land dispute.

On 17 September 2023, a joint task force of security operatives presumed to have comprised of soldiers and policemen engaged a Niger militia in an armed clash in a village near Pan Dongari (Rafi, Niger). 52 militiamen including six informants who lived in the community were killed.

On 18 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man and his daughter along Afon road (Asa, Kwara) while they were returning from the farm. The police claimed that the girl was rescued, there are no reports on ransom demands for the man.
On 18 September 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up one civilian and abducted two others from Koko town (Koko, Kebbi). A ransom of 15 million naira was demanded.

On 18 September 2023, IPOB/ESN militants who were enforcing a sit-in order engaged soldiers and policemen who were on patrol in an armed clash at Ezioha (Agwu, Enugu). Three militants were killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, arms and ammunition were recovered from the killed militants. A group called Intersociety claimed that the military's claims were false and that the persons who were killed were youths from the community that were labelled as militants.

On 18 September 2023, soldiers on a clearance operation engaged IPOB/ ESN militants in an armed clash at their hideouts in Igboro forest, between Arochukwu LGA and Ohafia LGA (Abia). Three militants were killed, and several of their camps were destroyed, weapons, ammunition and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 18 September 2023, the Zamfara militia attacked the Mayaba and Mai Kogo communities, coded to Bungudu (Bungudu, Zamfara). They killed four people and injured two others.

On 18 September 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Jesse-Igueleba road (Ethiope West, Delta). Four members of the group were killed, one rifle, one magazine and 25 rounds of ammunition were recovered by the policemen.
On 18 September 2023, Zamfara militia shot and killed a man and his wife along the Jengeme-Ruwan Kongo Road in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara).
Around 18 September 2023 (week of), Boko Haram/ISWAP abducted six persons, including two monarchs in the Damboa LGA, coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno).

On 19 September 2023, three naval ratings together with some other persons beat up three civilians at their residence in Egbo quarters of Uwheru (Ughelli North, Delta) over a land dispute. The ratings fled, while four persons were arrested in connection with the attack.

Around 19 September 2023 (week of), a presumed Sokoto militia killed and displaced many civilians most of whom were farmers at villages in Kebbi and Sokoto states. The villages affected in Kebbi include Zawaini Zawaini, Jangargari and Jaja, coded to Birnin-Kebbi (Birnin Kebbi, Kebbi). Many houses and shops were set ablaze, many fatalities coded as 10, split across two events and recorded as 5.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot a Fulani woman bathing in her bathroom in the Oke Akure area of Iba (Ifelodun, Osun). The victim was taken to the hospital and died on 21 September 2023. The victim was a nursing mother who left a three-month-old baby behind.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the Madaki of Pavu village in Kuje area council (FCT) when they invaded that area and also abducted nine others. The murdered victim who was the second in command to the village head was killed when he attempted to escape.

On 19 September 2023, ISWAP killed one of its members at Ajikur in Damboa LGA (Borno) over diversion of funds. The militant was sent to buy food stuff for the group but diverted the funds for personal use, he was tied up for two hours before he was slaughtered.

Around 19 September 2023 (week of), a presumed Sokoto militia killed and displaced many civilians most of whom were farmers at villages in Sokoto and Kebbi states. Karani village and three others were affected in Sokoto, coded to Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto). Many houses and shops were set ablaze, many fatalities coded as 10, split across two events and recorded as 5.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor in Ogaminana (Adavi, Kogi). The armed group seized him on his way home from Victory Hospital-Annex, Ogaminana. No ransom was demanded.

On 19 September 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed security agents of a joint task force comprised of soldiers, policemen and NSCDC officials at Ekenku in Umualumaku (Ehime Mbano, Imo). The agents were travelling in two patrol vans which were set ablaze, 8 of them were killed and set ablaze.
On 19 September 2023, ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants killed an unspecified number of farmers in Gwoza LGA (Borno). Ten farmers were killed in ten days, fatalities split across 3 events coded as 3.

Around 20 September 2023 (as reported), Kebbi communal militia abducted nine farmers from their farmlands in Tanga-ran village coded to Ribah (Danko, Kebbi). The military and the vigilantes rescued them in Lugga under Ayu District.

Around 20 September 2023 (as reported), the Nigerian troop killed four members of the Kebbi communal militia in Bakin Gulbi village coded to Ribah (Danko, Kebbi). The troop recovered weapons and rescued three kidnapped persons.

On 20 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of people from a commercial bus and a car in Ijagbe (Mopa-Muro, Kogi). The people were abducted after their vehicles were waylaid by the militia.
On 20 September 2023, Boko Haram (JAS) attacked the Nigerian military in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). They killed one soldier and injured two others. They seized a rifle from the Nigerian soldiers.
On 20 September 2023, the Sokoto Militia killed three people in Sabon Gari Dole, coded to Goronyo (Goronyo, Sokoto). They abducted an unspecified number of people from the village.

On 20 September 2023, the Nigerian troop and the vigilante group ambushed and killed 21 Kebbi communal militia in Tudun Bichi coded to Kainya (Danko, Kebbi). When ambushed and eliminated, the militia crossed into Kebbi through Mariga in Niger State. Another source reported that 17 militia members were killed, while two residents died. Fatality coded as 19. Arms, ammunition and motorcycles were recovered from the militia.

Around 20 September 2023 (as reported), Kebbi communal militia killed Marafan Mai Inuwa and abducted some people under Kanya District near Kainya (Danko, Kebbi). The military rescued the hostages after killing the militia, coded separately.

On 20 September 2023, an armed group suspected to be Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed three IDPs on their farm in Agagbe (Gwer West, Benue). Some pastoralists had displaced the victims before taking refuge in the camp. The victims' bodies were recovered from the farms.

On 20 September 2023, an unidentified armed group macheted and killed a man in Nsirimo community around Apumuri (Umuahia South, Abia). The victim was killed at night, and his body was discovered by a villager while fetching water.

On 20 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four people in Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). The Anambra Vigilante Group intercepted the abductors and released the hostages (coded separately).

On 20 September 2023, the Anambra Vigilante Group intercepted some abductors and killed one in Onitsha (Onisha North). The group had abducted four people before the vigilante intercepted them and rescued the victims. The rescue operation took place in two different locations in Onitsha. An AK-47 rifle, a pistol and three cars were recovered from the abductors.

On 20 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed two police officers in an ambush along the Udi-Ozalla Road, coded to Ozalla (Nkanu West, Enugu). The police team was on a routine patrol when the armed group attacked them. Other officers sustained injuries and were taken to the hospital for treatment.

On 21 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three Edo State Security Network members in the Okhun community near Okada (Ovia North East, Edo). About ten armed group members invaded the community, went straight to the ESSN members on duty, and killed them. The attack was reported to be a cult reprisal attack.

Around 21 September 2023 (week of), the Niger Communal Militia abducted 21 people from the villages around Munya LGA, coded to Sarkin Pawa (Muya, Niger). They kept the hostages in the temporary camp in Tsohon Kabula.
On 21 September 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a woman and abducted two of her children in Kaura LGA (Kaduna).

On 21 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians from Satellite town in Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The victims included a pastor, his daughter and one man who were taken away by the assailants in a boat.
On 21 September 2023, Nigerian soldiers, in collaboration with the CJTF, killed five Boko Haram/ISWAP after raiding their hideout in Abbaram (Bama, Borno).

On 22 September 2023, Sokoto militia shot and killed four people in Giyawa (Goronyo, Sokoto). The armed group injured and abducted many people. The community members raided the house of the suspected informant and killed him, coded separately.

On 22 September 2023, the Nigerian military confronted the Zamfara militia group who abducted Federal University Gusau female students in Sabon-Gida near Bugudu (Bungudu, Zamfara). A source reported that the troop pursued the militia and killed five, paving the way for some hostages to escape while the militia went away with the rest. 14 students and two workers who were abducted in a separate event [coded separately] were released around 25 September, other sources report that the troops of operation Hadarin Daji rescued 7 students and 3 workers and that six students were rescued on the day of the abduction. Other sources report that the abductees were 21 in total, and another 9 were released around 18 March after negotiations, the demands which did not include ransom were not clear. The remaining abducted students were released on 14 April, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 22 September 2023, Benue Communal Militia abducted two women and four men around Utonkon (Ado, Benue). The victims were going to the farm when the abductors seized them. The police raided the abductors' hideout, arrested four and released the hostages, coded separately.
On 22 September 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked a herder's community in Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). They killed three herders.

On 22 September 2023, Zamfara Communal militia abducted nine construction workers at the Federal University Gusau in Kulodo (Bungudu, Zamfara). The armed group arrived at the university early in the morning, broke into the building occupied by the construction workers, and took them away. The abduction was the second on the same day after some female students were abducted at the dawn of Friday, coded separately. Two of the workers were released along with 14 students who were abducted separately [coded separately] were released, other sources report that the troops of operation Hadarin Daji rescued 3 workers and 7 students. The remaining abducted students were released on 14 April, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 23 September 2023, a suspected Mwaghavul militia killed the leader of Fulani in Panyam district (Mangu, Plateau) in his locality as he was returning from a visit to the district head of Panyam as claimed by state chairman of MACBAN. The spokesperson of Mwaghavul development association denied the claim.

On 23 September 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed ten farmers and abducted several others in the fields between Bulankunkumma and Maiwa villages in Mafa LGA (Borno). Other sources report that between four and nine persons were abducted, the victims were killed when they insisted on having any money to pay as ransom.

On 23 September 2023, the Zamfara militia shot and killed a driver after waylaying his vehicle along the Yan-Kara-Gusau Highway in Gusau LGA. coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The armed group abducted four people, including a mother and three children.

On 23 September 2023, policemen and hunters repelled an unidentified armed group of six that attempted to abduct a man from his residence at the Katampe area of Sabon Wuse (Tafa, Niger). The police claimed that one of the assailants was killed, another was wounded and arrested while the others fled with gunshot wounds. Other sources claim that the assailants were attacked by the target who had a gun in his house.
On 23 September 2023, ISWAP fighters mounted an illegal Vehicle Check Point along the Maiduguri-Dikwa Road in Mafa LGA, coded to Mafa (Mafa, Borno). They abducted six people.

On 23 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the former chairman of Ukum LGA from his residence at Sankera (Ukum, Benue). The abductors established contact with the victim's family, a ransom of 12 million naira which was later reduced to 10 million and then 5 million was demanded. The victim died in captivity despite the payment of some part of the ransom.

On 23 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the PDP chairman for Jos South LGA along Bukuru expressway (Jos South, Plateau). The party's state chairman claimed that the military was involved in the abduction, but the military denied the claims.

On 23 September 2023, a Zamfara militia killed four civilians and abducted nine others when they attacked Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). The abductees included women and children. Other sources report that eight persons were killed and 60 others were abducted.

On 23 September 2023, a Katsina militia who attempted to attack civilians were repelled by a team of soldiers, policemen and a local defense militia in Malumfashi (Malumfashi, Katsina). One civilian was wounded in the armed clash while the assailants who were up to 50 fled and six abductees including a judge were rescued.

On 23 September 2023, suspected Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] ambushed a convoy of security agents comprised of soldiers and Civilian JTF operatives who were escorting civilians along Gwoza-Limankara road (Gwoza, Borno). Five commercial vehicles including a security patrol van were set ablaze; one soldier and 3 to 5 civilians were killed, an unspecified number of passengers were missing while the abducted female passengers were released later that day.
On 23 September 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) sexually assaulted an unspecified number of women in Tsabre (Isa, Sokoto), and abducted others.

On 24 September 2023, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji clashed with the Sokoto Militia in the Tokhkatara forest in the northwest of Sokoto, coded to Wurno (Wurno, Sokoto). The Nigerian troops killed several (coded as 3), and many escaped with bullet wounds. The troops recovered numerous weapons from the armed group.

On 24 September 2023, an armed individual (reported to be an IDP) shot and wounded a soldier in Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The shooting heightened tension and fear among the people. Curfew was later imposed on the community to deescalate the tension, coded separately.
On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted eight people on Idah-Odolu Road, coded to Oforachi (Igalamela, Kogi).

On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person at Egbedion street in Okhunmwun community (Ovia North East, Edo) coded to Okada and one other in Benin City [coded separately]. The attacks were related to a youth leadership tussle.

On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the Benue state commissioner for information, culture and tourism from his residence in Zaki Biam (Ukum, Benue). The assailants who invaded the area on four motorcycles shot sporadically and forcefully gained entrance. A ransom of 60 million naira was demanded. The abductee was released around 5 October, the state chief press secretary claimed that no ransom was paid.

On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her three children from their residence at Ajilete (Ifelodun, Kwara). The abductors shot sporadically when they invaded the area, a ransom of 100 million naira was demanded.
On 24 September 2023, ISWAP fighters shot and killed a man on his farm near Geidam Chukun, coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno).
On 24 September 2023, the Kaduna militia attacked a residence in Kafanchan (Jema'a, Kaduna). They killed one person and abducted two others.
On 24 September 2023, the Zamfara militia shot and killed one person and abducted three others along the Yankara-Gusau Road, Chafe (Tsafe, Zamfara). The militia waylaid the victims' vehicle.

On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person at Sapele road in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) and one other in Okhunmwun community [coded separately]. The attacks were related to a youth leadership tussle.
On 24 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an INGO employee from his residence in Nsokpo Ogbaku, Ogbaku (Mbaitoli, Imo).

On 25 September 2023, the troops of Operation Hadarin Daji intercepted the Zamfara militia in Kayan Boggo, coded to Bukuyum (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The troops killed an unspecified number of the militia (coded as 3) and rescued 15 abductees.

On 25 September 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up the assistant to a businessman when they invaded his boss' in Jebba community (Moro, Kwara). Both the assistant and his boss were abducted while the assistant was later released following his boss' plea, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 25 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two people from a residence in Jebba (Moro, Kwara).

On 25 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot three students Isa Mustapha Agwai polytechnic in Ombi 1 coded to Ombi (Nasarawa, Nassarawa) and abducted one female. Some sources report that the number of wounded students is unknown, others report that two students were killed and that the attack was a robbery. A ransom of 50 million naira which was later reduced to 500,000 naira was demanded for the abductee's release. The abductee was released after 300,000 thousand naira was paid as ransom.
On 25 September 2023, suspected herders attacked and injured a man in Isuaniocha, along Urum Road, Isu Aniocha (Awka North, Anambra).

On 25 September 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up the chairman of Mgbuka Amazu market in Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra) before they took him away. The attack was related to the Monday sit-in protest.

On 25 September 2023, the Nigerian soldiers and CJTF clashed with Boko Haram/ISWAP, trying to abduct some farmers in Maiwa or Maiwa Kura (Mafa, Borno). The militias withdrew, and the soldiers rescued three women and four men. They recovered one AK rifle, magazine, and 30 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition. There were no fatalities.

On 25 September 2023, Nigerian army troops of 144 battalion ambushed Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] and killed 6 militants around Mandara mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno). The militants that were killed included Ari Gana; the group's second in command and five of his bodyguards.

Around 26 September 2023 (as reported), a Fulani pastoralist and a farmer engaged in an armed clash on a farm in Kertyo, Obi LGA (Nassarawa) following a disagreement over grazing. Both the farmer and pastoralist were killed after they sustained injuries from the fight.

Around 26 September 2023 (as reported), a Fulani pastoralist killed a farmer on his farm in Keana LGA (Nassarawa) following a disagreement over grazing. The pastoralist stabbed the farmer severely when he attempted to let the cows out of his farm.
Around 26 September 2023 (as reported), a suspected Fulani militia killed a civilian at his house in Kwamena community of Doka ward (Doma, Nassarawa).

On 26 September 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a driver and abducted seven of his passengers along Birnin Gwari-Kaduna road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The assailants blocked the road and shot sporadically at the victim's car.

On 26 September 2023, a Fulani militia attacked and killed six civilians at Takanai community (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa. The victims included two children, six other persons were wounded and the assailants fled when soldiers arrived.
On 26 September 2023, the Niger militia abducted a man and a woman from Igu Tsauni village in Sarkin Pawa district (Muya, Niger). The armed group later released the woman.
On 26 September 2023, the Katsina militia abducted two people from Safana (Safana, Katsina). No demand for ransom was made.

On 26 September 2023, an unidentified armed group of six that attacked civilians was engaged in an armed clash by a local defense militia at Alalubosa community (Ilorin West, Kwara). The militia rescued one abductee and killed one of the assailants, one civilian was killed and two others were wounded before the militia's arrival. Other sources report that two civilians were killed; one of whom was shot and later macheted to death while three others were wounded.

On 26 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of passengers along Ikang (Akpabuyo, Cross River). One of the victims was a fish seller who was on her way to buy fish for sale. A ransom of 5 million naira was demanded for her release.

On 26 September 2023, some professional hunters killed a civilian whom they tortured in an attempt to make him confess to stealing a male genital after he and other were accused. The police claimed to have arrested three hunters, location coded to Bauchi (Bauchi, Bauchi).
On 26 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the Nigerian Army checkpoint in Bama (Bama, Borno). They claimed to have forced the military to withdraw. There were no fatalities.
On 26 September 2023, the Katsina militia shot and killed one man and injured two others in Mahuta village near Kafur (Kafur, Katsina).
On 26 September 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a mechanic at Naharati, along the Abuja-Lokoja highway, Abaji (Abaji, Federal Capital Territory).
On 26 September 2023, a Kaduna militia killed one civilian, wounded three others and abducted one person when they invaded Kwankwami village in Igabi LGA (Kaduna).
On 26 September 2023, suspected herders killed three farmers and injured another in Kigam and Jebbu Miango communities, coded to Miango (Bassa, Plateau)

On 27 September 2023, the Benue militia abducted a former Education Secretary of Ogbadibo LGA around Agada Hill, close to Adum Oko, Orokam (Ogbadibo, Benue). The victim was returning from a burial ceremony when the abductors seized him and abandoned his vehicle at the roadside.
On 27 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed three farmers in Panyam (Mangu, Plateau). The victims were working on their farms when the assailants shot them dead.

On 27 September 2023, the police shot and killed four members of an armed group who had ambushed them in Warri (Warri South, Delta). The group ambushed and opened fire on the police while trying to rescue one of them. Two police officers sustained gun injuries. The police recovered two defaced AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 26 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, and (47) forty-seven empty shells of 7.62mm ammunition.
On 27 September 2023, ISWAP clashed with an unidentified armed group (a patrol of militia) near Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). They claimed to have forced the militia to withdraw. There were no fatalities.
On 27 September 2023, ISWAP claimed to have shot and killed two civilian Christians in Doutchi coded to Maggaria (Mobbar, Borno).
On 27 September 2023, suspected herders attacked Jebbu Miango community, Miango (Bassa, Plateau) and shot a farmer dead.

Around 27 September 2023 (week of), soldiers beat up a policeman who is presumed to have been off-duty at the Nigerian Army College of Nursing in Yaba (Lagos Mainland, Lagos) over claims that the victim broke a glass at the entrance of the school where he was also a student.

On 28 September 2023, the police, in collaboration with other security agencies, clashed with the Benue militia in Agbanor village around Okpoga (Okpokwu, Benue). The police were searching for some hostages when they came under fire from the assailants. They rescued six victims and arrested four armed group members. The police recovered a single-barrel gun loaded with two live cartridges. There were no fatalities.

Around 28 September 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia attacked Tsohon Kabula Community near Kabula (Muya, Niger) and displaced over 200 community inhabitants. The inhabitants abandoned their farms and homes and relocated to the neighbouring villages. The militia converted the village to their temporary waiting camp, where they kept their hostages for negotiation and onward movement to the permanent base in Kaduna state. It was not clear if the militia killed or injured civilians during the attack. Casualties unknown.

On 28 September 2023, IPOB/ ESN militants ambushed Nigerian troops with IEDs along Orsumoghu-Ukpor road (Ihiala, Anambra). The troops responded and killed at least 4 militants, two AK-47rifles were recovered and the others fled into nearby bushes with various degrees of gunshot wounds.

On 28 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man and stole his vehicle and other valuables along Nike Road, Trand Ekulu, Enugu North LGA. coded to Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The hostage escaped from the captivity.

On 29 September 2023, an unidentified armed group (suspected SDP supporters) shot and killed an APC woman during a political rally in Koton-Karfe (Kogi, Kogi). The victim had recently decamped from SDP to APC before she was gunned down by the assailants who invaded the APC solidarity walk for their Gubernatorial candidate.

On 29 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted twenty-five Christ Apostolic Church choir members on the Benin-Akure Expressway around Ifon (Ose, Ondo). The church's choir members were travelling to Ifon for a burial ceremony when they were seized and taken to the bush by the armed group. The Police rescued eight of them about 20 hours after the abduction. A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded, other sources reported that the remaining abductees were 11 an they were released around 7 October after the ransom was paid.

On 29 September 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and wounded two women from Chembe village when they went to fetch firewood. Location coded to Ugba (Logo, Benue). The victims were attacked with machetes.
On 29 September 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted seven people from the Kwaku community or Kpako (Kuje, Federal Capital Territory). No further details.

On 29 September 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram shot and killed a driver and abducted eight people after setting up an Illegal Vehicle Checkpoint along the Monguno- Gajiram Road coded to Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno).
On 29 September 2023, an unidentified armed group waylaid and abducted a retired military General in the Orji General area, coded to Orji (Owerri North, Imo).

On 30 September 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the police while trying to attack the convoy of the SDP governorship candidate en route to Koton-Karfe (Kogi). They made two attempts on the convoy, but the police repelled them with gunfire. Several people were injured during the clash. There were no fatalities.
On 30 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person at his residence in the Bumsa community (Gulami, Yobe). No further details.

On 30 September 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Anguwar Makeri community in Kufana Chiefdom (Kajuru, Kaduna) and killed one person. 19 other people, most of whom were women were abducted and one person was wounded.
On 30 September 2023, an unidentified armed group stabbed and injured a tricyclist in the Ofuluinu community, Nsukka (Nsukka, Enugu). The armed group carted away his tricycle.

On 30 September 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a staff of the Rivers state water corporation at Trans-Amadi area of Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The victim's car and other valuables were left untouched, while he was stabbed multiple times.

Around 30 September 2023 (week of), ISWAP militants abducted two traditional rulers from Burum village in Damboa LGA (Borno) after the militants blamed the villagers for an ambush against them by Nigerian troops. They accused the villagers of giving information to the troops. The abductees were the village head and ward head respectively.

On 1 August 2023, a Fulani militia were engaged in an armed clash by policemen and hunters who responded to a distress call at a church in Odu village near Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The assailants had attacked worshippers, raped one person and abducted 12 others who escaped when the police arrived, three of the assailants were arrested.
On 1 August 2023, an unidentified armed group raped and killed an 18-year old girl in Taraba. Location coded to Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba).

On 1 August 2023, a Niger militia abducted a catholic priest and a seminarian from their residence in Gyedna village (Tafa, Niger) coded to Sabon Wuse which is about one hour away. The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the village to scare residents and fled with the victims towards the village's boundary with Gwaram. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted one person from Igarra (Akoko Edo, Edo). Four other persons were abducted the following day [coded separately] and a ransom of 12 million naira was demanded from one of the victims.
On 1 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two healthcare workers who were on duty in Dandume LGA (Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 August 2023, Supreme Eiye Confraternity also known as Eiye killed one person who attempted to intervene in the abduction of a resident at Ire Akari estate in Isolo (Oshodi, Lagos). The victim's head was smashed with a stone.
On 1 August 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) killed 1 person and abducted twenty others in Tsoho Kabula (Muya, Niger).

On 2 August 2023, a Zamfara militia killed five farmers at Masa village in Gummi LGA (Zamfara). The assailants wounded three persons including one NURTW member and also abducted 8 persons consisting of seven teenage girls and one man. The male abductee escaped around 6 September.

On 2 August 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a civilian and abducted seven others while they were working on their farms at Unguwar Gajere community in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The abductees consisted of five females and two males, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 2 August 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians at Tsamaye town (Sabon Birni, Sokoto) and killed one person. Three others were abducted.

On 2 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia abducted four persons from Igarra (Akoko Edo, Edo). One other person was abducted the previous day [coded separately] and a ransom of 12 million naira was demanded from one of the victims.

On 3 August 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] killed two civilians whose bodies were discovered at Meleri village (Kala Balge, Borno) after they were abducted and negotiations were unsuccessful with their families.
On 3 August 2023, an unidentified armed group collecting produce fee for the council stabbed and killed a truck driver at Ugwuoba (Oji River, Enugu).

On 3 August 2023, a Sokoto militia were engaged in an armed clash with soldiers when they attempted to infiltrate Isa LGA (Sokoto). The militia was repelled, and an unspecified number of them sustained gunshot wounds.

On 3 August 2023, a Katsina militia were engaged in an armed clash with policemen who were on a search and rescue mission at the fringes of the fringes of Dutsinma LGA (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. Three civilians who were abducted by the militia were rescued, casualties are unknown.
On 3 August 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted two priests in Yaidna, also known as Gyedna (Tafa, Niger), and fired indiscriminately in the community. Casualties unknown.
On 3 August 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted at least thirty-five people, most of whom are women and girls, from Girigori, coded to the LGA HQ, Kagara (Rafi, Niger).

On 4 August 2023, a Zamfara militia that attempted to attack worshippers were engaged in an armed clash by policemen at Kwata village in Magariya district, Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). The clash lasted for one hour, one of the assailants was killed, the others fled with possible gunshot wounds. Two rifles, ammunition and a motorcycle were recovered by policemen.

On 4 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be land grabbers wounded a man whom they attacked on a disputed farmland at Idiagbon area (Ado-Odo, Ogun) coded as Ado Odo. The victim was taken to a hospital while the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the attack.

On 4 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a district head and wounded four other civilians when they attacked Zamtung village, coded to Wase LGA (Plateau). The attacked lasted for two hours, women and children were the major casualties.

On 4 August 2023, policemen repelled an attack by a Zamfara militia that attempted to attack a divisional police station in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). One of the assailants was killed, an unspecified number fled with bullet wounds and a suspected female informant was arrested.

On 4 August 2023, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants in armed clashed at Garin Ari Shira and Lawanti in Bama LGA (Borno). 5 militants were killed at Garin Ari Shira, the village was set ablaze by the troops and the militants ambushed the troops as they were withdrawing at Lawanti where one militant was killed.
On 4 August 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Danjibga village (Tsafe, Zamfara). Casualties are unknown.

On 4 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have engaged a militia that is presumed to be the Civilian JTF in an armed clash at Bambi, and also attacked Christian civilians. Ten persons were killed and wounded, coordinates are unknown and location was coded to Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno).

On 4 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian army headquarters and engaged troops in an armed clash at Monguno (Monguno, Borno). An unspecified number of soldiers were killed and wounded, one vehicle was damaged and unspecified equipment was seized. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 4 August 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians, killed scores, wounded an unspecified number of persons and abducted many others at Kwatar village in Kwatarkwashi district (Bungudu, Zamfara). Scores of fatalities coded as 20.

On 5 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian from Choba axis (Obio, Rivers) and released him after 2 million naira was paid as ransom. The abductors later called the abductee to demand for 3 million naira more.
On 5 August 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists and farmers engaged in armed clashes at Gadori and Waloloma (Mobbar, Borno) coded to Damasak. 11 persons were killed in the clashes.
On 5 August 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai engaged Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] in an armed clash at Lawanti in Bama LGA (Borno). One militant was killed.

On 5 August 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Gidan Jaja in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). The militia fled, some with possible gunshot wounds and 11 motorcycles were recovered by the troops.

On 5 August 2023, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF raided the hideout of Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants and engaged them in an armed clash in Kashimeri (Bama, Borno). 5 militants were killed, the troops pursued others who fled and captured 4 of them at Gaizuwa.
On 5 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians from El Rufai estate in Bwari (Bwari, FCT). The abductees were released after paying four million naira and a motorcycle each.

On 5 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man and dumped his corpse at Oshodi (Oshodi, Lagos) where it was found. The victim was an aide to a senator, other sources report that he was stopped at a checkpoint by security agents who attempted to verify his vehicle's documents at Berger area before his corpse was found with a gunshot wound. The senator claimed that the soldiers operating Nigerian Army checkpoints around Ikeja axis were responsible for the attack.

On 5 August 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants were engaged in an armed clash with soldiers who repelled the militants attempt to attack an IDP camp in Monguno town (Monguno, Borno) via Charlie 7 in the Marte axis. Two militants were killed, one IDP was hit and killed by a stray bullet, one soldier was wounded and two weapons were recovered.

On 6 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a Fulani pastoralist and wounded one other person at Heipang (Barkin Ladi, Plateau). The assailants had attacked traders who were returning from a cattle market before escaping. As they were well armed, the local defense militia that arrived did not engage them in an armed clash.

On 6 August 2023, troops of sector 3 in Sokoto who were on a fighting patrol engaged in an armed clash a Sokoto militia that attacked a village at Manu (Tangaza, Sokoto). The militia fled, two motorcycles, a mobile phone, blankets and engineering equipment were recovered by the troops.

On 6 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the emir of Gurku and his wife from his palace in Gurku (Karu, Nassarawa). There are no reports about ransom demands. The abductees were released around 14 August, there are no reports on ransom payment.
On 6 August 2023, a Zamfara militia in large numbers attacked a police station and engaged policemen in an armed clash at Bungudu town (Bungudu, Zamfara). One policeman was killed.

On 6 August 2023, a Katsina militia engaged troops of sector 2 of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on a routine patrol in an armed clash along Jibia-Magama-Maidabaru road (Jibia, Katsina). Three members of the militia were killed and two soldiers were wounded.

On 6 August 2023, suspected Boko Harm [JAS faction] militants abducted seven rice farmers while they were cultivating their farmland in Zabarmari (Jere, Borno). A ransom of 600 thousand naira for each abductee was demanded.
On 6 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted a healthcare worker from a healthcare facility in Dongon Dawa, Faskari LGA (Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 6 August 2023, a Katsina militia attacked and killed two commuters when they blocked the Jibia-Batsari road in the vicinity of Solar village in Batsari LGA (Katsina). The assailants set the victims ablaze in a vehicle.

On 6 August 2023, ISWAP fighters were repelled by troops of sector 3 of MNJTF in Monguno (Monguno, Borno) after they launched an attack from the Marte axis. An unspecified number of militants were killed, one soldier was wounded and various military equipment were recovered. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 6 August 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a man at Bebuachuan village (Obudu, Cross River). The victim was the family head of the village and was killed over an accusation of witchcraft. Other sources report that the assailants were leaders of the clan's youth council.
On 6 August 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants attacked and killed two IDPs at the Banki IDP camp (Bama, Borno). The victims were killed at line 15, within the camp.

On 6 August 2023, policemen engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Sabon Gida village in Malumfashi LGA (Katsina) and rescued five abductees who were initially taken by the militia. There were no casualties.

Around 7 August 2023 (as reported), the Niger militia abducted a man at Maikonkele (Bosso, Niger) and later killed him. The police found and recovered his body from a bush around the Gusasse area of Maikunkele, Bosso LGA. They arrested the abductors on 19/10/2023 and recovered 81 cattle and 41 sheep from them.

Around 7 August 2023 (as reported), troops of forward operating base Garin-Hausawa engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash, after the group was sighted in Madobiya village (Danko, Kebbi) coded to Wasagu. The assailants fled and three abductees were rescued by the troops. There were no casualties.

Around 7 August 2023 (as reported), troops of sector 3 of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Sokoto militia in an armed clash while on routine patrol at Gundumi village (Goronyo, Sokoto). One member of the militia was killed, others escaped with gunshot wounds, a rifle and a magazine loaded with ammunition were recovered.

On 7 August 2023, a Niger militia killed a man along Alawa-Pandogari road (Shiroro, Niger). The victim was a newly-wed groom who was returning with his bride when they ran into the militia and fled into the bush. The assailants stole foodstuff and fuel from the vehicle the victim was travelling in before they set it ablaze.

Around 7 August 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia abducted 24 farmers from Gulbin Boka in Mashegu LGA (Niger). Three abductees were released after an undisclosed ransom amount was paid; two others who were also Islamic teachers were shot dead, 5 men and 14 women were still held by the militia.
On 7 August 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one person and abducted six women when they attacked Boko town (Zurmi, Zamfara).

Around 7 August 2023 (as reported), troops of sector 1 of Operation Hadarin Daji responded to a distress call and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at a location between Tabanni and Tazame villages in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). An unspecified number of abductees were rescued, and the assailants fled. There were no casualties.

On 7 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed three civilians at Nchya village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The spokesperson of Operation Safe Haven claimed that the event was an assassination not an attack. Some sources report that five persons were killed, others report that four persons were killed in Mwaghavul and Nchya communities.

On 8 August 2023, troops of sector 1 of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Gada Zaima (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. The clash lasted for hours; nine abductees who were abducted from Sokoto state were rescued, 10 militiamen and a female abductee were killed, other militiamen fled with bullet wounds, several others drowned in a swamp while trying to escape and two others were captured. Weapons, ammunition, cash and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 8 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two soldiers who were providing security at a road construction site in Ogboloma (Obua, Rivers). An expatriate, the foreman and two other workers on the site and a farmer who was returning from the farm were abducted, the soldiers rifles were stolen by the assailants who fled through Esalla. Residents of the area fled over fears of a reprisal.
On 8 August 2023, a Katsina militia shot and wounded two people when they attacked Hayin Nuhu village in Safana LGA (Katsina).

On 8 August 2023, a Fulani militia of eleven abducted a Fulani pastoralist from his farm at Agbese village in Iwo LGA (Osun). The abductee was rescued by policemen who responded to a distress call and chased after the abductors [coded separately].

On 8 August 2023, policemen and hunters militia engaged a Fulani militia in an armed clash in a bush at Iwo (Iwo, Osun) in an attempt to rescue an abductee. Two militiamen were killed while others fled with gunshot injuries and the abductee was rescued.

On 8 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted over 10 persons in Isua community (Ahoada West, Rivers). The abductees were abducted while they were on their way to their farm, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 8 August 2023, a soldier shot and killed another soldier who is presumed to have been off-duty and was dressed in plain clothes in Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa). The soldier was enforcing a curfew when the victim who was her superior tried to intervene and she shot him with her already cocked rifle.

Around 8 August 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia attacked a man on his farm, wounded his son and attempted to kill him before the man wrestled the gun of the militia's leader away and shot him with it while the other members of the militia fled. Location coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna).
On 8 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted four women in Dantudu, at Wagini ward (Batsari, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 8 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed three farmers who were on their way to their farm in Funkwa village, Takum LGA (Taraba). The victims were from the Kuteb ethnic group.

On 8 August 2023, a Kaduna militia numbering 12 abducted two farmers from Kurmin Kola, near Janjala village (Kagarko, Kaduna) when they invaded the area on six motorcycles. The assailants also stole foodstuff and burgled a chemist.

On 8 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be abductors killed one hunter in the forest around Igarra (Akoko Edo, Edo) while he was on a search and rescue mission together with a local defense militia. The assailants fled and one of them was later arrested.

On 8 August 2023, troops of Operation Whirl Punch raided the hideout of a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). Three militiamen were killed, one was captured, rifles, magazines, motorcycles and other items were recovered.
On 8 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man along the Jos-Abuja highway in Riyom LGA (Plateau). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded.
On 9 August 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of people in the vicinity of Dinawa village (Wurno, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 9 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one woman from Maiturmi village in Rafin Iwa ward (Sabuwa, Katsina). The abductee was rescued by a local defense militia, there are no reports of a clash.

On 9 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted a family of four from their residence at Fondisho community along Kaduna-Zaria highway (Zaria, Kaduna). The abductees consisted of a couple and two of their children. An undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom which was paid however the victims were still held by the abductors 3 weeks later. The woman and their new born were released around 3 October, the abductors demanded for 10 million and three motorcycles as ransom to be paid within 10 days for the release of the man and their eldest son. The man was released on 10 October after an undisclosed amount was paid, his eldest son and brother in-law were held by the assailants.

On 9 August 2023, operatives of Operation Farauta comprised of soldiers, policemen and NSCDC operatives tortured and killed a 17-year old secondary student after he was accused of receiving a stolen phone. Location coded to Yola (Yola-North, Adamawa).
On 9 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted seven civilians from Yarkaka village in Gazari ward (Sabuwa, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 9 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted six civilians from Yallagwada village in Maibakko ward (Sabuwa, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 9 August 2023, a Katsina militia attacked civilians and killed the son of the ward head of Tundun Ali in Dandume LGA (Katsina).
On 9 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 1 person and abducted four others in Tulutu (Goronyo, Sokoto).

On 10 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed three women and wounded many others including children at Ngban community (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba. The victims were IDPs who were ambushed by the assailants on their way back to their camp from the farm.

On 10 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed 17 civilians at Batin village in Heipang district (Barkin Ladi, Plateau) and four others at Rayogot village [coded separately]. Other sources report that 20 persons were killed and over 10 others were wounded by the assailants who invaded the area in the early hours of the day.

On 10 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed 4 civilians at Rayogot in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). Other sources report that 17 persons were killed in Heipang and over 10 others were wounded [coded separately] by the assailants who invaded the area in the early hours of the day.

On 10 August 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked civilians, killed 17 persons at Tagwon Lawuru and three others Layowok communities in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). An unspecified number of persons were wounded in the attacks.

Around 10 August 2023 (as reported), troops of Operation Hadin Kai on an ambush operation engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants in an armed clash along Kuka in Konduga LGA (Borno). Two militants were killed, others fled, 63 rounds of ammunition, one IED shell, money and Pento injections were recovered.

On 10 August 2023, policemen beat up and wounded a civilian at Shokas Estate in Ijebu-Igbo (Ijebu North, Ogun). The victim claimed that he was attacked for speaking against the extortion and harassments of residents by policemen.

On 10 August 2023, Nigerian troops raided a hideout of ISWAP militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Dar el Jamal- Bula Yobe road (Bama, Borno). One militant was killed, 28 women were rescued and three dane guns were recovered by the troops.

On 10 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted two others from Kamadi village (Kwali, FCT). The murdered victim had attempted to escape abduction when he was shot dead, a ransom of 15 million naira was demanded for the abductees' release.
On 10 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed one civilian and wounded an unspecified number of people in Yar Runfa (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 10 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a man and his son from their residence and took them into the forest around Marke general area (Tsafe, Zamfara) where they were rescued by Nigerian troops on patrol. Location coded to where the abductees were rescued from.
On 10 August 2023, a Sokoto militia killed a policeman [presumed to be off-duty] when they attacked his residence at Tudun Wada A (Sokoto South, Sokoto). The victim's valuables were also stolen.

On 10 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot at the vehicle of an former spokesperson of the PDP at Akwakuma/ Mbieri road in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) as claimed by the victim. A shop owner was abducted in the process. There were no casualties.
On 11 August 2023, two unidentified armed groups engaged in an armed clash at the kingdom hall axis of Sangotedo (Eti-Osa, Lagos). Casualties are unknown.
On 11 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two people at Nyian village (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba.

On 11 August 2023, operatives of Operation Udo Ka II comprised of soldiers, policemen and DSS operatives raided a hideout of IPOB militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Imufu in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). Three militants were killed, other sources report that two militants were killed, others escaped with varying degrees of gunshot wounds. Weapons, ammunition and other items including military camouflages and fabrics with IPOB insignia were recovered.
On 11 August 2023, two unidentified rival cult militias engaged in an armed clash at the Osun-Oshogbo groove in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). Three persons were killed and 12 others were wounded.
On 11 August 2023, an unidentified armed group shot indiscriminately and killed two commuters at Neke (Isi Uzo, Enugu) and abducted an unspecified number of others.
On 11 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted three persons when they attacked Zakka village (Safana, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, an unidentified armed man, presumed to be a member of an armed group abducted one woman from Suka village, coded to Mamman Suka (Gwadabawa, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted at least 20 people when they attacked a commercial bus that was transporting passengers from Kaduna to Isa in Isa LGA (Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 11 August 2023, a Fulani militia attacked women who were returning from the market at Kinat community, Mangu Halle ward (Mangu, Plateau). Two of the women were killed and two others sustained injuries.

On 11 August 2023, troops sector 1 of Operation Hadarin Daji who were on a routine patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at the Marke general area (Tsafe, Zamfara). The clash lasted several hours, the troops rescued two abductees, the militiamen fled and two motorcycles were recovered by the troops. There were no casualties.

On 11 August 2023, Oyofo and Awha communal militias engaged in an armed clash over land dispute in Ezeagu LGA (Enugu). Four people were killed, one tricycle and five motorcycles were set ablaze. The police claimed that 12 persons were arrested in connection with the clash.

On 11 August 2023, troops of sector 1 of the Nigerian army conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kabode general area in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). Three militiamen were killed, one loaded rifle, three mobile phones and other items were recovered.

On 12 August 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked civilians at Kofar Gayan (Zaria, Kaduna) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. Two civilians were killed, one other person was abducted and other sources report that he was later rescued by security agents [no reports on a clash].
On 12 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked and killed two members of the Civilian JTF at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno).
On 12 August 2023, Nigerian troops and presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash in the vicinity of Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia numbering about 70 ambushed soldiers and a local defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash in Zungeru (Wushishi, Niger) as they were responding to a distress call from Akare community. 30 to 50 militia members, at least 10 soldiers and an unspecified number of local defense militiamen were killed. Other sources report that 23 soldiers were killed, some of whom were set ablaze in the convoy and eight other soldiers were wounded. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. The Defence headquarters claimed that 36 soldiers died in both the ambush and a helicopter crash [coded separately], total 43 fatalities coded.
On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia attacked a bus and killed four civilians including a one year old baby and abducted seven others from New Bussa (Borgu, Niger).

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others including women from Chibiani (Muya, Niger) and Zagzaga [coded separately]. Four people each were abducted from both locations.

On 13 August 2023, a Niger militia killed one civilian and abducted eight others including women from Zagzaga (Muya, Niger) and Chibiani [coded separately]. Four people each were abducted from both locations.
On 13 August 2023, a presumed unidentified cult militia killed one person at Ugbokolo town (Okpokwu, Benue). The reason for the attack is unknown.
On 13 August 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and wounded a motorcyclist along Gidan Katta-Masasa road in Illela LGA (Sokoto) and stole his motorcycle.
On 13 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two commuters along Adani-Ayamelum road, coded to Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra). A ransom of 40 million naira was demanded.

On 13 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian at Opu-Nembe community in Nembe LGA (Bayelsa) as claimed by members of the community. The PDP claimed that the assailants were working for the APC and also that the APC governorship candidate was behind the attacks, over the rejection of his candidature by the community.
On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians when they attacked Sabuwa town (Sabuwa, Katsina). The militia also rustled livestock and looted food supplies.

On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person out of the 20 civilians that they abducted from Madogara community (Batsari, Katsina). The victim was wounded when he struggled with the militia member that was holding him and sustained machete wounds. The other abductees consisted of 16 women and 3 men.

On 13 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a Nigerian army barracks in Logomani (Ngala, Borno) and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. The Defence Headquarters confirmed the attack and claimed that four militants were killed, 5 rifles, one RPG and other equipment were recovered.

On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed two civilians at Tsohuwar Kasuwa quarters in Dandume town (Dandume, Katsina) and wounded several others who attempted to escape in the process. An unspecified number of persons were also abducted. Other sources report that two people including a child were wounded.
On 13 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians, wounded three others and abducted an unspecified number of persons from Tsohuwar Makabarta in Dandume LGA (Katsina).
On 13 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) injured a civilian in an unspecified location in the Isa LGA, coded to the LGA HQ, Isa (Isa, Sokoto).
On 13 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed and injured an unspecified number of persons in an attack on Rimawa ward (Goronyo, Sokoto). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.
On 14 August 2023, a Niger militia ambushed soldiers and engaged them in an armed clash at Madaka ward (Rafi, Niger). Thirteen soldiers were killed.

On 14 August 2023, a Niger militia led by Dogo Gide claimed to have shot down a military helicopter that was carrying out an evacuation mission in Chukuba (Shiroro, Niger) and killed those on board. The military denied the claims and insisted that the weather and other conditions may have contributed to the crash. Unknown casualties coded as 3.
On 14 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian at Ayangba (Dekina, Kogi). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Sokoto militia engaged in an armed clash with soldiers who were deployed to repel the militia's attack at Gidan Kare (Tureta, Sokoto). The militia abducted an unspecified number of persons who were rescued by the soldiers, casualties are unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Fulani militia killed two teachers and wounded the vice principal of a school in Kwi (Riyom, Plateau). The assailants had invaded the school premises to graze their cattle and started shooting sporadically when they were confronted by the security men [presumed to be gate keepers]. The security men were not harmed.

On 14 August 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash and repelled the group when they attacked a group of journalists at Opu-Nembe in Nembe LGA (Bayelsa). The cameras of one of the journalists was seized by the assailants, casualties are unknown.

On 14 August 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one civilian and abducted seven others when they attacked Bungudu town (Bungudu, Zamfara). The abductees consisted of two males, one of whom was the son of the emir of Bungudu and five females, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted four civilians at Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina).

On 14 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters ambushed and engaged ISWAP fighters in a supremacy battle while they were on their way to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Sixty ISWAP fighters including three commanders were captured and taken to a Boko Haram prison at Kwatan Mota while others fled to the axis of Kukawa, Madayi and Kwatan Mota. Some ISWAP fighters had previously abandoned the group and joined forces with the Bakura led Boko Haram group that conducted the attack. There were no casualties.
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded three civilians and abducted four others at Kofa village in (Kusada, Katsina).
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of persons from Unguwar Dahiru and Unguwar Fadi villages in Funtua LGA (Katsina).
On 14 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person and rustled cattle from Wadi village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 14 August 2023, a Zamfara militia who were dressed in women's attire including hijabs abducted an unspecified number of civilians from Hayi community in Maru LGA (Zamfara). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area, the abductees included women and children and a businessman, other sources report that up to 50 people were abducted.

On 14 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins attacked a pastor and his wife at their church in New Benin, coded to Benin City (Oredo, Edo) after they had trailed them. The pastor's wife was killed, the pastor and his assistant sustained gunshot wounds.

On 14 August 2023, three soldiers beat up a LASTMA official at Ojota (Kosofe, Lagos) in a reprisal attack following a fight between their colleague and a LASTMA official. Two of the soldiers were dressed in their uniform and one in plain clothes. There were no casualties.

On 14 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) killed 1 person, injured two, and abducted several others during an attack in Tungar Loso, coded to the LGA HQ, Gwadabawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).
On 15 August 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a civilian and abducted three others when they attacked Idon town (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 15 August 2023, a Katsina militia was repelled by policemen who foiled their attack on Korogo village, coded to nearby Daddara (Jibia, Katsina). One militia member was killed, 60 rustled sheep, one rifle and 110 rounds of ammunition were recovered.
On 15 August 2023, a Zamfara militia fired indiscriminately and abducted 29 civilians from Janbako (Maradun, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 15 August 2023, a Sokoto militia wounded two civilians and abducted four others at Bakin Dutse village in Araba ward (Illela, Sokoto).

On 15 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted five civilians along Mile two axis of Ishiagu/Okigwe expressway (Ivo, Ebonyi). The abductees included a couple, their driver and a farmer whom they met and abducted as they were taking the other victims into the bush.

On 15 August 2023, policemen on patrol engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group suspected to be abductors at Ugbolokposo (Uvwie, Delta). Three members of the group were killed, four others were arrested.
On 15 August 2023, a Boko Haram commander [JAS faction] killed seven Boko Haram fighters at Bukkaram Island in Kukawa LGA (Borno) over an attempt by the fighters to surrender to Nigerian troops.

On 15 August 2023, a Sokoto militia wounded an unspecified number of commuters who were fleeing the militia's attack along Kunawa village (Goronyo, Sokoto). The assailants shot indiscriminately when they invaded the axis.
On 15 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person and abducted an unspecified number of others at Unguwar Maigayya in Dandume LGA (Katsina).
On 15 August 2023, Nigerian troops and presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash in the vicinity of Gabchari (Konduga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 16 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians in Bassambiri (Nembe, Bayelsa) over presumed political disputes. Casualties are unknown.

On 16 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked commuters around Abaji (Abaji, FCT), the driver and one other passenger were killed, while an NYSC member in the car was abducted. A ransom of 300 million which was later reduced to 1 million was paid for the abductee's release and she was released on 19 August. The NYSC denied the payment of ransom.
On 16 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded two civilians when they fired indiscriminately in Unguwar Gulbi (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.
On 16 August 2023, ISWAP/Boko Haram fighters engaged in an inter-ethnic clash amongst themselves at Baga (Kukawa, Borno). 82 fighters were killed, some fighters who survived fled into Chad.
On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be oil thieves engaged the state anti-oil bunkering unit in an armed clash at TTC in Okwuzi (Ogba, Rivers). Casualties are unknown.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three civilians from Sanger and Billiri Gorore villages in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). An undisclosed ransom amount was demanded for the abductee from Sanger.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the entrance of his apartment in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The abductee was rescued on the same day by policemen after the abductors abandoned him.

On 17 August 2023, an unidentified armed group of about seven abducted a woman and two of her maids from her shop in Elerinjare (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. The assailants shot sporadically and another person was hit and wounded by a stray bullet, the maids were later released and the abductee's husband claimed that the assailants included women. A ransom of 100 million naira was demanded and the police claimed to have arrested two persons in connection with the abduction. The abductee was released on 23 August after one million naira and food stuff were paid as ransom, the person who went to deliver the ransom was abducted [coded separately].
On 18 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians and abducted several women when they attacked Sabon Garin Unguwar Ganau, coded to Dan Musa (Dan-Musa, Katsina).
On 18 August 2023, a Katsina militia in their numbers killed a man and abducted his wife when they attacked Maidabino, coded to Maidabino A (Dan-Musa, Katsina) and conducted a house to house raid.

On 18 August 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group of four in an armed clash at Rumukwashi (Obio, Rivers) coded to Rumuodomaya after the group abducted a civilian in the area. Two of the assailants were killed and the abductee was rescued, and one other person was abducted.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from Yadagungume town in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductee was a nursing mother and also the wife of a businessman based in the town.

Around 19 August 2023 (as reported), a Sokoto militia in their numbers abducted a man from Tambuwal town (Tambuwal, Sokoto). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the town and headed towards Kebbe after the attack.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians at Gumau (Toro, Bauchi). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area to scare residents.
On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians at Bargan-Fulani and Fishere communities in Toro LGA (Bauchi).

On 19 August 2023, policemen shot sporadically into the air when they attempted to quell tensions between two groups in Itobe (Ofu, Kogi). A commercial tricycle rider was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five passengers at Rumuodogo junction (Emohua, Rivers). The abductees were rescued by policemen who went to the scene and combed the bushes [no reports of a clash].

On 19 August 2023, a Fulani militia abducted five women along the Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu). One person was killed earlier on the same day [coded separately] at the same location. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded for the release of one of the abductees.

On 19 August 2023, a Fulani militia killed one tipper driver along the Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu). Five women were abducted later on the same day [coded separately] at the same location.

On 19 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted eight NYSC members in Zamfara state while they were on their way to the orientation camp in Sokoto, Location coded to Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). Eleven NYSC members were initially abducted; three of them escaped, while the bus driver was also abducted. Other sources report that the abductors demanded a ransom of 4 million naira for the release of one of the abductees. A ransom of 13 million was paid for the abductees' release, but the militia demanded another 200 million naira ransom. A female abductee was released on 20 October. The militia released an additional two female hostages on 8 December 2023, there are no details on ransom payments, and another two were released around 5 February 2024, the NYSC claimed that they were rescued through the efforts of security operatives. An unspecified number of the remaining abductees were released on 14 April 2024, there are no details on ransom payment.

On 19 August 2023, ISWAP fighters led by Abou Idris engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash near Marte (Marte, Borno) as a reprisal for the capture of 60 ISWAP militants by Boko Haram [coded separately]. More than 100 militants from both sides were killed in the clash that continued to the following day, some sources report that more Boko Haram militants were killed. 100 fatalities split across two events coded as 50.

On 19 August 2023, an unidentified armed group in their numbers attacked a police station in Lau LGA (Taraba) after they invaded the town in search of a target whom they were unable to find. There were no casualties, some community members claimed that the assailants shot sporadically in the air when they invaded the area.

On 20 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted an off-duty soldier along Birnin Gwari road (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) while he was traveling to resume at his duty station. A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded with a three-day payment ultimatum.

On 20 August 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash around Centenary City (Enugu South, Enugu) coded to Uwani. Two of the assailants were killed, others escaped with bullet wounds, one abductee was rescued, his car was recovered; a gun loaded with four cartridges was also recovered by the policemen.

On 20 August 2023, ISWAP fighters led by Abou Idris engaged Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash near Marte (Marte, Borno) as a reprisal for the capture of 60 ISWAP militants by Boko Haram [coded separately]. More than 100 militants from both sides were killed in the clash that started the previous day, some sources report that more Boko Haram militants were killed. 100 fatalities split across two events coded as 50.

On 20 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed a man who was returning home from Tashar Biri, coded to Dan Ali (Dan-Musa, Katsina) where he was headed. The victim was hacked to death with a cutlass, the assailants also rustled several animals from residents in Dan Ali.

On 20 August 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot and killed a commander of the Benue state livestock guard who is presumed to have been unarmed at Tine Nune (Ukum, Benue). The victim was the fifth ward commander of the livestock guard to have been killed in the LGA.

On 20 August 2023, IPOB fighters engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash when they attempted to infiltrate the troops' forward operating base at Ukwuorji, along Owerri-Onitsha expressway (Owerri Municipal, Imo). One of the militants was killed, two were arrested and the others fled, a machete and other items were recovered by the troops.

On 21 August 2023, troops of 1 brigade garrison ambushed and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash while they were en route to attack civilians at Bobo village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). Two militia members were killed, two rifles and four motorcycles were recovered.
Around 21 August 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia killed two abductees out of the 24 that were previously abducted from Gulbin Boka in Mashegu LGA (Niger). The victims were Islamic teachers.

Around 21 August 2023 (week of), an unidentified armed group shot and killed a pastoralist at Ukwulu community (Dunukofia, Anambra). The victim's decomposing corpse was found with gunshot wounds on August 23 after he went missing since 21 August.

On 21 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted six persons from the Aworo/Asi area (Odo-Otin, Osun) coded to Okuku. The abductees included the Iyalode of Oyan who escaped while the other five persons were still in captivity. The remaining 5 abductees were released after 7 million naira was paid as ransom, the NSCDC spokesperson denied knowledge of any ransom payment.

On 21 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted the wife and daughter of a man when they invaded his residence at Damba, coded as Dunba (Gusau, Zamfara) and met his absence. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 21 August 2023, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Chito (Ukum, Benue) and continued the clash the following day [coded separately]. Five persons were killed; the market was also set ablaze by the assailants, other sources report that four persons were killed in Chito and one was killed in the suburbs.

On 22 August 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed an off-duty policeman in his house, one of the assailants was arrested by the police at Rumuodogo community (Emohua, Rivers). Location coded to where the assailant was arrested.

On 22 August 2023, a DSS operative stabbed and wounded a man in Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun) following a disagreement over a debt of 3000 naira which the assailant owed for electricity. Other sources report that the assailant stabbed the victim in order to escape a mob that attempted to attack him over accusation that he was an internet fraudster.

On 22 August 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted 42 IDPs women near Mafa town (Mafa, Borno). The abductees were from the Shuwari camp who went in search of firewood, 4 women were released while the other 42 were taken away. Other sources report that at least 48 women were abducted and they were released on 23 August after paying 20 thousand naira each as ransom.
On 22 August 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants ambushed Civilian JTF operatives at Kolkol junction in Mafa LGA (Borno). The operatives escaped the ambush. There were no casualties.
On 22 August 2023, two rival Benue militia engaged in an armed clash at Gbeji (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera which started the previous day [coded separately]. Three persons were killed.
On 22 August 2023, two factions of the NURTW engaged in an armed clash along Port Harcourt-Aba expressway (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The reason for the clash and casualties are unknown.

On 23 August 2023, masked security operatives presumed to have been policemen shot sporadically in two motor parks in Nkpor (Idemili North, Anambra) in an attempt to disperse traders from their shops. The shooting caused a stampede which resulted in the sustaining of varying degrees of injuries by many people, other sources report that 5 persons were wounded by the shooting and a state official claimed that the state government was responsible for sacking the occupants.

On 23 August 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed a man on his farm at Rahwol Gassa in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). The assailants were fleeing with their cows after being driven from farmlands in the area when they met the victim who was tied to a tree and slaughtered.
On 23 August 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked and killed a man while he was working on his farm in Kujama (Chikun, Kaduna). The victim was also a pastor.

On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed soldiers who were on patrol at Kukar Babangida in Jibia LGA (Katsina) and wounded two soldiers. The militia also abducted about 20 civilians from the village.
On 23 August 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked a police checkpoint near Geidam town (Geidam, Yobe), killed two policemen and captured one SUV as claimed by the militants.

On 23 August 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked and engaged rival Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters in an armed clash at Duguri axis (Kukawa, Borno). 41 fighters from both sides including their major commanders were killed.
On 23 August 2023, the Nigerian military shot and killed four ISWAP fighters in Pulka (Gwoza, Borno) and Firgi, coded separately. Fatalities split across two locations, 2 coded.

On 23 August 2023, a Zamfara militia who rode on motorcycles attacked civilians and shot sporadically when they invaded Gidan Damo in Bilbis district (Tsafe, Zamfara). Four persons were killed on the spot while three others sustained injuries. Other sources report that three persons were killed, seven were wounded and eight others were abducted.
On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person from Bakori town (Bakori, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 23 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed a couple and wounded two other civilians when they attacked Dandume town (Dandume, Katsina). One of the wounded victims was the child of the couple.

On 23 August 2023, a presumed Ezza militia engaged soldiers in an armed clash in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) after the soldiers attempted to repel the assailants from a church which they were vandalizing. The assailants fled and casualties are unknown.

On 23 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a civilian who went to deliver ransom for another victim who was previously abducted from Elerinjare village (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. The victim for whom the ransom was paid was released, a ransom of 5 million naira was demanded for the abductee's release.
On 23 August 2023, the Nigerian military shot and killed four ISWAP fighters in Firgi near Gwoza (Gwoza, Borno) and Pulka, coded separately. Fatalities split across two locations, 2 coded.

On 24 August 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged customs operatives who were on a stop and search duty in an armed clash along Daki Gari Koko road in Koko LGA (Kebbi). Two customs operatives were killed. Other sources report that the assailants were suspected drug smugglers.

On 24 August 2023, an unidentified armed group of three who were on a motorcycle attacked policemen at a police station in Isiokolo division, coded to Isiokolo-Agbon (Ethiope East, Delta). One policeman was killed, another sustained a gunshot injury and one constable escaped.

On 24 August 2023, an armed Fulani pastoralist cut the hand of a farmer at Jital village, coded to Jitar (Bauchi, Bauchi) following a fight that ensued between them over grazing on the victim's farm. The assailant was armed with a stick and a machete and he was arrested by the police.

On 24 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have engaged Nigerian soldiers in an armed clash after they ambushed them and detonated an IED on their convoy along Waijroko-Azir road (Damboa, Borno). An unspecified number of soldiers were killed and wounded and an armored vehicle was damaged. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 24 August 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted eight persons from Ore, coded to its ward, Samama (Binji, Sokoto).
On 25 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted the organizing secretary of the APC from his residence in Yakasai village (Soba, Kaduna). There are no reports on ransom demands.
