On 25 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted two civilians from a residence in Kasuan Shanu, Bama LGA (Borno). A ransom of 5 million naira was demanded and the abductees were later released after 200,000 naira was paid as ransom.
On 25 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a village head and three farmers in Nasarawa-Burkullu (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 25 August 2023, a local defense militia engaged a Katsina militia that abducted civilians in an armed clash at Jofalwa village in Kusada LGA (Katsina). Two out of the three abductees were rescued by the local defense militia.

On 25 August 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted two siblings when they invaded Wusasa (Zaria, Kaduna) and shot sporadically to scare residents away. One of the abductees is a health worker, there are no reports on ransom demands.
On 25 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded three farmers when they attacked a farm at the outskirts of Sabuwa town (Sabuwa, Katsina).
On 25 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists shot and killed one person at Ukwulu community (Dunukofia, Anambra).
On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two wedding guests at Nsukka LGA (Enugu).

On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman who was on escort duty at D-Line in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The rifle and beret of the policeman who was escorting his principal were taken away. Other sources report that the attack was an attempted abduction.
On 25 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted a woman and her child when they attacked a residence in Musari village (Mobbar, Borno) coded to Damasak. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 25 August 2023, ISWAP militants killed one civilian and wounded another person when they fired indiscriminately in Azir community, coded to Azir Multe (Damboa, Borno).
On 25 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five civilians from Kabusa community (Abuja Municipal, FCT). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 25 August 2023, a Benue militia attacked commuters and killed scores of persons along Chito-Zaki Biam road (Ukum, Benue). The attack was a reprisal following a clash between two militias in the area [coded separately]. Scores of fatalities coded as 20.
On 25 August 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person when they attacked Sayaya village (Matazu, Katsina).
On 26 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted the village head of Kwali village (Bukkuyum, Nigeria) coded to Bukuyum when they invaded the area. Four farmers were abducted alongside the village head.
On 26 August 2023, an unidentified cult militia attacked and shot at a local defense militia member who was wounded in the leg at a burial ceremony in the Baga Eriyo area of Shagamu LGA (Ogun).

On 26 August 2023, a Niger militia killed four civilians and abducted an unspecified number of others when they attacked Tudun Magaji, Rijiyan Nagwamatse and Farin Shinge villages in Nagwamatse ward (Kontagora, Niger).
On 26 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted eight farmers when they invaded a farm and shot sporadically at Maiwa, coded to Maiwa Kura (Mafa, Borno).

On 26 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a militia which is presumed to have been the Civilian JTF in Sambisa Forest. Location coded to Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno), one militia member was killed by the militants.

On 26 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a tractor driver while he was working on a farm in Tsohon Achodi village in Abaji area council (FCT). The driver was in the company of two other persons who fled upon sighting the abductors.
On 26 August 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked and killed a farmer who was returning from his farm in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara).

On 26 August 2023, a policemen foiled an attack by a Katsina militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Ruwan Lafiya village in Kankara (Katsina). One abductee was rescued, 94 cows, 17 sheep and two motorcycles were recovered. Casualties are unknown.

On 26 August 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked unarmed gate keepers at an oil spil site in Bodo (Gonaka, Rivers). Two of the victims were killed, five others escaped with various degrees of gunshot wounds. Other sources report that several other persons were missing.

On 26 August 2023, a soldier killed one person at Otto community (Lagos Mainland, Lagos) following a disagreement between locals and railway construction workers over a fence which the local claimed would obstruct a road in the community. The soldiers shot sporadically in the area.
On 27 August 2023, troops of 2 battalion engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kwana Shehu village in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). One militia member was killed and four abductees were rescued.

On 27 August 2023, an unidentified armed group that was dressed in military uniform abducted a man from his residence in Kofa village (Bebeji, Kano). The abductee is the center officer for the Kano state pilgrims welfare board in the local government area. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 27 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 18 civilians from along the Okigwi expressway (Okigwe, Imo) where they shot indiscriminately at a commercial bus.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted a commercial driver in Magumeri LGA (Borno). The abductee was released on 30 August after 2 million naira was paid as ransom.

On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants fired indiscriminately at commercial vehicles at an illegal vehicle checkpoint that the mounted along Gajiram-Maiduguri road (Nganzai, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted four civilians along Maiduguri-Monguno road (Guzamala, Borno) coded to Gudumbali. The militants had set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint along the road.
On 27 August 2023, ISWAP militants abducted four civilians when they attacked a commercial vehicle at Tasha Kashim village in Magumeri LGA (Borno).
On 27 August 2023, a Niger militia shot a man, wounded him and abducted his wife when they attacked Farin Shinge village in Kontagora LGA (Niger).

On 27 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged Nigerian troops whose position they attacked in an armed clash at Ngoshe village (Gwoza, Borno). Casualties are unknown and there are no further details.

On 27 August 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants were repelled by Nigerian troops when they attacked Bale general area (Damboa, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 28 August 2023, policemen killed a member of an unidentified armed group at Choba (Obio, Rivers) when he went to receive an additional ransom amount. The assailant's group had abducted and released a man after 2 million naira was paid, before making demands for an additional 3 million.

On 28 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted four farmers when they invaded their farmlands at Damfami (Kiyawa, Zamfara) coded to Birnin Magaji. There are no reports on ransom demands, farmers in the area abducted two milkmaids in retaliation [coded separately].

On 28 August 2023, a group of farmers from Birnin Magaji community abducted two milkmaids who were suspected to be Fulani in retaliation for the abduction of four farmers on the same day [coded separately] at Damfami (Kiyawa, Zamfara) coded to Birnin Magaji. The abduction of the women was an attempt by the farmers to open negotiations with the militia.

On 28 August 2023, two groups of maqurede supporters engaged in an armed clash at Aku community (Igbo Etiti, Enugu) following a disagreement over the date for closing the masquerade year. One person was killed, other sources report that at least 100 locals were hospitalized, the police claimed that one person was arrested and a firearm was retrieved from him.
On 28 August 2023, the Nigerian military attacked ISWAP fighters and killed one of them around Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno).

On 29 August 2023, presumed soldiers engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in the vicinity of Amagu Ishiagu and Lokpanta (Ivo, Ebonyi) coded to Ishiagu. One member of the group was killed, another was injured, three others were arrested. Two abductees were rescued and weapons were recovered.

On 29 August 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded Dan Umoru (Danko, Kebbi). The assailants were repelled, they escaped with gunshot wounds while one rocket launcher was recovered by the policemen.
On 29 August 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants ambushed a local defense militia that was on patrol in Mafa LGA (Borno). Three local defense militiamen were killed.
On 29 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from his residence in Janmbutu (Yola-North, Adamawa) coded to Yola.
On 29 August 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two persons and abducted eleven others at Unguwan Pete in Jere town (Kagarko, Kaduna). The abductees consisted of seven bakery workers and four tenants.
On 29 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a militia group suspected to be CJTF in Jakana (Bama, Borno). One of the militiamen was killed by ISWAP in the attack.

On 29 August 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at along Umuezorokam-Avu road (Owerri West, Imo) coded to Umuoguma. Two of the assailants were killed, others fled with various degrees of gunshot wounds and one abductee was rescued.
On 29 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 15 civilians at Magazu village (Tsafe, Zamfara) where they set up an illegal vehicle checkpoint.

On 29 August 2023, security operatives consisting mainly of policemen and suspected NDLEA operatives shot sporadically in an attempt to scare traders away at Timber and Allied industrial market in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). One trader was hit and killed by a stray bullet. The spokesperson of the NDLEA denied the operatives' participation, the police spokesperson claimed that the victim was not shot by policemen.

On 29 August 2023, a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideout in Elerinjare axis (Ifelodun, Kwara) coded to Share. One of the assailants was killed and five others were arrested.
On 30 August 2023, suspected armed pastoralists wounded a man and abducted his wife and daughter at a residence in Bumgai (Gujba, Yobe).

On 30 August 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian and abducted two others at Itapaji (Ikole, Ekiti). The abductees were released on 3 September, there are no reports on ransom demands and payment.
On 30 August 2023, former Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted six civilians from a farm in the vicinity of Jege village (Gwoza, Borno).
On 30 August 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a revenue collector in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). A student was also hit and killed by a stray bullet following the assailants' attack.

On 30 August 2023, a local defense militia numbering about 60 killed two Fulani pastoralists at Bungudu central market (Bungudu, Zamfara) when they invaded the market. The assailants targeted persons whom they accused of having links with militia activities within the area.

On 30 August 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they responded to a distress call around Borromeo roundabout in Onitsha (Onisha North, Anambra). One abductee was rescued, two of the assailants were arrested while others fled with gunshot wounds. One pistol, ammunition and the bus used by the assailants were recovered.
On 30 August 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a revenue collector around Okhoro junction in Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The attack is related to a cult war between different militias.
On 31 August 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two women from Dan Musa town (Dan-Musa, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 31 August 2023, a Katsina militia killed two civilians and abducted one other person at Tashar Icce (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa.
On 31 August 2023, the Nigerian military carried out a cross-border raid on an unnamed faction of Boko Haram coded to Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). Four militiamen were killed in the raid.

On 31 August 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted scores of passengers near Ochonyi village along Lokoja-Abuja highway (Lokoja, Kogi). The abductors shot at the tires of the buses that the abductees were travelling in and forced them to stop.
On 31 August 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a police outpost near Geidam (Geidam, Yobe) and captured the police vehicle. No report on fatality claims.

On 31 August 2023, the Nigerian military intercepted and killed six ISWAP fighters on the Molai- Damboa road close to Damboa (Damboa, Borno). They were intercepted on their way to Sambisa Forest. The military recovered AK-47 rifles, bicycles and other items from them.
On 31 August 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted at least 15 farmers from their farms in Moriki (Zurmi, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 31 August 2023, suspected Black Axe also called Aiye, Supreme Eiye Confraternity also called Eiye and Maphite militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy which led to the killing of 6 persons in different areas of Benin City (Oredo, Edo). The affected areas included Upper Mission, Okhun, Oluku and Aikhionbare.

On 31 August 2023, Nigerian troops in collaboration with Civilian JTF who were on a clearance operation ambushed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants who were transporting large quantities of logistics along Molai-Damboa road (Jere, Borno). Six militants were killed, one was captured alive while others escaped and the logistics were recovered by the troops.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a member of a local defense militia who is presumed to have been unarmed at Ankpa town (Ankpa, Kogi). Two other civilians were wounded by the assailants.
On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted at least 3 persons from their vehicles when they attacked Nkwelle Ezunaka junction and Umunya (Oyi, Anambra).

On 1 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two civilians when they attacked Teng and Pwaskop communities in Pushit district (Mangu, Plateau). The attack lasted for several hours, several houses were burnt and the assailants shot sporadically.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by So Safe operatives at Abule-Ori (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode when they attacked a church, killed a pastor and abducted seven parishioners. One of the assailants were killed, many of them sustained serious injuries, the abductees were rescued. The family of an abductee who was previously abducted claimed that the second person who was murdered was their relative not one of the assailants; he was taken to the location by the group and killed by the policemen over a mistaken identity.
On 1 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed a man while he was attending a wedding ceremony at Rakpami community in Toto LGA (Nassarawa). The victim was a farmer.

On 1 July 2023, Karimjo ethnic militia engaged Wurkum ethnic militia in an armed clash at Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba). At least 50 persons were killed; the police claimed two fatalities, scores of others were wounded, at least five villages were burnt and many domestic animals were stolen. The state government imposed a dusk to dawn curfew in the area.

On 1 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons on the road between Ogbomu and Egbe (Yagba West, Kogi). The victims who consisted of two siblings and the vehicle's driver were on transit when the abductors flagged down their vehicle. A ransom of two million naira was demanded.

On 2 July 2023, a policeman shot an artisan a few steps away from his house at Oregun (Epe, Lagos). The victim's family members rushed him to the nearby before the policeman came, threatened them with a gun and took the victim in his bus and went away. The victim was found dead later.

Around 2 July 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a woman and dumped her body near Tamigbe town (Burutu, Delta), after she was abducted from her home in the town a few days earlier. The victim's family paid 1 million naira as ransom before the assailants shot her in the forehead.
On 2 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person, wounded two and abducted two others when they attacked Garin Masau village in Safana LGA (Katsina).
On 2 July 2023, ISWAP fighters were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by MNJTF troops in Monguno town (Monguno, Borno). The clash lasted for up to one hour, casualties are unknown.

On 2 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed three persons at Jenuwa Nyifiye community in Takum LGA (Taraba). The assailants shot sporadically, while the police spokesperson in the state claimed that they were interrupted following measures by policemen and soldiers. Other sources report that 8 persons were killed, some of whom were burnt beyond recognition and that local defense militiamen attempted to repel the attack but were overpowered.

On 3 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed three farmers and abducted 15 others when they ambushed them on their farms at Gwaram village (Talata Mafara, Zamfara). The assailants claimed that the attack was in protest over the refusal of the new state government to negotiate with them. They were heard chanting in Hausa language saying 'they must negotiate with us now'.

On 3 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed an operative of the Benue community volunteer guards at a checkpoint in Ugba town (Logo, Benue). The assailants also abducted two people and robbed some other persons. Other sources report that the assailants were armed robbers.
On 3 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted an unspecified number of civilians from Magama town in Jibia LGA (Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 3 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed an unspecified number of persons, wounded and abducted others at Borin Dawa (Malumfashi, Katsina). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 3 July 2023, IPOB members from the Simon Ekpa faction abducted a commercial bus driver and set his bus ablaze in the vicinity of Ngwa road in Aba (Aba South, Abia) for disobeying a sit-in order.

On 3 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked worshippers who were returning from church and killed eight persons at Takum (Takum, Taraba). Houses were also set ablaze, the attack happened in from of the 83 battalion Ada Army barracks.

On 3 July 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops who repelled the militant's attempt to attack farmers in the vicinity of Wanori, Konduga LGA (Borno). The militants retreated, casualties are unknown.
Non-violent activity: On 3 July 2023, a Zamfara militia mounted an illegal vehicle checkpoint along the Magami-Gusau highway (Gusau, Zamfara).
On 4 July 2023, IPOB militants from Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order shot sporadically at policemen at a checkpoint in Isieke (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The policemen in the area fled.
On 4 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed a farmer on his farm and also stole from the victim's farm at Tse Uikpam (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba. Some other farmers were able to escape.

On 4 July 2023, IPOB militants from Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order killed three tricycle riders at Ishieke market in Abakaliki (Abakaliki, Ebonyi) and shot sporadically into the air when they invaded Afiaohu market along Abakaliki/Enugu expressway. The assailants were demanding the release of Nnamdi Kanu.

On 4 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives ambushed and engaged Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants in an armed clash at Mandara mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno). One militant commander was killed, one rifle with loaded ammunition was recovered.

On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order beat up teachers and primary school pupils at different locations across Enugu West senatorial district, coded to Awgu (Agwu, Enugu). The victims were flogged for not obeying the order.
On 5 July 2023, Amotekun corps and officials of NIS engaged in an armed clash at Oke Fia area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The cause of the clash and casualties are unknown.
On 5 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man at his residence in Imasayi community (Egbado North, Ogun) coded to Aiyetoro. The victim was macheted to pieces.

On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order were repelled by soldiers at Trans Ekulu (Enugu East, Enugu). The attackers managed to escape. There were no casualties.
On 5 July 2023, IPOB militants clashed with policemen at Abakpa, coded as Abakpa Nike (Enugu East, Enugu). One militant was killed.

On 5 July 2023, ISWAP militants raided the camp of Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters and engaged them in an armed clash at Bula Alhaji Garwaye in Bama LGA (Borno). Scores of Boko Haram fighters, their women and children were killed, a few of them escaped while their properties were looted by the ISWAP fighters. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 5 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a man who was accused of being a sorcerer at Bukarti in Yunusari LGA (Yobe). The militants claimed to have killed the victim in front of other villagers and given them a sermon on the dangers of sorcery to Islam.

On 5 July 2023, two unidentified cult militias clashed and killed one person at Oke-Apomu quarters in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). The clash was preparatory to the 7/7 anniversary of the militias, the victim was killed when his older brother who was the target was not found at home when the assailants arrived.

On 5 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one woman and wounded another when they attacked Kwahas community in Kombun district (Mangu, Plateau). The assailants were passing along the Mangu-Bokkos road and attacked the residents when they reached the village.

On 5 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a lawyer and the welfare Secretary of the Nigerian Bar Association after they abducted him from his house in Kwatarkwashi (Bungudu, Zamfara). The victim was taken away and his body was found along the road with several machete injuries. The victim was also the candidate of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP).

On 5 July 2023, Black Axe militia also known as Aiye confraternity and SEC militia engaged in an armed clash at Bariga (Somolu, Lagos) following a clash over the annual 7/7 celebration. Three militia members were killed, one was wounded and in a coma, the clash spread to other areas and passers-by were wounded at the Somolu area. Other sources report that the clash was between two factions of Black Axe militia, and that 5 persons were killed.

On 5 July 2023, Ebube Agu operatives and policemen engaged in an armed clash at the Imo state secretariat in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo) when a group of policemen bullied an Ebube Agu operative who in turn invited his colleagues to defend him. Scores of persons who were trying to flee were wounded as a result of a stampede.

On 6 July 2023, Ishinkwo and Abba-Omega communal militias engaged in an armed clash and seven locals from Abba Omega were killed. Location coded to Abba Omega (Onicha, Ebonyi). The police spokesperson in the state denied the report of a clash and killings.
On 6 July 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants abducted a farmer at Dalori (Konduga, Borno). The abductee was a displaced person who was working as a small scale farmer.

On 6 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked civilians at Kogul community in Panyam district (Mangu, Plateau) and killed five persons. An unspecified number of others were wounded and several houses were burnt.
On 6 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted 10 civilians from Kasai village in Batsari LGA (Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 6 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one woman and wounded another when they attacked Milet community in Kombun district (Mangu, Plateau) in their numbers.
On 6 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person in the vicinity of Pole Wire, along Jos-Abuja highway in Riyom LGA (Plateau).

On 7 July 2023, policemen raided the hideout of an unidentified cult militia and were engaged in an armed clash at Obelle town (Emohua, Rivers). Six militiamen were killed, six were arrested while others ran in different directions with bullet wounds.

On 7 July 2023, policemen repelled an attack by a Katsina militia on a Fulani settlement in Unguwan Rogo (Danja, Katsina) and Rafin Gora [coded separately]. One militiaman was killed, two others were arrested and over 100 cattle were recovered. Fatalities split between the two locations, coded as 1.
On 7 July 2023, suspected IPOB militants who were enforcing a sit-in order shot indiscriminately in the vicinity of Nkwelle Ezunaka community (Oyi, Anambra). Casualties are unknown.

On 7 July 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia fired indiscriminately and wounded an unspecified number of people around the Igbariam campus (Anambra East, Anambra) of Chukwuemeka Odumegu Ojukwu university.

On 7 July 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted three farmers at Dalori (Konduga, Borno) while they were ploughing the field. The militants had also abducted one farmer the previous day [coded separately].
On 7 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed two policemen when they attacked Sakajiki and Sabon Gida (Kaura Namoda, Zamfara). One civilian was abducted.

On 7 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit in order engaged in an armed clash with policemen at Awkunanaw (Enugu South, Enugu) coded to Obeagu Awkunanaw. Four of the militants were killed, others fled with bullet wounds, weapons, ammunition, two petrol bombs and other items were recovered. Other sources report that 5 militants were killed.
On 7 July 2023, Black Axe militia killed three members of SVC who are presumed to have been unarmed in different parts of Auchi (Etsako West, Edo) in a reprisal attack.

On 7 July 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering five abducted a businesswoman from her store at Mile 2, Diobu (Port Harcourt, Rivers). The abductors demanded for money and abducted the victim when she was unable to provide the amount they demanded. They shot sporadically before taking her away. The abductee was released on 14 July, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 7 July 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering over 60 led by a land grabber attacked residents of Ipetu Baba Ode community along Idiroko road (Ipokia, Ogun) . Many of the residents were shot and wounded, many others were missing. Other sources report that one of the victims was in a coma as a result of the attack.

On 7 July 2023, operatives of Operation Rainbow and a Mwaghavul ethnic militia attacked over eight Fulani settlements in Mangu LGA (Plateau) as claimed by MACBAN. 15 pastoralists were killed, 78 hamlets were razed and over 2000 cows and several other livestock were missing. MACBAN added that the operatives attacked in an armored tank while the militia set the hamlets ablaze.

On 7 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians and killed three persons at Adogo Ugbaam (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera. After killing the three civilians, the assailants also invaded a local market in the community. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 7 July 2023, policemen repelled an attack by a Katsina militia on a Fulani settlement in Rafin Gora (Danja, Katsina) and Unguwan Rogo [coded separately]. One militiaman was killed, two others were arrested and over 100 cattle were recovered. Fatalities split between the two locations, coded as 0.

On 7 July 2023, troops of 223 Battalion operating under sector 1 of operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Kabugu Lamba village in Maru LGA (Zamfara). Four militiamen were killed, 24 abductees were rescued.
On 7 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted the wife of a traditional ruler in Maru LGA (Zamfara). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 July 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye and Supreme Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Somolu (Somolu, Lagos) during the preparation to celebrate the 777 day. The clash began at Idi-Aba area [coded separately] and spread to Akilo, Sungas and Olorunkemi street in Somolu, an unspecified number of passers-by were wounded.
On 7 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot indiscriminately in the vicinity of Nwagu community, Agulu (Aniocha, Anambra). Casualties are unknown.

On 8 July 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in armed clash with soldiers at Tine-Nune community on the Zaki Biam-Wukari road (Ukum, Benue) after they fled from the villages where they attacked civilians at Zaki Akpunna I and Diom [coded separately]. Casualties are unknown.
On 8 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted two civilians when they attacked Janbako (Maradun, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 8 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted three civilians when they attacked Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.
Around 8 July 2023 (as reported), a Katsina militia abducted one civilian at a housing estate in Kankia town (Kankia, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 8 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the Ekiti state chairman of the APC along the Agbado-Imesi-Ekiti road (Aiyekire, Ekiti). The victim was driving along the road when they abductors shot at the tires of his car before he was taken away. A ransom of 20 million naira was demanded; the abductee and two others whom other sources reported were abducted alongside him were released around 13 July. There are no reports on ransom payment and the police claimed three persons were arrested in connection with the abduction.

On 8 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit in order killed a commercial tricycle at Akwakuma intersection (Owerri North, Imo) coded to Uratta. The militants shot sporadically in the air and the people in the area fled. Some sources report that two people were killed, others reported that a part of the Orie Amaraku market, together with vehicle parked there were set ablaze.

On 8 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed nine people and set six houses ablaze at Sabon Gari community in Mangu LGA (Plateau). Many other properties were destroyed and some sources claimed operatives of Operation Rainbow brought the situation under control [mode of response not mentioned].

On 8 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Zaki Akpunna I and Diom (Ukum, Benue) coded to Sankera. The assailants killed at least 24 civilians, which later increased to 30 following the discovery of more corpses and the death of some of the badly injured victims. The attackers set villages ablaze before fleeing.
On 9 July 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted six civilians from Saja village in Dogon Daji district (Tambuwal, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 9 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Farin Lamba community in Vwang district (Jos South, Plateau). Eight civilians including an eight-month old baby were killed.
On 9 July 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a civilian while he was coming out of church in Benin City (Oredo, Edo).

On 9 July 2023, Nigerian troops attacked and overpowered (no further information) a Kebbi militia (described as bandits) along the Danko/Wasagu axis, coded to the LGA HQ, Ribah (Danko, Kebbi). Casualties unknown.

Around 10 July 2023 (as reported), policemen from the Bauchi state command engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they raided their hideouts in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). Two members of the group and one informant were killed, two other informants were arrested.

On 10 July 2023, IPOB militants from the Simon Ekpa faction who were enforcing a sit-in order were engaged in an armed clash with policemen at Umuobona Uburu, coded to Uburu (Ohaozara, Ebonyi). One of the assailants was killed, other sources report that other militants fled with varying degrees of bullet wounds.

On 10 July 2023, policemen beat up two civilians at Warri along Port Harcourt-Okuokoko (Warri South, Delta) and extorted 53 thousand naira from them. The victims claimed that the attack was over some cannabis that was found with one of them.

On 10 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic Chancellor and three other persons close to his parish at Mgbaleze Isu, coded to Isu (Onicha, Ebonyi) while he was on the way back from pastoral duties. The abductees were released on 11 July, the Diocesan Chancellor claimed that they were released unconditionally.

On 10 July 2023, a Zamfara militia ambushed policemen at a checkpoint and engaged them in an armed clash along Bungudu-Gusau (Bungudu, Zamfara). Four policemen were killed, the clash took place around midnight.

On 10 July 2023, an unidentified armed group of six were engaged in an armed clash by policemen and hunters at Fere village (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode after they attempted to abduct a civilian. Two members of the group were killed and the others fled.

On 10 July 2023, Marlian boys cult militia wounded many people, burned shops and destroyed properties in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). The attack was a reprisal on a shop owner who stabbed a member of the group during a fight between them.
On 10 July 2023, a Zamfara militia shot one civilian in the hand and rustled many cattle at Tagero village in Furifuri district (Bungudu, Zamfara).
On 10 July 2023, ISWAP militants fired mortar shells that were targeted at Nigerian troops at Buni Yadi (Gujba, Yobe). There was no impact from the shelling.

On 10 July 2023, Black Axe militia also called Aiye confraternity and Maphites engaged in an armed clash in Oluku, Uselu-Ugbowo axis of Benin City (Oredo, Edo). Three persons were killed. The assailants also hit a policeman with their car and snatched his rifle.

On 11 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a businessman at his residence in Balele village Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The victim was killed for refusing to open the door for the assailants.

On 11 July 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged by policemen and the operatives of the state vigilante services in an armed clash at Ichida community (Aniocha, Anambra). Two members of the group were killed, a female abductee was rescued, weapons, ammunition and the victim's car were recovered.
On 11 July 2023, troops of 195 battalion killed an unspecified number of Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants in the axis of Mafa LGA (Borno). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 11 July 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants killed a farmer, injured another and abducted a woman at Banki (Bama, Borno). The abductee was taken through the axis of Kumshe and Kote where she will be held hostage.

On 11 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at a joint security team presumed to have consisted of policemen and soldiers at a checkpoint along Uga-Ezinifite expressway (Aguata, Anambra) in an attempt to evade a security check. The assailants fled, the security team recovered one car, guns and ammunition. There were no casualties.

Around 11 July 2023 (as reported), a Kebbi militia (described as bandits) abducted 30 people in Danko LGA, coded to the LGA HQ in Ribah (Danko, Kebbi). The abductees were rescued by Nigerian troops on 11 July 2023 (no reports of interaction/clashes).
On 12 July 2023, a security operative presumed to be policeman killed a farmer at Mandarari community (Konduga, Borno) when he attempted to cross a trench to his farm.
On 12 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three people and abducted an unspecified number of others when they attacked Amuro (Okigwe, Imo).

On 12 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a police checkpoint and shot at policemen near Evwreni axis (Ughelli North, Delta). One policeman was killed, his rifle was stolen, the other policemen escaped. The spokesperson of the state police command denied the report and claimed there was no attack.

On 12 July 2023, troops of 3 division Haven, Operation raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash along Mangu-Pushit road (Mangu, Plateau). Three members of the group were killed, an unspecified number fled, three rifles, a police constabulary identity card and items were recovered.
On 12 July 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired indiscriminately on a farm at Galtimari, Konduga LGA (Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 13 July 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one person and abducted two others at Isanlu-Isin town (Osin, Kwara). The wounded victim was shot because he was unable to walk when the assailants attempted to abduct him while the abductees were a clergyman and his father.

On 13 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman as she was returning from a market in Ijebu-Ode (Ijebu Ode, Ogun). The abductee was rescued by operatives of So Safe Corps on 15 July [coded separately].

On 13 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed or wounded an unspecified number of travelers when they attacked commuters between Uturu and Okigwi (Okigwe, Imo). An unspecified number of the commuters were abducted, unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 13 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a businessman from his residence in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 13 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted two civilians when they attacked Katoge quarters in Batsari town (Batsari, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 July 2023, operatives of Nigeria Customs Service shot at the car of the chief of staff of the Katsina state governor around Gorar Yammama, coded to Yammama (Malumfashi, Katsina) as he was traveling alongside his driver. There were no casualties, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 13 July 2023, Nigerian troops engaged in an armed clash with ISWAP fighters at Awada in Mafa (Borno). Two fighters were killed, two others were arrested and one civilian was rescued.

On 13 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor from a hospital at Atimbo area (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The abductors had pretended to be in need of medical attention before the abduction of the victim. They also seized the phones of onlookers and the gate keepers. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 14 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed two people and wounded four others at Yan Nakwari village in Kurfi LGA (Katsina).

On 14 July 2023, a Zamfara militia engaged in an armed clash with troops of Operation Hadarin Daji in Mailere village, Gwashi district (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). Nine abductees were rescued, casualties are unknown.
On 14 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attempted to abduct a civilian at Maitama (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The assailants were arrested by policemen, there are no reports of a clash.
On 14 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a man at his residence in Tsauni area of Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara).
On 14 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed seven people including four children when they attacked Nakwari village in Barkiya district (Kurfi, Katsina).

On 15 July 2023, operatives of So Safe corps engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Oke-Ako (Ijebu Ode, Ogun) after the group abducted a woman on 13 July [coded separately]. One member of the group was arrested and the abductee was rescued and one pistol was recovered.

Around 15 July 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a man from Angware (Jos East, Plateau). The victim was released after the person who went to deliver his ransom was abducted and murdered [coded separately].

On 15 July 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be land grabbers who numbered over 50 killed a chief in Lotu town (Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos) coded to Lekki. The victim's wife claimed that she was also assaulted by the assailants when she attempted to shield her husband from attack.

On 15 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her son at Ota Efun area of Oshogbo (Osogbo, Osun). The abductees were released at Ikirun the following day, the husband of the abductee claimed that no ransom was paid.
On 15 July 2023, a Katsina militia shot indiscriminately at Yan Maradi/ Unguwar Ude quarters in Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). Two civilians were wounded and eight others including a baby were abducted.

On 15 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a military checkpoint at Tungushe (Jere, Borno) which forced the soldiers station there to flee. They also claimed to have captured a medium machine gun. There were no casualties.
On 15 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed at least three persons and stole properties from Hayin Magaji community Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara).
On 15 July 2023, a Katsina militia shot and killed the village head of Gyazamar Barebari in Dandume LGA (Katsina) when they invaded the area.

On 16 July 2023, an unidentified armed group who rode motorbikes killed 6 civilians when they invaded Igba-Ukyor and Tse Baka communities (Ushongo, Benue) coded to Lessel. Five persons were killed at Igba-Ukyor and one ate Tse-Baka.
On 16 July 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot and killed the PDP councilor representing Eha-Ulo ward at his residence in Eha-Alumona ward (Nsukka, Enugu).
On 16 July 2023, a Sokoto militia killed at least five persons and vandalized properties when they attacked Gayeji (Gudu, Sokoto) coded to Balle.
On 16 July 2023, a Katsina militia shot and wounded two civilians in Babban Duhu A community (Safana, Katsina).
On 16 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked people working on a farmland and killed one person along Isa-Sokoto road (Isa, Sokoto). Two others were wounded.
On 16 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a policeman at Maradun town (Maradun, Zamfara).

On 16 July 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged an unidentified armed group of 6 to 7 persons in an armed clash at Mpape (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The assailants had abducted two civilians who were rescued by the police, the assailants fled. There were no casualties.

On 17 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted eight passengers near Oben (Orhionwon, Edo) as they were traveling from Sapele to Asaba. The driver and one passenger of the vehicle that was attacked escaped, the abductees include the daughter of a newspaper vendor who claimed that a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded for her release.

On 17 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed the traditional ruler of Nguru (Aboh Mbaise, Imo) at his palace. The victim died at a hospital due to the injuries he sustained after he was shot severally.

On 17 July 2023, a Civilian JTF operative fired several shots and wounded an unspecified number of Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants who attempted to rob shops at Yan-dandari village in Konduga (Borno). The operative recovered two rifles which he submitted to Nigerian troops.
On 17 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked two settlements in Balle community (Gudu, Sokoto). There are no further details and casualties are unknown.

On 17 July 2023, ISWAP militants engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash along Sabon Gari- Waijroko road (Damboa, Borno) after detonating an IED targeted at the troops. One armored vehicle was damaged, several people were wounded and ISWAP claimed the attack.

On 17 July 2023, ISWAP militants attack Nigerian troops at a checkpoint in Njimtilo (Magumeri, Borno) which led to the troops' escape. ISWAP claimed to have captured some equipment from the troops, casualties are unknown.

On 17 July 2023, soldiers, policemen and DSS operatives responded to a distress call and engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at Fuji junction general area in Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta). Two militants were killed and five others were arrested while weapons, cartridges and a boafeng radio receiver were recovered by the troops.

On 18 July 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted a woman while she was working on her farm at Amaonye community in Ishiagu (Ivo, Ebonyi). The abductee was released on 24 July, following a search by security agents, there are no reports on ransom payment or an armed clash.

On 18 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia shot sporadically at travelers in an 18-seater bus at the Ekwegbe section along the Enugu-Ugwogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Igbo Etiti, Enugu) during an attempted to abduct them. Two of the passengers were wounded and all the passengers escaped.

On 18 July 2023, suspected IPOB militants engaged in an armed clash with policemen and a local defense militia when they attacked the palace of a traditional ruler at Amaifeke (Orlu, Imo). The militants fled with varying degrees of injuries, one defense militia member was killed after he sustained bullet wounds and one other was wounded.
On 18 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked commuters along Gandi-Bakura road (Rabah, Sokoto) and wounded one person. One other person was abducted.
On 18 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked people working on a farmland and killed two persons along Isa-Sokoto road (Isa, Sokoto).
On 18 July 2023, a Sokoto militia shot and wounded a boy as he was passing through a farmland in Tukudawa (Isa, Sokoto).

On 18 July 2023, suspected IPOB militants engaged policemen in an armed clash when they attacked the police divisional headquarters at Ikem (Isi Uzo, Enugu). The militants who screamed 'release Nnamdi Kanu' and 'no Nnamdi Kanu no peace' stole arms and ammunition from the station's armory before they fled, the police claimed that the attack was repelled. There were no fatalities.

On 18 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia were engaged in an armed clash by security personnel stationed at Gwarim who repelled the militia's attack on civilians at Wereng, Kuru Station, Gwon, Rinyan and Gwarim in Riyom LGA (Plateau). The militia killed three civilians before they were repelled.

On 19 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a school teacher in Barkin Ladi (Barkin Ladi, Plateau) as he was about to close his shop. The assailants also robbed the victim's wife in their residence which was beside the shop.

On 19 July 2023, troops of the forward operating base in Anka engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Makakari village in Gwashi district (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). Two militiamen were killed and their weapons were recovered.

On 19 July 2023, troops of sector 1 team 3 of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Dan Sadau (Maru, Zamfara). Several militiamen were killed and 20 abductees were rescued, fatalities coded as 3.

Around 19 July 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia attacked a bridal party and abducted two persons near Kafin Koro (Paikoro, Niger). Other members of the bridal party fled into the bush while the abductees later escaped.

Around 19 July 2023 (between 17 July - 20 July), policemen in collaboration with hunters went on a routine patrol and clashed with an unidentified armed group at Dutsen Sidi, Zanya, Zori, Kafin Gora, Dukutu in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). Two members of the armed group were killed, one was arrested and the others fled with bullet wounds, 10 abductees were rescued. Two fatalities were split across two events coded as 1.

Around 19 July 2023 (between 17 July - 20 July), policemen in collaboration with hunters went on a routine patrol and clashed with an unidentified armed group at Runu, Kwapto, Gwari, Rafin Gora, Jimi and Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). Two members of the armed group were killed, one was arrested and the others fled with bullet wounds, 10 abductees were rescued. Two fatalities were split across two events coded as 1.
On 19 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed a civilian and abducted an unspecified number of others when they attacked Jibia town (Jibia, Katsina).
On 19 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed a man that was accused of being a government appointed agent at Futchimiram (Geidam, Yobe).
On 19 July 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of persons from Bunkari ward (Binji, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 19 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed three civilians and rustled livestock when they attacked Kikkibawa village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 20 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives invaded the hideouts of Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Bula Daloye, Bulongu Dina and Mairamiri Dina in Bama LGA (Borno). Eight militants were killed, others fled, women and children were rescued by the troops.

On 20 July 2023, policemen raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and were engaged in an armed clash in Emohua LGA (Rivers). One member of the group was killed, another was arrested, many others fled with injuries while a gun and 22 cartridges were recovered.

On 20 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one pastoralist and abducted two others in a Fulani settlement near Dnago village in Gwargwada chiefdom (Kuje, FCT). The murdered victim had attempted to escape after he was abducted when the assailants shot and killed him.
On 20 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person from Kinfau village in Safana LGA (Katsina).

On 20 July 2023, troops of sector 2 team 9 of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash while on a fighting patrol at Gobirawa Garin Ruji in Batsari LGA (Katsina). Four militiamen were killed and their weapons were recovered.

On 20 July 2023, ISWAP militants on motorcycles, foot and anti-aircraft gun fitted vehicles were engaged in an armed clash with troops of Sector 3 of the MNJTF when they attacked Monguno town (Monguno, Borno). ISWAP claimed to have wounded several troops and seized a medium machine gun.

On 20 July 2023, troops of Sector 1, forward operating base of Operation Hadarin Daji ambushed and clashed with a Zamfara militia at Bagabuzu crossing point between Maradun LGA (Zamfara) and Talata Mafara axis. Two militiamen were killed, other sources report four killed, rifles and ammunition were recovered by the troops.
On 21 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two residents when they attacked Tamba village (Ningi, Bauchi).

On 21 July 2023, a suspected Fulani militia engaged a team of policemen, hunters and local defense militia who were on a rescue mission in an armed clash at Isanlu-Isin (Osin, Kwara). The assailants shot and killed two abductees in an attempt to escape, some of the assailants were wounded, one abductee was rescued while two of the assailants were arrested.
On 21 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two residents of Kafin Lemo (Ningi, Bauchi). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 21 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Faru, likely refering to Faru Magami, a ward in Maradun LGA, coded to known village in the ward, Magami Diddi (Maradun, Zamfara). At least four members of the militia were killed, and an unspecified number escaped with bullet wounds.
On 21 July 2023, a Zamfara militia that was dressed in military uniform shot and wounded four commuters when they blocked the Anka-Bagega road (Anka, Zamfara).

On 21 July 2023, armed Fulani pastoralists abducted and killed a farmer whom they ambushed on the way to his farm at Isanlu (Yagba East, Kogi). The victim whose corpse was found two days later by hunters and local defense militiamen, was ambushed alongside his brother who escaped. The attack was as a result of a dispute over grazing on his farm. The youths in the community carried out a reprisal [coded separately].

On 21 July 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed a policeman who is presumed to have been off-duty near his home at Alasia community in Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos). The attack was a result of a misunderstanding between the assailants and the victim, whose body was found with injuries inflicted with axes on his head. The police claimed that one suspect was arrested.
On 21 July 2023, IPOB militants killed two Neighbourhood Watch operatives at Umuagama in Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu).

On 21 July 2023, 40 youths armed with guns, iron rods and cutlasses attacked a warehouse, several shops, offices and a radio station in Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba) where they looted and destroyed properties including food items. police forces intervened, fired shots to disperse the looters and in the process two were shot dead.

Around 21 July 2023 (as reported), a Zamfara militia beat up an unspecified number of persons in Danbaza community (Maradun, Zamfara) for refusing to give them directions to the house of a popular food vendor. The militiamen also abducted four persons consisting of three females and one male who were relatives of a politician who was the target but was away when the militia arrived. A ransom of 80 million naira was demanded for their release.
On 21 July 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted twenty eight civilians from Unguwar Bawa in Randangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The abductees included women and children.
On 21 July 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked Homawa village in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). Casualties are unknown and there are no further details.

On 21 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the director of news at the Rivers state broadcasting corporation while she was on her way home from work and in the company of her husband in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). A ransom of 150 million naira was demanded, the ransom was reduced to 10 million naira and the abductee was rescued on 27 July. The police spokesperson in the state denied knowledge of ransom payment and claimed that the abductee was rescued after policemen chased after the abductors.
On 21 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian whose corpse was found along Damaturu Stadium-Maiduguri road (Maiduguri Metro, Borno).
On 21 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed five people and abducted 16 others when they attacked Jihia village in Maradun LGA (Zamfara).

On 21 July 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be opposition to the traditional monarch attacked widows in front of the monarch's palace in Oworonsoki (Kosofe, Lagos) as they were receiving benefits. An unspecified number of people were wounded.
On 22 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed one civilian when they attacked Kankia town (Kankia, Katsina). The assailants also abducted one boy whom they released before they fled from the area.

On 22 July 2023, Aladja and Ogbe-Ijoh communal militias engaged in an armed clash and shot sporadically on the road leading to Ogbe-Ijoh (Warri South, Delta). Two persons from each of the communities were killed, many others sustained injuries and both parties claimed that the other was the aggressor. Aladja community claimed that two of the wounded victims were shot by soldiers who were aiding Ogbe-Ijoh community.

On 22 July 2023, an unidentified armed group in large numbers wounded three to four security guards who attempted to prevent them from gaining entrance into the house of a former minister in Ola, Akwanga LGA (Nassarawa). The assailants who spoke in Hausa shot sporadically and scaled the fence of the compound to gain entrance, the minister claimed that the attack was the third on his residence. There were no casualties.

On 22 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted travelers from two vehicles along Ngodo-Isuochi road (Nneochi, Abia). The Army director of public relations claimed that 13 abductees were rescued by troops who conducted search and rescue operations for two days.

On 22 July 2023, a Katsina militia were engaged in an armed clash with policemen and a local defense militia on the outskirts of Kwari village in (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. The militia fled, one person was killed.

On 22 July 2023, troops of 63 brigade garrison carried out clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants in an armed clash at their hideout in Asaba (Oshimili South, Delta). The militants fled, weapons and other items were recovered by the troops who also destroyed the militants' camp. Casualties are unknown.
On 22 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted five siblings from Mada community (Gusau, Zamfara). The abductees included four females and one male.

On 22 July 2023, Nigerian troops responded to a distress call and arrested two members of an unidentified armed group at Makabat village in Bokkos LGA (Plateau). Two locally fabricated rifles were also recovered. No casualties.
On 22 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked commuters along Igarra-Ibillo road (Akoko Edo, Edo). One person was killed, the two others in the car were abducted.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two private security operatives who were guarding a herbalist in Oba (Idemili South, Anambra). The herbalist was abducted, a ransom of 300 million was demanded, it was paid together with an additional 50 million naira before the abductee was released on 29 July.
On 23 July 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted a man from his residence in Kebbe town (Kebbe, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three policemen who were on a stop and search duty by the Ole roundabout (Isoko South, Delta) and set the police van ablaze. It is unclear whether the assailants stole the policemen's rifles, other sources report that the rifles of the policemen were stolen and that the assailants were suspected armed robbers. Two out of the six assailants were arrested by the police.

On 23 July 2023, soldiers in collaboration with hunters and operatives of Anambra state vigilante service conducted clearance operations and engaged IPOB militants and an unidentified armed group in armed clashes at their hideouts in Umuem Anam (Anambra East, Anambra) coded to Otuocha. At least six armed group members were killed, nine persons other including one IPOB member were arrested. IPOB claimed that the raided camps belong to criminal groups and not ESN.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor and one unidentified woman while they were on duty at Ugbaam (Ukum, Benue). The abductees were going to supervise a project in the area when they were abducted, there are no reports on ransom demands. The doctor was released on around 27 August, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified cult militia shot and wounded three students in Ilesa (Ilesha West, Osun) while they were charging their phones in a barber's shop. Other sources report that the assailants were engaged in a fraternity war with a rival group in the area, the victims sustained serious injuries.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five travelers at Andaha village, coded to nearby Akwanga (Akwanga, Nassarawa). The abductees were abandoned by the abductors over fear that a joint military patrol team were closing in on them.
On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the chief security officer of Efab Estate at Apo, Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT) and wounded at least three others.

On 23 July 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged a Niger militia of about 100 who were moving herds of cattle in an armed clash at Garun Gabas (Rafi, Niger). Two militiamen were killed, two security operatives were wounded, three villagers including a nursing mother and her child were abducted by the militia before looting an unspecified number of cows. Some cows were recovered by the policemen. Other sources report that the militiamen set one police vehicle, a private car and residents' properties ablaze.

Around 23 July 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group shot and wounded the driver of the Olu of Odeda along the Ikija axis (Obafemi, Ogun) of Abeokuta-Ibadan expressway. The Olu was almost abducted by the assailants.
On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group raped a female student at knife and gunpoint inside a primary healthcare center in Ughelli North LGA (Delta) coded to Ughelli.
On 23 July 2023, Marlian boys attacked and killed an off-duty police constable in Maiduguri (Maiduguri Metro, Borno). 10 persons were arrested by the police in connection with the attack.

On 23 July 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed Toto militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Utu-Okpaka in Toto LGA (Nassarawa) when they attempted to rescue timber operators that were attacked by the group. The defense militia commander and one other person were killed, the LGA chairman shutdown forests and suspended tree cutting activities.

On 23 July 2023, ISWAP militants attacked civilians at Jokka and Modu Gullori villages (Mobbar, Borno). The head of the villages was wounded, seven residents consisting of three males and four females were abducted.

On 23 July 2023, ISWAP militants were engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops when they attempted to attack Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). The militants withdrew and fled towards the axis of Ma'afa village, casualties are unknown.
On 23 July 2023, a Sokoto militia killed 1 person, wounded 2 others when they attacked Gidan Makera village in Illela LGA (Sokoto) and fired indiscriminately.

On 24 July 2023, scores of a Zamfara militia attacked and killed four farmers at Mairairai farming area in Gwashi/Adabka ward (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The assailants ordered the farmers to leave the fields, and abducted around a dozen others in an attack that lasted six hours. Fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 24 July 2023, scores of a Zamfara militia attacked and killed four farmers at Mairairai farming area in Adabka/Gwashi ward (Bukkuyum, Zamfara). The assailants ordered the farmers to leave the fields, and abducted around a dozen others in an attack that lasted six hours. Fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 24 July 2023, scores of a Zamfara militia attacked residents at Ruwan-Kura, Farar-Kankara, Tungar-Maigunya, Tungar-Jauro, Tungar-Maiguru, Kuryar-Mari and Tajaye in Zauma (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Zarummai wards [coded separately]. The attack lasted six hours across Mairairai including at Adabka and Gwashi wards [coded separately], hundreds of residents of the areas fled and one of them claimed that the assailants insisted on attacking civilians until the government stops killing their militia. Casualties are unknown.

On 24 July 2023, scores of a Zamfara militia attacked residents at Ruwan-Kura, Farar-Kankara, Tungar-Maigunya, Tungar-Jauro, Tungar-Maiguru, Kuryar-Mari and Tajaye in Zarummai (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) and Zauma wards [coded separately]. The attack lasted six hours across Mairairai including at Adabka and Gwashi wards [coded separately], hundreds of residents of the areas fled and one of them claimed that the assailants insisted on attacking civilians until the government stops killing their militia. Casualties are unknown.
On 24 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two civilians, wounded one person and abducted one other person when they attacked Tashan Mai-Turare in Girei LGA (Adamawa).

On 24 July 2023, soldiers and hunters engaged IPOB militants and an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in their hideouts at Awoko and Mmiata Anam communities (Anambra East, Anambra) coded to Otuocha. The security operatives were alerted to the area based on reports of the camps of the armed groups in the area, many armed group members and one IPOB militant were killed, others fled to their camp where the clash continued, some items were recovered and others were set ablaze. One militant was arrested, unknown fatalities coded as 3. IPOB claimed that the raided camps belong to criminal groups and not ESN.

On 24 July 2023, a Zamfara militia led by Ali Kachalla ambushed soldiers who were responding to a distress call and engaged them in an armed clash at Kangon Garacce community in Dan Gulbi district (Maru, Zamfara). Seven soldiers and 19 to 22 residents were killed, an unspecified number of others were wounded by the militia who split themselves into groups during the attack. Other sources report that 6 soldiers, one policeman, 20 defense militia men were killed, two other soldiers were missing in action and that the militiamen were led by Ali Kawajo, Damina and Black.
On 24 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man on his farm at Iregun (Obokun, Osun). A ransom of 30 million naira which was later reduced to 15 million was demanded.
On 24 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five civilians, two of whom were later released around Ikija axis of Abeokuta-Ibadan road (Obafemi, Ogun).
On 24 July 2023, ISWAP militants abducted about 7 Fulani pastoralists when they snuck into Monguno town (Monguno, Borno) through the axis of Ajilari. There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 24 July 2023 (as reported), ISWAP militants abducted an unspecified number of Fulani pastoralists at Garere village in Gudumbali (Guzamala, Borno). The militants demanded a ransom of 40 million naira for the release of the abductees.

On 24 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a checkpoint of the Nigerian army, wounded one soldier and forced others to withdraw at Pulka (Gwoza, Borno). The militants also claimed to have seized a rifle.

On 24 July 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked troops of Operation Hadarin Daji and engaged them in an armed clash at Kango Sabuwal village in Wanke district (Gusau, Zamfara). Seven militiamen were killed, one machine gun, ammunition and 6 motorcycles were recovered by the troops when they repelled the attack.

On 24 July 2023, policemen attached to the Ife-Olukotun division in collaboration with a local defense militia [coded as KSVS] engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash after the group abducted a civilian at Ife-Olukotun (Yagba East, Kogi). Two members of the group were killed, one abductee was rescued, one rifle and 19 rounds of ammunition were recovered.

On 24 July 2023, officials of the DSS and correctional services clashed at a federal high court in Lagos (Lagos Island, Lagos) over whose custody the suspended CBN governor will be given after his trial as both services wanted the governor to be in their custody. There were no casualties.

On 25 July 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash along Jannaret-Washina-Changal and Gyambwas (Mangu, Plateau). The assailants fled, 3 motorcycles and one gun were recovered by the troops. No casualties.

On 25 July 2023, Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] abducted six women including five young girls from Boda (Mobbar, Borno) coded to Damasak. The abductees were taken across the Komadougou river, to Niger.
On 25 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two national forest park officers at Boni community (Olorunsogo, Oyo) coded to Igbetti.

On 25 July 2023, soldiers, policemen and a local defense militia engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Erawah village (Isoko North, Delta) after the group attacked policemen at Ole roundabout [coded separately]. One member of the group was killed, others fled with bullet wounds and were trailed to a spot where one rifle was recovered.
On 25 July 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted two persons near Eka farm in Birnin Gwari (Kaduna).

On 25 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man, his wife and driver at Ikija village (Obafemi, Ogun) after they ambushed them as they were traveling to Abeokuta from Olodo and shot sporadically into the air. The man was the immediate past provost of the FCE Osiele, his wife was later released by the abductors and there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 25 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted a woman and her son from their residence at Saminaka community, along Gusau-Sokoto road (Gusau, Zamfara).

On 25 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted at least 35 people when they attacked farms in Nahuta, Madogara, Dan Tsuntsu, Zamfarawa and Salihar Dadare villages in Batsari LGA (Katsina). The abductees included women and children.

On 25 July 2023, ISWAP militants who were manning a checkpoint killed seven men after they were accused of smuggling drugs into the militants' territory. Location coded to Borno Yesu (Magumeri, Borno) which is a boundary between Gubio and Magumeri.

On 25 July 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the convoy of the commissioner for trade and commerce and engaged the policemen attached to it in an armed clash near Faulks road in Aba (Aba South, Abia). Two policemen were killed, one car on the convoy was set ablaze, policemen returned to the area, fired teargas canisters and gunshots in the air. Other sources report that the policemen wounded civilians and destroyed properties. The police claimed to have arrested 3 suspects.

On 25 July 2023, ISWAP militants killed 20 Fulani pastoralists whom they accused of trespassing at the Kukawa axis (Kukawa, Borno). The militants killed 14 pastoralists earlier by beheading them, then intercepted and killed an additional six others after warning them to leave the area. Other sources report that 21 to 25 victims were killed and their livestock was stolen.

On 25 July 2023, Nigerian troops responded to a distress call and cleared the hideout of an unidentified armed group at Rumfar Gwamna, Unguwan Haruna, Kibam and DogonDaji forest in Mangu LGA (Plateau). A total of nine abductees were rescued, 2 cars were recovered and 2 suspects were arrested. Casualties are unknown.

On 25 July 2023, militants suspected to be affiliated with ISWAP ambushed and engaged policemen attached to Operation Hadarin Daji in an armed clash at Magami (Gusau, Zamfara). Five policemen were killed.

On 25 July 2023, two unidentified rival armed groups engaged in an armed clash at Odo-Osun area (Ibadan North, Oyo) coded to Agodi. The groups were drug gangs and at least five persons were seriously wounded in the clash.
On 25 July 2023, a Niger militia (described as bandits) abducted three people from Garun Gabas (Rafi, Niger).

On 26 July 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed troops of Operation Hakorin Damisa IV and engaged them in an armed clash along Rugan/Basiru village in Barkin Ladi LGA (Plateau). Ten of the assailants were arrested, the rest fled, weapons, ammunition and a pair of camouflage were recovered. Casualties are unknown.

On 26 July 2023, troops of Operation Hakorin Damisa IV foiled an attempted attack by an unidentified armed group and engaged them in an armed clash at Mangun and Patlong villages (Mangu, Borno). Scores of the armed group members were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, fatalities coded as 20.
On 26 July 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted the chief imam of Gudun village in Illela LGA (Sokoto) when they invaded the area. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife, daughter and driver of a popular businessman in Yadagungume in Ningi LGA (Borno). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 26 July 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with soldiers and policemen who attempted to repel their attack on civilians at Gara and Gamji villages in Burra district (Ningi, Bauchi). The assailants who came in large numbers killed seven civilians and one security volunteer guard in the two villages, burgled shops and stole food items. One soldier was wounded and three assailants were killed. 11 fatalities.

On 26 July 2023, a Kaduna militia shot a man on his farm at the Rema area of Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna). The victim who was the vice chairman of JIBWIS in the local government area was killed as a result of the injuries he sustained.
On 26 July 2023, a Kaduna militia killed one person and abducted nine others at Unguwan Roka in Kakangi ward (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna).

On 26 July 2023, a Zamfara militia were repelled by soldiers when they invaded Talata Mafara town (Talata Mafara, Zamfara) and abducted 10 staff of a construction company from their houses. The militiamen operated in the town for one and a half hour before they were repelled. Other sources report that one boy was injured, 12 persons were abducted and four of them escaped.

On 26 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three female bank staff near UNEC campus in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The abductees were returning from work when they were ambushed, one of them was a heavily pregnant woman. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 July 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of farmers when they attacked a farm in Isa town (Isa, Sokoto). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed five civilians, wounded three others and abducted two women when they attacked Unguwar Dinya in Funtua LGA (Katsina).
On 26 July 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one civilian and abducted three persons when they attacked Garin Nature village in Sabon Birni LGA (Sokoto) and shot indiscriminately.
On 26 July 2023, a Zamfara militia abducted 23 women from Damaga (Maradun, Zamfara) when they went into the bush in search of firewood. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 26 July 2023, Aro Baggers and Black Axe also called Aiye militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy for control at Eke Awka market, coded to Awka (Awka South, Anambra). One person who was suspected to be a leader of Black Axe militia was shot and killed. The assailants also beheaded the corpse and removed his private part before they fled.

On 26 July 2023, NDLEA operatives who shot sporadically and killed two civilians during a raid in Idi Oro (Mushin, Lagos) to scare hoodlums attempting to scuttle their plan in the community. The spokesperson of NDLEA claimed that the shots were fired in self-defense.

On 27 July 2023, policemen raided the hideout of an unidentified armed group and were engaged in an armed clash in Ahoada (Ahoada West, Rivers) coded to Akinima. One member of the group was killed, others escaped, the policemen recovered a rifle, ammunition, cartridges and some charms.
On 27 July 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person when they attacked a residence at Safana town (Safana, Katsina). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 27 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a patrol of the Nigerian army at Ajiri-Mafa road (Mafa, Borno), killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers and destroyed an armored vehicle. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 27 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked the positions of militias loyal to the Nigerian army [presumed to be Civilian JTF] at Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). The militants claimed that the militants were forced to withdraw and that they captured three rifles, casualties are unknown.
On 27 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed a spy of the Nigerian government at Gujba (Gujba, Yobe).

On 27 July 2023, a Kaduna militia killed one person and abducted seven members of the same family at Unguwan Fulani and abducted four farmers at Yelwa community in Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). Six persons were also abducted on their way to the Birnin Gwari weekly market.
On 27 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a broadcast journalist whom they trailed and ambushed in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 27 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a woman whom they attacked in her house at Ketu (Kosofe, Lagos). The victim's throat was slit, her apartment was set ablaze while her phones were stolen.

On 28 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji cleared hideouts of a Zamfara militia led by Alhaji Ilu and engaged them in an armed clash at Sangeku (Maru, Zamfara), Kaboro, Kabugu Lamba and Danmani [coded separately]. One militia member was killed, several others escaped with gunshot wounds. Fatalities split accross three locations.

On 28 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji cleared hideouts of a Zamfara militia led by Alhaji Ilu and engaged them in an armed clash at Kaboro (Maru, Zamfara), Sangeku, Kabugu Lamba and Danmani [coded separately]. One militia member was killed, several others escaped with gunshot wounds. Fatalities split accross three locations.
On 28 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked civilians, killed one person and abducted nine others at Kandeza in Binji LGA (Sokoto). The abductees included two children.
On 28 July 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one person at Boyekai (Goronyo, Sokoto) and abducted two of the dead victim's relatives.

On 28 July 2023, soldiers and policemen shot at IMN members who were observing their Ashura procession in Abuja (Abuja Municipal, FCT). Two people were hit by bullets and wounded, tear gas was shot at the procession and other sources report that one person was hit by a bullet in the head.

Around 28 July 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants abducted nine farmers from Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). The abductees and three persons who went to deliver the demanded ransom were shot because the militants were offended that the orders they gave regarding number of persons to deliver the ransom were flouted [coded separately].
On 28 July 2023, a Katsina militia killed one person and abducted 10 females when they attacked Katsalle village in Faskari LGA (Katsina).

On 28 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked Nigeria Immigration operatives and engaged them in an armed clash at a checkpoint in Mamman Suka (Gwadabawa, Sokoto) and killed two operatives. An unspecified number of operatives were wounded, others were abducted while the operatives recovered five rifles from the assailants. Other sources report that four operatives were wounded.

On 28 July 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji cleared hideouts of a Zamfara militia led by Alhaji Ilu and engaged them in an armed clash at Kabugu Lamba and Danmani in Maru LGA (Zamfara), Sangeku, Kaboro [coded separately]. One militia member was killed, several others escaped with gunshot wounds. Fatalities split across three locations.
On 29 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons at Angware (Jos East, Plateau) when they went to deliver ransom for abducted persons.

On 29 July 2023, an unidentified armed group raped and killed an eighteen-year old girl and dumped her corpse behind along a bush path at Rankaviri near Jalingo (Jalingo, Taraba). The victim's corpse was found the following day.

On 29 July 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with policemen at a checkpoint, when they were flagged down for a stop and search. One member of the group was killed, the others escaped and an abductee who claimed to have paid 700 thousand naira as ransom was rescued, location coded to Ebrumede (Uvwie, Delta) where the police team were deployed from.

On 29 July 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five staff of an electricity firm along Ogbagi-Ikare road (Akoko North East, Ondo). The abductees who were working on a federal government electrification project in Ikare-Akoko were released after four days and a ransom of 2.2 million naira, cooked food and other items were paid as ransom.

On 29 July 2023, a Zamfara militia that attempted to attack civilians were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by soldiers at Januhu village in Shinkafi LGA (Zamfara).
