The militia fled and left one motorcycle which was seized by soldiers, they later returned to the village and gave the villagers until August 5 to pay 500 thousand naira as replacement for their seized motorcycle or risk being attacked.

On 30 July 2023, soldiers and a local defense militia conducted a clearance operation and engaged a Sokoto militia in an armed clash at Kafarma forest in Wurno LGA (Sokoto). An unspecified number of militiamen were killed and wounded, unknown fatalities coded as 3.
On 30 July 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked a location in Binji LGA (Sokoto). Security operatives were deployed to the area [there are no reports of a clash]. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 July 2023, policemen killed one person and wounded another when they invaded Hausa communities in Nekede (Owerri West, Imo) together with officials of two state government agencies. Properties and shops were set ablaze, including at other locations [coded separately] as claimed by the traders.

Around 30 July 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a commercial motorcyclist in Aladja community (Warri South, Delta). The victim was stabbed and shot to death, his corpse was found with multiple stabs and his throat was slit.

On 30 July 2023, soldiers attacked and wounded several traders at Holy Ghost and Old Park in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The victims' goods worth millions of naira were also destroyed, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 31 July 2023, a Niger militia abducted one civilian from Tsohon Kabula (Muya, Niger) coded as Kabula. The assailants proceeded to Zagzaga where they looted shops [coded separately].

On 31 July 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 20 and were affiliated with a local political leader attacked four APC chieftains in Efon-Alaiye (Efon, Ekiti). The victims were wounded, goods worth millions of naira were destroyed in the attack which is connected to the forthcoming local government elections slated for December. One of the victims claimed that he was attacked over his refusal to step down for another aspirant.

On 31 July 2023, soldiers, policemen and other security agencies raided the hideouts of IPOB militants and were engaged in an armed clash with them in Orsumoghu forest (Ihiala, Anambra) spanning Anambra and Imo states. The militants detonated IEDs and fired at the troops using locally fabricated mortar tubes, five soldiers and two policemen sustained varying degrees of injuries. The militants fled with gunshot wounds, five of them were arrested and various items were recovered by the troops.

On 31 July 2023, a Niger militia killed one person who is suspected to have been their informant and proceeded to loot shops and houses of foodstuff, valuables and cattle at Zagzaga community (Muya, Niger). The victim was assumed to have been killed for providing false information to the assailants, the villagers fled before their arrival. Other sources report that two farmers were killed and an unspecified number of persons were abducted.

On 31 July 2023, troops of the Nigerian Army during a clearance operation engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash at Kajuru LGA (Kaduna) where they also destroyed the militia's camps. Four abductees were rescued, while the militiamen fled with gunshot wounds.

On 31 July 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a farm supervisor and wounded his driver on the leg when they attacked the farm at Isapa (Ekiti, Kwara). The farm belonged to a former senator, the supervisor was killed for resisting abduction while the driver was abandoned after the assailants sighted motorcyclists and went after them.

On 31 July 2023, suspected Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants killed about ten farmers when they attacked them on their farms in Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). Other sources report that 11 persons were killed while one escaped with gunshot wounds, nine of the victims were abductees while the other three were attacked when they went to deliver the ransom for the abductees.

On 31 July 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked policemen at a checkpoint in Geidam (Geidam, Yobe) and wounded two of them. Other sources report that the attack took place at Garin Gada, 10km away from Geidam and that two NSCDC and NDLEA operatives were killed.

On 31 July 2023, a Zamfara militia killed two civilians and abducted 13 others in Mayanchi community (Maru, Zamfara). The abductees included the sons of a former state NUJ treasurer, a local defense militia leader and others who were hiding in a mosque. Other sources report that 3 persons were killed.

On 1 June 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity ambushed Kaduna Militia and killed three along Road Tsohon Kabai-Kubusu Forest, coded to Kakau (Chikun, Kaduna). The military recovered two AK 47 rifles, four magazines, 16 rounds of 7.62mm,hard drugs, assorted charms and one motorcycle.
On 1 June 2023, ISWAP militants claimed to have killed an aid worker whom they abducted at Damasak (Mobbar, Borno). The victim was staff of Red Cross, according to the militants.

On 1 June 2023, suspected pirates abducted 15 passengers on a speed boat along the Calabar-Oron waterways, coded to Calabar (Calabar Municipal, Cross River). The passengers were taken on their way to Akwa-Ibom.

On 2 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Uburu (Ohaozara, Ebonyi) and Okposi [coded separately]. One passer-by was shot, three vehicles were set ablaze. Other sources report that two of the burnt vehicles belonged to the President-General of the community, whose residence was attacked after their target the youth president was not found. A dusk to dawn curfew was imposed on the communities and Ugwulangwu by the local government chairman. No fatalities.

On 2 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked Okposi Achara (Ohaozara, Ebonyi) and Uburu [coded separately]. One passer-by was shot, three vehicles were set ablaze. Other sources report that two of the burnt vehicles belonged to the President-General of the community, whose residence was attacked after their target the youth president was not found. A dusk to dawn curfew was imposed on the communities and Ugwulangwu by the local government chairman. No fatalities.

On 2 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked a local headquarters of the Nigerian Army at Gajigana (Magumeri, Borno) which led to the soldiers' withdrawal. They also claimed to have captured an unknown of ammunition.
On 2 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a soldier when they attacked a position of the Nigerian Army at Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). Other soldiers fled, and one motorcycle was seized by the militants.

On 2 June 2023, ISWAP militants attacked Nigerian troops providing reinforcement and were repelled at a firm base in Metele (Abadan, Borno). The militants deployed a VBIED; two soldiers were killed, many others were wounded; other sources report 11 wounded soldiers, an unspecified number of militants including the suicide bomber were killed. Unknown fatalities coded as 3. ISWAP claimed that around 20 soldiers were killed or wounded, other sources also reported that several soldiers were killed.

Around 2 June 2023 (between 31 May - 4 June), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at their enclaves in Chibok LGA (Borno), Tirke, Mandari, Molgoi, Bale, Yarwa and Ngurna [coded separately]. 11 militants were killed, fatalities were split across 4 events coded as 2.

Around 2 June 2023 (between 31 May - 4 June), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at their enclaves in Bego (Damboa, Borno), Tirke, Mandari, Molgoi, Bale, Yarwa, Ngurna and Chibok LGA [coded separately]. 11 militants were killed, fatalities were split across 4 events coded as 3.

Around 2 June 2023 (between 31 May - 4 June), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at their enclaves in Yerwa (Damboa, Borno), Tirke, Mandari, Molgoi, Bale, Bego, Ngurna and Chibok LGA [coded separately]. 11 militants were killed, fatalities were split across 4 events coded as 3.

Around 2 June 2023 (between 31 May - 4 June), troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF clashed with ISWAP militants during a clearance operation at their enclaves in Bale (Damboa, Borno), Tirke, Mandari, Molgoi, Bego, Yarwa, Ngurna and Chibok LGA [coded separately]. 11 militants were killed, fatalities were split across 4 events coded as 3.
On 2 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest while he was driving from Awka (Awka South, Anambra) to Nnewi. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 2 June 2023, a Katsina militia abducted a man from his residence at Unguwar Mare quarters in Dandume town (Dandume, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 2 June 2023, rival Niger militias (described as bandits) under the leadership of Dogo Gide and Ali Kachalla, respectively, clashed along the Shiroro axis, coded to the LGA HQ, Kuta (Shiroro, Niger). An unspecified number of men from the Dogo Gide faction were killed. It is suspected that the Dodo Gide militia faction plans further attacks on other militia factions operating along the axis. Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

On 3 June 2023, Operation Hadarin Daji troops at the forward operating base in Bakura pursued and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash after the militia attacked Rogoji village in Bakura LGA (Zamfara). Five militiamen were killed, two rifles, ammunition and an unspecified amount of cattle, goats and donkeys were recovered.

On 3 June 2023, a Zamfara militia riding on motorcycles attacked civilians at Janbako village (Maradun, Zamfara) and Sakkida [coded separately]. Over 20 people were killed in Janbako and 5 others were killed in Sakidda. Other sources report that the victims included a local defense militia who were ambushed when they were on the way to Sakidda to repel the assailants.

On 3 June 2023, supporters of the Kogi state SDP governorship candidate clashed with the convoy of the Kogi state governor near Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi). Some of the governor's aides sustained injuries, cars and cars were destroyed. Both parties accused the other of being responsible for the attack.

On 3 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons from Ketti community (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductees included the village head, his aide and one resident. A ransom of 9 million naira was demanded, it is unclear whether a ransom was paid for the two abductees who were released on 9 June, the village head died the day after they were abducted due to trauma.

On 3 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Imande Mbakange community in Mbacher (Katsina Ala, Benue) and other neigboring communities. The attacks happened simulteanously, 13 people were killed and many others were wounded. Other sources report that over 25 persons were killed and houses were set ablaze.

On 3 June 2023, a Zamfara militia were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers when they attacked Gora-Namaye village, coded to Gora (Maradun, Zamfara) killed 20 people and abducted at least 30 others. The assailants withdrew from the area and nine abductees were rescued, other sources report that only nine persons which consisted of boys and girls were abducted and later rescued by a joint team of policemen and security operatives who went on a search and rescue mission.

On 3 June 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Sakkida village coded to Sikida (Maradun, Zamfara) and Janbako [coded separately]. Over 20 people were killed in Janbako and 5 others were killed in Sakidda. Other sources report that three persons were killed.
On 3 June 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted three people when they invaded Ruggar Liman and four women from More in Kware LGA (Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 3 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted four residents from Mashafa area of Mpape (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The assailants shot sporadically during the attack which lasted for about one hour. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 3 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed civilians at Raka Dutse and Filin Gawa villages, coded to Raka (Tangaza, Sokoto) and Raka (coded separately) for not paying a levy that was imposed by the assailants. Between 25 and 37 people (18 in Raka, 17 in Filin Gawa and 2 in Raka Dutse) were killed. Fatalities coded at 37 considering the type of information, fatalities coded as 18 in this event.
On 3 June 2023, Tiv and Jukun ethnic militias clashed along Wukari-Tsokundi road in Wukari LGA (Taraba). Two persons were killed.

On 3 June 2023, an unidentified armed group (diverging reports mention bandits and ISSP, coded as UAG) attacked civilians at Raka village (Tangaza, Sokoto), Raka Dutse and Filin Gawa (coded separately) for not paying a levy that was imposed. On 3 June 2023, a Sokoto militia killed 18 civilians when they attacked Bilingawa (Gwadabawa, Sokoto).
On 4 June 2023, suspected armed pastoralists killed five people in Rafin Kada (Wukari, Taraba).
Around 4 June 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted two Fulani men from Ware Ware and Yelwa villages in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a civilian at Isiodu community (Emohua, Rivers). The victim who was a former state government house staff was shot and taken away by the assailants who had previously been decleared wanted by the local government chairman. Other sources report that the victim was indiscriminately shot at and abducted. The police claimed to have discovered the victim's decomposing charred remains in a shallow grave in a forest at Elibrada on 22 June.
On 4 June 2023, a Katsina militia attacked a farm on the outskirts of Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina). Casualties are unknown.
On 4 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Jing Kobili in Mangu LGA (Plateau). Nine persons were wounded and seven houses were set ablaze.

On 4 June 2023, Nigerian troops killed an unspecified number of Sokoto militia members (described as bandits) under the leadership of a named Sububu in Gwalama, coded to the LGA HQ, Isa (Isa, Sokoto). Unspecified fatalities coded as 3.

Around 5 June 2023 (as reported), a Niger militia in their numbers attacked civilians, killed one person and stole 100 cattle in Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). The militia also abducted 55 persons from other communities [coded separately] during attacks that were carried out simulteanously.

On 5 June 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two persons and abducted about thirty others at Shiwaka, Unguwan Bagudu (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) and Sabon Layi [coded separately]. The attack was over the communities' failure to pay levies imposed by the militia, an unspecified number of persons who fled onto the bush were missing. Fatalities split across two events coded as 1.

On 5 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three members of the same family at Ganaja in Ajaokuta LGA (Kogi). The prime target was a retired security officer, an undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom.

Around 5 June 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a man and his son as they were on the way to their farm in Ijagba (Ose, Ondo). The man was murdered despite the payment of 400 thousand naira ransom while his son was released.

Around 5 June 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a man whom they had abducted from Ijagba (Ose, Ondo) together with his son. The assailants had threatened to kill the victim if the ransom was not paid, 400 thousand naira was paid a s ransom, the man's son was released while his own body was found in the bush.
On 5 June 2023, suspected pirates killed one civilian when they hijacked two boats conveying passengers from Abonnema to Kula (Akukutoru, Rivers).

On 5 June 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot and killed a university professor on his way home in the Moniya area (Akinyele, Oyo). The assailants took the victim's car away.
On 5 June 2023,ISWAP militants attacked Banki town (Bama, Borno). There are no further details and casualties are unknown.

On 5 June 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two persons and abducted about thirty others at Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna), Shiwaka and Unguwan Bagudu [coded separately]. The attack was over the communities' failure to pay levies imposed by the militia, an unspecified number of persons who fled onto the bush were missing. Fatalities split across two events coded as 1.

On 20 June 2023, a Fulani militia killed at least one resident at Bwai (Mangu, Plateau). A church, and houses around the market were set blaze.

On 20 June 2023, a Fulani militia killed residents at Chisu community in Mangu LGA (Plateau) when they invaded the area. The residents fled to the house of their community where they were attacked, 11 burnt bodies were found the following morning, the house was also burnt.
On 20 June 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants fired indiscriminately at farmers and pastoralists in Malari village (Mafa, Borno). Two persons were wounded and five others were abducted.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a POS operator in Ugba town (Logo, Benue). There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person at Nitel junction in Agege (Agege, Lagos). There are no reports on ransom demands.

Around 21 June 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a man as he was returning from a beer parlor in the Kola Rewire area (Ondo West, Ondo) coded to Ondo. The victim was a civil servant and the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 21 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed 6 persons who are presumed to be civilians at Ijoko-Ogbayo in Ifo LGA (Ogun). Two persons were killed in the early hours of the day and four others were killed later that day.
On 21 June 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged in an armed clash with security operatives presumed to have been soldiers at Enugu Umunze (Orumba South, Anambra). Two persons were wounded.
On 21 June 2023, a Katsina militia killed five civilians and wounded five others when they shot indiscriminately at residents of Doma village in Faskari LGA (Borno).

On 22 June 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group led by Kabir Bala, also known as Okwo in an armed clash at Ejule (Ofu, Kogi). The group's leader who the police claimed was responsible for a number of attacks in the area was killed, other members of the group fled with varying degress of injuries. Other sources report that Okwo was used by politicians to attack their opponents and that he was killed for withdrawing his support for the governor and giving it to the governorship candidate of the SDP.

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed at least two civilians when they invaded Ejule (Ofu, Kogi) and shot sporadically. One of the victims was hit by a stray bullet, another was the wife of community youth leader, a house was also set ablaze by the assailants.

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a member of the central neighborhood watch at Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The assailants were masked, numbered up to 30 and were marching through the streets whe the victim ran into them.

Around 22 June 2023 (between 20 June - 23 June), a suspected Fulani militia attacked commuters along Enugu-Ugwuogo-Opi-Nsukka road (Nsukka, Enugu), abducted 16 persons and wounded several others. Some sources report that about seven abduction incidents took place within those days.
On 22 June 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives abushed and killed 6 ISWAP militants in Banki (Bama, Borno).

On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three women, a newly-wed bride and her two sister in-laws from their house at Emir's road in Ilorin (Ilorin West, Kwara). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded and the abductees were released on 25 June after 7 million was paid as ransom.

On 22 June 2023, a Kaduna militia killed three farmers and abducted scores of other persons when they invaded Sabon Layi (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna) in large numbers around 12pm. The abductees consisted of farmers, travellers and traders, other sources report that the attack was a reaction to ongoing military operations in disturbed areas.
On 22 June 2023, a Sokoto militia attacked farmers in Lajinge village (Sabon Birni, Sokoto). The assailants killed one person, wounded three and abducted two others.
On 22 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians when they attempted to abduct them on the road between Owo and Benin (Owo, Ondo). One traveler was hit and killed by a stray bullet.

On 22 June 2023, a soldier ordered a man to swim in a canal and threatened to stab anyone who came close at Fayose market in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti). The soldier who was invited by someone at the market to help collect rent was arrested by the police later that same day.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed one person at Muna, coded to Muna Dalti (Jere, Borno) and seven others at different locations in Mafa LGA [coded separately]. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed three youths at Baram-Karuwa and Shuwari in Mafa LGA (Borno) and five others at different locations [coded seaparately]. Two persons were killed in Baram-Karuwa and one was killed in Shuwari. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted.

On 22 June 2023, Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants killed four youths who were fetching firewood at Tamsu Ngamdua (Mafa, Borno) and four others at different locations [coded seaparately]. One person was spared to report the story, the victims had their hands tied to their backs and were shot. Other sources report that the victims were farmers and that 10 others were abducted

On 22 June 2023, Nigerian troops ambushed and engaged ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in an armed clash along Bula Yobe - Dar el Jamal (Bama, Borno) as they were crossing into Nigeria from Cameroon. Five militants were killed.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two civilians from Gamji and Tabla villages in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductee from Gamji was a businessman and undisclosed amount was demanded for his release, while 10 million naira was demanded for the release of the abductee from Tabla.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed a car and abducted the driver of the university's bursar on the road between Okigwe and Abia state university, code to Onuaku Uturu (Isuikwuato, Abia). The assailants did not see the bursar who is assumed to have been the target. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 23 June 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Ijoko town (Ado-Odo, Ogun). One person was killed.
On 23 June 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Bakin Gidan Gabas in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara) and wounded two people.

On 23 June 2023, Boko Haram [JAS Faction] fighters on motorcycles ambushed two vehicles conveying ISWAP fighters and engaged them in an armed clash on the road between Gajiganna and Gajiram (Nganzai, Borno). Several Boko Haram fighters were killed, their rifles and motorcycles were seized by ISWAP. Fatalities coded as 10.

On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically when they invaded Sabaja area of Iwo town (Osin, Kwara). The chief of Sabaja was killed by a stray bullet and three other persons including a cleric, a gate keeper and manager at a fuel station were abducted.
On 23 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked miners at a mining site around Tanjol in Jol community (Riyom, Plateau). Three persons were killed and two others were wounded.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group of three abducted a farmer from his farm at Saparu village (Imeko-Afon, Ogun) coded to Imeko and shot sporadically to scare away the other persons who were on the farm. The abductee was abandoned when villagers chased the abductors into the bush.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman and her daughter from the entrance of their residence at Oju-Ilu in Imeko (Imeko-Afon, Ogun). The woman was made to drive to the outskirts of the town where her daughter was abandoned in the car while she was taken away. There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons at Owube (Ogba, Rivers) after they attacked the commercial vehicle which they were traveling in. The victims were a passenger and the driver of the vehicle, other sources report that the assailants were a suspected cult militia.
On 24 June 2023, an SVC militia shot and wounded a member of Black Axe militia who is presumed to have been unarmed in Auchi (Etsako West, Edo). The victim was also an NYSC member.

On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the Yotomi area in Owode Egba (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode. An undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom, the abductee's family claimed that he was murdered by policemen on 1 July [coded separately] after he was mistaken for an abductor.
On 24 June 2023, suspected ISWAP fighters were repelled by troops of 115 Task Force battalion when they attacked Dille (Askira Uba, Borno). One soldier was killed.

On 24 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a patrol of the Nigerian Army and killed two soldiers at Dikwa (Dikwa, Borno). The militants also claimed that others were forced to withdraw, and that a rifle and three motorbikes were seized.
On 24 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters traveling from Aba to Umuahia, coded to Aba (Aba South, Abia).

On 24 June 2023, presumed IPOB militants attacked commuters at Arondizuogu junction, coded to Ndizuogu (Ideato North, Imo) and diverted their bus to a hamlet away from the road. Two of the commuters were killed, the others were robbed, one of the victims claimed that the assailants were over 50 at the hamlet, 20 of them were armed and they claimed the victims who were from Umuahia were attacked for not obeying sit-in orders and for voting in the 2023 elections.

On 25 June 2023, a Katsina militia in large numbers engaged the head of a local defense militia in an armed clash when they invaded his home in (Dan-Musa, Katsina) coded to Dan Musa. The leader was killed and his house was burnt in a revenge mission after the assailants claimed that he was responsible for the destruction of their hideouts. Two other persons were shot [not specified whether they died] and three women were raped.

On 25 June 2023, troops of 5 Battalion operating under 16 Brigade of the Nigerian Army engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideout in Azuzuama community (Southern Ijaw, Bayelsa). The armed group were suspected unrepentant militant and oil bunkers, they fled after the soldiers engaged them, the camp was destroyed and various kinds of weapons were recovered. There were no casualties.
On 25 June 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked and killed one person in Okokolo community (Agatu, Benue).

On 25 June 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash in Lokpanta (Nneochi, Abia) when the group invaded their hideout. An abductee whose husband was killed [previously coded] was rescued, three members of the group were killed and eight others were arrested.

On 25 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a naval rating who is presumed to have been off-duty at Ajegunle (Ajeromi, Lagos). The victim was walking around Olowojeunjeje area when he was killed.
On 25 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and wounded one person at Fass district in Riyom LGA (Plateau). The victim was ambushed and beaten into a coma.
On 25 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed two people at Wereng camp, coded as Unguwar Wereng (Riyom, Plateau). Two others were wounded.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person, wounded another and abducted two others when they invaded Magamin Kano in Ningi LGA (Bauchi). The abductees were the wife and son of the village head, who were taken in his place because he escaped.
On 26 June 2023, Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants ambushed and killed seven farmers at Bula Njimbam (Damboa, Borno). One other person sustained varying degrees of injuries.

On 26 June 2023, suspected pirates attacked policemen and engaged them in an armed clash at a divisional police headquarters in Ogbia (Ogbia, Bayelsa). The assailants were repelled, there were no fatalities.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at Rumu-Osi (Obio, Rivers) as she was returning from her shop. The abductee was rescued by a team of policemen and EMOLVICE operatives [there are no reports of a clash].
On 26 June 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted three farmers from Taka-Lafiya and rustled 60 cows from Gidan-Makeri in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 26 June 2023, ISWAP militants killed six people when they attacked Koyeri village (Damboa, Borno).

On 26 June 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed eight civilians in various houses at Kyarang in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The attacked lasted through the night and the victims included a six month old baby.
On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed five persons at Kerang community in Mangu LGA (Borno). Other sources report that seven persons were killed.

On 26 June 2023, an unidentified armed group dressed in military uniform abducted eight staff of MRS petroleum company on the Tin Can waterways (Apapa, Lagos) coded to Tin Can Island as they were returning from work. There are no reports on ransom demands.
On 27 June 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of passengers when they attacked a commercial bus at Karasti community in Illela LGA (Sokoto).

On 27 June 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a student of the Akwa Ibom state university on the school's main campus in Ikot Akpaden (Mkpat Enin, Akwa Ibom). Some sources report that the victim was killed over his emergence as winner in a contest, to the chagrin of the assailant group.
On 27 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted seven persons from Yewuti village in Kwali Area Council (Federal Capital Territory). A ransom of 7 million naira was demanded.

On 27 June 2023, a Niger militia killed six passengers travelers when they blocked the road between Pandogari and Alawa (Shiroro, Niger). One other person sustained gunshot injuries, the baby of one of the victims was also found alive the following day.

On 27 June 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins attacked a journalist and attempted to kill him at his residence in Mararaba (Karu, Nassarawa). The victim who is the deputy political editor of media at daily trust escaped, he claimed that he was shot at several times and the assailants stole his phone, wallet and car keys.

On 27 June 2023, a Katsina militia in large numbers were repelled by policemen who engaged them in an armed clash at Ruwan Doruwa village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. The militiamen had attacked the village, one of them was killed and a GPMG was recovered. Other sources report that two militiamen were killed.
On 27 June 2023, a Katsina militia attacked Wallaro village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. Casualties are unknown.

Around 27 June 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram [JAS Faction] fighters killed four members at Mandara mountains in Gwoza LGA (Borno) after they were accused of rebellion. The murdered fighters were killed for attempting to form a faction.

On 28 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a woman at Tamigbe town (Burutu, Delta). The abductee was shot in the head, her body was found by family members after they paid a ransom of 1 million naira [coded separately].

Around 28 June 2023 (as reported), policemen killed one civilian who was among the three that they arrested in Aguleri community (Anambra East, Anambra). According to his family, the victim died from torture by the policemen while the spokesperson of the police in the state claimed that he was killed by a fellow suspect.
On 28 June 2023, a Yansakai militia attacked civilians and killed six persons at Kadamutsawa community in Bungudu LGA (Zamfara). The assailants also wounded four persons and escaped from the area.
On 28 June 2023, a policeman killed a tricycle rider at the Bulumkutu axis (Maiduguri Metro, Borno) for refusing to stop at a roadblock.
On 28 June 2023, ISWAP claimed to have captured and killed a member of a local defense militia, presumed to be the Civilian JTF at Kirenawa (Marte, Borno).
On 28 June 2023, a Sokoto militia (described as bandits) abducted a man around Gundumi town (Goronyo, Sokoto) as he was repairing his vehicle.

On 29 June 2023, soldiers attached to the 82 division of the Nigerian army shot at operatives of the Eke Neighborhood Watch who responded to a distress call over armed robbery on the road leading to Eke (Udi, Enugu). One of the operatives and a woman who was on a motorcycle were killed, three other operatives were wounded of whom were in critical states. The spokesperson of 82 division claimed that the claims of the victims were untrue.
On 29 June 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted an unspecified number of farmers in Gandi district (Rabah, Sokoto).
On 30 June 2023, Onna and Eastern Obolo militia engaged in an armed clash over a land dispute at the Ikot Abasi/ Eket axis (Eastern Obolo, Akwa Ibom) coded to Okoro Ete. Casualties are unknown.

On 30 June 2023, an unidentified armed group shot at Benue community volunteer guards and killed one of them at Tse Anwhwan (Logo, Benue) coded to Ugba. The volunteer guards were returning from a police station in Ugba when they were ambushed.

On 30 June 2023, ISWAP militants engaged operatives of Civilian JTF in an armed clash when they attacked the operatives' location in Damboa town (Damboa, Borno). The militants also fired a mortar bomb into the town, six people including women were killed, over 20 others including two Civilian JTF operatives were wounded.
On 30 June 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with a local defense militia at Dugul village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. Six local defense militiamen were killed.
On 30 June 2023, policemen in a minivan ran over a civilian who was in handcuffs at Ekpoma (Esan West, Edo). The victim was seriously wounded.
On 30 June 2023, two unidentified cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Two suspected militia members were killed.

On 30 June 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman at Ikenegbu Layout in Owerri (Owerri Municipal, Imo). The abductee resisted being abducted and the assailants shot sporadically into the air to scare bystanders away. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 May 2023, a Kaduna militia were engaged in an armed clash with security operatives at Dorayi village in Zaria LGA (Kaduna) where they abducted about 20 persons and rustled cattle. The assailants abandoned the abductees, burnt down one house and two motorcycles before they fled.

On 1 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two passers-by when they invaded the home of a customs officer in Kofar Doka, Zaria LGA (Kaduna). The officer's wife, daughters and one other person were abducted by the assailants who arrived in their numbers and went straight to the house.

On 1 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man while he was on his way to Andaha in Akwanga LGA (Nassarawa). The abductee is a member of the Nassarawa football association board and a former NULGE chairman in the state. The ransom reported is 2 million naira while the abductee's relative claimed the abductors insisted on taking more.

On 1 May 2023, presumed IPOB militants shot and killed one civilian at Agudene Akpawfu community, coded to Amagunze (Nkanu East, Enugu) in retaliation over claims that the locals provided information to security agencies about ESN members in the community. A second person was wounded and left in critical condition, other sources claimed that residents accused the traditional ruler of the community of being responsible for the attacks.

Around 1 May 2023 (between 28 April - 3 May), Nigerian troops on clearance operations clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at villages and forest areas in Damboa LGA (Borno), Kaga, Ngala and Gwoza LGAs [coded separately]. 18 militants were killed, 10 abductee were rescued, weapons and ammunition were recovered by the troops. 18 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 5.

Around 1 May 2023 (between 28 April - 3 May), Nigerian troops on clearance operations clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at villages and forest areas in (Kaga, Borno) coded to Benisheikh, Damboa, Ngala and Gwoza LGAs [coded separately]. 18 militants were killed, 10 abductee were rescued, weapons and ammunition were recovered by the troops. 18 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 5.

Around 1 May 2023 (between 28 April - 3 May), Nigerian troops on clearance operations clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at villages and forest areas in Ngala LGA (Borno), Kaga, Damboa and Gwoza LGAs [coded separately]. 18 militants were killed, 10 abductee were rescued, weapons and ammunition were recovered by the troops. 18 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 4.

Around 1 May 2023 (between 28 April - 3 May), Nigerian troops on clearance operations clashed with Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants at villages and forest areas in Gwoza LGA (Borno), Kaga, Damboa and Ngala LGAs [coded separately]. 18 militants were killed, 10 abductee were rescued, weapons and ammunition were recovered by the troops. 18 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 4.

On 2 May 2023, a Niger militia abducted four farmers when they invaded Alawa community (Shiroro, Niger). The abductees were returning from the farm, they were released after soldiers engaged their abductors in armed clash [coded separately].

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted over 12 persons along Auchi-Ihievbe-Afuze road (Owan East, Edo). Other sources claimed that 9 persons were abducted and two of them escaped, the police claimed that the two persons were rescued. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person in Eku community (Ethiope East, Delta). Two houses and other properties were set ablaze and destroyed, other sources report that the attack may have been as a result of suspected cultists and youths of the community.

On 2 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted a lady from her residence in Fadan Ikulu (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) after shooting sporadically for almost two hours. The abductors arrived in vehicles and motorcycles, there are no reports about ransom demands.

Around 2 May 2023 (as reported), policemen and local hunters were engaged in an armed clash with an unidentified armed group when they invaded the group's hideout. Two members of the group were killed, one was arrested and others escaped with bullet wounds, two rifles and five rounds of ammunition were also recovered. Location coded to Maiha LGA (Adamawa) which is one of the locations where the police claimed that the group operated in.

On 2 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed a couple and their son at Idi-Ogogo village in Iragbiji (Boripe, Osun). The attack was in retaliation for the killing of a pastoralist's cow by unidentified persons, the murdered woman was pregnant.
On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three local defense militia operatives at Etiti Ohazu area of Aba (Aba South, Abia).

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash along East street in Aba (Aba South, Abia). One policeman was killed and beheaded, the other members of the team fled. The assailants took the policeman's head, gun and service uniform away, other sources report that the murder was in retaliation for the death of an armed group's leader who was killed on 23 April.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two staff of the federal ministry of works and a contractor at Tse-Agbete village in Kendev ward (Ukum, Benue). The abductee was taken from a construction site in the area, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 2 May 2023, troops of Sector 1 of the MNJTF conducted Operation Scorpion and killed some Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants around Kirta Wulgo (Monguno, Borno). 8 repentant militants were also received, fatalities coded as 3.

On 2 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons at Hoss (Riyom, Plateau). Two other persons who sustained injuries died on 4 May, residents who protested the against the attack the following day claimed that the victims were killed a few meters from a military checkpoint.
On 3 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer who was working on his farm along Ise-Emure road, coded to Emure-Ekiti (Emure, Ekiti). A ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 3 May 2023, policemen beat up a man at Oko-Oba abattoir, coded to Agege (Agege, Lagos) over his refusal to submit his phone for a search. The policemen were attached to the Agege Abattoir police station.

Around 3 May 2023 (between 2 May - 5 May), Black Axe also known as Aiye confraternity and SEC members engaged in an armed clash following a battle for supremacy at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). Three persons were killed, one of whom was killed on 4 May [coded separately], several other persons were wounded

On 3 May 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed the youth leader of Abarikpo community (Ahoada, Rivers) in his fathers compound in the same community. Some sources report that the victim's stance against cultism and insecurity in the area may have been the reason for the attack.

On 3 May 2023, policemen on surveillance patrol engaged a Zamfara militia that they intercepted in an armed clash at Gidan Giye village in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara). The clash lasted for one hour, two militiamen were killed, one rifle and one pump action gun were recovered while the other militiamen fled.
On 3 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a Turkish national and one other person from his residence at Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia clashed with soldiers who were keeping surveillance in Bafai Gora village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna). Two persons were killed, one soldier and one civilian were wounded.

On 4 May 2023, a Niger militia ambushed soldiers and engaged them in an armed clash in Alawa area (Shiroro, Niger), one soldier was killed, another was wounded. The soldiers had trailed an abductee who the militiamen had sent to buy food items, because they suspected him based on the amount of food he purchased. The abductees who were abducted on 2 May [coded separately] were released and the militiamen fled from the area.

Around 4 May 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a woman whom they had abducted on 27 April [coded separately] after a part payment of 6 million naira was paid as ransom. The victim's body was found along Ojoku road, coded to Afon (Asa, Kwara), she was abducted because her husband who was the target was not at home.

On 4 May 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash at Yardadi village, coded to Rini district (Bakura, Zamfara). The militiamen had attacked one civilian who was in route to Bakura town, one militiaman was killed in the clash and the others fled with gunshot wounds.

On 4 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed three policemen at a police checkpoint in Enugu Umunze (Orumba South, Enugu). The assailants shot sporadically for over an hour, other sources report that some others many have sustained injuries.
On 4 May 2023, ISWAP claimed a grenade attack on a Nigerian army base in Malam Fatori (Abadan, Borno) using a 40mm grenade which caused some fire. Casualties unknown.

Around 4 May 2023 (as reported), troops of 21 armored brigade in Bama engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash at the Banki axis (Bama, Borno). Two out of the three aid workers who were abducted on 26 April [coded separately] were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 5 May 2023, Black Axe also known as Aiye confraternity and SEC members engaged in an armed clash following a battle for supremacy at Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). One person was killed, several other persons were wounded in the clash which started on 2 May [coded separately].
On 5 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian in Gbajimba (Guma, Benue).

On 5 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one civilian at Oshigbudu village (Agatu, Benue). The assailants also blocked the roads and robbed passers-by of their motorcycles, monies and other valuables.

On 5 May 2023, a Gure militia armed with cutlasses, guns and other weapons attacked residents of Kitimi community, coded to near by Gure (Lere, Kaduna) following a communal clash over a piece of land bordering both villages. Three persons sustained gunshot wounds, one person died as a result of increased blood pressure which was induced by fear during the attack, properties and farms of some residents were set ablaze.

On 5 May 2023, an Ezza militia attacked Effium communities and were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers and policemen who repelled them in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The clash lasted for three days [coded separately], casualties are unknown.
On 5 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed four civilians in Hirnyam village (Guma, Benue). The victims included a catechist and his wife.

Around 6 May 2023 (as reported), some soldiers beat up staff of a hotel in Kaduna state, coded to Kaduna (Kaduna North, Kaduna) after they were invited by hotel's manager to punish the staff who demanded to be paid for work which they did.

Around 6 May 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a businessman whom they had abducted from Owerri Akokwa and dumped his corpse at a locality in (Orumba South, Anambra) coded to Enugu Umunze. The victim was killed despite the payment of 10 million naira ransom.

On 6 May 2023, troops of 222 battalion, 199 special forces and Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives conducted a clearance operation and engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash in Yuwe axis of Konduga LGA (Borno). Several militants including two commanders and one civilian JTF operative were killed, unknown fatalities coded as 10, ammunition and other items were recovered. Other sources report that the troops cleared out the militants' hideout in Chore, Habasha, Wurgal Gardawaji and Kacheri villages after the militants fled on sighting the troops. ISWAP claimed the attack, and stated that it attacked a patrol of soldiers. Killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers. Total fatalities coded as 13 (10 unknown, 2 commanders and 1 civilian)

Around 6 May 2023, (sometime between 1 and 8 May), special task force operatives presumed to comprise of soldiers and policemen killed a Jengere youth leader in Jos (Jos North, Plateau) where he was tortured following his arrest. The victim was released from custody on 1 May and dies on 8 May, residents of the town claim that he died from injuries he sustained while in custody.

On 6 May 2023, an Ezza militia attacked Effium communities and were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers and policemen who repelled them in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi). The clash started on 5 May and lasted for three days [coded separately], casualties are unknown.

On 7 May 2023, Black Axe militia and Klansmen Konfraternity engaged in an armed clash at Idu (Uruan, Akwa Ibom) and Uyo [coded separately], over control of minibus parks and toll collection. About four persons were killed, other sources report 16 and properties worth millions of naira were destroyed and residents fled. 4 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 7 May 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash with security operatives along Nkpor-Umuoji-Ideani (Idemili North, Anambra). Four members of the group were killed and some others were arrested. Other sources report that two members of the group were killed, two others were arrested, locally made explosives, one rifle, ammunition, magazines and other items were recovered.

On 7 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 40 worshippers from a church along Buruku Baringi road, coded to Buruku (Chikun, Kaduna) when they invaded the area and shot sporadically while the church service was ongoing. 15 of the abductees escaped while the assailants went away with the remaining 25, there are no reports about ransom demands. Other sources report that 11 abductees were released on 10 May and another 17 were released on 11 May; there are no reports on ransom payment, 12 others are yet to be freed. Around 5 June, 16 abductees were freed after an undisclosed amount and a motorcycle were paid as ransom.

On 7 May 2023, policemen on routine patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia who were dressed in military camouflage at Kidandan (Giwa, Kaduna). One militia member was killed and an operation motorcycle was recovered.

On 7 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 12 persons from Kagarko town (Kagarko, Kaduna) when they invaded the area. The abductees consisted of nine children and grand children of the emir of Kagarko and three persons from the town, the emir's youngest wife was also abducted but she escaped, one of the grand children also escaped after he recognized some of the abductors. A ransom of 150 million naira was demanded, the abductors threatened to abduct the emir if the ransom was not paid. Three of the grandchildren were released on 10 June after an undisclosed ransom was paid.
On 7 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have killed a Christian civilian whom they shot in the head at Usmanti, coded to Damaturu (Damaturu, Yobe).

On 7 May 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged the police orderly of the Takum LGA caretaker committee chairman in an armed clash along Chanchanji road near Agaraga village (Takum, Taraba) where they mounted a checkpoint. The policeman was killed, the chairman was abducted, his SUV and orderly's gun were taken away by the assailants, there are no reports about ransom demands. The abductee was released on 11 May, there are no reports about ransom payment.
On 7 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a pastoralist in Kuchimi village (Kagarko, Kaduna).

On 7 May 2023, Black Axe militia and Klansmen Konfraternity engaged in an armed clash in parts of Uyo (Uyo, Akwa Ibom) and Idu [coded separately], over control of minibus parks and toll collection. About four persons were killed, other sources report 16 and properties worth millions of naira were destroyed and residents fled. 4 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 7 May 2023, Greenlanders and Icelanders cult militias engaged in an armed clash over supremacy along the East-West road section of Ahoada LGA (Rivers). Three persons were killed, the militiamen fled when policemen arrived the area and no arrests were made by the policemen.

On 7 May 2023, an Ezza militia engaged soldiers and policemen in an armed clash in Effium (Ohaukwu, Ebonyi) and set a police station ablaze. The militiamen had attacked Effium communities and were repelled by the security operatives, there were no casualties on the part of the operatives, the casualties from the militiamen is unknown.
On 7 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed six civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 8 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a couple at Oogui Ojodo town, coded to along Ode Omu (Aiyedade, Osun) which was the route on which they were traveling. The husband escaped, and there are no reports on ransom demands for the wife.

On 8 May 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up members of a family and abducted one woman at Sekona (Ede South, Osun) while they were traveling to the state. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 8 May 2023, suspected Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed three civilians at Tse-Vambe and Tse-Iortim Torough Mbaniyar (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba.

Around 8 May 2023 (as reported), policemen and KSVS operatives engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideouts in Udulu forest (Kogi, Kogi) coded to Koton-Karfe and Sardauna [coded separately]. 134 abductees who were abducted from the FCT, Kogi and Nassarawa states were rescued, one abductee was killed after he sustained an injury while the armed group's members fled with various degrees of injuries.

On 8 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a man from the front of his residence at Eket LGA (Akwa Ibom). The abductee was a staff of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, a ransom of 10 million naira was demanded.

On 8 May 2023, about ten soldiers invaded the office of NDLEA and were repelled by the operatives in Dutse (Dutse, Jigawa) in an attempt to free their colleague who was arrested for selling illicit drugs. There were no casualties.

Around 8 May 2023 (as reported), policemen and KSVS operatives engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash when they invaded their hideouts in Sardauna forest, Toto LGA (Nassarawa) and Kogi state [coded separately]. 134 abductees who were abducted from the FCT, Kogi and Nassarawa states were rescued, casualties are unknown.

On 8 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have attacked two barracks of the Nigerian army with machine guns at Khaddamari (Jere, Borno), burned down the two barracks and seized a rifle. Other sources report that the militants attacked a small deployment of troops in the area, engaged them in an armed clash, set two checkpoints ablaze and stole one rifle. There were no fatalities.
On 8 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed seven civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 9 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed one civilian when they invaded Runji village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa. A community leader claimed that the assailants arrived with a herd of cattle as cover and shot into the air during the attack which lasted for a few minutes before fleeing in the direction of Zango Urban.
On 9 May 2023, a Niger militia killed one person in Sikiti village (Paikoro, Niger) and abducted dozens of farmers from there and other villages [coded separately].

On 9 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia ambushed a joint patrol of policemen, Benue community volunteer guards and hunters on the road between Ortese and Ngban (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba. Six persons including three volunteer guards, one hunter and two other persons who other sources report were locals were killed, the special adviser to the state governor on security claimed that the assailants have been calling to claim that they were promised land to settle and graze in the area by the state government.

On 9 May 2023, policemen repelled an attack by IPOB militants at Nkwor market in Ihiala (Ihiala, Anambra). The militants who ere enforcing a sit in order tried to rob a bank and shot sporadically before policemen engaged them and forced them to flee, the chief security officer of the bank was hit in the leg by a stray bullet during the indiscriminate shooting of the militants, as claimed by the state police command.

On 9 May 2023, a Niger militia abducted dozens of farmers from Abolo, Kudani, Nani, Kuna, Shunakwa, Sikiti, Zubakere and Jubidiga (Paikoro, Niger) coded to Paiko. One person was murdered at Sikiti during the attack [coded separately].

On 9 May 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins shot and wounded a contestant for the throne of Akama-Oghe community in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The victim claimed that the assailants trailed him from his house to Enugu Timber market where they shot at his car.

On 9 May 2023, suspected ISWAP militants in droves and mounted on motorcycles were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by Nigerian troops in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). One military vehicle was destroyed, an unspecified number of casualties are recorded. ISWAP claimed the attack, the killing and wounding of several soldiers, and the destruction of an armored tank and an SUV.

On 9 May 2023, ISWAP militants attacked IDPs who went in search of firewood about 7km away from Damboa (Damboa, Borno). Three victims were killed bullet wounds in their heads, one other escaped with injuries.

On 9 May 2023, Nigerian soldiers beat up residents of Yelwa town, also called Peva (Takum, Taraba) while they were on a search and rescue mission to find an abductee. Some residents claimed that the soldiers broke down doors and that shop owners were forced to close down their shops.

On 9 May 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP militants during an operation at the militant's enclave in Talala (Damboa, Borno). An unspecified number of militants were killed, the militants fired RPGs which wounded 12 people consisting of soldiers and civilians. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 9 May 2023, suspected IPOB militants ambushed and killed a member of the Imo state's APC presidential campaign council of Oru-East LGA around Awo-Omamma technical school (Oru East, Imo). The assailants dumped body of the victim, who was also a kinsman of the state governor and a retired military officer in the booth of his car, where it was later found.

On 9 May 2023, an unidentified armed group were engaged in an armed clash by security operatives who repelled an attempted abduction of students from the female hostel of Plateau state university in Bokkos (Bokkos, Plateau). One student was abducted, there were no abductions.
On 9 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed eight civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 10 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers who repelled their attack on Runji village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa. The militia arrived in their numbers, killed one woman and set houses and a Baptist church in the area ablaze before they were repelled. The number of wounded persons is unknown.

On 10 May 2023, a Nigeria militia in their numbers abducted an unspecified number of farmers from Kafin Koro (Paikoro, Niger) and adjoining villages. The militiamen operated in the area from 4pm till 7pm without intervention from security operatives.

On 10 May 2023, policemen from the rapid response squad at Awkuzu engaged an unidentified armed group in an armed clash at Ifite in Ogbunike (Oyi, Anambra) while attempting to rescue two abductees. Two members of the armed group were killed, an SUV together with several military and police uniforms were recovered.

On 10 May 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in conjunction with troops of sector 4, MNJTF engaged ISWAP militants who attempted to them in an armed clash at Arege (Abadan, Borno). Several militants were killed, together with aerial support from the air task force, a VBIED was destroyed, other sources report that about 10 militants were killed and two of their vehicles were destroyed. ISWAP claimed that the attack was a successful detonation of a VBIED that killed, wounded soldiers, damaged and destroyed several vehicles.

On 10 May 2023, Black Axe also called Aiye confraternity and SEC also called Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at some areas in Owo (Owo, Ondo). Three persons were killed and their bodies were taken away by the assailants.

On 10 May 2023, policemen engaged suspect IPOB militants in an armed clash at Akwa-Ihedi (Nnewi South, Anambra). Five militants were killed, two rocket launchers, four AK-47 rifles, other weapons and ammunitions and other items were recovered. IPOB denied involvement in the clash and claimed that the claims by the police was an attempt to discredit the group in the international community.

On 10 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with patrols of Nigerian soldiers near Alargano forest, in the axis of Chiralia (Damboa, Borno), killed and wounded an unspecified number of soldiers an destroyed an armored tank and a four wheel drive belonging to the troops. other sources report that the militants detonated an IED on pen of the troops' Hilux vehicle which caused some injuries and fatality. The militants fled before troops arrived. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 10 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a local politician and his son at Bureh village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The victim's wife was wounded by the assailants.

On 10 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one of the abductees whom they abducted together with 80 others at Wanzamai village in Tsafe LGA (Zamfara) [code separately]. The murdered victim was among the last 12 abductees who were held back after the others were released after an additional ransom was paid.

On 10 May 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted a chieftain of the APC from his residence at Umuarugo village in Umueze II (Ehime Mbano, Imo). The abductors trailed the abductee who is the APC's chairman in the village to his residence and shot sporadically before taking him away. There are no reports about ransom demands.
On 10 May 2023, a Fulani militia killed seven civilians at Mbawa council ward (Guma, Benue).

On 11 May 2023, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Gwanja community in Karu LGA (Nassarawa) and killed four persons. The attack was reprisal over the death of a pastoralist who was killed during a fight with a farmer.

On 11 May 2023, a suspected local defense militia killed 11 civilians from the Fulani ethnic group at Iganna community (Iwajowa, Oyo). The victims included pregnant women, nursing mothers and children and 72 houses were burnt. The Fulani leaders in the communtiy claimed that members of the militia claimed that a farmer was stabbed by a suspect who was traced to the Fulani community.

On 11 May 2023, troops of Operation Desert Sanity II engaged ISWAP militants in an armed clash when they invaded the militant's hideout in Yale (Konduga, Borno). Two militants were killed and one young boy was rescued.
On 11 May 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists raped three girls in Bokkos LGA (Plateau) during an attempted abduction of the victims when they were returning from a search for firewood.

On 12 May 2023, a suspected Fulani militia in their numbers attacked and killed about seven civilians at Warkan village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa. Several houses were set ablaze and an unspecified number of persons were wounded.
On 12 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of persons from communities in Dirindaji (Sakaba, Kebbi).
On 12 May 2023, Amazaba and Ikot Akpan Udo communal militias engaged in an armed clash and resulted in the killing of four persosn, Location coded to Okoro Ete (Eastern Obolo, Akwa Ibom).

On 12 May 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed a team of policemen an engaged them in an armed clash at Rumuji (Emohua, Rivers). The policemen belonged to the counter terrorism unit attached to the Delta state government house, one of them was killed while the others escaped.

On 12 May 2023, a Fulani militia attacked civilians in Takalafiya community in Karu LGA (Nassarawa) and killed 34 persons. The attack which was a reprisal over the death of a pastoralist who was killed during a fight with a farmer began the previous day in Gwanja [coded separately], before the assailants attacked residents who they learned were taking refuge in Takalafiya.
On 12 May 2023, a Kaduna militia killed two civilians when they attacked Mawofi village (Zangon Kataf, Kaduna) coded to Zonkwa in large numbers.

Around 12 May 2023 (as reported), security agents comprised of soldiers, policemen and local hunters engaged a Kebbi militia in an armed clash in (Danko, Kebbi) coded to Wasagu. The militia leader, Yellow was killed together with an unspecified number of his group members. Unknown fatalities coded as 3 + one militia leader fatality, total 4 fatality coded.
On 12 May 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted 21 persons from Kago, Tsauni-Abe, Doguwa and Akoti in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). One of the abductees was a pastor, there are no reports on ransom demands.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a policeman at a checkpoint around the Emohua axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers). The assailants arrived and shot sporadically, a civilian who was driving in a private vehicle was hit by a stray bullet.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group led by a faction of the Obubu community leaders attacked and wounded five members of the community (Udu, Delta) over a leadership tussle. An unknown number of houses were also destroyed.

Around 13 May 2023 (between 13 May - 14 May), a suspected Fulani killed three civilians when they attacked Ijaha village (Apa, Benue) coded to Ugbokpo and set two other villages ablaze [coded separately].

Around 13 May 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a woman from her store in Rumu-Olumene community (Obio, Rivers). The abductee was released around 20 May after a ransom of 200,000 thousand was paid, the initial amount demanded was 15 million naira.

On 13 May 2023, soldiers of 21 armored brigade of Operation Hadin Kai killed one ISWAP militant at Ukuba in Bama LGA (Borno). The troops recovered a large cache of weapons which included submachine guns, hand grenades, mortar bombs, shika rounds among others.

On 13 May 2023, ISWAP militants were engaged in an armed clash and repelled by troops of Operation Hadin Kai when they attacked Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). The militants withdrew and casualties are unknown.

On 13 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a medical doctor who was heading to work in Makurdi (Makurdi, Benue). An undisclosed amount was demanded as ransom, the abductee was rescued when security agents raided their hideout [coded separately].

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer along Otu-Alaga road (Itesiwaju, Oyo) after they ambushed him and shot sporadically into the air to scare away other motorists and passers-by. The abductee is also a cattle dealer and a ransom of 30 million naira was demanded.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a businessman at Oba (Idemili South, Anambra) as he was driving from a meeting. The assailants shot the victim and ensured that he died without stealing any valuables from him.

On 14 May 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Katoge, Matsematsi, Tabanni villages and Matankari town (Maru, Zamfara) as a reprisal for the killed of one villager who was associated with them by local defense militiamen. 10 persons were killed across the locations while 10 others were killed in another village [coded separately]. 30 persons were wounded across the locations in the attacks which lasted from 10am to 3pm.

On 14 May 2023, a Zamfara militia attacked civilians at Dankurmi village (Maru, Zamfara) as a reprisal for the killed of one villager who was associated with them by local defense militiamen. 8 persons were killed while 10 others were killed in other villages [coded separately]. 30 persons were wounded across the villages in the attacks which lasted from 10am to 3pm.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 15 persons from an estate at Pegi community in Kuje Area Council (FCT). The abductors shot sporadically into the air during the attack, there are no reports about ransom demands. Other sources report that three persons were abducted and a ransom of 50 million naira was demanded for one abductee's release from his family.
On 14 May 2023, a policeman shot and wounded a civilian in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) following a disagreement over taking turns at a tea shop.

On 14 May 2023, ISWAP militants engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian soldiers and MNJTF troops in Arege (Abadan, Borno). ISWAP claimed the attack and that it burned a barracks and military vehicles, seized two rifles and a machine gun. Other sources report that the militants attacked the troops in twin VBIED attacks which killed 3 soldiers and wounded 10 others while the militants were also repelled.

On 14 May 2023, Wurkum and Karimjo ethnic militias clashed in Karim Lamido (Karim Lamidu, Taraba) following a disagreement over the installation of a new monarch and between 13 to 20 persons including children who were from both sides were killed. A Wurkum representative claimed that the Karimjo militia were responsible for the attack after they burnt shops and building belonging to Wurkum people, while the Karimjo representative denied the claims and added that the police and local defense militia were responsible for the death of 10 Karimjo people. The state police command claimed that only two casualties were recorded.

On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked two pickup vehicles as they were conveying cattle to a local market in Takum LGA (Taraba). One driver was killed while the second one escaped and the cattle being conveyed were set ablaze.
On 14 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an unspecified number of commuters when they fired indiscriminately at their bus along Mararaba-Takum road in Takum LGA (Taraba).

On 14 May 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to distress call over the militia's attack on Bajinawa village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. One militia member was killed; others are assumed to have fled with bullet wounds, one rifle was recovered, five women who were abducted were rescued by the policemen

On 14 May 2023, policemen repelled an attack by a Sokoto militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Giremshi community in Sokoto (Sokoto North, Sokoto). The clash lasted for over two hours, casualties are unknown.
On 14 May 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash in the vicinity of Khaddamari (Jere, Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 15 May 2023, a Sokoto militia killed one person when they fired indiscriminately at Ilela Hudu village in Goronyo LGA (Sokoto). The assailants also abducted three persons.
On 15 May 2023, a Zamfara militia killed one farmer and abducted two others in Askawa village, Zurmi LGA (Zamfara).

On 15 May 2023, an unidentified armed group of between five and seven persons attacked travelers in a commercial bus on the Iju-Itaogbolu-Ikere road (Ikere, Ekiti). Three sustained gunshot wounds while the other three were abducted.

On 15 May 2023, a Boko Haram militant detonated a suicide vest which he was wearing and killed himself during a joint raid by operatives of DSS, policemen and soldiers on militants' hideouts at Keke community of Millenium City (Chikun, Kaduna) and Kano [coded separately]. Other suicide jackets, IEDs, and weapons were recovered and three persons were arrested. No one else was killed or injured.
On 15 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with Nigerian soldiers on patrol at Allagarno forest (Damboa, Borno) which led to the troops' withdrawal.

On 15 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to targeted a Nigerian army patrol with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher on the Bosso-Malam Fatori road (Abadan, Borno). An SUV was burned and an unspecified number of soldiers were wounded.
On 15 May 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted the chief imam of Giribishi jumaat mosque in Giribishi village (Wamakko, Sokoto) coded to Wamako.
On 15 May 2023, a Zamfara militia shot indiscriminately and killed an unspecified number of commuters along Kaura-Shinkafi road, Shnikafi LGA (Zamfara). Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group of five killed one person and abducted three others on Ijara - Isanlu-Isin road (Osin, Kwara). The murdered victim was a local chief from Pamo Isin who was passing on his motorcycle, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted twelve NYSC members on the Rumuji axis of East-West road (Emohua, Rivers) as they were returning from orientation camp in Ondo state. Five of the abductees escaped, the remaining seven were released on 21 May after an undisclosed ransom amount was paid.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded two locals in Yarimawa (Tofa, Kano) when attempted to help a family that the assailants attacked. One assailant mistakenly shot and killed his partner, three suspects were arrested.

On 16 May 2023, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants engaged policemen who were on a convoy of US embassy staff in an armed clash along Atani-Osamale road (Ogbaru, Anambra) before a reinforcement of policemen and soldiers arrived. Two to four policemen who were part of the convoy, a driver and two consulate staff were killed, their bodies and vehicle were set ablaze, two other policemen, other sources report three, were abducted, an unspecified number of persons were wounded and nine persons were killed. On 19 May, the abductees were rescued unhurt by a joint team of security forces. IPOB denied being involved in the attack, and claimed that it's accusers were responsible for the attack.

Around 16 May 2023 (as reported), MNJTF troops clashed with ISWAP militants at Fedondiya and Arege general areas (Abadan, Borno). Several militants were killed, on dushka gun, dushka turrell and gun truck were recovered. Unknown fatalities coded as 3.

On 16 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to have clashed with a patrol of the Nigerian Army at Allagarno forest (Damboa, Borno). A suicide bomber detonated a SVBIED which killed and wounded a number of soldiers. Fatalities coded as 3.
On 16 May 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted six persosn when they attacked Moore community in Kware LGA (Sokoto). The abductees included the wife and two sons of the local government area chairman.

On 16 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed 29 women and children at Fungai and Kunwat villages in Mangu LGA (Plateau). Several persons were wounded, houses with valuables worth millions of naira were destroyed. Other sources report that the fatalities rose to 85.

On 16 May 2023, policemen together with other security agents assumed to be soldiers responded to a distress call and repelled an attack by an unidentified armed group at Tanknale village in Mangu LGA (Plateau). The assailants killed 30 civilians before they fled following the arrival of the security agents, they abandoned 4 motorcycles and a car which were recovered.
On 16 May 2023, a Katsina militia wounded a man and his son and abducted his wife at a residence in Badole villages (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma.

On 16 May 2023, suspected armed pastoralists attacked civilians at Uchen (Gwer West, Benue) coded to Naka. Seven members of the same family including a six-month old baby were killed, others were wounded. The state police command claimed that five persons were killed, other sources report that six people were killed in the attack while one other person fell and died after discovering the bodies of others.
On 17 May 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two persons and abducted six others at Yangoji (Kwali, FCT).

On 17 May 2023, soldiers attacked and beat up a group of special hunters [presumed to be unarmed] and wounded one of them at Zumba community (Shiroro, Niger). The soldiers accused the hunters of wearing red berets which is part of the soldier's uniform, one civilian was knocked down by the soldiers' patrol vehicle.

On 17 May 2023, a Niger militia wounded three persons and abducted eight others along Wawa-Luma road (Borgu, Niger). The abductees were passengers and the driver of a bus, one person escaped into the bush. Three of the abductees were released after a ransom of 1.5 million naira each was paid, another was murdered over delayed payment of a 2 million naira ransom [coded separately].

On 17 May 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering over 20 killed the youth leader of Patanyi village in Bugana ward (Omala, Kogi) whom they abducted when they invaded the area and shot sporadically. The victim's body was found beheaded in a river, he was abducted while on a hunting expedition with four others.
On 17 May 2023, ISWAP claimed to targeted a Nigerian army patrol with a 40mm automatic grenade launcher on at Arege (Abadan, Borno). There were no casualties.

On 17 May 2023, suspected IPOB/ ESN militants numbering over 50 who were dressed in black attire killed two brothers at their residence in Aba (Aba South, Abia) after they were suspected to have been informants for the police. The assailants also set the victims' house ablaze.

On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted two staff of the Nigerian Railway Corporation at Owa-Oyibu (Ika North East, Delta). The car that he abductee were driving was destroyed, its windshield was shattered, a ransom of 40 million naira was demanded. The police spokesperson in the state denied any record of the event.
Around 18 May 2023 (as reported), some policemen beat up and wounded a commercial okada rider near a bridge at Abule Egba area (Alimosho, Lagos) as he tried to prevent him from stealing his bike.

On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians at Eke Awgbu market in Awgbu community (Orumba North, Anmabra) and killed 4 persons. One person was burnt alive in his shop, three others were shot and goods worth millions of naira were destroyed. The attack was a retaliation for the killing of two of the group's members by a mob the previous day.
On 18 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one civilian from along NTA road in Mgbuoba (Obio, Rivers).

On 18 May 2023, soldiers shot and killed a man suspected to have been an informant for a Kaduna militia when they raided a hideout in Kagarko town (Kagarko, Kaduna). The victim who was decleared wanted previously attempted to escape and was shot dead, six others were arrested.

On 18 May 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants engaged Civilian JTF operatives who were escorting civilians to work in the fields in an armed clash at Kirawa (Gwoza, Borno). One Civilian JTF was killed after he ran out of ammunition and the militants beheaded him.

On 18 May 2023, ISWAP militants fired some mortar shells targeted at Nigerian troops in Arege (Abadan, Borno). The shells fell some distance away without causing impact and the troops responded with heavy fire which caused the militants to flee.
On 18 May 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants clashed with Nigerian troops on the outskirts of Wudula in Konduga LGA (Borno). Casualties are unknown.
On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted three persons from Umutu community (Ukwuani, Delta). The abductees were rescued by a local defense militia who searched the bushes.

On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a catholic priest while he was preparing for mass at his new adoration site in Ogii village (Onuimo, Imo). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 19 May 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who were conducting a stop and search in an armed clash at Ekredjebor community (Ughelli North, Delta) coded to Ughelli. The policemen were attached to the Ofuoma police division, two of them were killed and their rifles were stole by the assailants, one was wounded.

On 19 May 2023, the suspected Zamfara militia clashed with the Nigerian troops around Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The troops were trying to rescue the five students abducted by the armed group. The troops rescued the hostage.
