Around 20 March 2023 (as reported), a Kaduna militia killed one of the wives of the Chief Imam of Nomadic Central mosque whom they had abducted from Rugan Ardo in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). The victim was abducted along with 3 other of he husband's wives [coded separately] and was killed after the militiamen received a ransom of 2 million naira. The militiamen told the family members that they had buried the victim's corpse.
On 20 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the campaign office of the APC in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara) and killed at least two persons. The office was also vandalized by the assailants.

On 20 March 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with a Sokoto militia and killed two of them as they were enroute to a militia camp around Kagara, coded to Isa LGA (Sokoto). The militiamen were riding on a motorcycle and were crushed by a military artillery vehicle.

On 20 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the INEC electoral and returning officers for Zamfara state elections as they were on their way to Gusau from Maradun (Maradun, Zamfara). The abductees who were headed to the INEC headquarters to deliver the governorship result were released later on the same day, there are no reports on ransom payment.

On 21 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists ambushed residents in Sobe (Owan West, Edo) and inflicted machete cuts on one person. Several other persons were displaced as a result of the attack.

On 21 March 2023, two unidentified rival political parties engaged in an armed clash at Kofar Domi (Bauchi, Bauchi) coded to Bauchi over the outcome of the governorship election. At least four people were killed and an unspecified number were wounded, security operatives were deployed to the location.

On 21 March 2023, a Kaduna militia clashed with soldiers who responded to a distress call at Akpoti village, near Kagarko town (Kagarko, Kaduna). One soldier was killed, three others were wounded, one civilian who was hit by a stray bullet was also wounded. The militiamen had rustled 80 cows and were passing through the area when the soldiers were alerted.

On 21 March 2023, Nigerian troops repelled an attack by Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Banki (Bama, Borno). The soldiers pursued the militants towards the forest and engaged them further in a clash. There were no casualties from the soldiers, the militants' casualties are unknown.
On 22 March 2023, a Katsina militia wounded one person and abducted another at Sabon Garin Gamji in Safana LGA (Katsina).
On 22 March 2023, a Katsina militia abducted one person from a residence in Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina). There are no reports on ransom demands.

On 22 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked tipper drivers who were loading sand and wounded six of them at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo). The assailants who were armed with guns and machetes also wounded a farmer whom they attacked with machetes on his farm.

On 22 March 2023, a Sokoto militia killed at least four people when they invaded Moore village and Buddo community in Kware LGA (Sokoto). Two others were wounded and at least 10 persons were abducted.
On 23 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed four fishers at a fishing pond in Nyiev council ward (Guma, Benue). The victims included three women and one man.

On 23 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the house of assembly member-elect for Gboko West constituency at Gyado junction in Gboko (Gboko, Benue) as he was going home. The man escaped unhurt, his car was burnt by the assailants.
On 23 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked farmers and killed one person at Iwili community (Otukpo, Benue).

On 23 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists raped several women and killed four persons in Ogbaulu (Agatu, Benue) and Atakpa [coded separately]. One person was wounded and one other is missing, four fatalities split across two events coded as 2.

On 23 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists raped several women and killed four persons in Atakpa (Agatu, Benue) coded to Bagagi and Ogbaulu [coded separately]. One person was wounded and one other is missing, four fatalities split across two events coded as 2.
On 23 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists abducted two persons in Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo). A ransom of 10 million naira was demanded from the family of one of the victims.

Around 23 March 2023 (as reported), APC supporters attacked residents in Isara (Remo North, Ogun) who they suspected voted against the party in the governorship elections (assumedly PDP supporters). The assailants invaded the palace of the monarch and shot sporadically, several people's houses were also forced open. Casualties are unknown.
On 23 March 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a pastor and abducted his wife from their residence in Kasuwan Magani (Kajuru, Kaduna).

On 24 March 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kaiin conjunction with civilian JTF and hunters ambushed and killed 4 Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants in the axis of Beta (Gwoza, Borno). The militants were suspected to be from Ali Ngulde camp, two of them were captured alive, three weapons were recovered by troops.
On 24 March 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Pansheke area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). One other person who was hit by a stray bullet died. Total 2 fatalities.

On 24 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer and a commercial motorcyclist on Ugbokuli-Ekiadolor road (Ovia North East, Edo). The abductees were ambushed while they were returning from the farm with farm produce, the driver of the vehicle conveying the produce escaped and there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 March 2023, troops of 21 Task Force Brigade and the Civilian JTF raided the camps of Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Bula Umar (Bama, Borno), Bula Agaida, Bula Yaga, Bula Lambai, Kuluri and New Churchur [coded separately]. The troops discovered and destroyed a large camp, an unspecified number of militants were killed and one gun truck was recovered. Unknown fatalities assumed to be 3, split across 2 events and coded as 1.

On 25 March 2023, troops of 21 Task Force Brigade and the Civilian JTF raided the camps of Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Bula Agaida, Bula Yaga, Bula Lambai, Kuluri and New Churchur in Bama LGA (Borno), Bula Umar [coded separately]. The troops discovered and destroyed a large camp, an unspecified number of militants were killed and one gun truck was recovered. Unknown fatalities assumed to be 3, split across 2 events and coded as 2.

On 25 March 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with hunters and civilian JTF killed four Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants in the outskirts of Bama (Bama, Borno). One civilian JTF member was killed, weapons were recovered from the militants by the troops. Total 5 fatalities.
On 25 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a civilian in Chongu community (Guma, Benue).

Around 25 March 2023 (between 20 March - 3 April), a Niger militia attacked civilians at Sahon Rami, Tashan Hajiya in Mashegu LGA (Niger), Kulho and other communities [coded separately]. Seven persons were killed and 26 others were abducted across the communities, most of the villagers deserted the communities to an IDP camp in Kontagora. 7 fatalities split across two events coded as 3. Other sources report that 12 persons were abducted, 9 out of 12 abductees were killed while the other 3 escaped [coded separately].

On 25 March 2023, ISWAP fighters clashed with troops of 222 battalion Operation Hadin Kai in Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). Seven militants were killed by the troops who chased them as they attempted to escape towards the axis of Sambisa forest.

On 25 March 2023, Nigerian troops and Civilian JTF operatives raided the hideout of ISWAP militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Mukdolo and Bone (Ngala, Borno) coded to Gamboru. 41 militants including one commander were killed.

On 25 March 2023, a Katsina militia abducted a presumed off-duty prison guard while he was on his way to Tsaskiya village (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 25 March 2023, a Zamfara militia on about 11 motorcycles abducted a man from his residence in Mareri (Gusau, Zamfara). The abductee is the special adviser to the state governor on political matters, the assailants asked to be directed to his room when they invaded his residence, the abductee was released on 28 March after an undisclosed amount was paid as ransom.

On 25 March 2023, an AVS operative killed a staff of a fast food in Umuahia (Umuahia North, Abia) over a missing phone. The AVS claimed that the attack was a result of an accidental discharge, the assailant also worked as a security staff at the fast food, other sources claimed that the victim was beat up and later shot.
On 25 March 2023, a Zamfara militia killed a taxi driver along the Kaura Namoda-Shinkafi road (Shinkafi, Zamfara).

Around 25 March 2023 (between 20 March - 3 April), a Niger militia attacked civilians at Kulho (Mashegu, Niger), Sahon Rami, Tashan Hajiya and other communities [coded separately]. Seven persons were killed and 26 others were abducted across the communities, most of the villagers deserted the communities to an IDP camp in Kontagora. 7 fatalities split across two events coded as 4. Other sources report that 12 persons were abducted, 9 out of 12 abductees were killed while the other 3 escaped [coded separately].
On 26 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer between Omu-Ekiti and Ayede-Ekiti (Oye, Ekiti) as he was returning from his farm. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 26 March 2023, Icelanders and Greenlanders cult militias engaged in an armed clash and killed 6 persons in Odiokwu community (Ahoada West, Rivers) coded to Akinima. The assailants invaded a compound where the rival group was holding an event and killed the victims.

On 26 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a girl from her home at Ukwuinyi area of Enugu-Ezike (Igbo Eze North, Enugu). The abductee was rescued by policemen after the abductors abandoned her on 27 March.
On 26 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two policemen when they attacked a police checkpoint in Enugu (Enugu North, Enugu). The policemen were on stop and search duties.

On 26 March 2023, ISWAP militants were repelled by troops of Operation Hadin Kai when they attempted to attack them at Kawuri (Konduga, Borno). The militants fired two RPGs which had no impact and fled when the troops responded with gunfire. Casualties are unknown.

On 26 March 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a retired customs officer and abducted his son from their residence in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The victim was killed when the assailants were trying to abduct him.
On 26 March 2023, Igaluwa and Efeyi communal militias clashed in (Otukpo, Benue) coded to Oturkpo. Casualties are unknown.

On 26 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be from Afor-Nkune killed a member of MACBAN at Akpugo (Nkanu West, Enugu) coded to Agbani and other persons at different locations [coded separately] as claimed by MACBAN. An unspecified number of cattle were also killed during the attacks.

On 27 March 2023, troops of 112 task force battalion, 199 special force battalion, hunters and civilian JTF clashed with Boko Haram fighters [JAS faction] during a fighting patrol at Gavaya Modu, Gujuri, Daimalari and Dogumba villages (Mafa, Borno). Many militants were killed, fatalities coded as 10.

On 27 March 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked soldiers at a mining site in Akparavuni (Biase, Cross River) coded to Akpet Central. The assailants were illegal miners, the soldiers sustained injuries.

On 27 March 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed NSCDC operatives and killed three of them at Obiangwu (Ngor Okpala, Imo). The operatives were in a moving vehicle when the attack took place, some sources report that two operatives were killed, others report two NSCDC operatives and two staff of MTN were killed and that the rifles of the operatives were taken.
On 27 March 2023, a Katsina militia attacked policemen between Dan Musa and Maidabino village (Dan-Musa, Katsina). One policeman and one militiaman were killed.

On 27 March 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash when they attacked a police station in Udung Uko (Udung Uko, Akwa Ibom). Two policemen were killed and an unspecified number were wounded, weapons were stolen.

On 27 March 2023, a Niger militia raped three women and killed three persons out of the 60 others that they abducted [coded separately] from Adunu and Beni villages (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The murdered victims were 2 retired policemen and 1 other person, all of whom were from Beni village, they were killed as a warning to the communities for the demanded ransom to be paid, the women were released to relay the message to the community. Other sources report that 5 five persons were killed.
On 27 March 2023, the joint task force of Operation Hadin Kai repelled an by ISWAP militants on a military formation at Kurnari (Biu, Borno). Ten militants were killed and one soldier was wounded.
On 27 March 2023, a Zamfara militia wounded one person when they attacked Gabake Mesa community in Kaura Namoda LGA (Zamfara).

On 27 March 2023, policemen responded to a distress call and engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at the Danmusa- Yan Tumaki road (Dan-Musa, Katsina). One militiaman was killed, others fled with bullet wounds, one rifle and ammunition were recovered at the scene by the policemen.

On 27 March 2023, Black Axe and SEC militias engaged in an armed clash at Bariga (Somolu, Lagos) and three persons were killed. The clash was a reprisal for the killing of Black Axe member [coded separately].

On 27 March 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants engaged Nigerian troops in an armed clash when they attacked the troops' position at the eastern outskirts of Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 28 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed one person and wounded an unspecified number of others at Sobe (Owan West, Edo). The assailants invaded the house of the deceased who was a driver.

On 28 March 2023, an unidentified armed group with affiliation to the APC attacked the home of the PDP house of assembly candidate for Shagamu constituency 2 at Ewuga area of Shagamu (Shagamu, Ogun). The gate keeper was tied up, the candidate escaped and valuables were stolen by the assailants.

On 28 March 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked travelers, killed one person and abducted 10 others after Gayam (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The assailants attacked the part of the road where there were rocks on both sides and hid them from view, other sources report that at least two persons were killed, soldiers were alerted and the assailants had deserted the area when they arrived.
On 28 March 2023, Nigerian troops clashed with a Zamfara militia at their hideouts in Tungan Fulan forest in Zurmi LGA (Zamfara). Two militia leaders; Kachallah Yellow and Dan Chaki were killed.
On 28 March 2023, a Kaduna militia attacked three villages including a pastoralists camp at Kala, Kutar and Taka-Lafiya in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). Three persons were killed and abducted 16 others.

On 28 March 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged hunters and policemen in an armed clash in Bisodun village (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode when they abducted a couple from the village. One hunter was killed, the abductees were abandoned by the assailants who fled from the area.

On 28 March 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Oluwo area of Abeokuta (Abeokuta South, Ogun). The assailants accosted the victim along a narrow path and shot him three times with close range.
On 28 March 2023, an ISWAP commander, Abu Muhammed killed his deputy in the presence of other fighters in Kajeri Dogumba, Mafa LGA (Borno) for allowing a military operation in their camp.

On 28 March 2023, troops of 25 Task Force Brigade ambushed ISWAP militants at their crossing point. Location coded to Damboa (Damboa, Borno), some militants fled and abandoned their bicycles, logistics and foodstuff, casualties are unknown.

On 28 March 2023, a Katsina militia abducted 10 persons from Ikulawa community (Dutsinma, Katsina) coded to Dutsin Ma. A local defense militia trailed the abductors and rescued 6 of the abductees while the remaining four were taken away. There are no report about ransom demands.

Around 29 March 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted three others in Kori-Oja (Obafemi, Ogun) coded to Owode. The murdered victim was killed when he attempted to escape, the other abductees were released after they paid ransom between 100,000 to 88,000 naira.

On 29 March 2023, a Zamfara militia shot and wounded a man who resisted being abducted from his residence in Gusau (Gusau, Zamfara). The man's wife and daughter were abducted, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 29 March 2023, ISWAP militants attacked a military base and were engaged in an armed clash by Nigerian troops and the Civilian JTF in Ajiri (Mafa, Borno). The attack was led by Abou Muhammed as a reprisal for the troops attack on their camps in Mukdolo and Bone [coded separately], the militants also ambushed the reinforcement team deployed from Mafa who also repelled them. An unspecified number of militants and one Civilian JTF operative were wounded.

On 29 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be from Uhouana, Amama and Ugbawka killed a member of MACBAN, coded to Amagunze (Nkanu East, Enugu) and other persons at different locations [coded separately] as claimed by MACBAN. An unspecified number of cattle were also killed during the attacks.

On 30 March 2023, an unidentified armed group of Oro worshippers attacked and wounded four muslim worshippers at a mosque in Ilare, Ile-Ife (Ife Central, Osun). The victims were attacked for flouting the order to stay indoors by the Oro practitioners.

Around 30 March 2023 (as reported), Boko Haram militants [JAS faction] abducted two civilians from Kuburmbula (Chibok, Borno). The abductees were rescued by troops who were on a fighting patrol [no report of a clash].

On 30 March 2023, Nigerian troops of the Army and Air Force engaged a Kaduna militia in an armed clash in Mariga LGA (Niger). The militia's escape route was bombed by NAF while ground troops shelled the over 500 militiamen who raided villages in the area in a convoy of about 100 motorcycles. Scores of militiamen were killed, over 2000 cows were intercepted and 2 soldiers were wounded and 100 of abductees were rescued. Fatalities coded as 20.

On 30 March 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists wounded an unspecified number of students and teachers when they invaded a school at Alaropo Nla (Ori Ire, Oyo). The assailants who numbered up to 20 invaded the school with their cattle which they wanted to graze, but were resisted and the victims were cut with swords and machetes.

Around 30 March 2023 (as reported), Nigerian troops clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at Kulumukuwa village in Geidam LGA (Yobe). The militants were imposing taxes on civilians in the area, one militant was killed and the others fled.

On 31 March 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 60 attacked residents of Garin Baka (Ardo Kola, Taraba), killed at least 15 persons and abducted about 60 others. The assailants invaded the village and shot sporadically, burnt houses, looted shops and warehouses and rustled cows. Many people escaped into the bushes with gunshot wounds, several others including women and children were missing.

On 31 March 2023, a Niger militia ambushed a joint team of security operatives and a local defense militia and engaged them in an armed clash in (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa. The assailants killed 6 civilians, abducted 14 others made up of mostly women, two local defense militiamen were also killed while several of the assailants fled with bullet injuries. Total of 8 fatalities.
On 31 March 2023, Nigerian troops on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at the Kaso general area in Kajuru LGA (Kaduna). The patrol began the previous day. Casualties are unknown.

On 31 March 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed a construction worker whom they abducted in Yenagoa (Yenagoa, Bayelsa). The victim was abducted along the Akenpai axis and his body was found with a gunshot wound the following day. The police said that the attack was cult related.

On 31 March 2023, suspected armed pastoralists abducted five travelers along Ikirun-Oshogbo road (Ifelodun, Osun). The abductees included the driver and four passengers. A female passenger and driver of the vehicle were rescued.

On 31 March 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be from Ubahu killed a member of MACBAN while another fled with gunshot injuries, at Agbogazi Nike (Enugu East, Enugu) and killed other persons at different locations [coded separately] as claimed by MACBAN. An unspecified number of cattle were also killed during the attacks.
On 31 March 2023, a Katsina militia killed five persons in Barebari village (Funtua, Katsina).
On 31 March 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a businessman from his residence in Umuchu community (Aguata, Anambra). A ransom of 50 million naira was demanded.

On 31 March 2023, troops of Operation Forest Sanity clashed with ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants during a fighting patrol which began the previous day in Kubusu forest in Chikun LGA (Kaduna). Five militants were killed, other fled with gunshot injuries, rifles, magazines, ammunitions, motorcycles and other items were recovered by the troops as claimed by the Defense Headquarters.

On 1 February 2023, Black Axe militia [also called Aye militia] members clashed with Eiye militia at Etegbin (Ojo, Lagos) after the Aye members trailed an Eiye member who they accused of killing one of their members to a drinking joint. The clash escalated towards Ajangbadi and several persons were wounded.

On 1 February 2023, an unidentified armed group in their numbers armed with IEDs, petrol bombs and other explosives attacked a police station and a residential building within the same premises at Nnobi (Idemili South, Anambra). The assailants killed a 16 year old male civilian and wounded another girl, both victims were related to policemen.

On 1 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the commissioner for women's affairs in Cross River state along Mayne avenue (Calabar South, Cross River) coded to Anantigha. There are no reports about ransom demands, other sources report that she was abducted alongside an unidentified woman and that the abductors had pretended to be soldiers who demanded for why the abductee was driving a car with covered number plates. The abductee was rescued around 8 March by soldiers who raided the abductor's hideout [coded separately].

On 2 February 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia clashed with operatives of the Anambra vigilante service who were on a routine patrol in Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). The clash lasted for several minutes and one vigilante member was killed.

On 2 February 2023, troops of 1 Division of the Nigerian army on a fighting patrol clashed with a Kaduna militia at Manini village (Chikun, Kaduna). 30 abductees were rescued by the troops who also recovered two motorcycles, casualties are unknown.

On 2 February 2023, an unidentified armed group invaded a police anti-cult unit and were engaged in an armed clash by policemen on duty at Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). The assailants who threw petrol bombs into the police station were repelled, one policeman was killed, some were fatally wounded and the assailants' bombs destroyed some building in the station.

On 2 February 2023, suspected Ebube Agu operatives ambushed the convoy of the APGA gubernatorial candidate, wounded his police orderly who later died and two others at Okpoto (Ishielu, Ebonyi). The driver of the APGA candidate was killed, his backup Hilux van was set ablaze and at least five persons were missing. The state commander of Ebube Agu denied the attack.

On 2 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and wounded a farmer on his farm near Oloke village in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). The victim was attacked with a machete and was asked by the assailants to inform the other residents of their coming.

On 2 February 2023, soldiers beat up security officers on night duty at the main campus of the University of Benin at Ugbowo (Egor, Edo) after they scaled the perimeter fence to gain entrance. The attack was a reprisal following a clash between the soldiers and students earlier [coded separately]; scores of civilians including students were wounded and several vehicles on the campus were destroyed.

On 2 February 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed a local defense militia that was pursuing them at Mji community in Kankara LGA (Katsina). The assailants received information about the local defense militia's movement from informants, residents claimed that at least 30 local militiamen were killed and several others were wounded. The police area command disputed the fatality figures.

On 2 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a judge while he was presiding over a court sitting in Ejemekwuru (Oguta, Imo). The assailants who operated on motorcycles dragged the victim out of the court, shot him and left.

On 2 February 2023, a Katsina militia ambushed Yansakai militia from 11 villages who trailed them to a location at Yargoje forest (Kankara, Katsina) and attempted to recover cattle that were stolen the previous day by the Katsina militia [coded separately]. 41 Yansakai militiamen were killed; and later increased to between 72 and 102, two others were wounded, some sources report unspecified number of wounded persons, others report that the clash lasted for over 48 hours. 72 fatalities split across two events coded as 36.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering five beat up a community bank CEO whom they abducted alongside two other persons at Nnobi (Idemili South, Anambra). The CEO was escaped from the abductors who fired shots at his car windshield and tires before taking him away.
On 3 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed two civilians in Ikobi (Apa, Benue). Two other persons were missing.
On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two travelers along Iwuru-Turunkekpem (Biase, Cross River). An unspecified number of other travelers were abducted.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with policemen at a police station in Abagana (Njikoka, Anambra) and killed three operatives of the Anambra vigilante service who were on patrol before arriving at the police station. The policemen repelled the assailants who threw petrol bombs, destroyed some structures in the police station and set inmates free. Other sources report that two vigilante operatives were killed.

On 3 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed two persons when they attacked the residence of LP House of Representatives candidate for Lere federal constituency at Gure village (Lere, Kaduna). The candidate was away from his house.

On 3 February 2023, a Katsina militia clashed with Yansakai militia from 11 villages who trailed them to a location at Yargoje forest (Kankara, Katsina) and attempted to recover cattle that were stolen by the Katsina militia [coded separately]. Some sources report that the clash lasted for over 48 hours; 41 Yansakai militiamen were killed; and later increased to between 72 and 102, two others were wounded, other sources report unspecified number of wounded persons. 72 fatalities split across two events coded as 36.

On 4 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the wife, two sons of the traditional ruler of Bukpe and three other residents from their houses at Bukpe, Kwali Area Council (FCT). The wife and one of the ruler's sons were released after 2.5 million naira foodstuff, hard drugs and other items were paid as ransom around 27 March, a ransom of 3 million naira was demanded for the release of the remaining abductees.

Around 4 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed 7 members of the family of the district head of Mutum Biyu who were abducted [coded separately] from Mutum Biyu (Gassol, Taraba). 8 persons including the head's two wives and six children were abducted, one of them escaped and the rest were killed and their decomposing bodies were found.
On 4 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed three farmers when they attacked Ikobi (Apa, Benue). Other sources report that 4 persons were killed.

On 4 February 2023, a Fulani militia ambushed troops of Operation Whirl Stroke and engaged them in an armed clash at Mbapa (Gwer West, Benue). Three soldiers sustained various degrees of injuries, the troops overpowered the militiamen.

On 4 February 2023, suspected Kalare Boys Gang members attacked the residence of a PDP chieftain at Gombe (Gombe, Gombe) where he had arranged a meeting with women and youths. Five persons were wounded and the house was vandalized before policemen intervened, the chieftain claimed that the attack was related to his defection from APC to PDP.
On 4 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted an NGO intern around Jahi axis (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The abductee was released on 8 February, there are no reports about ransom demands.

On 4 February 2023, Nigerian troops raided the hideouts of ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants and engaged them in an armed clash at Balange village, on the fringes of the Sambisa Forest Reserve (Gwoza, Borno). Five militants were killed and 55 abductees were rescued.

Around 5 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group abducted a farmer from his farm at Oko Oparun village (Ondo East, Ondo) coded to Bolorunduro. A ransom of 700 hundred thousand naira was demanded, the body of the victim was discovered four days later following the family's failure to pay the ransom.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins invaded the house of a PDP chieftain at (Akpabuyo, Cross River) coded to Ikot Nakanda. The chieftain and his family were not at home, the gate keeper was beat up and stabbed multiple times, the assailants who were armed with machetes, sticks and firearms also vandalized properties. The PDP claimed that the APC was responsible for the attack.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed the convoy of the PRP governorship candidate in Cross River at Betem axis (Biase, Cross River). Two persons were killed and four others were wounded, the candidate who is also a former minister survived. Some sources report that 3 persons were killed, a large number of others were abducted and the car of murdered victims was mistaken to have been that of the governorship candidate, others report that four persons were also abducted and several others were wounded.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted nine locals in Monu village, coded to Rubochi (Kuje, FCT) while they were loading logs of wood into a truck in the forest. Eight of the abductees were released after the abductors asked them to return, claiming that they had found their target. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 5 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked civilians and killed three persons at Maiyanga, Bokkos LGA (Plateau). The assailants shot sporadically during the attack, two other persons sustained gunshot wounds.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku and Omor militias clashed over a suspected boundary dispute at Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra) and Omor [coded separately]. Five persons were killed, some sources report that at least 10 persons were killed, others report that one to six others were abducted, houses were set ablaze and IEDs were planted and yet to be detonated. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 2.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku and Omor militias clashed over a suspected boundary dispute at Omor (Ayamelum, Anambra) and Anaku [coded separately]. Five persons were killed, some sources report that at least 10 persons were killed, others report that one to six others were abducted, houses were set ablaze and IEDs were planted and yet to be detonated. 5 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 6 February 2023, Amasiri and Nde Ndukwe residents attacked farm settlements in Oso (Afikpo South, Ebonyi) and killed one person during the attacks which lasted for 3 days before the intervention of security operatives. Houses, farm produce and properties were destroyed, four others were abducted and later released after a peace meeting organized by council chairmen and monarchs. The murdered victim was behead, his head was taken away by the assailants. Fatality split accross 3 events, coded as 1.

On 6 February 2023, Anaku militia clashed with soldiers who were sent to enforce peace in Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra). One soldier was abducted and his rifle was stolen, the soldiers retaliated and raided the community [coded separately].
On 6 February 2023, ISWAP fighters attacked and clashed with Boko Haram fighters who were moving towards the axis of Tumbun Gini (Abadan, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 6 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists killed one man while he was fishing and also attacked his brother at Ugboanyim-Aniyi in Amagunze (Nkanu East, Enugu). The murdered victim's body was found the following day with machete cuts, residents of the community fled the area due to fear.

On 6 February 2023, Nigerian conducted several artillery fire missions against ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants at Tumbun Barebare, Tumbun Mata, Kaye Kura, Kwatan Yobe, and Dumba in Kukawa LGA (Borno). 42 militants were killed.

On 7 February 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji invaded the hideout of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Danmarke forest (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. Scores of militiamen were killed in the clash that lasted overnight [coded separately]. 20 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 10.

On 7 February 2023, Amasiri and Nde Ndukwe attacked farm settlements in Oso (Afikpo South, Ebonyi) and killed one person during the attacks which started the previous day and lasted for 3 days before the intervention of security operatives. Houses, farm produce and properties were destroyed, four others were abducted and later released after a peace meeting organized by council chairmen and monarchs. The murdered victim was behead, his head was taken away by the assailants. Fatality split across 3 events, coded as 0.
On 7 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted one person from Gwandu town (Gwandu, Kebbi). The abductee was rescued by policemen on 10 February.

On 7 February 2023, a Kaduna militia killed the chief Imam of Nomadic Central mosque and the son of a Fulani chief at Rugan Ardo in Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). Six other people were also abducted, four of whom were the wives of the victim. Three of the wives were released after a ransom of 2 million naira was paid, the first wife was killed by the abductors [coded separately].

On 7 February 2023, ISWAP fighters clashed with rival Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters at Kuwa Nguro and Ngoldiri villages in Damboa LGA (Borno). The clash lasted about 3 hours; scores of fighters from both sides were killed, coded as 20, many other fighters were wounded, some ammunition and motorcycles were seized from the JAS faction.

On 7 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the brother of the spokesperson of CUPP who is also a PDP candidate for the House of Representatives at Akokwa (Ideato North, Imo) and vandalized his house according to him, the house came under heavy gunfire by the assailants who were armed with explosives and shot water tanks because they assumed he was hiding inside.
On 7 February 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted eight civilians when they invaded Janjala community (Kagarko, Kaduna). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 7 February 2023, soldiers invaded a market and beat up some traders in Ado-Ekiti (Ado Ekiti, Ekiti) after they were invited by one trader to intervene in a civil matter. Some customers were also harassed by the soldiers.

On 7 February 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a university lecturer at his residence in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). The victim attempted to escape when he saw the assailants who shot him four times in the chest. The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 8 February 2023, soldiers attacked civilians, killed an unspecified number of people and set houses and other properties ablaze in Anaku (Ayamelum, Anambra) over claims that their colleague was killed in a clash that occurred between Anaku and Omor. The soldiers demanded that the corpse of their colleague by produced. Fatalities coded as 3.

On 8 February 2023, troops of Operation Hadarin Daji invaded the hideout of a Zamfara militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Danmarke forest (Bukkuyum, Zamfara) coded to Bukuyum. Scores of militiamen were killed in the clash that started the previous night [coded separately]. 20 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 10.

On 8 February 2023, Amasiri and Nde Ndukwe attacked farm settlements in Oso (Afikpo South, Ebonyi) and killed one person during the attacks which started two days earlier, before the intervention of security operatives. Houses, farm produce and properties were destroyed, four others were abducted and later released after a peace meeting organized by council chairmen and monarchs. The murdered victim was behead, his head was taken away by the assailants. Fatality split across 3 events, coded as 0.

On 8 February 2023, policemen shot the chairman of Ekpan development committee and abducted him along Warri-Sapele road (Warri South, Delta). Some sources claim that the policemen were acting on the orders of the state governor and the PDP governorship aspirant.

On 8 February 2023, troops of 1 Division in collaboration with the air component of Operation Whirl stroke clashed with a Kaduna militia and cleared Manini-Kuriga, Farin Ruwa, Kwanan Yashi, Makera, Dogon Dawa-Maidaro, Kidandan-Yadi and Sabon Birnin in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna) and Giwa LGA [coded separately]. The operation lasted for about 48 hours; 4 militiamen were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, one loaded rifle and six motorcycles were recovered by the troops. 4 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.

On 8 February 2023, troops of 1 Division in collaboration with the air component of Operation Whirl stroke clashed with a Kaduna militia and cleared Dogon-Dawa-Kidandan in Giwa LGA (Kaduna) and Birnin Gwari LGA [coded separately]. The operation lasted for about 48 hours; 4 militiamen were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, one loaded rifle and six motorcycles were recovered by the troops. 4 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.

On 8 February 2023, a Kaduna militia abducted five civilians from Maraban Kajuru (Kajuru, Kaduna). The abductees included a pastor, his wife, another resident and his two children. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 8 February 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai ambushed and clashed with a large number of Boko Haram/ ISWAP militants who were moving logistics along Damboa road (Damboa, Borno). Several militants were killed, a large quantity of logistics supply was seized by the troops. Fatalities coded as 3.

Around 9 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed a farmer whom they had abducted about four days earlier from his farm [coded separately] at Oko Oparun (Ondo East, Ondo) coded to Bolorunduro. The abductees demanded for a ransom of 700 thousand naira, but killed the abductee over this family's inability to pay and because his wife alerted Amotekun corps and other villagers. The victim's body was found with chemical all over it.

On 9 February 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed soldiers on patrol and killed three of them at Asemokwu community (Ndokwa East, Delta) coded to Aboh. Three of the soldiers were killed on the spot, one who was among the others that were wounded died in the hospital, the traditional ruler of the community was beheaded by the assailants.

On 9 February 2023, troops of 1 Division in collaboration with the air component of Operation Whirl stroke clashed with a Kaduna militia and cleared Manini-Kuriga, Farin Ruwa, Kwanan Yashi, Makera, Dogon Dawa-Maidaro, Kidandan-Yadi and Sabon Birnin in Birnin Gwari LGA (Kaduna) and Giwa LGA [coded separately]. The operation lasted for about 48 hours; 4 militiamen were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, one loaded rifle and six motorcycles were recovered by the troops. 4 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.

On 9 February 2023, troops of 1 Division in collaboration with the air component of Operation Whirl stroke clashed with a Kaduna militia and cleared Dogon-Dawa-Kidandan in Giwa LGA (Kaduna) and Birnin Gwari LGA [coded separately]. The operation lasted for about 48 hours; 4 militiamen were killed and others escaped with gunshot wounds, one loaded rifle and six motorcycles were recovered by the troops. 4 fatalities split across 4 events coded as 1.

On 9 February 2023, Nigerian troops pursued an unidentified armed group that attacked civilians at Nagi community in Mbachohon council ward (Gwer West, Benue) away. 5 civilians; two women and three men were killed by the attackers who also and set more than 50 houses including the palace of the traditional ruler ablaze before the arrival of the troops.

On 9 February 2023, a Kaduna militia in large numbers attacked civilians in Riche village which is 2 km away from Kagarko town (Kagarko, Kaduna). Three persons were wounded and 18 others were abducted.

On 9 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins who were dressed in police uniforms shot at car of the Rivers state director-general of the PDP presidential campaign in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers) when he went to inspect the venue of the PDP's rally. The victim claimed that the rally venue was set ablaze and that the assailants were policemen who arrived the venue with police vehicles that were attached to the state governor. The governor denied the claims and accused the supporters of Atiku of spreading propaganda.
On 9 February 2023, a Katsina militia attacked and killed the village head of Daurawa village in Batsari LGA (Katsina).

On 9 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a student in Sabo (Kuje, FCT) after they dragged him out of his room and shot him in the chest. The assailants did not take anything from the victim's room and claimed that they were only hired to kill the victim.
On 9 February 2023, ISWAP militants attacked and clashed with rival Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Arege (Abadan, Borno). Several militants were killed, coded as 3.

On 9 February 2023, ISWAP fighters led by Ba'ana Chingori attacked the convoy of a newly appointed Boko Haram Amir and engaged them in an armed clash at Gulmari village in Konduga LGA (Borno). 15 Boko Haram fighters were killed, one of their gun trucks was seized while the Amir escaped.

On 9 February 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed a student on the Calabar campus (Calabar Municipal, Cross River) of University of Cross River. They drove into the campus and drove straight to where the victim was, they covered his face with his shirt after he was shot twice and took his bag before they drove off. The reason for the attack is unknown, other sources report that the assailants were operatives of the joint task force backed by the state government which is comprised of soldier, policemen, DSS and NSCDC operatives.
On 9 February 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with Nigerian military forces who repelled their attack on Naka town (Gwer West, Benue). Casualties are unknown.

On 10 February 2023, a Niger militia that attempted to attack a market was repelled by a local defense militia in Chibiani (Muya, Niger). An unspecified number of Niger militiamen were killed, coded as 3.
On 10 February 2023, a Niger militia invaded Zagzaga community (Muya, Niger). Casualties are unknown.

On 10 February 2023, troops of 21 Armored Brigade in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram [JAS faction] operatives during an offensive patrol at Churchur, Mbaiwa and China in Bama LGA (Borno) and Kashimeri [coded separately] and other new established villages. 7 militants were killed, others fled and abandoned women, children and old persons who were rescued by the troops. The camps were set ablaze, 7 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 3.

On 10 February 2023, troops of 21 Armored Brigade in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives clashed with Boko Haram [JAS faction] operatives during an offensive patrol in Kashimeri (Bama, Borno), Churchur, Mbaiwa and China [coded separately] and other new established villages. 7 militants were killed, others fled and abandoned women, children and old persons who were rescued by the troops. The camps were set ablaze, 7 fatalities split across 2 events coded as 4.

On 10 February 2023, an unidentified armed group ambushed and killed three policemen along Ihiala-Orlu road (Ihiala, Anambra). The policemen who were aides of the Delta state governor were end route Umuahia on official duty, the fourth policeman was wearing plain clothes and was set free by the assailants.

On 10 February 2023, an unidentified armed group suspected to be affiliated with a politician attacked and wounded 15 supporters of the House of Representatives candidate representing Obokun/Oriade federal constituency at his residence in Osogbo (Oshogbo, Osun). The victims were house residents who went to declare their support for the House member and they were attacked with machetes and clubs. One of the assailants was apprehended and he claimed that they were sponsored by an Osogbo based politician.

On 10 February 2023, Boko Haram [JAS faction] fighters ambushed ISWAP fighters in a reprisal attack at Burmari village in Konduga LGA (Borno). At least 6 ISWAP fighters were killed, the rest were forced to withdraw to Hasanari village in Konduga LGA.
On 10 February 2023, a Kaduna militia killed a farmer in Maro (Kajuru, Kaduna). The militiamen were riding on motorcycles when they saw the victim clearing his farm and shot him.
On 11 February 2023, a Niger militia attacked Kafin Koro (Paikoro, Niger). There are no further details and casualties are unknown.

Around 11 February 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group suspected to be assassins killed a pub owner at his pub in Odoba (Ogbadibo, Benue). Many other persons were injured, the murdered victim was not the target of the attack, a female suspect was arrested and later released by the police.

On 11 February 2023, a Niger militia engaged policemen who attempted to repel them in an armed clash around Kwakuti-Dajigbe village in Lambata (Gurara, Niger). 5 policemen and scores of militiamen were killed, other militiamen fled with bullet wounds.

On 11 February 2023, Eiye confraternity clashed with Black axe militia (also called Aiye confraternity) at Ijanikin (Ojo, Lagos) when the Eiye members invaded the home of the leader of the Aiye killer squad. The targeted Aiye member was not around, his brother was macheted and severely injured while two other militia members were killed.

On 11 February 2023, suspected APC members attacked and wounded LP members at Jakande (Eti-Osa, Lagos) as claimed by the LP members. The number of wounded persons was unspecified and their phones were stolen, some sources report that four persons were wounded and the assailants were armed with clubs and machetes. Other sources report that several vehicles were vandalized and many of the supporters were wounded. The APC in Lagos state described the LP claims as baseless and untrue.

On 11 February 2023, policemen engaged an unidentified armed group of 5 in an armed clash at Ndoki waterside in Port Harcourt (Port Harcourt, Rivers). One member of the armed group was killed; another was arrested, an abductee was rescued, arms and ammunition were recovered by the police.

On 11 February 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and wounded the PDP chairman of Ogbaku ward at his residence in Umunomo Nsokpo (Mbaitoli, Imo) coded to Ogbaku. The victim was shot in one his legs by the assailants who gained entrance into the compound by scaling the fence and fled after the shooting.

On 12 February 2023, Black Axe (also called Aiye Confraternity) and Red Axe militias clashed in Gboko (Gboko, Benue) following a disagreement by some party supporters after a political rally over the money to be shared among them. The clash lasted for three days [coded separately], eight people were killed and seven houses were burnt, 8 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 3.

On 12 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted the district head of Maigamu community and his son, coded to Angware town (Jos East, Plateau) where the community is located. The district head was rescued by local defense militiamen, there are no reports on ransom demands for his son.

On 12 February 2023, suspected Icelander cult militia members abducted a woman in Abarikpo community (Ahoada East, Rivers). The corpse of the abductee who was a pastors' wife was found hours later [coded separately]. Her husband claims that she was accused of gossiping with the name of a militia member.

On 12 February 2023, suspected Icelander cult militia members raped a women to death after they abducted her [coded separately] from Abarikpo community (Ahoada East, Rivers). The victim's body was found with multiple injuries after she was gang-raped. Her husband claims that she was accused of gossiping with the name of a militia member.

On 13 February 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia killed an aide of a PDP chieftain in front of his residence at Agege area (Agege, Lagos). The assailants shot sporadically when they invaded the area, other sources report that the victim was killed during a clash involving transport workers.
On 13 February 2023, a Sokoto militia abducted one person along Gundumi-Isa road (Goronyo, Sokoto). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 13 February 2023, policemen in collaboration with hunters and a local defense militia clashed with an unidentified armed group that was tracked and sighted at Lawanti axis (Akko, Gombe). One member of the group was killed; two others escaped with gunshot wounds, a rifle, a magazine with 5 live bullets and a motorcycle were recovered.

On 13 February 2023, Black Axe (also called Aiye Confraternity) and Red Axe militias clashed in Gboko (Gboko, Benue) following a disagreement by some party supporters after a political rally over the money to be shared among them. The clash started the previous day and lasted till the next [coded separately]; eight people were killed and seven houses were burnt, 6 persons were arrested in connection with the clash, 8 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 3.

On 13 February 2023, ISWAP militants clashed with Nigerian troops when they attacked a checkpoint on the outskirts of Damboa (Damboa, Borno). The militants fled and also claimed to have targeted and fired a 40mm grenade launcher at a camp of the Nigerian army. Casualties are unknown.

On 13 February 2023, troops of 152 battalion Banki of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives and hunters ambushed Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants at Banki (Bama, Borno). 8 militants were killed, 6 rifles, two motorcycles and other items were recovered.

On 13 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attempted to attack a police station and were engaged in an armed clash by policemen at Ogidi (Idemili North, Anambra). One of the assailants was killed, many expended cartridges and 25 liters of PMS were recovered.
On 13 February 2023, presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants who were mounted on motorcycles shot at farmers in the vicinity of Wuturo, Konduga LGA (Borno). Casualties are unknown.

On 14 February 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted 15 NYSC members at Ihiala junction (Ihiala, Anambra) while they were heading to Lagos from the Imo state orientation camp. The abductees were rescued by policemen who chased the abductors to along Isseke where they abandoned them and fled.

On 14 February 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the Anambra State Vigilante Service at Nkpor (Idemili North, Anambra) when the defense militia attempted to repel them. One woman who was a beggar was killed by the assailant's stray bullet when they shot at an abductee who fled, the defense militia also fled following superior gunfire from the assailants who proceeded to riddle two cars used by the defense militia as cover with bullets.

On 14 February 2023, Black Axe (also called Aiye Confraternity) and Red Axe militias clashed in Gboko (Gboko, Benue) following a disagreement by some party supporters after a political rally over the money to be shared among them. The clash started on 12 February [coded separately]; eight people were killed and seven houses were burnt, 10 persons were arrested in connection with the clash, 8 fatalities split across 3 events coded as 2.

On 14 February 2023, a Katsina militia killed at least two people and abducted 12 others when they invaded Mahuta B village (Dandume, Katsina) and shot sporadically. The abductees included women and children.

On 14 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked the campaign team of a PDP House of Representatives candidate in Katsina metropolis (Katsina, Katsina). One person was killed and unspecified number of others were wounded.
On 14 February 2023, a Katsina militia attacked a residence and killed one person at Wagini town (Batsari, Katsina).

On 14 February 2023, two factions of Greenlander cult militia that are loyal to 'VIP' and 'Ebuka' clashed over a leadership tussle at Ikata community, coded to Abarikpo (Ahoada East, Rivers). 10 persons were killed, including a civilian who was hit by a stray bullet and died from his injuries a few days later, the police claimed that two persons were arrested in connection with the clash.

On 14 February 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to a distress call along Danja-Bakori road (Danja, Katsina) where the militiamen blocked the road and were robbing commuters. One militia member was killed, others fled with injuries, the policemen recovered one stick, one cutlass and three mobile phones.

On 14 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed two residents and abducted many others when they attacked Munu community in Abaji Area Council (FCT). A provision store and a pub were looted by the assailants in the attack which lasted one hour, other sources report that scores of residents were abducted.

On 14 February 2023, a Katsina militia engaged in an armed clash with policemen who responded to a distress call at Kitibawa village, coded to Dutsin Ma (Dutsinma, Katsina). The militiamen who were in their numbers shot sporadically and abducted one civilian; it is unclear whether the abductee was rescued, one of the militiamen was killed an the others fled with gunshot wounds.

On 14 February 2023, Nigerian troops engaged presumed ISWAP/ Boko Haram militants in an armed clash in the vicinity of Gamboru town (Ngala, Borno). Casualties are unknown.

Other sources report that the clash was between two militant groups.

On 15 February 2023, ISWAP and Boko Haram [JAS faction] militants clashed at Wuyafchi village, Damboa LGA (Borno). 16 militants were killed.
On 15 February 2023, ISWAP militants killed one civilian and abducted his mother in Jakana (Bama, Borno).

On 15 February 2023, soldiers attacked and beat up a commuter who was on his way to Ikorodu (Ikorodu, Lagos) for having a police sticker on his car. The soldiers were on a reprisal over the murder of their colleague by a policeman around the area [coded separately].
On 15 February 2023, a local defense militia killed a taxi driver at 2nd East Circular junction in Benin City (Oredo, Edo) as claimed by the victim's family. The cause of the attack is unknown.

On 16 February 2023, an unidentified armed group was repelled by joint security operatives (police and military forces) when they attacked a training at Ukpor (Nnewi South, Anambra) where INEC staff and ad hoc staff including NYSC members were preparing for the elections. There were no casualties, joint security patrols in the area were intensified.

On 17 February 2023, a suspected Fulani militia killed two people and injured many others when they attacked Awgu Egbeleli (Agwu, Enugu) coded to Awgu. On 17 February 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia loyal to a governorship candidate killed a member of the APC in Mowe community (Obafemi, Ogun). The reason for the attack is unknown.

On 18 February 2023, an unidentified armed group shot sporadically when they invaded the campaign rally of the APC at Agba ward (Ishielu, Ebonyi). There were no casualties.

On 20 February 2023, suspected IPOB militants in their large number engaged policemen in an armed clash when they attacked a police station at Awada, coded to nearby Obosi (Idemili South, Anambra). On 20 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and wounded some supporters of the ADC senatorial candidate for Abia North senatorial district at Nneato (Nneochi, Abia) coded to Nkwoagu Isuochi. On 25 February 2023, Boko Haram [JAS Faction] militants who attacked voters were engaged in an armed clash by soldiers in Gwoza LGA (Borno). The militants shot at the voters from the top of Mandara mountain, 5 voters consisting of two females and three males were wounded, the militants fled.
On 26 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed 8 persons at Tse-Lgar and Tse-Magu (Guma, Benue) coded to Gbajimba and another two at Tse-Dudu [coded separately].
On 26 February 2023, an unidentified armed group drove towards voters and attempted to run them over and disrupt voting at Morogbo area of Badagry LGA (Lagos).

On 26 February 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed 7 persons including a Benue Community Volunteer Guard who is presumed to have been unarmed at Tse Fela in Mbabuande (Gwer West, Benue) and Tse Akyegh [coded separately]. The attacks took place simultaneously from two fronts, properties and food barns were destroyed, the volunteer who was killed was the ward commander. 7 fatalities split across two events coded as 4.

On 26 February 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering about 20 beat up and injured the mother and gate keeper of an APC supporter when they attacked his home at Itele (Ado-Odo, Ogun). The assailants shot sporadically, riddled the house with bullets, destroyed properties and claimed they were attacking APC supporters in the axis.

On 26 February 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked and killed 7 persons including a Benue Community Volunteer Guard who is presumed to have been unarmed at Tse Akyegh coded to Naka (Gwer West, Benue) and Tse Fela [coded separately]. The attacks took place simultaneously from two fronts, properties and food barns were destroyed, the volunteer who was killed was the ward commander. 7 fatalities split across two events coded as 3.
On 26 February 2023, suspected APC members abducted five INEC presiding officers in Kogi state, location coded to Lokoja (Lokoja, Kogi).
On 26 February 2023, suspected armed Fulani pastoralists attacked and killed 2 persons at Tse-Dudu (Guma, Benue) coded to Daudu and 8 others at Tse-Lgar and Tse-Magu [coded separately].

On 26 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked a bus conveying INEC staff and NYSC members in (Ukwuani, Delta) coded to Obiaruku Quarters as they were returning from election duty. The INEC staff was killed, while some corps members sustained injuries.

On 27 February 2023, suspected APC loyalists attacked PDP supporters at the House of Representatives collation center for Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa at Bununu town (Tafawa Balewa, Bauchi). Many people were wounded, and more than 10 vehicles were damaged, as claimed by the PDP.

On 27 February 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen in an armed clash when they invaded the police divisional headquarters at Ndagbo Nkporo (Ohafia, Abia). Three policemen were wounded; the armory was broken into, weapons, an unspecified amount of ammunition and sets of service uniforms were stolen by the assailants.

On 27 February 2023, an unidentified armed group killed the traditional ruler of Umuezeaka (Ezza North, Ebonyi) at his residence and his children fled into hiding. The state government claimed that the gubernatorial candidate of APGA was responsible for the attack and that the victim was killed over his refusal to support the party, the accused candidate denied the claims and insisted that it was a desperate move to tarnish his image.

Around 27 February 2023 (as reported), ISWAP fighters clashed with Boko Haram [JAS Faction] fighters after they intercepted them at Choliye village in Konduga LGA (Borno). The Boko Haram fighters were fleeing the area with their families and 200 persons most of whom were women and children were killed.

On 27 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and wounded traders when they invaded Balogun market, coded to Lagos Island (Lagos Island, Lagos), Ladipo and Ebute-Ero markets [coded separately]. Shops were robbed, some traders claimed that they received threatening messages warning them to stay away from the market. The police spokesperson in Lagos dismissed the claims of attacks and claimed that the assailants were enforcing an agreement the traders made to close shop on Sunday and Monday.

On 27 February 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and wounded traders when they invaded Ladipo and Ebute-Ero markets, coded to Ebute-Metta (Lagos Mainland, Lagos) and Balogun market [coded separately]. Shops were robbed, some traders claimed that they received threatening messages warning them to stay away from the market. The police spokesperson in Lagos dismissed the claims of attacks and claimed that the assailants were enforcing an agreement the traders made to close shop on Sunday and Monday.
On 28 February 2023, a Niger militia shot and killed a farmer on his farm at Baje-Patiko (Muya, Niger) coded to Sarkin Pawa.

On 1 January 2023, a Kaduna militia was engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops who responded to a distress call at Rafin Sarki village in Giwa LGA (Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed, split across two events coded as 1 and one rifle was recovered.

On 1 January 2023, troops of 222 batallion Konduga in collaboration with Civilian JTF operatives intercepted and clashed Boko Haram [JAS] militants at Konduga (Konduga, Borno). Two militants were killed.

On 1 January 2023, troops of Operation Hadin Kai in collaboration with hunters clashed with Boko Haram [JAS] militants who abducted two civilians in the axis of Mafa (Mafa, Borno). The militants abandoned the abductees and fled.

On 1 January 2023, Black Axe cult militia also known as Aiye and Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shibiri, Igbede and Imude areas of Ajangbadi (Ojo, Lagos). The clash lasted from 28 Dec to 3 January [coded separately] and was sparked by the killing of an Aiye member by the Eiye group. Two other militia members were killed, split across 7 events and coded as 0.

On 1 January 2023, a Kaduna militia in large numbers abducted six civilians in Jere (Kagarko, Kaduna). One of the abductees was taken when the militia invaded the residence of the former emir, the other five were taken from his neigbor's residence. There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 January 2023, a Kaduna militia that attacked residents were engaged in an armed clash by a local defense militia in Anguwar Salanke, Kagarko LGA (Kaduna). The assailants overpowered the local defense militia; two civilians were wounded, one by a stray bullet and the other from a shattered window pane, one other person was abducted.
On 1 January 2023, a policeman shot and killed two civilians at Filin Canada in Katsina (Katsina, Katsina). Three teenagers sustained gunshot wounds, the reason for the attack is unknown.

On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a woman in Owutu (Afikpo South, Ebonyi). The victim was the wife the Ebube Agu commander in Afikpo South LGA, the assailants also set their home ablaze. The victim's husband claimed that his two daughters were also killed and the assailants who numbered as many as 19 were led by one of the develpment coordinators in the LGA.

On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a permanent secretary of Plateau state ministry of works from the entrance of his residence in Jos (Jos North, Plateau). The abductee was rescued by policemen in Bassa LGA after the abductors abandoned him and his vehicle.

On 1 January 2023, a Zamfara militia in large numbers abducted 15 civilians who were traveling along Magazu (Tsafe, Zamfara). The abductees were rescued after the militiamen abandoned them following a search and rescue operation by security operatives.

On 1 January 2023, a Zamfara militia in large numbers abducted a retired colonel, two of his children and two other persons near Yan Doton Daji (Tsafe, Zamfara). The abductors shot sporadically and scared people, there are no reports about ransom demands.
On 1 January 2023, an unidentified armed group wounded one man, abducted him and three other men at Baipe community in Kubwa (Abuja Municipal, FCT). There are no reports about ransom demands.

On 1 January 2023, policemen on patrol engaged a Zamfara militia in an armed clash along Gusau-Magami-Dansadau road (Gusau, Zamfara). One militia member was killed and the others fled, guns, ammunition and charms were recovered by the policemen.
On 2 January 2023, Waja and Lunguda militias clashed in Lafia (Lamurde, Adamawa). Over 4 houses and 11 shops were set ablaze, there were no fatalities.

On 2 January 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia shot and killed the president-general of Obosi community in the community (Idemili South, Anambra). The victim was shot while he was in his car, some sources claim that the victim was attacked by the leader of a cult militia whose arrest by the police he facilitated.

On 2 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a truck driver, wounded three labourers and abducted six other persons at Rudu village (Toto, Nassarawa). The driver had attempted to run away before he was killed, a ransom of 20 million has been demanded for the abductees' release.

On 2 January 2023, a Kaduna militia was engaged in an armed clash with Nigerian troops who responded to a distress call at Rafin Sarki village in Giwa LGA (Kaduna) for the second day in a row. Two militiamen were killed, split across two events coded as 1, and one rifle was recovered.

On 2 January 2023, Black Axe cult militia also known as Aiye and Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shibiri, Igbede and Imude areas of Ajangbadi (Ojo, Lagos). The clash lasted from 28 Dec to 3 January [coded separately] and was sparked by the killing of an Aiye member by the Eiye group. Two other militia members were killed, split across 7 events and coded as 0.

On 2 January 2023, a soldier shot and killed a civilian at Asokoro (Abuja Municipal, FCT). The soldier had tried to halt the motorcyclist's movement and shot at them which resulted in the death of the victim who was the passenger. The soldiers fled and abandoned the corpse.

On 2 January 2023, policemen repelled a Katsina militia in their numbers that attacked a police nipping point along Jibia-Katsina road (Jibia, Katsina). One of the assailants was killed, the others fled with various degrees of wounds, one rifle, ammunition and money were recovered by the policemen. Two policemen were also wounded.

On 2 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked and killed four persons at Okpuno (Awka South, Anambra). The assailants had pursued someone into the compound where the victims were and shot them, one of the victims was a PDP chairman in the area.
On 2 January 2023, Boko Haram [JAS] fighters clashed with ISWAP fighters at Garin Ba'aba in Bama LGA (Borno). An unspecified number of fighters were killed, coded as 3.
On 2 January 2023, Zamfara Communal militia attacked commuters around Kucheri, along the Funtua- Tsafe Road, coded to Tsafe (Tsafe, Zamfara) and abducted many people.
On 2 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed two persons at Ekeh Awka in Awka (Awka South, Anambra) during a cult related reprisal attack and battle for supremacy.

On 3 January 2023, the Nigerian military clashed with Kaduna Communal Militia around Tungan Rafin Toba village in Birnin Gwari LGA, coded to Birnin Gwari (Birnin Gwari, Kaduna). The troop killed two militia members and recovered several weapons, including 2 AK47 rifles, 51 rounds of 7.62mm special, 4 AK47 riles magazines, five mobile phones, motorcycles and the sum of Two Hundred and Six thousand Naira (N206,000). 2 fatalities reported.

Around 3 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed one of the persons among the 16 others that were abducted on 11 November 2022 [coded separately] as they were returning to Gwombe (Kuje, FCT). The victim was killed over claims of non-cooperation by the abductors, the other abductees were relased after ransom.

On 3 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked residents in Nagi village at Gaambe-Ushin ward (Gwer West, Benue). Several people were injured by the assailants. Other sources report that two persons were wounded.

On 3 January 2023, Black Axe cult militia (also known as Aiye) and Eiye confraternity engaged in an armed clash at Shibiri, Igbede and Imude areas of Ajangbadi (Ojo, Lagos). The clash lasted from 28 Dec to 3 January [coded separately] and was sparked by the killing of an Aiye member by the Eiye group. Two other militia members were killed, split across 7 events and coded as 0.

On 3 January 2023, Nigerian troops carried out an ambush operation against a Kaduna militia and engaged them in an armed clash at Rafin Taba (Giwa, Kaduna). Two militiamen were killed, two rifles, ammunition, money and other items were recovered by the troops.
On 3 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed three people around Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). 3 fatalities reported.

On 3 January 2023, ISWAP claimed its fighters attacked the JTF base in Shara, coded to Biu (Biu, Borno) with machine guns. They killed two JTF fighters, burnt houses and went away with some properties. 2 fatalities reported

On 3 January 2023, Hausa and Fulani ethnic militias clashed in a market at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo) following a fight between a Hausa and Fulani in the market. The clash lasted till the next morning [coded separately]; one person was killed, many on both sides were wounded and shops were set ablaze.

On 3 January 2023, a suspected unidentified cult militia who rode on a motorcycle killed two commercial tricycle riders in Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Other sources report one fatality and that the attack is cult related.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a hotelier at his farm in Serafu village, coded to Iseyin (Iseyin, Oyo). The commandant of Amotekun claimed that the abductee was released.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted five family members along the Ochadamu- Ajaokuta road, coded to Ofu (Ofu, Kogi).
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group engaged policemen who were on patrol in an armed clash in Nunku town (Akwanga, Nassarawa). Two of the assailants and one policeman were killed.

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed four persons in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The victims included a legislative leader in the area, two businessmen and one of their staff. The reason for the attack is unknown.

Around 4 January 2023 (as reported), an unidentified armed group killed two boys and dumped their bodies in a river in Sapele (Sapele, Delta). The victims had been declared missing two days earlier, the reason for the attack is unknown.
On 4 January 2023, an unidentified cult militia killed one person at Ifite-Awka (Awka South, Anambra). Some sources report that the attack is a result of reprisal attacks between cult militias.
On 4 January 2023, Katsina Communal Militia abducted a woman along Wagini-Garin Dodo Road, coded to Wagini (Batsari, Katsina). No further details

On 4 January 2023, ISWAP claimed to have raided the headquarters of a local defense militia and killed two operatives in Chara, coded to Damaturu (Damaturu, Yobe). The militants also claimed to have set a number of houses ablaze.

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group numbering up to 25 invaded the office of the Anambra vigilante service and killed one operative at Ndikokwu village in Uli (Ihiala, Anambra). Two other operatives were wounded, the assailants set the building and vehicles ablaze before they escaped through the Ubahudara axis in Imo state.

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group of eight shot at communter in a vehicle around Kabba junction (Kabba, Kogi). Some of the bullets hit the car and tyres, the commuters were able to escape.

On 4 January 2023, policemen and a local defense militia engaged a Katsina militia in an armed clash at Karfi (Malumfashi, Katsina) after the militia had abducted one civilian from his residence in the area. One of the assailants was killed, the others fled with varying degrees of injuries and the abductee was rescued.

On 4 January 2023, Hausa and Fulani ethnic militias clashed in a market at Ayede-Ogbese (Akure North, Ondo) for the second day in a row, following a fight between a Hausa and Fulani in the market. The clash started the previous evening [coded separately]; one person was killed, many on both sides were wounded and shops were set ablaze (fatality coded on 3 January).

On 4 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man and abandoned his body in his car in Nawfia (Njikoka, Anambra). The victim was discovered with marks of violence and a suspected gunshot injury.

On 5 January 2023, Sokoto Communal Militia attacked Gidan Altine village, coded to Illela (Illela, Sokoto) and shot indiscriminately at the people; One person was shot dead in the attack. 1 fatality reported.
On 5 January 2023, the Obudu Communal group and the Tiv ethnic militia clashed along the Vande Ikya - Obudu road, coded to VandeIkya (VandeIkya, Benue). Casualties unknown.

On 5 January 2023, a suspected Fulani militia attacked residents in Tse-Girgi Dajo village at Gaambe-Ushin ward (Gwer West, Benue). One person was injured by the assailants. Other sources report that two persons were wounded.
On 5 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed a man in Ukpor town (Nnewi South, Anambra). There are no further details.
On 5 January 2023, an unidentified armed group killed one person and abducted another at Mosogar (Ethiope West, Delta). The murdered victim was shot when he resisted being abducted.

On 5 January 2023, an unidentified armed group beat up some traders and forcefully evicted them from their shops in Watt market shopping complex, coded to Anantigha (Calabar South, Cross River). The victims included the vice chairman of Watt market petty traders association, some sources report that the assailants were sent by local council chairman of Calabar South.
On 5 January 2023, Sokoto Communal militias abducted two commuters at Isa Junction, Isa (Isa, Sokoto).

On 5 January 2023, a suspect unidentified cult militia killed one person and dumped the body in Akure metropolis (Akure South, Ondo). The victim's body was burnt and put in a metal box, his identity is unknown. Other sources report that the attack was a result of an ongoing cult war.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group shot and killed a man in Chigari, Fufore (Fufore, Adamawa), when resisting abduction. A five-member armed group attempted to abduct the man but later shot him when he resisted. 1 fatality reported.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group abducted a girl in Kano (Kano Municipal, Kano) and demanded a ransom of two million naira for her release. The police arrested three teenagers of 19 years old as suspects of abduction.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group clashed with the police at the residence of the Plateau State House of Assembly's speaker in the Federal Low-Cost Housing, coded to Riyom (Jos South, Plateau). The gunfight erupted when the armed group attempted to abduct the speaker. No casualty reported.

On 6 January 2023, an unidentified armed group attacked INEC PVC collection centers in Ikpoba Okha LG, coded to Idogbo (Ikpoba Okha, Edo).
